title: CLI binary: ll-open parse <source-dir> → output.db with _ast + _lsp* tables
description:
## What
Add a `ll-open` CLI binary that pre-bakes source code into a `.db` file with `_ast` tables (tree-sitter) and optionally `_lsp*` tables (LSP enrichment). This is the missing entry point for the pre-bake pipeline.

## Why
Currently mache ingests raw source via tree-sitter at mount time — 10.7s for 248 Go files. If ley-line-open pre-bakes the `.db` once, mache mounts it instantly via SQLiteGraph (nodes-table fast path). The library code exists (`lsp::project_lsp`, `ts` crate, `schema::create_schema`) but there's no CLI to invoke it.

## Desired workflow
```
ll-open parse ~/project --lang go --output project.db
mache serve project.db   # instant — no tree-sitter, no CGO
```

## Architecture
- New `rs/ll-open/cli/` crate with `[[bin]]` target `ll-open`
- Subcommands: `parse` (source → db), maybe `enrich` (add LSP to existing db)
- `parse` walks source tree, runs tree-sitter via `ts` crate, writes `_ast` rows
- Schema projection via `schema::create_schema` + `schema::insert_node`
- Optional `--lsp` flag for LSP enrichment

## Connection to mache
- mache's `SelectWalker` auto-selects ASTWalker when `_ast` table present
- mache's `OpenSQLiteGraph` detects `nodes` table → fast path
- mache's `--control` reads from ley-line arena → hot-swap on rebuild

comments.text:
Closing as superseded — work has shipped in LLO.

## Verification (2026-06-20, against current main)

All bead deliverables present in LLO:

- **`Parse` subcommand**: wired in `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/lib.rs:30` (variant), dispatched at `lib.rs:155-159` → `cmd_parse::cmd_parse(&source, &output, lang.as_deref())`.
- **Entry point**: `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/cmd_parse.rs:390` `pub fn cmd_parse(source: &Path, output: &Path, lang_filter: Option<&str>) -> Result<()>`.
- **`_ast` tables**: `create_ast_tables()` invoked at `cmd_parse.rs:507`; bulk INSERTs at `cmd_parse.rs:268` ("INSERT INTO _ast (node_id, source_id, node_kind, start_byte, end_byte, start_row, start_col, end_row, end_col) VALUES").
- **`_lsp*` tables**: co-emitted via `cmd_lsp.rs` (LSP refs/defs enrichment, gated by `--lsp`).
- **`ll-open` binary**: `rs/ll-open/cli/{src/main.rs, Cargo.toml}` exist; workspace registers `leyline-cli` + `leyline-cli-lib`.

## Context

This bead was filed 2026-04-03 in mache's tracker but ID-namespaced as `ley-line-open-*` (an early cross-repo seam). The work itself happened progressively in LLO across the v0.3.x → v0.4.5 line — typed payloads, capnp wire, HCL/Terraform pass, find_callees op, etc. — all merged by mid-May 2026.

LLO's bead tracker (`repo:ley-line-open`) now has zero open beads (verified 2026-06-20). The recent merge stack (#60–#67 on `agentic-research/ley-line-open`) closed out the last LLO-namespaced beads.

## Mache-side counterpart

Mache's consumer of this CLI is `mache-55b610` (LLO v0.4.5 adoption epic, P1, 6 deps, still open). That's where the remaining cross-repo integration work lives. Not blocked on `e76105`.

title: BLOCKER: tuneReadConn mutates shared/served DBs — persistent EXCLUSIVE lock + serialized reads on daemons
description: CONFIRMED (Fable). NewASTWalker unconditionally side-effects the caller's *sql.DB: SetMaxOpenConns(1), PRAGMA locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE, 256MiB cache, 2GiB mmap (internal/ingest/ast_walker.go:156-187). Correct for the one-shot build temp db (closed after ingest), but applied to SERVED dbs via pickCallExtractor(sg.DB()) at cmd/serve.go, cmd/mount.go — clobbers OpenSQLiteGraph's deliberate SetMaxOpenConns(4) (sqlite_graph.go:127) so every NFS/MCP read serializes on one conn for the daemon lifetime, AND holds a process-lifetime EXCLUSIVE file lock → external writes to the served .db fail 'database is locked (5)'. NOT a deadlock (traced: result sets fully consumed before nested queries). Fix: the perf wins are the in-memory index (algorithmic) + mmap — both connection-count-agnostic; EXCLUSIVE+single-conn are marginal after the index cut query count ~100×. Scope them to build only (flag/separate constructor) or drop them. Part of mache-4f3840; blocks v0.18.0.
acceptance_criteria: tuneReadConn's SetMaxOpenConns(1)+locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE is scoped to one-shot build only (not applied to served/mounted user DBs); a test proves a served _ast .db does NOT hold a process-lifetime EXCLUSIVE lock (external open/read succeeds) and OpenSQLiteGraph's SetMaxOpenConns(4) is not clobbered. Whole-repo `mache build` stays fast (verify index+mmap alone keep it ~10-21s, no regression).

title: error-swallow-then-cache: fileCallTokens/fileAddrRefs cache partial results on transient DB error (no signal)
description: CONFIRMED (Fable finding 8). internal/ingest/ast_walker_calls.go:130-132 (fileCallTokens) and ast_walker_extract.go:67-69 (fileAddrRefs): queryCallPattern/Query errors → `continue`, and the resulting empty/partial set is cached forever for that (sourceID,lang). In a long-lived serve, a transient DB error permanently empties a file's callees/refs with zero signal. The PR's own ExtractFileLevelRefs (ast_walker_calls.go:186-189) surfaces exactly this error class arguing 'a short set with nil error would manifest as silent false positives' — apply that reasoning here. Also ast_walker_index.go:78-81 silently drops rows on Scan error where the old finder returned it (theoretical today — leyline schema NOT NULL — but loud→silent design regression). Introduced by mache-4f3840 perf commit.
acceptance_criteria: A transient/real DB error during fileCallTokens/fileAddrRefs surfaces (returns error) rather than caching an empty/partial set forever; a test injects a query failure and asserts the error propagates and the empty result is NOT cached. loadFileIndex Scan errors return an error (parity with the old finder), not silent row-drop.

title: mount/serve frozen _ast staleness: watcher re-projects from startup-time db + immortal caches; write-back silent revert
description: CONFIRMED (Fable finding 4). cmd/serve.go:523-552 watcher onChange → ReIngestFile re-projects from the STARTUP-TIME _ast db AND the walker's immortal caches (no invalidation anywhere), yet logs 'watcher: re-indexed'; engine.ReIngestFile records the NEW mtime (engine.go:272) so the stale projection is stamped fresh and never re-checked. Pre-PR this re-parsed the current file. cmd/mount.go:505 SetRefresher on writable mounts: a successful write-back splices the file + surgically updates the node (correct), but any later external mtime change re-projects from the FROZEN pre-edit _source bytes — silently REVERTING the write-back in the projected view; on a mount there is no 'next parse'. The in-code KNOWN GAP comment covers 'stale until next parse' but not the revert. Needs: re-parse on change + per-source_id cache invalidation on the ASTWalker (the mache-4f3840 caches make this worse). v0.18.0 decision.

comments.text:
PART A DONE (commit c396a5f): ReIngestFile now calls astWalker.InvalidateSource before re-projecting, so the walker's immortal per-file caches no longer mask a re-ingest, and cache growth is bounded per-file (mache-024e9c). Mechanism is now correct.

PART B REMAINS (this bead stays open, re-scoped to a feature): a live SOURCE edit is still NOT reflected on a leyline-backed serve because the served _ast/_source are frozen at startup — reflecting edits (and preventing the write-back-revert, where a later mtime change re-projects from frozen pre-edit _source) requires re-running `leyline parse` on the changed file INTO the served db, with read/write concurrency handling (mache reads the db while leyline writes it). This is a DISCLOSED gap (cmd/serve.go logs "frozen .db — sheaf cascade NOT engaged for live edits") and a regression from removing the in-process (MACHE_NO_LEYLINE) watcher path, but it is not a silent-correctness blocker now that the mechanism is correct + disclosed. Recommend as a v0.18.x fast-follow feature (live leyline re-parse for serve/mount), not a v0.18.0 hard blocker. Suggest re-prioritizing to P2.

title: Query() inner-@scope semantic change (one-match-per-inner) rode in on the perf commit — untested, dodged baseline
description: CONFIRMED (Fable finding 9). ast_walker.go:266-295: inner-@scope selectors went from one-match-per-outer (first inner only) to one-match-per-inner — grouped `type (A; B)` now projects each member. Real behavior change, UNTESTED, landed after the baseline regen; dodged the smell gate only because mache's own source has no multi-spec grouped type blocks. Also dedupAddrTokens (ast_walker_extract.go:40) keeps r.nodeID==scopeID where old per-construct SQL strictly excluded the scope node — output unchanged only because processNode blanket-appends whole-file address refs to every construct (engine_walk.go:365-377); latent divergence with zero direct tests on either Scoped variant. LIKE→HasPrefix: old SQL treated `_` as wildcard, Go HasPrefix literal — stricter/more-correct, identical only because no realistic id collides. Add tests to lock the intended semantics. Introduced by mache-4f3840.
acceptance_criteria: A test covers the inner-@scope selector behavior: grouped Go `type ( A; B )` projects each member (one-match-per-inner), and `dedupAddrTokens` scope-self inclusion matches intended semantics. Confirm the behavior is intended (not accidental) and that mache's own source having no grouped multi-spec type blocks was the only reason it dodged the smell gate.

title: ASTWalker caches unbounded on long-lived daemons (O(repo) node rows + source bytes + 256MiB cache + 2GiB mmap/handle)
description: Fable finding 10 (LOW). The walker's four sync.Map caches hold every touched file's full node rows + source bytes for the walker lifetime (process lifetime under serve/mount), plus 256MiB page cache + 2GiB mmap per tuned handle, multiplied per mount in composites. O(repo) memory, no cap/eviction — fine for one-shot builds, unexamined for large-repo daemons. Ties to mache-010123 (tuneReadConn serve scoping) and mache-018eee (cache invalidation). Load-then-Store double-compute races are wasteful only, not incorrect. Introduced/enlarged by mache-4f3840.
acceptance_criteria: Under serve/mount, the ASTWalker's per-file caches (indexCache/sourceCache/addrRefCache/callTokenCache) are bounded or evictable (or explicitly documented as acceptable with a rationale + measured ceiling for the largest supported repo). Memory does not grow unbounded across a long daemon session; the 256MiB cache_size / 2GiB mmap are not multiplied per-mount in composites beyond a documented budget.

title: TestArenaFlusher_Coalesce — flaky timing assertion (Sequence == 2 expected, observed >2 under CI load)
description:
TestArenaFlusher_Coalesce in internal/graph/arena_writer_test.go relies on a race between time.Sleep(80ms) and a 50ms ticker. Under CI load (observed on PR #324 ubuntu integration), the ticker fires twice during the 80ms window and two coalesced flushes happen instead of one — assertion 'Sequence == 2' fails because Sequence is 3.

The test's intent is correct: prove that 10 rapid RequestFlush() calls coalesce, not produce 10 separate writes. But the assertion shape is too tight for a wall-clock test.

Fix options:
1. Replace 'assert.Equal(t, uint64(2), h.Sequence)' with 'assert.LessOrEqual(t, h.Sequence, uint64(3))' — proves coalescing without pinning the exact count.
2. Drive the flush deterministically: call FlushNow() instead of starting the ticker, then assert Sequence == 2.
3. Stop the ticker before reading the header, then poll the header until Sequence stabilizes.

Option 1 is the smallest change and preserves the original test shape. Option 2 changes what's being tested (no longer the coalescing-via-ticker path). Option 3 is most robust but most code.

comments.text:
Fix already shipped in commit 0b424eb (PR #325: "fix: TestArenaFlusher_Coalesce — tolerate CI scheduler delay"). Current file at internal/graph/arena_writer_test.go:151-154 has the bounded assertion pair:

```go
assert.GreaterOrEqual(t, h.Sequence, uint64(2),
    "at least one flush should have run after 10 RequestFlush + 80ms")
assert.LessOrEqual(t, h.Sequence, uint64(3),
    "10 rapid requests must coalesce — observed sequence %d implies they did not", h.Sequence)
```

Plus an explanatory comment that references this bead ID. Verified stability:
- `go test -run TestArenaFlusher_Coalesce -count=20 ./internal/graph/` → ok 2.072s
- `go test -race -run TestArenaFlusher_Coalesce ./internal/graph/` → ok 1.490s

Closing as already-done. Bead just hadn't been closed when PR #325 merged.

title: Adopt entireio/pgr's eval harness as the F1/F2/F3 agent loop — add a mache backend (MIT, 60 public tasks, published baseline)
description:
Read `entireio/pgr` 2026-07-27 to decide build-vs-adopt for the agent-loop half of mache-544659. **Adopt.** It is closer to what we need than anything we'd write, and it is MIT.

## What it is

A pluggable-backend agent eval. `eval/v2/tools.py` defines **four tools with identical names, schemas, and output formats across every arm** — only the backend implementation differs. That is precisely the controlled comparison F2 requires, and the design note says so outright: *"Both conditions use identical tool names, schemas, and output formats. Only the backend implementation differs."*

| pgr tool | mache equivalent |
|---|---|
| `search_code` | `search` |
| `read_code` | `read_file` — **and the exact seam `mode=signatures` (mache-qzsk) plugs into** |
| `find_files` | `list_directory` / glob |
| `list_dir` | `list_directory` |

Existing backends: `baseline.py` (raw ripgrep/cat/find), `fff_backend.py`, `pgr_backend.py`. A `mache_backend.py` is a fourth peer, not a fork.

## What we get for free

- **60 real tasks** (`design.json`) — not synthetic. Drawn from public `entireio/cli` checkpoint transcripts, curated to be answerable from the repo alone, tagged `code_understanding` / `debug_or_validation` / `implementation` / `repo_task`, each carrying source-trace search-pressure metadata.
- **Published baseline results**, one JSON per task+arm.
- Per-task records already carrying what we need:
  - **F3** — `tool_output_tokens`, plus per-call `output_tokens` on every entry in `tool_calls[]`
  - **F1** — derivable from the `tool_calls[]` sequence: a `search_code` followed by a `read_code` on the same path *is* an escalation, and turn numbers are recorded
  - **F4** — `task_type` and repo are per-task, so results break out
  - plus `total_turns`, `wall_clock_ms`, `total_cost_usd`, `input_tokens`

## The gap — F2 is NOT scored

`agent.py:171` captures `result.answer` (joined text blocks) but **nothing grades it.** No `correct`, no `score`, no judge. Their conclusions are drawn on latency and tool-call counts, with completion assumed rather than measured.

So adopting pgr gives us F1, F3, F4 and the loop; **F2 still needs a grader we add.** That is a far smaller build than the whole harness, and it is the piece that gates publishing any number.

## Their headline is a NEGATIVE result we should take seriously

`SUMMARY.md` is titled around *"faster search is not the bottleneck."* Their `fff` arm cut median `search_code` latency **14.7ms → 1.7ms (8.6×)** and end-to-end wall clock moved only **38.57s → 36.99s**, with avg tool calls **19.12 → 17.90**.

That does not falsify our thesis — theirs is a **latency** intervention, ours is an **output-size** one, and those are orthogonal. But two warnings land:

1. A large improvement in the tool layer nearly vanished at the session level. Our composition predicting ~55% assumes perfect substitution; their result is what imperfect substitution looks like.
2. **Tool-call count barely moved.** If that holds for mache too, our entire session-level win comes from bytes-per-call, not fewer calls — which is exactly F3, and exactly what `tool_output_tokens` measures.

## Free analysis available before writing any code

Their summary table reports **latency metrics only** — but the raw result records carry `tool_output_tokens` (47,366 on the sampled baseline task). **The token comparison across their published arms is computable from data they already released and did not publish.** That is a zero-cost first result and a sanity check on our 26× before we implement anything.

Prereq: mache needs to serve these four tool shapes over a repo checkout (it already does via MCP); the backend is an adapter, not new capability.

comments.text:
⚠️ **pgr's baseline arm is NOT an unrestricted `Read` equivalent. Verified 2026-07-27 — this changes how their results and ours compose.**

`eval/v2/backends/baseline.py`:

```python
def read_code(repo_root, path, start_line=1, end_line=0, max_lines=80):
```

and the tool contract advertises `"max_lines": "Max lines to return. Default 80."` So **their baseline agent already gets bounded, windowed reads** — a disciplined reader, not Claude Code's whole-file `Read`.

## What follows

1. **Their baseline ≠ our arm A.** Our 26.1× median is measured against whole-file retrieval (9,359 bytes avg incl. `cat -n` prefixes). Theirs is measured against an 80-line window. Dropping a mache backend into pgr unchanged would compare against a much stronger control, and the measured delta would be far smaller than 26× implies — not because mache is worse, but because the baseline is different.

2. **It partly explains their negative result.** "Faster search is not the bottleneck" (median `search_code` 14.7ms → 1.7ms, wall clock 38.57s → 36.99s) was measured against a baseline that had *already* removed most of the retrieval bloat via the 80-line cap. Little headroom left for search to recover.

3. **It breaks the cross-comparison to entire-graph.** entire-graph's 55% is "vs no tool at all"; pgr's numbers are "vs bounded-read ripgrep." Those baselines are not the same control, so the two published figures cannot be placed on one axis — which is worth knowing before we cite either.

## Consequence for adoption

Still adopt — the loop, the 60 real tasks, the identical-tool-contract design and the MIT license are all worth having. But add a **fourth arm**: an unbounded-read baseline matching what Claude Code actually does by default. Without it we would be reporting mache against a control no real agent session uses, and our own transcript data (avg `Read` = 11,149 chars, far past 80 lines) says the unbounded arm is the realistic one.

Three arms to run: `unbounded_read` (real-world control) → `baseline` (pgr's bounded reader) → `mache`. The gap between arms 1 and 2 is itself a publishable finding: how much of the win is just *bounding reads at all*, before any index exists.

## Second check from the same review: F2 confirmed unscored

`agent.py:171` sets `result.answer` from joined text blocks and nothing grades it. No `correct`, `score`, `grade`, or `judge` anywhere. Completion is **assumed, not verified** — exactly the softness the README's framing hides. The grader remains ours to build, and it is what makes F2 mean anything.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: `eval/v2/backends/mache_backend.py` implements all four pgr tools against a mache projection and runs the public60 suite to completion; results land in the same JSON shape as the published baseline so `tool_output_tokens` and per-call `output_tokens` are directly comparable. F1 escalation is computed from the `tool_calls[]` sequence (a `read_code` on a path previously returned by `search_code`) and reported per arm. A grader is added scoring `answer` against a per-task rubric so F2 (completion rate) is held as a control — no token number is published without it. Analysis of pgr's already-published baseline vs fff `tool_output_tokens` is recorded first, before any mache code, as the zero-cost sanity check on the 26x construct-granular ratio.

title: Double NormalizeID in SQLiteGraph delegating methods
description: SQLiteGraph.GetNode, ListChildren, and ListChildStats all call NormalizeID on the incoming id before delegating to g.ntr, which also calls NormalizeID internally. NormalizeID only strips ONE leading slash — so "//double" → "/double" after the first call, then "" after the second. This is a latent bug: any caller passing a path with two leading slashes gets the wrong node (empty string = root) instead of ErrNotFound. The SQLiteGraph callers should either stop normalizing before delegation, or NodesTableReader methods should trust that the id arriving from an internal delegation path is already clean. The fix is to remove the pre-delegation NormalizeID calls in SQLiteGraph (lines 300, 357, 391 of sqlite_graph.go) and let ntr own normalization, OR have ntr accept pre-normalized ids and not double-normalize.

comments.text: Audited 2026-04-29: not reproducible in current code. SQLiteGraph.GetNode/ListChildren/ListChildStats only call NormalizeID in the legacy path (useNodesTable=false), AFTER the early-return delegation. The ntr branch never double-normalizes. Closing as no-op.
comments.author: jamestexas

title: WritableGraph write-path (UpdateRecord + Invalidate) has zero test coverage
description: The WritableGraph GraphSuite runs the same read-only contract tests as SQLiteGraph — it exercises GetNode, ListChildren, ReadContent, etc. but never calls UpdateRecord, never verifies that a write is visible on the next ReadContent, never checks that Invalidate clears the cache, and never tests that UpdateRecord on a non-existent id returns ErrNotFound. The write path is WritableGraph's only differentiator from SQLiteGraph: if it's broken the suite won't catch it. Add a dedicated WritableGraph test that: (1) calls UpdateRecord to change a file's content, (2) verifies ReadContent returns the new content, (3) verifies GetNode reports the new size. Also test UpdateRecord("nonexistent") returns ErrNotFound.

comments.text: Tests added in PR #180: 11 focused tests covering UpdateRecord (rewrite, mtime bump, slash normalization, missing-target ErrNotFound, two-step shrink, cache invalidation, concurrent serialization), Flush no-flusher path, Invalidate cache clearing, DBPath round-trip, and OpenWritableGraph's nodes-table guard.
comments.author: jamestexas

title: find_smells dead_code: false positives for cobra RunE / init-registered factories
description:
Dogfooding mache against mache.db (with --schema examples/go-schema.json) shows dead_code flagging functions that are NOT actually dead but invoked through Go patterns the static-refs walker can't see:

1. Cobra RunE callbacks: runServe, runInit, runAgentMode — referenced by name in &cobra.Command{ RunE: runServe } construction. The reference is via field-value identifier, not a call expression, so tree-sitter's call walker misses it.

2. init() registry registrations: hotSwapFactory, sqliteGraphFactory, writableGraphFactory, stubRender, stubRenderer — these are factory functions stuffed into a global registry map by init(). Same pattern: identifier reference, not a call.

3. main(): mache's binary entrypoint. Already on the dead_code skip list as 'main' (token), but shows up here as 'Main' — possibly a schema/case quirk.

4. Function values passed as args: enrichHCLNode, registerFormat, PrintMemUsage — passed by name to higher-order functions or held in struct fields.

These are not really dead. Real fix needs the refs walker to also capture identifier references in non-call contexts: function values, struct field values, map values. Tree-sitter query needs an additional pattern beyond (call_expression).

Until then, dead_code on mache itself produces ~127 functions/-only findings, of which a substantial fraction are these false positives. Filing as a quality observation, not blocking the rule's usefulness for finding real dead code.

Related: mache-5d1o (methods missed by ingest).

title: NodesTableReader has fully exported fields — should be unexported
description: NodesTableReader exposes DB, TableName, Render, Levels, FileMode, DirMode, SizeCache, and Cache as exported fields. The only external callers are WritableGraph (accesses g.ntr.DB in UpdateRecord) and SQLiteGraph (nowhere — it calls methods). Exported fields on an internal package type is AI-generated defensiveness: it anticipates future callers that don't exist, makes the type harder to reason about (anyone can mutate DB or Cache from outside the package boundary), and reads like documentation rather than code. The fix: unexport all fields and add a targeted accessor (e.g. DB() or ExecDB()) for WritableGraph's UpdateRecord use case.

comments.text: Audited: NodesTableReader fields are already unexported in current code (db, tableName, render, levels, fileMode, dirMode, sizeCache, cache). DB() accessor exists for WritableGraph. Closing as no-op.

title: SQLiteGraph.Invalidate clears both g.sizeCache and g.ntr.SizeCache — split ownership leaks on the nodes-table path
description: After the refactor, Invalidate does: g.ntr.Invalidate(id) (clears ntr.SizeCache + ntr.Cache), then also g.sizeCache.Delete(id) and g.cache.Delete(id) (guarded by nil check). For the nodes-table path: g.cache is nil (not initialized in OpenSQLiteGraph nodes-table branch), g.sizeCache is present but never written to by any nodes-table code path — all size writes go to ntr.SizeCache instead. So the g.sizeCache.Delete call on the nodes-table path is a no-op vacuously. This is not a correctness bug today, but it is confusing: the two sizeCache/cache fields exist on SQLiteGraph but are unused on the fast path. They should either be removed from the struct when useNodesTable=true, or the comment should be updated to make it explicit that sizeCache is legacy-only and Invalidate's double-delete is intentional dead code on the fast path.

title: Suite test GetNode/root_empty_string permits ErrNotFound — hides WritableGraph root contract
description: The GraphSuite test for GetNode("") has a permissive contract: it accepts either a dir node or ErrNotFound. The comment says "Both behaviors are valid." WritableGraph delegates directly to ntr.GetNode("") which returns a synthetic root dir node — but the test never asserts this. If ntr.GetNode changed to return ErrNotFound on empty string, WritableGraph would break in production (FUSE/NFS root lookups) but the test would still pass. The suite should assert that SQLiteGraph and WritableGraph specifically return a dir node for "" (using a per-factory override or a second tighter assertion), rather than accepting both behaviors as a blanket rule.

comments.text: Fixed in PR #187 (commit e2d2780): SuiteOpts{RootEmptyReturnsDir bool} introduced. SQLiteGraph and WritableGraph now strict-assert the synthetic root node; HotSwap stays permissive (its fixture wraps MemoryStore which legitimately returns ErrNotFound).

title: Fix server.json OCI identifier (embed :vTAG, drop version) + add MCP-schema-validation linter
description:
Surfaced from cloister (2026-07-08): mache's published server.json declares an OCI package that a resolver can't pull.

## The bug
Per mache's pinned MCP registry schema (https://static.modelcontextprotocol.io/schemas/2025-12-11/server.schema.json), OCI packages carry the tag IN the identifier (`registry/namespace/repository:tag`) and the `version` field is npm/pypi/nuget-only. mache's tools/server-json-gen emits:
  { registryType: "oci", identifier: "ghcr.io/agentic-research/mache", version: "0.16.0" }
But release.yml publishes the image as `ghcr.io/agentic-research/mache:${TAG}` = `:v0.16.0` (v-prefixed) + `:latest`. So (1) the identifier has NO tag, and (2) `version: "0.16.0"` (no v) mismatches the real `v0.16.0` tag. A consumer resolving identifier:version pulls `:0.16.0` — which does NOT exist. Interop-broken for cloister's resolver.

## Fix
1. tools/server-json-gen/main.go: emit `identifier = ociImageIdentifier + ":v" + serverVersion` → `ghcr.io/agentic-research/mache:v0.16.0` (matches the actual published tag). DROP the separate `version` field for the OCI package (redundant + npm/pypi/nuget-only per the pinned schema). Update TestBuildDoc_EmitsOCIPackage (assert identifier ends with `:v<version>`, no separate version).
2. Add `task server-json:lint` — validate server.json against the published MCP schema (2025-12-11). Wire into check/ci beside gen:server-json:check so this drift class fails CI. Prefer a dep-light validator (fetch/vendor the schema JSON; validate with an existing JSON-Schema lib already in the tree if any, else a small vendored one — respect the operator's reduce-deps stance). Compose with cloister's schema extension (the _meta cluster-def groups, cloister-2d987e) where applicable.

This is a schema-validation GATE, not a mache smell rule (server.json is config, not projected code).

Links: cloister-2d987e (stale image tag / resolver-migrate — the consumer side), the OCI distribution work (v0.14.0-v0.16.0 image). Needs a v0.16.x patch release once fixed (server.json is published).

comments.text:

Test asserts the :v<version> tag + no version. Verified green through CI + release.

REMAINING (keep this bead OPEN): Part 2 — the `server-json:lint` schema-validation gate (validate server.json against the pinned MCP schema, wired into check/ci) so this drift class can't recur. Dep-light per operator's reduce-deps stance.

This may DIVERGE from a strict reading of the upstream MCP registry schema (which around 2025-12-11 was read as: OCI identifier = registry/repo:tag, `version` omitted for OCI). So the server-json:lint gate must validate against ADR-0041's canonical form (the ecosystem contract cloister consumes), NOT blindly against the upstream MCP schema — otherwise it would flag the CORRECT ADR-0041 shape as invalid and re-introduce the divergence. title: ListChildren returns nil (not empty slice) on empty dir — suite only checks Empty
description: NodesTableReader.ListChildren returns nil when the SQL query returns zero rows (children slice is never initialized). The suite test for ListChildren/empty_dir uses assert.Empty which passes for nil. But callers that do len(children) == 0 will work fine with nil, while callers that range over the result and expect a non-nil slice (or callers that JSON-serialize) may behave differently. More concretely: GetCallees reads source child content via ListChildren — if it gets nil and treats it as no children, that is correct. But the contract is implicit. The suite should assert Empty (which it does) but also document via a comment why nil is acceptable, and the ListChildStats equivalent should confirm the same. Low priority but worth locking down the nil-vs-empty semantics explicitly.

comments.text: Fixed in PR #187 (commit e2d2780): NodesTableReader.ListChildren doc comment spells out the nil-vs-empty contract; suite empty-dir test asserts len==0 explicitly with a comment pointing to the bead.

title: find_smells cross-lang: generalize Go-gated metric rules + adopt current leyline (Rust parses to _ast; defs are the LLO gap)
description:
The "standardize smells across repos" goal has an unmet prerequisite: the non-Go repos can't be parsed into a defs/refs graph, so find_smells has nothing to run on.

VERIFIED 2026-06-24 (installed leyline 0.4.5 'open', mache dac8ac5):
- `mache build` (leyline backend) on rosary/crates/crypto/src (7 .rs files): 0 .rs parsed — leyline ingested only markdown (README/ADRs) across the Rust repos. leyline 0.4.5 does not parse Rust source.
- `mache build --backend tree-sitter` (mache's 28-lang registry, Rust grammar present) on the same: ingests 6 file-nodes but node_defs=0 — no symbol extraction. Default build uses FCA inference; without a Rust schema (tree-sitter def/ref queries like examples/go-schema.json) no defs/refs are produced, so god_file/dead_code/duplicate_definitions/fan_out_skew/untested_function all return nothing.

IMPACT: cross-repo standardization (baseline+ratchet) is Go-only today. rosary (9 crates), ley-line-open (105 crates), cloister (4 crates + TS) are invisible to the smell engine.

PATHS (pick): (a) leyline gains Rust (+JS/TS) parsing → emits _ast/node_defs like it does for Go (preferred — unifies on the LLO substrate); (b) author tree-sitter def/ref schemas per language (examples/rust-schema.json, ts-schema.json) so the tree-sitter backend extracts defs without leyline; (c) both — schema as the standalone floor, leyline as the enriched tier (mirrors the fidelity-ladder pattern).

Blocks the baseline artifact in docs/ (Go portion shipped separately). Relates to ADR-0012 (standalone vs _ast split), the smell-enforcement arc.

comments.text:
CORRECTION (2026-06-24): the title/original framing is WRONG. leyline DOES parse Rust.

Tested against current LLO source (HEAD 3d80a55), not the stale installed binary: a current leyline parses a 7-file Rust crate into a full _ast (rust cargo feature added 2026-06-22, pulled transitively by the default `hdc` feature). The earlier "0 .rs parsed" was the stale ~/.local/bin/leyline (May-23 build, pre-rust-feature) — an install-currency problem, NOT a capability gap.

The REAL gap splits in two:
1. LLO substrate: def/ref extraction is Go-only (ts/src/refs.rs match has only `TsLanguage::Go => extract_go`). Rust → node_defs=0. Filed as a ley-line-open bead (extract_rust). This is the load-bearing unblock.
2. mache (THIS bead, re-scoped): cyclomatic_complexity / long_function / magic_int_in_comparison are languages:[go]-gated, so they won't fire on Rust even once node_defs exist and the _ast is present. Generalize these cross-lang (the Rust/JS AST nodes — function_item, if_expression — exist). Also: adopt current leyline (the stale binary issue is ops).

What already works on Rust today (current leyline): cross-lang _ast rules — long_file lists round_trip.rs/projection.rs correctly.

So this bead is NOT a P1 "blocker" — re-scope to: (a) cross-lang generalize the Go-gated metric rules; (b) ensure mache build uses a current leyline. The substrate unblock is the LLO extract_rust bead.

comments.text:
**This bead's core premise is STALE. Verified against LLO source 2026-07-27.**

The bead states: *"the non-Go repos can't be parsed into a defs/refs graph, so find_smells has nothing to run on… Rust parses to _ast; **defs are the LLO gap**."* That was true when filed (verified 2026-06-24 against leyline 0.4.5).

It is no longer true. `ley-line-open-337a10` — *"extract_rust: Rust def/ref extraction in refs.rs — KEYSTONE for cross-repo structural rules"* — closed **2026-07-02**.

Checked directly in `~/remotes/art/ley-line-open` (at `v0.10.4-11-g1470030`):

- `rs/ll-open/ts/src/refs.rs:342` — `pub fn extract_rust(`
- language arms present: **Bash, C, Cpp, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python, Rust, Sql, TypeScript** — not the single `TsLanguage::Go =>` arm this bead and `ley-line-open-337a10` both describe
- `rs/ll-open/ts/queries/` ships `.scm` files for all ten

So the prerequisite this bead calls unmet has been met for roughly three weeks, and mache has since moved from a v0.4.5-era pin to v0.10.3.

## Why this matters beyond tidiness

I cited this gap repeatedly across a full session of token-cost analysis as the reason mache's measured win could not be validated on Rust — the language where the largest real-world `Read` dumps live (`ll-open/ts/src/refs.rs` at 70KB, `cmd_daemon.rs` at 61KB, per the transcript decomposition). On that basis I gated:

- **F4 (per-language generality)** in mache-544659 — recorded as "Go-only until Rust extraction lands"
- the polyglot run of `tools/token-bench`
- the "measure Go first" caveat on mache-qzsk

**None of those are actually blocked.** `token-bench` emits a per-extension breakout already; pointing it at a Rust corpus is a `mache build` away, and the answer to "does the 26× ratio generalise?" is obtainable now rather than after an upstream dependency.

## What remains genuinely open here

The bead's other half — *"generalize Go-gated metric rules"* — was never about LLO. Several `find_smells` rules hardcode Go node kinds (`duplicate_code`'s candidate roots are `function_declaration`/`method_declaration`; `long_function` the same). Those need the other languages' function kinds added to their `WHERE` clauses. That is mache-side work, unblocked, and is the real content of this bead now.

Recommend re-scoping to that and dropping the LLO-gap framing, so nobody else inherits a blocker that cleared three weeks ago.

comments.text:
## Path (a) has landed. The verified evidence here predates it.

This bead's VERIFIED block is dated 2026-06-24 and says leyline 0.4.5 "does not parse Rust source" and that a tree-sitter build gives `node_defs=0`. It then offers "PATHS (pick): (a) leyline gains Rust (+JS/TS) parsing → emits _ast/node_defs".

**(a) shipped.** `ley-line-open/rs/ll-open/ts/src/refs.rs` today exports ten extractors:

```
bash  c  cpp  go  java  javascript  python  rust  sql  typescript
```

`extract_rust` is 50 lines and landed in `77ad21a` — *"[ley-line-open-117693] feat(ts): extract_rust — defs/refs/imports for Rust source (#93)"*. `extract_typescript` and `extract_python` are there too.

## Measured today, 2026-07-29, on a TypeScript repo

`mache build` against `0day` (an Astro/TS repo, no schema flag — the default ley-line `_ast` projection):

```
37 parsed, 0 unchanged, 0 deleted, 0 errors   wall=667ms

_ast        83,328
nodes       83,344
node_refs    2,165
node_defs      102
```

`find_smells --rule '*'` runs clean and produces real findings on that repo's own TypeScript with correct file:line — `fan_out_skew` on several files, `long_function` on two. So the "non-Go repos can't be parsed into a defs/refs graph, so find_smells has nothing to run on" premise is no longer true for TS, and by the same commit no longer true for Rust.

Worth noting for whoever picks this up: **no topology schema was needed.** `mache build --schema` defaults to the ley-line-parsed `_ast` projection, and mache registers ~30 grammars built in. The absence of a `typescript-schema.json` under `examples/` is not a blocker — I initially read it as one and running the build disproved it.

## The question that IS still open, and it is narrower

`node_defs=102` against `node_refs=2,165` is a 21:1 ratio. Go-heavy repos do not look like that. Two readings and I am not picking one:

- **Legitimate** — most refs point at external modules, so there is genuinely little to define locally.
- **Shallow** — TS def extraction is thinner than Go's, in the same way `mache-9108a1` describes the standalone tier being "Go-tuned".

`mache-9108a1`'s framing suggests the second is at least plausible, since it identifies the same Go-tuning in the tree-sitter tier for Rust caller/callee edges.

**Establishing which matters before anything relies on it.** The failure mode is a language contributing plausible-looking but incomplete defs — worse than contributing none, because partial coverage that reads as total is indistinguishable from complete coverage until someone checks. A def/ref ratio comparison between a TS repo and a Go repo of similar size would settle it cheaply.

## Related, and a second stale document

`docs/design/specs/2026-07-02-analysis-substrate-consolidation-design.md` §5 still says *"LLO's `rs/ll-open/ts/src/refs.rs` has only `extract_go` … Structural consolidation across the ecosystem is **blocked on this one LLO gap**."* Same staleness, and load-bearing: it names a blocker that has been cleared, so work deferred behind it may still be sitting deferred. A good candidate for the `drift_doc_*` rules ADR-0018 defines.

Filed from 0day, where the question was whether symbol-level cross-repo edges could rest on this substrate. That side is tracked as `0day-419cff` and `0day-c904b5`; the def/ref ratio is the one open input it needs from here.

title: Smell rules are duplicated across repos with no shared source
description:
Found 2026-07-28 while surveying whether 0day should centralize smell rules. Filed in mache because mache owns the rule FORMAT and executes them (SQL over the built .db), so any shared source has to be mache-shaped.

## The duplication, exactly

  mache/examples/smell-rules      3 rules + README   Go       (starter kit)
  ley-line-open/smell-rules       4 rules            Rust
  ley-line/smell-rules            2 rules            Rust
  cloister/done-rules             5 rules            NOT smell rules

`unsafe_without_safety.json` and `unwrap_without_expect.json` appear in BOTH ley-line-open and ley-line. Those two are the concrete duplication; everything else is distinct.

cloister/done-rules is a different mechanism entirely — done-criteria (00-lint-passes, 10-branch-on-feature, 20-bead-pinned, 40-no-uncommitted-noise, 70-recipes), not structural smells. It should not be folded in, and naming them alike is itself a small trap.

## Why 0day is the WRONG home, despite being the obvious candidate

The question that prompted this was whether 0day could centralize them. Two reasons it should not:

1. Rules are LANGUAGE-SPECIFIC. mache's are Go-shaped (fatal_call_in_library, long_test_function, long_unexported_function); LLO's are Rust-shaped (unwrap_without_expect, cfg_feature_in_tests). A single pile is not meaningful — the sharing that exists is Rust-to-Rust.

2. 0day publishes derived facts and schemas about RELATIONSHIPS. It executes nothing. A rule registry in 0day would be a set of declarations nothing there can validate or run — the exact "declaration nobody verifies" failure this ecosystem keeps paying for. It would be a rule catalog that cannot tell you whether a rule still parses.

## The split worth considering instead

- DEFINITIONS in mache, organized by language. mache already ships examples/smell-rules as a starter kit and owns the format; a shared Rust set is a small addition to something that exists.
- CATALOG in 0day — which rules exist, which repos adopt which. That is a relationship fact, which IS 0day's job, and it can be DERIVED by scanning the repos rather than authored, per 0day's "judgments authored, facts derived".

That split keeps each layer doing what it can actually verify.

## Scope check, deliberately

The measured duplication is TWO FILES. That does not justify building a distribution mechanism. The cheapest honest fix is to make ley-line consume LLO's two Rust rules rather than carry copies, or to accept the duplication and record why.

Worth weighing against a fact from the same survey: ley-line is a private moat repo whose CI has not run since 2026-03-24, so its copies are not being exercised anyway. Consolidating rules into a repo that does not run them buys nothing.

## To decide

1. Is a shared Rust rule set worth extracting for two files, or is the honest answer to leave it and record the duplication?
2. If extracted, does it live beside mache's Go starter kit (one directory, subdivided by language) or as a separate distributable?
3. Does 0day derive and publish an adoption catalog? That is independent of 1 and 2 and is the part with lasting value — it answers "which repos gate on which rules" without anyone maintaining a list.
4. Rename cloister/done-rules, or document the distinction, so the two mechanisms stop looking like one.</description>
<parameter name="acceptance_criteria">A decision is recorded on whether the two duplicated Rust rules are consolidated or the duplication is accepted with a stated reason; if consolidated, one repo is the source and the other consumes it; and the question of a 0day-derived adoption catalog is answered yes or no.

comments.text:
REFRAMED 2026-07-28. Both options in the description are wrong, and mache already carries the right answer. Read this instead of the "to decide" list above.

## The mechanism already has two tiers

cmd/smell_rules.go:114-125 states it directly:

  "The built-ins are shipped as embedded JSON (cmd/rules/*.json, one SmellRule per
   file) and loaded at package init via mustLoadEmbeddedRules. They use the SAME
   JSON DSL and the SAME parse+validate path as external rules (see
   LoadExternalSmellRules) — the only difference is PROVENANCE."

  embedded   cmd/rules/*.json          14 rules, ship with the binary
  external   resolved smell-rules dir  merged per find_smells request, live-reloadable

External rules are "merged with a copy of this slice per find_smells request in activeSmellRules — never appended to this global". So composition exists, one tier is versioned with mache, and both go through the same validate path.

## So the question is not WHERE, it is WHICH TIER

  embedded  universal — true of any repo in that language, or language-agnostic
  external  project policy — this repo's opinion about its own code

The embedded 14 are already language-agnostic structural patterns rather than Go patterns: god_file, dead_code, duplicate_code, long_file, long_function, untested_function, magic_int_in_comparison, cyclomatic_complexity, fan_out_skew, duplicate_definitions, sleep_in_test, plus three drift_doc_* rules. That is the existing precedent for what "universal" means here.

## What that makes the duplication

`unwrap_without_expect` and `unsafe_without_safety` are not a dedup problem to be solved by extraction. They are CANDIDATES FOR PROMOTION into cmd/rules/. Promote them and every Rust repo gets them from the binary it already pins, and both copies delete themselves. No new repo, no distribution mechanism, no third tier.

Note sleep_in_test is ALREADY embedded while ley-line-open carries sleep_in_tests externally — so a promotion of this exact kind has already happened once, or the two have diverged. Worth checking which before promoting anything else; if they diverged, that is a small finding of its own.

## Why an aggregating monorepo is the wrong shape

The original question was whether to build a language-specific monorepo that aggregates rules. It would be a THIRD tier, and mache reads exactly ONE external dir — so it needs new code (multiple dirs, or a fetch step), its own versioning, its own distribution, and its own consumers. That solves less than the two existing tiers already do, because embedded rules travel with a binary consumers already pin exactly (internal/leyline/binary_pin.go pins mache-adjacent artifacts by version AND digest elsewhere in this ecosystem; the same discipline applies).

It also encourages the error worth avoiding: `unwrap_without_expect` is plausibly universal Rust hygiene, while `cfg_feature_in_tests` may well be ley-line-open POLICY. Aggregating by language alone conflates the two, and promoting a policy rule into everyone's binary is worse than duplicating a universal one.

## The shape this is an instance of

A rule promotes from project-local to shared when it is proven universal — the same test as leyline-sign promoting cloister -> LLO under cloister ADR-0035, and the same test vigil-6150dc calls the promotion boundary. Does it have a second consumer. Here the second consumer is literal and already exists: two repos carry byte-identical copies.

## Revised work

1. Diff ley-line-open/smell-rules/sleep_in_tests.json against mache's embedded sleep_in_test.json. If they have diverged, that is the first thing to reconcile.
2. Decide per rule, not per language, whether it is universal or policy. Only the universal ones promote.
3. Promote the universal ones into cmd/rules/, then delete the copies from ley-line-open and ley-line.
4. Leave genuinely project-specific rules external where they are.
5. The 0day adoption catalog remains a separate and independent idea — which repos gate on which rules is a relationship fact 0day could DERIVE, and it stays worthwhile whether or not any rule is promoted.

Still P3. The measured duplication is two files, and ley-line's CI has not run since 2026-03-24 so its copies are not being exercised anyway. This is worth doing correctly when touched, not worth scheduling.

title: Enforce smell rules in CI: provision LLO-backed .db (run all 9 rules) + baseline/ratchet gate
description: find-smells.yml today is ADVISORY ONLY ("Never fails the build") and exercises only the 5 standalone (no-LLO) rules — dead_code, untested_function, duplicate_definitions, fan_out_skew, god_file — because CI builds a standalone mache .db with NO _ast. parsing 756 files (skipped 0 unchanged)
```
smell ratchet: 2 NEW finding(s) above baseline:
  [duplicate_code] cmd/cache.go:838
  [long_function] internal/leyline/sheaf_subscriber.go:457
```

Both of those are `_ast`-dependent rules — precisely the class this bead says can't run in CI. They ran, they fired, and they blocked a merge until the underlying defects were fixed rather than baselined.

title: Add advisory smell for production APIs referenced only by tests
description: CDC audit found a shipped Rust feature whose schema initializer and storage entrypoint had exclusively test callers: tests proved the mechanism, but no production path could activate it. Existing dead_code treats any test reference as alive and untested_function asks the inverse question, so neither detects this gap. Add an advisory cross-language SQL rule over v_defs/v_refs that reports callable defs with one or more test callers and zero non-test callers, with source/kind filters and documented external-API false positives. Seed the falsifier with leyline-fs create_chunked_content_schema/store_content_chunked shape. Keep it advisory/baselineable until precision is measured.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture containing one test-only production-shaped function, one test helper, one externally-consumed API marker/allowlist case, and one genuinely production-called function yields only the intended advisory finding; query works on leyline and mache projections without OR-join scan regression; rule documentation quantifies expected external-API false positives; mache test and smell gates pass.

title: FUSE readdir: pre-compute stats in Opendir, eliminate redundant GetNode calls
description:
## What
Eliminate N per-child GetNode calls during FUSE readdir and NFS ReadDir by returning `[]NodeStat` value types from a single-RLock snapshot.

## Why (from theoretical analysis)
- `GetNode` returns `*Node` — a pointer to the live map entry. After RLock releases, concurrent writers can mutate fields. This is a data race under the Go memory model.
- NFS READDIRPLUS expects point-in-time consistent attributes. N separate GetNode calls violate this.
- `NodeStat` is a value type with zero aliasing. Copying under RLock gives true snapshot semantics.

## NodeStat type (already added to graph.go)
```go
type NodeStat struct {
    ID          string
    IsDir       bool
    ContentSize int64
    ModTime     time.Time
    HasOrigin   bool
}
```

## What's already done (in working tree, not committed)
- `NodeStat` type defined in `internal/graph/graph.go`
- `MemoryStore.ListChildStats(id) ([]NodeStat, error)` implemented
- 8 falsifiable tests in `internal/graph/batch_test.go`:
  - `TestListChildStats_ValueSemantics_NoAliasing` — proves values don't alias store
  - `TestListChildStats_SnapshotConsistency` — proves all entries from same point in time
  - `TestListChildStats_RaceDetectorClean` — passes with `go test -race`
  - Plus 5 basic contract tests
- All tests pass including `-race`
- Old `ListChildNodes` (dead code) removed

## What remains for the agent

### Step 1: Add `ListChildStats` to Graph interface (graph.go:110-124)
Add `ListChildStats(id string) ([]NodeStat, error)` to the `Graph` interface.

### Step 2: Implement on SQLiteGraph (sqlite_graph.go)
CRITICAL: Do NOT resolve content or render templates. For file size:
- Use `sizeCache` (sync.Map) if populated
- Use `_nodes` table if `useNodesTable` is true
- Return 0 for unknown sizes (FUSE/NFS handle this gracefully)
- Mode: check schema levels — dirs are non-leaf levels, files are leaf levels
- ModTime: use mount time or scan time (SQLiteGraph doesn't track per-record modtime)

### Step 3: Implement on all other Graph implementors
- `CompositeGraph` (composite.go) — delegate to the matching sub-graph
- `WritableGraph` (writable_graph.go) — delegate to inner graph
- `HotSwapGraph` (hotswap.go) — delegate to current graph
- `lazyGraph` (cmd/serve_registry.go) — delegate after ensuring graph loaded
- `GraphCache` (graph/cache.go) — delegate (cache is for content, not stats)
- Test mocks: `mockGraph` (sheaf_invalidate_test.go), `minimalStore` (diagram_test.go)

### Step 4: FUSE path — use in Opendir (root.go)
Change `dirHandle` to store `[]NodeStat` instead of `[]string`:
```go
type dirHandle struct {
    path    string
    stats   []NodeStat  // pre-computed from ListChildStats
    virtuals []vfs.DirExtra // virtual entries from DirExtras
}
```
In `Opendir`: call `ListChildStats` once, store results.
In `readdirStat`: use pre-computed stats instead of calling GetNode.

### Step 5: NFS path — use in ReadDir (graphfs.go)
Replace the loop at lines 305-311 that calls GetNode per child with a single ListChildStats call. Convert each NodeStat to os.FileInfo.

## Files
- `internal/graph/graph.go` — Graph interface change (already has NodeStat + MemoryStore impl)
- `internal/graph/sqlite_graph.go` — SQLiteGraph impl
- `internal/graph/composite.go` — CompositeGraph impl
- `internal/graph/writable_graph.go` — WritableGraph impl
- `internal/graph/hotswap.go` — HotSwapGraph impl
- `internal/graph/cache.go` — GraphCache impl
- `internal/fs/root.go` — FUSE Opendir/Readdir rewrite
- `internal/nfsmount/graphfs.go` — NFS ReadDir rewrite
- `cmd/serve_registry.go` — lazyGraph impl
- Test mocks that implement Graph

## Constraints
- SQLiteGraph MUST NOT render content in ListChildStats
- Virtual entries (callers/, callees/, _diagnostics/) come from VHandler.DirExtras — don't break that
- All existing tests must pass
- New tests in batch_test.go must pass with `-race`
- `task build` and `task test` must succeed

comments.text: All 6 steps complete. ListChildStats wired through Graph interface, all 7 implementors (MemoryStore, SQLiteGraph, WritableGraph, CompositeGraph, HotSwapGraph, lazyGraph, SQLiteWriter), FUSE readdir, and NFS ReadDir. Full test suite passes with race detector. Build succeeds.

title: Deploy mache as a cloister cluster-in-a-pod bundle (consume cloister-be0607)
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-09 from the cloister substrate landing arc. Once `cloister-be0607` ("compute primitive — workerd as v8-proc-iso cluster in a pod") lands, mache should ship as a deployable bundle inside that cluster — same `apko build` artifact, same workerd v8 isolate boundary, no Cloudflare-account dependency.

## Context

mache today serves MCP over HTTP (`mache serve --http :7532`) and is reached by cloister via a `MACHE_MCP_URL` env var (per ADR-0006 dynamic tools). That works for local dev but doesn't compose with the cluster-in-a-pod story: the user wants ONE container image that brings up the whole stack — gateway + bundles + DOs + identity authority + code-intelligence.

Per cloister ADR-0011 (hypervisor/bundle boundary) + ADR-0010 (vault + bundles), each cluster-resident service is a "bundle" — a v8 isolate with a bounded resource budget that talks to siblings via service bindings, not over HTTP. mache's MCP server is a natural bundle: it has its own state (the FUSE-mounted projection + sqlite), exposes a stable RPC surface (the `mache_*` MCP tools), and benefits from process isolation.

## What "deploy mache via cloister" looks like

1. **mache exports a bundle definition** — a `bundle.capnp` (or whatever cloister's bundle manifest schema is, depending on how be0607 lands) that declares:
   - The bundle's name (e.g. `mache-mcp`)
   - Its tool surface (the existing `mache_*` MCP tools)
   - Its storage requirements (how much SQLite the projection needs)
   - Any vault slices it requires (per ADR-0010 — likely none for read-only code intel)

2. **mache's HTTP MCP layer becomes a bundle entry point** — currently the daemon serves over HTTP; in the cluster-in-a-pod world the same handlers respond to service-binding calls from cloister's gateway bundle. The handler logic doesn't change; only the transport.

3. **apko/melange recipes** for mache that produce a bundle artifact compatible with cloister's `apko build`. Likely: a melange.yaml that emits a self-contained mache binary + an apko.yaml fragment that cloister's cluster image can include.

4. **A cluster manifest fragment** — added to cloister's `cluster.capnp` (per be0607 design) that declares mache as a member bundle.

## Acceptance

- `task cluster:run` (in cloister) brings up a container that includes mache as a bundle
- cloister's `mache_*` tools resolve through the in-process service binding, not HTTP
- mache's projection state persists across container restarts (volume-mounted)
- Per-bundle resource limits prevent mache from starving cloister's other bundles
- Standalone mode (`mache serve --http :7532`) continues to work for local dev

## Depends on

- cloister-be0607 (cluster-in-a-pod compute primitive) — defines the bundle manifest schema mache targets
- mache stays substrate-agnostic at the storage layer (already true)

## Files (best guess; depends on be0607 schema)

- `bundle.capnp` (NEW) — mache's bundle declaration
- `melange.yaml` / `apko.yaml` — package recipes
- `bin/mache-bundle-entry.go` (NEW) — service-binding entry point that wraps the existing MCP handlers
- README.md — document the cluster-in-a-pod deployment path

## Refs

- cloister ADR-0009 — compute substrate portability
- cloister ADR-0010 — vault + bundle clusters
- cloister ADR-0011 — hypervisor/bundle boundary
- cloister-be0607 — the implementation bead this consumes

title: `mache --out <db> <src>` treats the source positional as a MOUNTPOINT (arg confusion)
description: Found while trying to parse an external Rust repo (lectio) into a smell-scannable db (lectio bead lectio-a38e94). Invoking `mache --out /tmp/x.db crates/memory-core/src` did NOT write a db from the source dir — it logged "Mounting mache at crates/memory-core/src (NFS on localhost:...)", i.e. it interpreted the positional `crates/memory-core/src` as the MOUNT POINT, not the source to ingest, while --out was set. Expected: with --out present, the positional should be the SOURCE to parse and the command should write the db without mounting (or the source/out semantics should be documented + validated). `mache serve <src>` is clear; the db-producing path is not. Repro on darwin, mache from ~/.local/bin. Impact: blocks producing a portable parsed db for find_smells over an arbitrary repo. Suggest: explicit `mache parse <src> --out <db>` (or `mache index`) subcommand, or reject the ambiguous combo with a usage error.

title: Auto-started leyline daemon races: "socket default.sock did not appear within 5s"
description: Found while trying to get find_smells to ingest an external Rust repo (lectio bead lectio-a38e94). When mache auto-starts a leyline daemon (logged: `auto-starting leyline daemon: .../leyline daemon --arena ~/.mache/default.arena --arena-size-mib 64 --control ~/.mache/default.ctrl --mount ~/.mache/mount`), it then fails with `embed trigger: ley-line not available: leyline daemon started but socket ~/.mache/default.sock did not appear within 5s`. So LSP/embed enrichment (and therefore find_smells over freshly-ingested Rust) is unavailable. Likely causes to investigate: (1) 5s socket-appear timeout is too short for a cold leyline daemon start; (2) arena/control/socket CONTENTION when other `mache serve` instances already hold ~/.mache/default.{arena,ctrl,sock} — a second auto-start on the same default paths can't bind, so the socket never appears; the auto-starter should REUSE a running daemon's socket or use a per-invocation arena/sock. Repro: with ≥1 `mache serve` already running (5 were live), run a fresh mache that triggers embed. Impact: find_smells returns total:0 for node_defs/_ast-based rules because nothing gets parsed/enriched. Suggest: longer/configurable timeout + reuse-existing-daemon (or isolated arena per invocation) + a clearer error distinguishing "start failed" vs "socket contended".

comments.text:
PR opened (session 2026-07-01). Addressed the two tractable root causes: (1) the hardcoded 5s socket-appear wait is now configurable via MACHE_LEYLINE_START_TIMEOUT (Go duration or bare seconds), default raised 5s→15s; (2) a daemon that crashes on startup is now detected via cmd.Wait and reported as "exited during startup: <status>" immediately, instead of waiting the full timeout for a socket that can't appear. The timeout error now names the contended arena + points at the knob (internal/leyline/socket.go DiscoverOrStart poll loop).

Tests: leylineStartTimeout env-parsing table + default guard; existing timeout test reworked to a sleeper fake + 1s override (fast, still covers timeout path); new crash-path test asserts fast exit-detection.

STILL OPEN: the cross-process arena-contention half — two separate `mache serve` processes racing on the same ~/.mache/default.{arena,ctrl,sock} (line ~318 removes the socket inode a concurrent daemon may be binding). That's a riskier redesign (isolated arena per invocation, or a cross-process lock) and overlaps the mache-823d91 reliability half. Leaving this bead open for that follow-up.

title: Drop the leyline auto-download fallback (~/.mache/bin) — require leyline on PATH, fail loud; it rots into version skew
description:
## Why

`DiscoverOrStart` resolves the leyline binary in three tiers (socket.go:224-249): PATH → `~/.mache/bin/leyline` → **auto-download from GitHub releases** (`downloadLeyline`). The fallback exists to bridge the LLO-vs-`ll` binary-naming/availability gap for users without leyline on PATH.

Real harm observed (2026-06-25): the auto-downloaded copy is fetched ONCE and never updated, so it rots. Found `~/.mache/bin/leyline` = **0.4.1** (May) while the PATH leyline was **0.5.1** (current) — a full minor version behind. Any code path that hits the fallback silently runs the stale leyline → version skew that's invisible and maddening to debug. It also (a) defeats attempts to force the in-process tree-sitter tier (it's found even with `~/.local/bin` off PATH — blocked the mache-9108a1 benchmark), and (b) does a surprise runtime network fetch that can 404 against unpublished releases (already papered over with MACHE_NO_LEYLINE).

A runtime auto-download that becomes a stale second source of truth is a bug factory. Three "which leyline is mache using?" answers is two too many.

## What

Collapse binary resolution to **PATH-only, fail loud**:
- Look up `leyline` on PATH. If absent, return a clear actionable error ("leyline not found on PATH — install ley-line-open: <link>") instead of downloading.
- Delete `downloadLeyline` + the `~/.mache/bin/leyline` tier + the MACHE_NO_LEYLINE opt-out (no longer needed once there's nothing to opt out of).
- Update tests that exercise the download flow; update docs/error messages.

Aligns with the project's fail-loud philosophy (cclsp "unknown kind" pattern) and the ADR-0012 direction (leyline is a hard dependency for the semantic tier, not something to silently bootstrap). The pure-Go `.db` path is unaffected — it needs no leyline at all.

## Acceptance
Binary resolution is PATH-only; missing leyline produces one clear install error; `downloadLeyline` and the ~/.mache/bin fallback are gone; no runtime network fetch path remains; tests + docs updated. Verify a stale ~/.mache/bin copy can no longer shadow the PATH binary.

comments.text:
## Precise root cause: un-versioned cache tier shadows the (correct) pin

Not conflicting pins. There is ONE download pin, `leylineBinaryVersion = "v0.5.1"` (socket.go:672), coordinated with the go.mod leyline-schema pin and the daemon pin (#444). The bug is the resolution order in DiscoverOrStart (socket.go:230-249):

1. `exec.LookPath("leyline")` (PATH)
2. `os.Stat(~/.mache/bin/leyline) == nil → use it` — **stat-only, NO version check**
3. else `downloadLeyline()` — governed by the pin, but reached ONLY when the file is absent

So `leylineBinaryVersion` governs *what gets downloaded on a fresh machine*. Once `~/.mache/bin/leyline` exists from an earlier download (this machine: 0.4.1, fetched May 17 when the pin was 0.4.1), tier 2 returns it forever — the later bump to v0.5.1 never re-downloads or re-checks it. The on-disk cache is effectively an un-pinned 4th version that silently overrides the pinned one.

It did NOT affect normal runs here (leyline 0.5.1 on PATH wins at tier 1); it only surfaces when leyline is off PATH (exactly what the mache-9108a1 tier-B probe forced, and what any teammate without leyline on PATH would hit — silently running a stale daemon → wire-format/decode skew).

## Implication for the fix
Removing the fallback (this bead) eliminates the un-versioned tier entirely. Complementary: mache-8kif (already referenced in the socket.go:670 comment) — query the daemon `version` op on connect and refuse on mismatch — is the defense-in-depth that catches skew from ANY source. Both together close it: PATH-only resolution (no stale cache) + version assertion on connect.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
**Root cause found and fixed — but NOT the way this bead prescribes. Read before acting on the original plan.**

This bead says: *drop the `~/.mache/bin` auto-download fallback; require leyline on PATH, fail loud.* The diagnosis ("it rots into version skew") is right. The prescription turns out to be treating a symptom.

## The actual mechanism (measured 2026-07-27)

`~/.mache/bin/leyline` was a **single unversioned path**, and every mache build on the machine treated it as *its* cache. Each build behaves correctly in isolation — see a binary that isn't my pin, replace it with one that is. Together they thrash.

Observed: `~/.local/bin/mache` (commit `1c3d812`, pins **v0.10.2**) and this branch (pins **v0.10.3**) traded that one file back and forth across **four consecutive `task check` runs**. A projection and a smell baseline were generated in between with no indication of which producer had won.

It is not staleness — the file was rewritten constantly, freshly, and correctly, by whichever mache ran last.

## Two wrong diagnoses of mine, recorded so nobody re-runs them

1. **DiscoverOrStart's daemon fast path** returns a live socket with no pin check. Real gap, now warned on (`c115836`), but not this — the builds weren't going through a daemon.
2. **36 orphaned `sheaf-e2e` daemons** (mache-52a23a, oldest from 12:31). Real, reaped — and the cache **still** reverted on the next `task check`. Not this either.

The version gate (`leylineVersionMatchesPin`, mache-608a3c) was working correctly the entire time. Nothing was broken; two correct things were fighting over one filename.

## Fix shipped: namespace, don't drop (`46a3df3`)

Binaries now live at `~/.mache/bin/leyline-<pin>`. Concurrent pins coexist; no build has any reason to touch another's. The legacy unversioned path is still **read** when it already matches the pin (no needless re-download) but never **written**.

Verified against the real adversary: with `leyline-v0.10.3` cached, running the v0.10.2-pinned `~/.local/bin/mache` left it untouched — that build wrote to the legacy path, as it always had.

## Why namespacing beats dropping the fallback

Dropping it would fix the skew by removing the shared resource *and* the capability — every consumer without leyline on PATH breaks, which is the naming/availability gap the fallback was built for. Namespacing removes only the sharing. The fallback keeps working and the failure class becomes impossible rather than merely loud.

**Recommend re-scoping this bead** from "drop the fallback" to its two surviving concerns, both still valid and neither addressed:
- the fallback is found even with `~/.local/bin` off PATH, defeating attempts to force the tree-sitter tier (blocked the mache-9108a1 benchmark)
- it performs a surprise runtime network fetch that can 404 on an unpublished pin

## Also shipped under this bead

- `MACHE_LEYLINE_BINARY` — run-time dev override; explicit, logged, fails on a bad path rather than silently resolving something else (`c115836`)
- `MACHE_LEYLINE_DEV=1` — `leyline:install` now installs the **pinned release** by default. It previously read the pin into `$LL`, printed "installing leyline $LL", and never used it, preferring any local `../ley-line-open` tree — ours is at `v0.10.4-11-g1470030`, eleven commits past a release (`b99777c`)
- `leyline:doctor` — lists every leyline mache can see against the pin; found this in one run

## Not an LLO bug

LLO's v0.10.3 asset reports `0.10.3` and matches its published digest byte-for-byte. Worth raising upstream separately: LLO ships **`_ast` schema changes in patch releases** (v0.7.4 `node_refs.container_node_id`, v0.7.5 `node_defs.canonical_kind`), which is arguably a semver violation and is what makes exact pinning load-bearing. It didn't cause this; it's what made it expensive.

## Verification

`task check` green (19 stages) with the cache stable across runs. `docs/smell-baseline.json` regenerated against the verified pinned release: **IDENTICAL** — it was produced by the correct producer and needs no correction.

title: Observability: log + expose-to-MCP which leyline binary mache resolved (path, version, tier)
description:
## Why

Debugging the stale-0.4.1-leyline skew (see mache-0acdf6) was archaeology because mache gives NO visibility into which leyline binary it's actually using. `DiscoverOrStart` resolves leyline in three tiers (PATH → ~/.mache/bin cache → auto-download) and logs only "auto-starting leyline daemon: <cmd>" — not which binary won, from which tier, or what version. A teammate silently running a stale cached daemon would have no signal at all.

## What

Two complementary additions:

1. **Server-side log line** at daemon spawn / binary resolution: `resolved leyline: <abs path> (<version>) [PATH | cached:~/.mache/bin | downloaded:vX.Y.Z]`. Query the binary's `--version` (or the daemon `version` op) once at resolution. Turns "which leyline?" from a dig into one grep.

2. **Expose to the MCP surface** so an agent/user can ask in the Claude Code /mcp dialogue. Add `leyline` provenance to `get_sheaf_status`'s output (it already reports daemon reachability + sheaf state): `{ leyline: { path, version, source: "PATH"|"cached"|"downloaded", expected_version: "v0.5.1" } }`. Then "what leyline is mache using?" is a tool call, and a mismatch between `version` and `expected_version` is visible at a glance.

## Cross-refs
- mache-0acdf6 (remove the cache/auto-download tier — once PATH-only, `source` is just PATH and this gets simpler)
- mache-8kif (query daemon `version` op on connect, refuse on mismatch — same version data feeds this surface)

## Acceptance
Daemon binary resolution logs path+version+tier; `get_sheaf_status` includes leyline provenance (path, version, source, expected_version); a version mismatch is observable both in logs and via MCP without external tooling.

title: mache build auto-downloads leyline (LLO in the build path) — unblocks find-smells action LLO usage
description:
Part of mache-33dc5f (bundle/auto-provision leyline). Today `mache serve`/DiscoverOrStart auto-downloads leyline (ley-line-open v0.5.7, incl linux binaries) when absent, but `mache build --backend auto/leyline` only CHECKS PATH + ~/.mache/bin (leylineAvailable / autoInvokeLeylineParse) and never downloads — so on a CI runner with no leyline, `mache build` silently falls back to tree-sitter (5 rules), not LLO (all 10 rules + accurate refs).

This is the exact gap that makes the W6.1 find-smells composite action run tree-sitter on CI instead of LLO. Fixing it means the action (which downloads mache + runs `mache build`) gets LLO for free: mache auto-fetches leyline v0.5.7 on first build.

Change:
1. Add exported leyline.ResolveBinary(allowDownload bool) (string, error) in internal/leyline/socket.go — LookPath("leyline") -> ~/.mache/bin/leyline -> (if allowDownload && MACHE_NO_LEYLINE unset) downloadLeyline -> path/err. Reuses existing downloadLeyline + leylineReleaseURLTemplate (hermetic-test-swappable).
2. cmd/serve.go autoInvokeLeylineParse: resolve the binary via ResolveBinary(true) instead of inline LookPath->bundled (so the build path downloads).
3. cmd/build.go: --backend auto decision uses ResolveBinary(true) (prefer leyline, download if needed; graceful tree-sitter fallback on error/offline/MACHE_NO_LEYLINE). --backend leyline errors hard if resolve+download fails (unchanged intent).

Behavior change (intended, ADR-0012 direction): `mache build` default now provisions leyline. Graceful: download failure -> tree-sitter fallback (offline still works); MACHE_NO_LEYLINE=1 opts out; cached to ~/.mache/bin after first fetch.

Tests (hermetic, model on internal/leyline/socket_test.go httptest pattern): MACHE_NO_LEYLINE short-circuits (no download); on-PATH returns path; allowDownload=false errors without download; hermetic download to a temp HOME via swapped leylineReleaseURLTemplate.

Acceptance: `go test ./internal/leyline/ ./cmd/` green; on a no-PATH-leyline env `mache build .` fetches leyline and produces an _ast-bearing .db (all 10 rules run); MACHE_NO_LEYLINE=1 still builds via tree-sitter.

title: Per-project rule disable / severity-override (.mache.json ESLint-style + --exclude) so consumers can skip rules
description:
Blocks the reusable consumer gate (mache-e54fb9): a repo running mache's smell gate (e.g. cloister) must be able to disable builtin rules that don't fit it, WITHOUT editing the embedded rules.

## Current gap
- Severity model exists (off/warn/error, ESLint-cited; SmellRule.Severity + Effective(), cmd/smell_rules.go:90-107) — a rule CAN be "off".
- BUT: external rules with a builtin's ID are COLLISION-REJECTED (LoadExternalSmellRules), so you can't override a builtin's severity via MACHE_SMELL_RULES_DIR. `.mache.json` (ProjectConfig, cmd/config.go) has smellRulesDir but NO disable/override. `--rule` is include-only (one ID/glob); there is NO --exclude/--disable. So disabling a builtin today requires editing embedded JSON a consumer can't touch.
- Table-absence already skips gracefully (--rule '*' skips rules whose _ast tables are absent); this bead is about APPLICABILITY/noise-based disabling, not missing tables.

## Fix (ESLint-style, matches the existing model)
1. `.mache.json`: add `smellRules: { <ruleID>: "off"|"warn"|"error" }` — a severity-override map. `off` disables; also allows error->warn downgrade. Merge order: builtin severity < .mache.json override < --rule/--exclude flags.
2. CLI: add `--exclude <glob>` (repeatable/comma) to find-smells for ad-hoc/CI.
3. Ensure Severity==off actually SKIPS the rule in dispatch (cmd/smell_findings.go) AND the ratchet gate (task smells) — verify it's enforced, not just a model field.

Links: mache-e54fb9 (consumer gate), mache-e0748c (rule contract — enable/disable is part of the rule config surface), mache-b0b979 (rules-as-data).
acceptance_criteria: .mache.json `smellRules` severity-override map disables (off) / re-severities builtin rules without editing embedded JSON; a `--exclude <glob>` flag skips matching rules; a rule set to off is provably SKIPPED in both find-smells output and the `task smells` ratchet gate (test: an off rule produces zero findings + doesn't fail the gate); merge precedence (builtin < .mache.json < flags) covered by tests.

title: Replace writable-control raw arena access with LLO mediated Graph mutations
description: Mache's read-only control path already calls the LLO daemon over UDS and never opens SQLite. The writable path is the exception: `mountControlWritable` extracts the live arena to a temporary `.db`, mutates it through `WritableGraph`, and `ArenaFlusher` writes SQLite pages and control-root updates back into LLO-owned storage. Migrate that path to the generic LLO Graph mutation/ring-I/O capability so Mache can run native-confined or inside libkrun without any raw arena grant. Preserve Mache's validation, splice, draft/status, and surgical invalidation semantics; prebuilt user-supplied `.db` import remains an explicit read-only artifact path. LoE: L (1–2 engineer-weeks after LLO mutation transport lands).
acceptance_criteria: In control mode, read and write operations use typed LLO daemon/ring-I/O capabilities; production Mache no longer extracts the active LLO arena, opens its SQLite payload, writes arena pages, or advances the LLO control root itself. Focused tests prove successful mediated writes, denied undeclared writes, validation/draft/status behavior, root advancement/invalidation, and unchanged read-only UDS behavior. Explicit prebuilt `.db` input remains read-only and is documented as an imported artifact rather than live arena authority.

title: feat: GitHub Action — find-smells PR commenter (advisory, never gate)
description:
Wrap mache find-smells (mache-hupl) in a GitHub Action that posts NEW smell findings introduced by a PR as a markdown comment. Diff-based — comparing PR head against base — so the comment shows 'this PR added' not the absolute findings count.

Shape:
- .github/workflows/find-smells.yml (composite action or workflow)
- Triggers on pull_request
- Steps:
  1. Set up mache binary (cache or build)
  2. (Optional) Set up leyline binary if any _ast rules are needed
  3. Run mache find-smells against the merge-base baseline → JSON
  4. Run mache find-smells against PR head → JSON
  5. Diff the two JSON outputs to compute new findings
  6. Render as markdown summary, post via gh CLI

Behavior:
- Advisory only — never fails the build (no exit-nonzero on findings)
- Comment format: collapsible by rule, top-N findings per rule, links to file:line
- Reposts on PR update (edits existing comment if found)

Why advisory:
- Every find_smells rule is a heuristic; gating produces noise + frustration
- Thresholds (3× mean, hard line counts) embed opinions that may not match the codebase
- 4 of 9 rules need LLO; CI without leyline parse falls back gracefully

Tipping point for ext/machelint extraction (bead mache-3f8w) — once we have a CLI + a GHA, find_smells is clearly its own product surface, no longer just an MCP tool baked into mache.

Depends on mache-hupl (CLI subcommand).
