title: SQLiteGraph.ListChildStats legacy: walkSchema children[0] causes wrong file classification
description:
In SQLiteGraph.ListChildStats (legacy scan path, ~lines 528-545), walkSchema(segments) is called to determine which children are files vs dirs. walkSchemaLevels (line 1067) always descends via current.children[0].

For schemas with multiple children at the same level — e.g. go-schema where the pkg level has six children (imports, functions, methods, types, constants, variables) — this returns the wrong schema level for most branches. File detection then checks the wrong leaf file names against each child base name.

Currently accidentally correct because all go-schema leaves use the same file name (source), so even the wrong level's files list hits the right answer. Would silently break for any schema with different file names per branch (e.g. functions has [source, doc] but types has [source, spec]).

Fix: store dir/file kind explicitly in the scan alongside recordIDs, rather than re-deriving from schema structure at readdir time. recordIDs already identifies leaf-dir containers; a parallel fileEntries set could track the actual file paths stored during collectPathEntries (line 1419 stores childPath+/+f.Name to entries).

comments.text: Fixed in PR #171: pickChildLevel matches static children by segment name, falls back to first dynamic child. Test exercises six static siblings under a single dynamic level.
comments.author: jamestexas

title: evolve-simplify-sqlite-graph-schema-walk
description: Extract schema-walking logic into sqlite_graph_schema.go: Move walkSchemaLevels (1135-1176), pickChildLevel (1182-1197), findRootLevel (1516-1523), and related schemaLevel compilation (compileLevels/compileOneLevel lines 253-276). WHY: ~100 LOC dedicated to path traversal and schema matching. These are pure graph-schema utilities, not database I/O, and could be tested independently. Clean separation of concerns.

title: dirHandle.stats field in MacheFS is dead weight — allocated but never read
description:
In internal/fs/root.go, the dirHandle struct gained a stats []graph.NodeStat field in the perf/readdir-nodestat-snapshot PR. The field is assigned during Opendir (line ~102) but never accessed thereafter — statMap serves the actual O(1) lookup. The stats slice keeps the backing array alive for the lifetime of the open dir handle, wasting memory proportional to the number of children.

The comment also incorrectly describes stats as 'indexed by child base name' — that describes statMap, not stats.

Fix: remove the stats field entirely. statMap is sufficient for all lookups. If the raw slice is ever needed (e.g. for ordered iteration without map overhead), it can be derived from statMap at that point.

title: Smell-gate heuristics create moving targets / benign failures — duplicate_definitions taxes test-helper naming; count rules shift on small refactors
description: User observation (2026-07-22) after a benign gate failure: (1) duplicate_definitions is NAME-based (GROUP BY token HAVING copies>1) — so two identical-named test helpers in different packages FAIL the gate, forcing a 'distinct-naming tax' (macheRepoRoot vs repoRoot vs moduleRoot; resolvePinnedLeylineForIngest/ForLattice). Import cycles often FORCE the duplication (ingest can't import lltest), so distinct-naming is the only escape. Consider excluding _test.go from duplicate_definitions gating, or auto-skipping test-helper patterns. (2) More generally, count/LoC-shaped rules are a MOVING TARGET — small refactors shift counts and trip the ratchet even when no real debt is added (user's ../canonical-hours had a LoC moving-target because impls are small). The failure 'doesn't seem meaningful' when it's refactored-equivalent, not new. Relates to project_smell_enforcement (match-truth-not-model) + feedback_prefer_go_tests_over_shell_and_smell_rules. NOTE: this same class is why the placeholder drift_doc_outdated_count exists (mache-949de6).

comments.text:
Concrete, causally-verified instance of this bead's moving-target concern, from PR #551 (mache-90b89b).

The smell gate flagged 2 NEW god_file findings:
  internal/ingest/sqlite_writer.go
  testdata/snapshots/medium-rust-rosary/src/sprites.rs

Neither is new sprawl:
- The branch added ZERO definitions to sqlite_writer.go — verified by 'git diff main -- internal/ingest/sqlite_writer.go | grep -E "^\+(func|type) "' returning nothing. Its def count is unchanged.
- sprites.rs is a testdata snapshot the branch never touched at all.

Mechanism: god_file fires on 'n >= 10 AND n > 3.0 * AVG(n)' (cmd/rules/god_file.json), deliberately relative to the codebase's own distribution. The branch added six small new files, which pulled AVG(n) down, lowering the 3x threshold below two UNCHANGED def counts.

So an author who adds well-factored small files gets charged for unrelated files crossing a threshold that moved underneath them — and one of those files (external testdata) cannot be refactored at all. The failure message says 'NEW finding', which reads as 'you made this worse'.

Worth noting the relative threshold is a deliberate design choice, not a bug: the rule's own description argues for surfacing sprawl 'relative to the codebase's own distribution rather than a hard line-count cutoff'. The problem is attribution, not the statistic. Options if this is worth fixing:
  (a) report the metric and the threshold in the failure so a mean-shift is visible as such
  (b) gate on per-file metric deltas rather than on crossing an absolute-but-moving line
  (c) exclude testdata/ from the mean computation, since snapshots of external repos are not part of this codebase's distribution

Option (c) is the cheapest and would have removed one of the two findings here.
comments.author: rsry-cli

acceptance_criteria: A decision (+ implementation) on reducing smell-gate false-friction: e.g. duplicate_definitions excludes _test.go (test helpers legitimately share names across packages), and/or the ratchet distinguishes 'refactored-equivalent' from genuinely-new debt. Documented rationale; task smells still catches real duplication.

title: TestListChildStats_SnapshotConsistency accesses store internals directly — fragile test coupling
description:
TestListChildStats_SnapshotConsistency in internal/graph/batch_test.go (lines ~178-346 of the PR diff) directly accesses store.mu and store.nodes to drive a concurrent write. This requires the test to be in the graph package (white-box), which it is, but the pattern means:

1. The test breaks if MemoryStore's internal field names change (mu → rwmu, nodes → data, etc.).
2. The test cannot demonstrate the same property for SQLiteGraph or WritableGraph — those backends are entirely untested for snapshot consistency.
3. The writer goroutine calls close(flipReady) before acquiring the WLock, then immediately acquires it, giving the reader goroutine a tiny window to observe state. Under heavy load, the writer may acquire the WLock before any reader gets an RLock, meaning the test runs 500 iterations all-99 without ever exercising the all-10 case.

The test is still useful for the race detector, but it does not actually prove the single-RLock property for the concrete implementation — it just proves the value-copy property (which TestListChildStats_ValueSemantics_NoAliasing already covers more cleanly).

Note: the deleted TestMemoryStore_ListChildNodes_SingleRLock used a 2-second timeout to detect deadlock, which was a cruder but more portable approach. The replacement is technically superior as a race test but weaker as a single-lock proof.

title: FUSE readdirStat: virtual entries not in statMap fall back to nil (LOOKUP), but callers/ _diagnostics/ and .query/ were previously resolved by GetNode
description:
In the old readdirStat (before perf/readdir-nodestat-snapshot), for any entry not resolved by the virtual resolver, a GetNode call was made and its result used to fill stat. In the new readdirStat, after the statMap lookup and resolver.Resolve check, the function returns nil (LOOKUP fallback).

The question is whether any entry type was previously resolved by GetNode but is now neither in statMap nor the resolver. Virtual dirs (callers/, _diagnostics/, .query/, _schema.json, context) all go through resolver.Resolve. Graph children go through statMap. The only gap is if resolver.Resolve returns nil for an entry that GetNode would have succeeded on.

Specifically: if a graph child's ID is in the graph but filepath.Base(s.ID) collides with a non-child entry name, or if ListChildStats returns a child that GetNode for that child would have succeeded on but statMap lookup fails (name mismatch between filepath.Base(s.ID) and the entry name in the directory listing).

The statMap is keyed by filepath.Base(s.ID). The entries list contains filepath.Base(s.ID) for graph children. So these should be consistent. But verify: is there any case where an entry name added to dh.entries does NOT match filepath.Base(s.ID)? The loop at Opendir line ~91-95 adds filepath.Base(s.ID) to entries AND to statMap with the same key. Consistent.

However: if ListChildStats returns a NodeStat with ID that has a different base than what ListChildren would have returned for the same child, the FUSE kernel will get nil stat (forcing LOOKUP) for an entry it knows exists. This would not be a correctness bug (LOOKUP fallback works) but would defeat the perf goal for those entries.

No concrete case found, but the fallback behavior change from GetNode to nil should be explicitly tested with a mock graph that returns different base names from ListChildStats vs what the kernel expects.

title: CompositeGraph.ListChildStats root case uses time.Now() for ModTime — non-deterministic across calls
description:
In internal/graph/composite.go, CompositeGraph.ListChildStats for the root case (id == "") sets ModTime: time.Now() for each mount point NodeStat. This is consistent with CompositeGraph.GetNode which also uses time.Now() for mount points, but both are wrong.

Mount point directories are static — their names don't change between calls. Using time.Now() means every readdir of the root returns different ModTimes, which:
1. Defeats the NFS attribute cache (causes re-stat on every access)
2. Makes readdir results non-deterministic across FUSE stat calls
3. Differs from other backends that return zero ModTime (which falls back to mountTime in both nodeToFileInfo and statToFileInfo)

Fix: use a zero time.Time{} for mount point NodeStat.ModTime, consistent with how MemoryStore nodes without explicit ModTime are handled (zero falls back to mountTime in both NFS statToFileInfo and FUSE readdirStat). Pre-existing in GetNode but now amplified because ListChildStats is called in the hot readdir path.

comments.text: Fixed in PR #170 (commit 39b5196): mountTime captured at NewCompositeGraph; both GetNode and ListChildStats use it instead of time.Now().
comments.author: jamestexas

title: Operational perf bench — instrument + measure mache against real corpora
description:
PR #373 surfaced that we have ZERO real performance numbers for mache. The microbench measured wire-decode cost (~100µs work) and the correctness audit found 6 bugs, but neither produces the numbers you'd quote to compare against Sourcegraph, Zoekt, or agent-lsp on a real codebase.

## What we have today

- `cmd/all_tools_e2e_test.go` — phase-1 e2e harness on a small in-tree fixture. Captures `latency_ms` + `alloc_bytes` per tool. Test-only, runs against ~100-file fixture, gated on `E2E_PROFILE_OUT`. Phases 2-4 (pprof, regression detection) are stubs.
- `internal/leyline/socket_bench_test.go` — wire-decode microbench. Tests json encode/decode cost at the boundary. Not representative of real query latency.
- `cmd/build.go:176` — wall time + `engine.go:654` "Ingested N files" log. No MB/sec, peak RSS, .db size ratio.

## What we need

### 1. `wrapHandler` instrumentation (live MCP latency)

`cmd/serve_registry.go:126` `wrapHandler` is the chokepoint every MCP tool call passes through. Add an optional env-gated trace:

    if traceFile := os.Getenv("MACHE_TRACE"); traceFile != "" {
        defer func(start time.Time) {
            fmt.Fprintf(traceWriter, "%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n",
                time.Now().Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
                req.Params.Name,
                time.Since(start).Microseconds(),
                len(resultBody),
            )
        }(time.Now())
    }

Tab-separated JSONL-friendly format. Default off (zero overhead). When set, every call writes one row. Any session — synthetic bench OR real agent traffic — gets timing for free.

### 2. Ingest perf harness (`mache build` at scale)

A `benchmarks/ingest/` bash script that takes a list of corpora, runs `/usr/bin/time -v ./bin/mache build <corpus> <out.db>` for each, captures:

| Corpus | LOC | Wall time | Peak RSS | .db size | DB/source ratio | Files/sec |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| mache | 28K | ? | ? | ? | ? | ? |
| consul | 319K | ? | ? | ? | ? | ? |
| kubernetes | ~5M | ? | ? | ? | ? | ? |
| linux | ~30M | ? | ? | ? | ? | ? |

Emit a markdown report. Run on the same machine each time. Annotate methodology (no warm caches, etc.).

### 3. Read-path latency harness (per-tool quantiles on real corpora)

A Go binary at `benchmarks/cmd/readperf` that:
- Starts a mache MCP server with `MACHE_TRACE` enabled on a given .db
- Fires N=10K queries from a workload spec (mix of `find_callers`, `find_definition`, `list_directory`, etc.) against representative tokens harvested from the corpus
- Reads the trace output, computes p50 / p95 / p99 / max per tool
- Emits one row per corpus per tool

Workload spec lives in a YAML so different corpora can have different question mixes.

### 4. Comparative harness (mache vs the field)

Pick a fixed corpus + question set. Run the same 20 questions through:
- mache (this PR's MCP)
- Sourcegraph (their CLI or API)
- agent-lsp
- grep baseline

Emit `{tool × question × corpus → time_ms, result_count, token_count}`. Aggregate into a comparison table. Methodology should follow Serena's prompt structure (already vendored at `benchmarks/serena/upstream/`) — agent-self-eval with timing instrumentation added.

## What's out of scope

- Optimization. This bead is measurement-only. Optimization is a follow-up that requires baseline numbers to even start.
- Continuous benchmarking infrastructure. Manual reruns are fine until we have a stable baseline.
- Sourcegraph parity claim. We can measure both; whether we then claim "faster" requires honest framing (apples-to-oranges in some ways — Sourcegraph is full-text + symbol index at multi-tenant scale; mache is structural projection).

## Sequence

1. Add `wrapHandler` MACHE_TRACE instrumentation (~30 LOC, doesn't change behavior when env unset)
2. Add ingest-perf bash script + run on the 4 corpora above
3. Add `benchmarks/cmd/readperf` + run against mache repo + consul .dbs
4. Pick ONE shared corpus and ONE shared question for first head-to-head with Sourcegraph or agent-lsp; expand from there

## Why this matters

Without this, every "mache is X faster" or "mache is X slower" claim is unfounded. The flip side: every claim about a peer tool's superiority is also unfounded against mache. The bench from PR #373 closes the correctness gap; this bead closes the measurement gap.

Estimate: 1-2 sessions for steps 1-3 once you're ready to dig in. Step 4 is research-shaped and open-ended.

**Concrete methodology lifted from GrapeRoot (Codex-CLI-Compact, MIT)** — added 2026-05-13.

Their `benchmark/run_preinjection_benchmark.py` is the most actionable reference for step 4 (comparative harness). Three-way comparison:
1. Normal Claude — no MCP, baseline
2. MCP-DGC — Claude + their MCP server
3. Pre-injection — context packed into the prompt upfront

For mache we drop mode 3 (mache doesn't pre-inject; the projection IS the FS). Run modes 1 and 2 with our own MCP config.

**Per-prompt metrics they capture** (all from `claude -p --output-format json`):
- Input/output tokens, cache creation/read tokens
- Wall-clock duration
- Total cost USD (Claude's own accounting)
- Turn count
- **50-point custom quality scorer**: word_count (0-8), file_mentions (0-10), code_blocks (0-8), specificity / identifier mentions (0-10), structure / headings+lists (0-6), category_bonus (0-8)
- Resume support via JSONL append

**Their published numbers** (restaurant-CRM corpus, 15 prompts, Sonnet 4.6):
| Mode | $/prompt | Turns |
|---|---:|---:|
| Normal | $0.25 | — |
| MCP-DGC | $0.27 | 11.7 |
| Pre-injection | $0.17 | 8.9 |

**Note**: MCP-DGC is MORE expensive than baseline. The thesis "MCP tools = always faster/cheaper" is wrong; tools that inflate turns net-negative. **Mache's MCP surface must be measured for this exact failure mode.**

**Adoption plan for mache**:
1. Vendor `benchmark/run_preinjection_benchmark.py` (strip pre-injection mode and the dual-graph-specific MCP infra) → `benchmarks/cost-quality/bench.py`
2. Write Go-equivalent 15-prompt battery targeting the mache repo itself: keep their 6 categories (code_explanation / bug_fix / feature_add / refactoring / architecture / debugging), 2-3 prompts per category. Prompts reference real mache files/types so we can validate quality scores. Save as `benchmarks/cost-quality/prompts.json`.
3. Two modes: normal CC (no mache MCP) vs CC + mache MCP server on the mache repo.
4. Quality scorer ports almost verbatim — file-extension regex needs `.go|.md|.json|.yaml` instead of their Python set. Everything else (word count, headings, structure, code blocks) is language-agnostic.
5. Run once, commit the report to `benchmarks/cost-quality/results/`.

title: Ship apko + melange in-repo for `mache:0.8.0` (retire kiln dependency)
description:
Filed 2026-05-10 from cloister's deployment-readiness audit.

## What needs to happen

mache currently doesn't have apko/melange in-repo — the image came from `../kiln`. **kiln is being retired** (archived / no longer maintained). mache needs its own in-repo image build so the cloister cluster topology can consume `mache:0.8.0` without depending on a separate build tool.

cloister's `cluster.capnp` (at `~/remotes/art/cloister/cluster.capnp`) declares the mache bundle as:
```
image     = "mache:0.8.0",
ipcSocket = "/run/cloister-uds/mache.sock",
args      = ["serve", "--ipc-socket", "/run/cloister-uds/mache.sock"],
```

## Scope

1. **Add `apko.yaml` + `melange.yaml` at the repo root** (matching the pattern that notme and rosary use). Reference kiln's existing configs at `~/remotes/art/kiln/{apko,melange}.yaml` as the starting point — those built mache's image previously; lift the relevant parts. (Don't pull from kiln at build time; INLINE the config.)

2. **Add a `Taskfile.yml` target `task image`** that runs:
   ```
   melange build melange.yaml --signing-key melange.rsa --out-dir ./packages
   apko build apko.yaml mache:0.8.0 mache.tar --keyring-append melange.rsa.pub
   ```
   Pattern from cloister's `Taskfile.yml` (see `~/remotes/art/cloister/Taskfile.yml` section `## OCI packaging`).

3. **Verify `task image` produces `mache:0.8.0`** as an OCI artifact loadable via `docker load < mache.tar`.

4. **Verify the image runs**: `docker run mache:0.8.0 serve --ipc-socket /tmp/mache.sock` should start mache's MCP server bound to the UDS path. The wire is capnp ToolCall/Result over UDS (per cloister ADR-0005); if today mache speaks HTTP-over-UDS rather than capnp, flag it as a wire-shape concern (the cluster expects capnp).

5. **Document the build invocation** in mache's README so a cloister operator can reproduce.

6. **Don't reference kiln** anywhere in the new configs. The retirement of kiln is the motivation for this work.

## Context: mache no longer uses FUSE

mache's deployment story is simpler than it used to be — no FUSE, no kernel privileges required. The apko config should NOT request fuse-libs or device mounts. Just a regular subprocess container.

## Acceptance

- `task image` builds successfully on a clean checkout.
- `mache:0.8.0` tag is loadable + runnable.
- `mache serve --ipc-socket /tmp/X.sock` works inside the container.
- README has a "Building the image" section pointing at `task image`.
- No references to kiln in apko.yaml, melange.yaml, Taskfile.yml, or README.

## Cross-repo context

- **kiln** (`~/remotes/art/kiln`) is the retired predecessor. Its apko.yaml is the reference; lift, inline, move on. Don't depend on kiln being present.
- **cloister** at `~/remotes/art/cloister/cluster.capnp` is the consumer.
- The wire contract: `~/remotes/art/cloister/docs/adr/0005-internal-wire-leyline-net.md`.

## Out of scope

- Changing mache's MCP server implementation.
- Multi-replica scaling.
- WASM/wasi packaging (separate decision; mache being non-FUSE opens it up but that's a different bead).

title: find_smells: task-usage drift — workflow steps that inline a Taskfile command instead of calling `task <name>`
description:
## Idea (user-originated)

If a repo has a `Taskfile.yml` AND `task` is invoked in at least one CI workflow, then every other workflow step that re-implements a task's command inline (raw `go test`, `golangci-lint`, `gofumpt`, `go build`…) is drift: the Taskfile is the source of truth, and CI should run the same recipe a developer runs locally. Flag the inline re-implementations; allow an escape-hatch annotation for the cases where CI legitimately differs.

## Concrete evidence in mache (2026-06-20 audit)

`task` IS used in some workflows but not others:
- `ci.yml`: uses `task build`, `task test` — but `go vet ./...` (raw; `task vet` exists), `gofumpt -d -extra .` (raw install; `task fmt` exists), and `golangci/golangci-lint-action` (action; `task lint` exists) bypass the Taskfile.
- `cache-roundtrip.yml`: hand-rolled `go test -v -count=1 ... -run "TestCache|TestOCI"` instead of `task cache:test` / `task cache:roundtrip`.
- `find-smells.yml`: raw `go build -o /tmp/mache ./` instead of `task build` / `task smells`.
- `integration.yml`: uses `task test -- ...`.

When a task definition changes (new build tag, flag, env), the hand-rolled CI copies silently fall out of sync. That is the smell.

## Rule shape

Host-side rule (filesystem cross-reference, like the ADR-0018 `drift_doc_*` family — see mache-e1b6c8 / mache-faacf3), NOT a pure SQL-over-AST rule:
1. Detect `Taskfile.yml` + parse task names + their `cmds`.
2. Parse `.github/workflows/*.yml` `run:` steps.
3. If ANY workflow `run:` invokes `task <name>`, then for every other `run:` whose command is substring-equivalent to some task's `cmds`, emit a finding: "step re-implements `task <name>`; call the task instead."
4. Escape hatch: a `# smell:allow task-drift <reason>` comment on the step, OR a per-repo allowlist (consistent with mache-96341d per-rule excludes).

## Related
- mache-c7421e (rule-polarity: host must-hold / done-rules) — this is a must-hold rule.
- mache-e1b6c8 / mache-faacf3 / mache-fa569a (ADR-0018 doc-drift host-side rules) — same execution model.
- mache-96341d (rule categorization + allowlist surface) — escape-hatch mechanism.
- Sibling rule (divergent-default duplicate constants) filed separately.

title: find_smells: divergent-default duplicates — similarly-named constants/vars/env-vars carrying different default values
description:
## Idea (user-originated)

Env vars, constants, package vars, and globals with **similar names but different defaults** are a smell — they usually encode the *same fact* in multiple places, and the copies drift. Detect name-clusters that disagree on their literal default.

## Concrete evidence in mache (2026-06-20 audit) — the "mache version" fact lives in 3+ places with different values:

| Symbol | Location | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `cmd.Version` (ldflags) | `cmd/mount.go:25` | `"dev"` default, git-tag at build |
| `MacheProducerVersion` | `cmd/cache.go:54` | `"0.x.y"` (never-filled placeholder; TODO at :52 wants `cmd.Version`) |
| `serverVersion` | `tools/server-json-gen/main.go:63` | `"0.8.0"` (stamped into server.json; enforced by the `server-json-drift` CI gate but NOT synced to the git tag) |

And the "leyline version" fact lives in 2 places:
- `leylineBinaryVersion` (`internal/leyline/socket.go:669`) = `v0.4.5` (was `v0.4.1` — drifted, fixed in PR #426)
- `minLeyLineOpenVersion` (`tools/server-json-gen/main.go:83`) = `0.4.5`

These drifted in production: socket.go sat at v0.4.1 while server-json-gen was already at v0.4.5. That is exactly the smell — same fact, two constants, divergent defaults.

## Rule shape

Structural rule over identifiers + their literal initializers (AST/node data):
1. Collect `const` / `var` / `os.Getenv(...) default` sites with a string/numeric literal default.
2. Cluster by normalized name similarity (strip case, `Version`/`Ver`/`VERSION`, `min`/`max` prefixes; token-set or edit-distance).
3. Flag clusters of size >=2 whose literal defaults are NOT equal.
4. Severity higher when the values are version-shaped (`vX.Y.Z`, `X.Y.Z`) — those are almost always meant to be single-sourced.
5. Escape hatch: allowlist (mache-96341d) for intentionally-distinct look-alikes.

## Why it matters
The fix the rule nudges toward is single-sourcing (derive `MacheProducerVersion` + `serverVersion` from `cmd.Version`; one leyline-version const imported by both consumers) — which is the v0.9.0 cleanup this audit feeds.

## Related
- mache-96341d (rule categorization + allowlist), mache-c7421e (rule polarity).
- Sibling rule (task-usage drift) filed separately.
- Immediate consumer: the v0.9.0 version-single-sourcing PR.

title: Consume LLO BindingRecord capnp event log instead of canonical-view SQL JOIN
description:
Cross-repo paired bead for **ley-line-open-ce2281** (T8.4 of decade ley-line-open-9d30ac, thread T8/capnp-as-protocol).

## Why

Mache's canonical-view path (`internal/ingest/sqlite_writer.go:114-310` — `v_refs`, `v_defs` views over `_lsp_refs`/`_lsp_defs` JOINed against `_ast`) couples mache to LLO's SQL column names. be6136 was caused exactly by this: a one-byte path mismatch in `_source.path` made every JOIN miss. The L2/L3 reframe (2026-05-08) flips the ownership: capnp messages are the data plane, SQLite is a *projection*.

LLO now produces `${db_path}.bindings.capnp` alongside any `.db` produced by `leyline lsp` (T8.2, ley-line-open-49475bc). Mache should consume that file directly.

## Schema

Read the canonical schemas at `~/remotes/art/ley-line-open/rs/ll-core/schema-capnp/schemas/`:
- `common.capnp` — Position, Range, Hash, NodeRef
- `binding.capnp` — BindingRecord with `targetNodeId`, `refToken`, `refUri`, `refRange`, **`constructNodeId`** (function/method scope; matches `node_refs` shape — what falsifiability B was missing), **`refSiteNodeId`** (leaf identifier — most precise locator)

LLO commits the `.capnp` files; mache should vendor or submodule them, not duplicate. See `~/remotes/art/ley-line-open/rs/ll-core/schema-capnp/README.md` for file format conventions and Go consumer pattern.

## Concrete deliverables

1. **Add capnp-go dep** (`capnproto.org/go/capnp/v3`).
2. **Vendor schemas**: pull `common.capnp` + `binding.capnp` into a `schemas/` dir or a git submodule pointing at LLO's `rs/ll-core/schema-capnp/schemas/`.
3. **Build pipeline**: `capnp compile -ogo --src-prefix=schemas schemas/*.capnp` to generate Go bindings (commit to `internal/lsp/bindings/`).
4. **Reader** (`internal/lsp/binding_log.go`): iterate `${db}.bindings.capnp` via `capnp.NewDecoder` until EOF; expose `BindingRecord` slice or iterator.
5. **Migration**: replace `v_refs` JOIN-based queries (sqlite_writer.go:114-130, ~300-310) with the capnp reader. Keep the SQL views as a deprecated dual-read fallback during transition.
6. **Re-validate falsifiability**:
   - `cmd/falsifiability_skip_list_ablation_test.go` (A) should still pass (uses `target_node_id`, untouched by the migration).
   - `cmd/falsifiability_lsp_projection_test.go` (B) — was 100% mismatch on leaf vs call-expression paths. With the capnp `constructNodeId` field, this becomes a tight equality check against `node_refs.node_id`. Pass criterion: <5% discrepancy on real gopls-enriched .dbs.

## Acceptance

- `go test ./...` green
- Falsifiability A still PASS
- Falsifiability B reduced from 100% mismatch to <5% (or document the residual as schema-vs-extractor disagreement, file followup)
- Existing canonical-view consumers see no regression (dual-read window)

## File pointers in LLO

- Schemas: `rs/ll-core/schema-capnp/schemas/{common,binding}.capnp`
- Producer: `rs/ll-open/lsp/src/project.rs::project_references` (writes log when `binding_log: Some`)
- Wiring: `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/cmd_lsp.rs:163` (CLI always writes), `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/lsp_pass.rs::sibling_capnp_log` (daemon: file-backed only)

LLO will not break the SQL columns until consumers have migrated; T8 schemas are additive at the SQL layer.

title: Make install/uninstall first-class mache subcommands — provisioning only exists in the Taskfile, and PATH carries a stale leyline that shadows the pin
description:
Raised by jamestexas 2026-07-30 after `task install`: the leyline path is not added, so the pinned binary is unreachable from the shell.

## Measured three-way skew on a machine that has run `task install`

    ~/.local/bin/leyline            0.10.3   ON PATH   <- what a user gets typing `leyline`
    ~/.mache/bin/leyline-v0.13.0    0.13.0   not on PATH <- what mache actually uses (the pin)
    ~/.mache/bin/leyline            0.10.2   not on PATH <- orphaned legacy unversioned path

`~/.mache/bin` is not on PATH at all (verified). So `leyline cdc enable --db x.db` typed at a shell runs 0.10.3 against a .db mache built with 0.13.0. Same defect class as mache-0acdf6 (cache thrash silently changing _ast shape), relocated from the cache to PATH. It is invisible: both binaries are named `leyline` and neither announces the mismatch unless you run --version.

Note this does NOT break mache itself — ResolveBinary finds the pinned copy in the namespaced cache and logs when it ignores a non-pinned PATH entry (observed: "leyline on PATH (...) is not the pinned v0.13.0 — ignoring it"). The breakage is for a HUMAN or AGENT invoking leyline directly, which v0.13.0 made a real workflow (`leyline cdc enable`, `leyline cdc gc`, `leyline parse`).

## Why provisioning should not live in the Taskfile

`task install` (Taskfile.yml:15) and `task leyline:install`/`leyline:ensure` are the ONLY provisioning paths. All of them require a checked-out repo with a Taskfile. A user who installed mache from a release binary or Homebrew has neither — so the shipped artifact cannot provision its own required backend. That is backwards for a released tool, and it is why the stale ~/.local/bin/leyline persists: nothing owns removing it.

mache already has the machinery in-binary: ResolveBinary, EnsureCachedBinary (downloads + SHA-verifies), the pin constant, and the leyline:doctor diagnosis logic. Making install first-class is mostly relocating existing code behind a subcommand, not writing new provisioning.

Also asymmetric today: there is `unmount` but no `mount` (see mache-d55457), and no uninstall at all — nothing removes ~/.mache/bin, the namespaced binaries, or a stale ~/.local/bin/leyline.

## Design — and the trap to avoid

PROPOSED: `mache install` (provision pinned leyline, report PATH state, warn on shadowing) and `mache uninstall` (remove cache + report what was removed).

TRAP, must be honoured: do NOT resolve this by symlinking `~/.mache/bin/leyline` -> the pinned version. mache-0acdf6 deliberately made that unversioned path read-only-never-written precisely because it was a shared mutable resource that concurrent mache builds fought over. Reintroducing a write there re-opens that bug for anyone running two mache versions.

Safer directions to weigh:
  (a) `mache leyline path` printing the resolved pinned binary, so callers do `$("mache leyline path") cdc enable` — always version-correct, no PATH mutation, agent-first.
  (b) `mache leyline exec -- <args>` proxying to the pinned binary. Strongest guarantee; costs a process hop.
  (c) A per-pin shim dir mache owns and the user adds to PATH once — but this reintroduces "which version does bare `leyline` mean" the moment the pin moves.
  (d) install prints the export line and only writes shell rc with an explicit `--shell-init` opt-in (never edit dotfiles silently).

(a) or (b) look right because they make the version question unaskable rather than answered-by-convention. Whichever lands should also detect and offer to remove a shadowing ~/.local/bin/leyline, since that is the actual observed failure.

Related: mache-d55457 (no `mount` subcommand though README documents one) — same class of CLI surface drifting from what docs and users expect.

comments.text:
PR #584 (https://github.com/agentic-research/mache/pull/584) implements options (a) and (b) only — `mache leyline path` and `mache leyline exec`. Auto-merge armed (squash, delete-branch).

Scope shipped:
- `mache leyline path` — prints the resolved pinned binary as an ABSOLUTE path, nothing else on stdout, so `$(mache leyline path) cdc enable --db x.db` composes. ResolveBinary's "not the pinned <ver> — ignoring it" diagnostic stays on stderr.
- `mache leyline exec [--] <args...>` — `DisableFlagParsing` so leyline's own flags (incl. `--help`) reach leyline; strips one leading `--`; forwards stdin/stdout/stderr; exits with leyline's status via an injectable `leylineExecExit` (Execute() would otherwise flatten every failure to 1).
- Both go through `leyline.ResolveBinary(true)`; resolution errors are returned unwrapped so there is one error vocabulary.

TRAP honoured: nothing writes `~/.mache/bin/leyline` (unversioned). Provisioning is still entirely ResolveBinary's, which only ever writes the pin-namespaced path. There is an explicit regression test (`TestLeylinePath_NeverWritesUnversionedCachePath`) asserting the unversioned path stays absent, preserving mache-0acdf6. No PATH or shell-rc mutation.

title: Migrate from generation-polling to root-polling for arena hot-swap (LLO T2.4 mirror)
description:
Cross-repo paired bead for **ley-line-open T2.4** (in flight 2026-05-09). LLO is removing the `generation` field from `Controller` + `ArenaHeader`; ArenaHeader VERSION bumps 1 → 2; readers must migrate to `current_root` comparison.

## Why this needs to land in the same wave as mache-36d961

LLO ADR-0014's Σ root + canonical encoding makes content-addressing a substrate property. `generation` was a counter that coincidentally stayed in sync; `current_root` IS the substrate's identity. Once T2.4 ships, generation is gone and old mache binaries break.

The LLO agent's framing: ship T2.4 + mache CGO removal (mache-36d961) as ONE breaking wave, not two. Tagged release pair (LLO v0.2.0 + mache v0.2.0) so consumers running mismatched versions get a clear `ArenaHeader VERSION mismatch` error rather than silent corruption.

## Migration sites in mache

Surveyed 2026-05-09; four real sites:

| File | Lines | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `cmd/mount.go` | 522, 538, 612 | `ctrl.GetGeneration()` → `ctrl.GetCurrentRoot()` (or whatever LLO names the new API). The hot-swap polling loop's `currentGen <= lastGen` becomes `currentRoot != lastRoot` |
| `internal/graph/arena.go` | `ArenaHeader` struct | Bump support from VERSION 1 → 2. May keep VERSION 1 read path for legacy `.arena` files during a transition window, with a clear deprecation log |
| `internal/graph/arena_writer.go` | 153-219 | Writer-side arena mutations need to write VERSION 2 + the new root field |
| `internal/graph/store_local.go` | 35, 65, 89 | `Generation: generation` → `Root: rootHash` (or carry both during transition) |

Plus `internal/control/` (mache's wrapper around the LLO controller) gains the new API method.

## Sequence

1. **LLO T2.4 lands first** — locks the new API surface, publishes ArenaHeader VERSION 2 spec
2. **Mache filed branch consumes from LLO's main** before LLO tags v0.2.0 — verify the API ergonomics, surface any issues
3. **Mache PR combines this + mache-36d961** — single PR, single review, single merge. Drops CGO + migrates polling together
4. **Tagged release pair**: LLO v0.2.0 + mache v0.2.0. README + CHANGELOG note the breaking change

## Acceptance

- `cmd/mount.go` hot-swap polling uses root-based detection
- `internal/graph/arena.go` reads VERSION 2 (and optionally VERSION 1 during transition)
- All test fixtures + benches that pass `0` as a generation arg migrated
- `go test ./...` green against post-T2.4 LLO main
- Smoke: real `leyline serve` → mache mount round-trip; verify hot-swap fires when LLO writes a new arena

## Out of scope

- ADR-0014 (mache-in-constellation) is the framework context; this bead is a specific migration step not a re-design
- Hosted-mode (mache ADR-0010) considerations — orthogonal
- Performance characterization of root-polling vs generation-polling — LLO has done that work upstream

## Refs

- LLO T2.4 in flight 2026-05-09 (commits incoming)
- Pairs structurally with mache-36d961 (CGO removal epic) — recommended same-wave landing
- Mache ADR-0014 frames the constellation context: this bead is "step toward content-addressed identity throughout the substrate"

comments.text:
## LLO T2.4 wire format — locked, ready for mache to consume

LLO side passes `task ci` (check + clippy + workspace tests). Pinning the final wire format here so mache can implement against the frozen spec.

### Daemon UDS JSON — every state-publishing op

`generation` is **gone** from every response. Replaced by `current_root` (64-char lowercase hex of BLAKE3 over the serialized arena bytes).

| Op | Old (v0.1) | New (v0.2 / T2.4) |
|---|---|---|
| `op_status` | `{"ok":true,"generation":N,"phase":...,"arena_path":...,"arena_size":...,"enrichment":{...}}` | `{"ok":true,"phase":...,"current_root":"<64hex>","arena_path":...,"arena_size":...,"enrichment":{...}}` |
| `op_flush` | `{"ok":true,"generation":N}` | `{"ok":true,"current_root":"<64hex>"}` |
| `op_load` | `{"ok":true,"generation":N}` | `{"ok":true,"current_root":"<64hex>"}` |
| `op_reparse` | `{"ok":true,"generation":N,"parsed":..,...}` | `{"ok":true,"current_root":"<64hex>","parsed":..,...}` |
| `op_enrich` | `{"ok":true,"generation":N,"passes":[...]}` | `{"ok":true,"current_root":"<64hex>","passes":[...]}` |
| `op_snapshot` | `{"ok":true,"generation":N}` | `{"ok":true,"current_root":"<64hex>"}` |

Fresh controller / no snapshot yet → `current_root` is the 64-char zero sentinel `"0000...0000"`.

### ArenaHeader (.arena file format)

```
struct ArenaHeader {        // VERSION: 1 → 2
  magic: u32,
  version: u8,              // = 2
  active_buffer: u8,
  padding: [u8; 2],
  sequence: u64,
  data_size: u64,           // NEW T2.4 — exact length of payload in active buffer
}
```

`data_size` replaces the old "parse SQLite header bytes 28-31 to recover length" trick — that was unreliable (db_bytes.len()=20480 vs sqlite_db_size=28672 mismatch under WAL/freelist). Now LLO writers set `data_size = payload.len()` and readers hash `buf[..data_size]`.

### Controller (.ctrl file)

VERSION 1 → 2. `Controller::open_or_create` rejects mismatched VERSION with a descriptive error. The pre-T2.4 `OFF_GENERATION` slot is now a private sync atom used purely for Acquire/Release fencing — no public surface.

Public Rust API: `current_root() -> [u8; 32]` (Acquire-loads the sync atom to fence subsequent byte reads), `set_arena(path, size)` (no gen param; preserves current_root, bumps sync), `set_arena_with_root(path, size, root)` (no gen param; atomic publish via fence + Release-store).

### What mache must do

1. **Wire client** (probably `internal/control/`): swap `generation` parsing for `current_root` hex parse on `op_status` and any other status-checking call site.
2. **Hot-swap polling** (likely `internal/graph/arena.go` or equivalent): poll `current_root` for change detection rather than `current_gen`. LLO's HotSwapGraph has the canonical reference impl in `rs/ll-open/fs/src/graph.rs` — the swap predicate is `cached_root != current_root`.
3. **ArenaHeader parser** (likely `internal/graph/arena.go`): bump expected VERSION to 2; read the new `data_size` field; reject VERSION 1 with a clear "stale arena, need LLO ≥ 0.2.0" error.
4. **Reader-side σ verification** (optional but parallels T2.3): hash `buf[..data_size]` and compare to controller's `current_root`. Skip when root is the zero sentinel (legacy / pre-T2.2 writers). LLO impl: `rs/ll-open/fs/src/lib.rs::verify_arena_root`.
5. **CGO elimination** is a separate cutover but can land in the same release if the T2.4 changes are scoped narrowly enough to merge alongside.

### Coordination

LLO commit hash will be filed here once landed. Tag plan: LLO `v0.2.0` + mache `v0.2.0` shipped together as a coordinated breaking release. Old mache reading new arena → VERSION mismatch error (loud, correct). New mache reading old arena → same VERSION mismatch error (loud, correct).

LLO reference impl files (read-only authoritative source):
- `rs/ll-core/core/src/control.rs` — Controller / set_arena / set_arena_with_root / current_root
- `rs/ll-core/core/src/layout.rs` — ArenaHeader VERSION 2
- `rs/ll-open/fs/src/lib.rs::verify_arena_root` — reader-side hash verification
- `rs/ll-open/fs/src/graph.rs::HotSwapGraph` — root-polling swap pattern
- `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/ops.rs::read_root_hex` — wire format hex helper

title: drift_doc_undocumented_export: coverage-direction drift rule (exported def with no markdown reference)
description:
The missing fourth drift_doc_* rule, surfaced 2026-06-26 while deciding how to "integrate assay."

## Why this exists
assay (the doc-coverage research tool) computes two directions:
- **staleness** = doc refs with no matching code entity → this is already `drift_doc_dead_symbol_reference` (mache-fa12b3). DUPLICATE; mache's deterministic rule supersedes assay's fuzzy version.
- **coverage** = code entities with no doc reference (undocumented exports) → the INVERSE direction. NOT yet expressed by any drift_doc_* rule. THIS bead.

assay's coverage % (|C∩D|/|C|) was characterized by the user (ADR-0018) as "hard to falsify." The fix is to make it falsifiable: instead of a fuzzy ratio, emit one finding per undocumented exported symbol with a real location — `mypackage.Foo (exported) appears in no markdown backtick reference`.

## Spec
For every exported entry in `node_defs` (Go: name starts uppercase; generalize per lang later), assert at least one markdown backtick token (the same token projection mache-fa12b3 builds) references it. Violations = undocumented exports, severity `warn` (default; opt-in `error` for libraries that gate on public-API docs).

## Implementation notes
- Pure SQL over `node_defs` (defs) LEFT JOIN the markdown-token projection from mache-fa12b3. No CGO, no tree-sitter, no --from-db — mache already produces both sides.
- Reuse the `v_loc` join (mache-ae54d8) so findings carry file:line of the *definition*.
- Allowlist hook (e.g. `.mache/doc-coverage.toml`) for symbols intentionally undocumented (generated code, internal-by-convention exports).

## Provenance
This is the one falsifiable idea worth porting OUT of assay. Everything else assay does deterministically is already owned by ADR-0018; everything else it does fuzzily (Jaccard/trigram/embeddings) stays in assay as the deferred semantic frontier (assay-dk6.4). See the assay↔mache convergence decision bead in this decade.

title: [decision] assay ↔ mache convergence: falsifiable doc-coverage lands in mache as drift_doc_* rules; assay keeps the deterministic-graph + semantic frontier
description:
Decision of record, 2026-06-26. Triggered by "peep ../assay and integrate it here."

## The question
How to "integrate assay" (a doc-coverage verifier: tree-sitter-extract code entities + markdown doc refs → coverage/staleness set math) into mache. Surfaced a deeper architecture conflict (user): "assay should roll into mache" vs "mache is massive — monorepo waiting to happen."

## What the investigation found
1. assay re-links `smacker/go-tree-sitter` (CGO) to extract Go entities — re-deriving exactly what ley-line already parses into the `.db` (`_ast`, `nodes`, `_lsp_hover`). That duplicates the substrate the ecosystem just spent CGO-removal effort consolidating (ADR-0012, the `mache-pure-go-arena` decade).
2. mache **already owns** the falsifiable side of this domain: ADR-0018 (Accepted) promotes `find_smells` into the doc-drift workflow, and `drift_doc_dead_symbol_reference` IS assay's staleness check, deterministically. ADR-0018 explicitly names assay as "coverage-based, fuzzy, hard to falsify" and scopes the soft/semantic story OUT.
3. The drift_doc_* rules are registered as v1 placeholders (cmd/smell_rules.go:882) with implementation beads already filed (mache-fa12b3 / fa569a / faacf3) — they were just floating (no thread). Now grouped under decade `0018-doc-drift-executable-specs`.

## Decision
- **Do NOT** build `assay --from-db`, a `verify_docs` MCP shell-out, or an SDK extraction. None needed.
- **Port assay's ONE falsifiable contribution** — the coverage direction (undocumented exports) — into mache as `drift_doc_undocumented_export` (mache-1bdc95). assay's staleness is already mache-fa12b3.
- **assay stays a separate repo** (user: "keep as-is, decide later") for the work mache deliberately does NOT do:
  - the deterministic artifact/usage-graph redesign (rosary decade `deterministic-artifact-usage-graph`, assay-spec),
  - the semantic/experimental frontier: MiniLM↔HDC dual-readout matching (assay-dk6.4) and HTML/DOM claim extraction (assay-dk6.2).
- Repo topology is NOT the axis that matters (monorepo_polyrepo_isomorphism): the `.db` is already the federation seam (ADR-0014). New *analyses* are smell rules / consumers of that seam, not new subsystems. assay earns independence only via the semantic + deterministic-graph paradigms the find_smells substrate can't express today.

## Why this resolves the conflict
"Roll into mache" → YES for the falsifiable part (one rule, zero new infra). "mache is massive" → NO new subsystem added. assay shrinks to its genuinely-novel core.

## Cross-refs
- mache: ADR-0018 amended with a dated "Relationship to assay" section (this session).
- assay beads: assay-dk6.4, assay-dk6.2 (deferred; the retained frontier).
- assay redesign: rosary decade `deterministic-artifact-usage-graph` (8 threads incl. `drift-fallback`).
- Open follow-up (NOT decided here): whether assay's deterministic graph consumes ley-line's `.db`/arena rather than its own CGO tree-sitter — same architectural argument, tracked separately if assay-the-repo proceeds.

comments.text:
Sharpened rationale (session 2026-07-01, user): the language-agnostic angle makes the "roll assay into mache" question crisper. assay is Go-only (smacker/go-tree-sitter/golang, `filepath.Ext(path) != ".go"`) and reimplements its own graph traversal/entity extraction — which is *why* it can't be agnostic: it re-parses per-language instead of reading ley-line's already-multi-language `.db`. The decision here holds and the mechanism is the reason it's correct: the falsifiable coverage direction folds into mache as drift_doc_* rules (mache-1bdc95 coverage + mache-fa12b3 staleness) that are agnostic *because* they consume the .db arena.

The one item this decision explicitly left untracked — "whether assay's deterministic graph consumes ley-line's .db/arena rather than its own CGO tree-sitter" — is now filed as an assay-repo bead (Language-agnostic extraction: consume ley-line `.db` instead of Go-only smacker/go-tree-sitter). It's routed to assay (not mache) because it's assay's retained deterministic-graph frontier, gated on assay-the-repo proceeding. Cross-ref kept in that bead's description.

title: Self-referential schema pipeline — read nodes table as data source
description:
Allow mache to read its own --out SQLite output as a data source for another schema. This enables composable schema pipelines where Stage 1 normalizes/reshapes data and Stage 2 projects into a target format.

## The gap
mache reads .db files expecting a `results` table (id TEXT, record JSON). mache --out produces .db files with a `nodes` table (id, parent_id, name, kind, size, mtime, record). Different shapes.

## Proposed fix
Add a nodes-table loader path in ingestSQLiteDB that detects whether the .db has a `results` table (current path) or a `nodes` table (self-referential path). For nodes-table input, each file node (kind=0) becomes a record with its path as id and content as the record JSON.

## Why
- Enables venturi.db → normalize schema → intermediate.db → trivy-layout schema → trivy.db
- General composability: any mache output becomes valid mache input
- Eliminates need for per-format Go post-processors (trivy, osv, grype can all be pure schemas)
- The trivy-db projection (mache-1094a2) is the first consumer

## Design notes
- Detection: check for `results` table first (existing path), fall back to `nodes` table
- For nodes input: reconstruct the record from node content + path hierarchy, or just pass the record column through as-is
- Schema selectors work on the JSON record, so the intermediate format needs to produce queryable JSON

comments.text:
Closing as **obsolete** 2026-05-11 — superseded by the bundle deployment model.

## Why this is no longer applicable

This bead was filed 2026-04-27, anticipating a deployment where mache might be its own perimeter (raw `mache serve --http :PORT` exposed externally, doing X.509 / WIMSE verification at the request boundary).

Two things landed since that make the bead's premise wrong:

1. **Cloister ADR-0005 amendment (2026-04-30)** — codifies that the in-pod cloister↔companion↔mache wire is **IPC, not network**. Quote: "AEAD on a loopback hop within a trust boundary is ceremony, not security." Auth lives at cloister-router (the perimeter) where bytes actually traverse a network. Mache, sitting behind cloister inside the same pod, trusts every UDS peer because the pod boundary + filesystem ACL already authenticated them.

2. **Bundle deployment model shipped (PR #370, 2026-05-11)** — mache now ships as a distroless OCI image (`mache:0.8.0` via in-repo apko + melange). The image IS the deployment unit. Cloister deploys it into a pod where mache is unreachable except via the cloister-mediated UDS. "Raw mache exposed to the internet" is not a sanctioned deployment mode going forward.

## Trust layout (canonical)

```
[external traffic] → cloister-router  [auth terminates HERE — WIT / bridge cert / whatever]
                            ↓
                    cloister-companion  [in-pod, plain capnp, IPC trust]
                            ↓
                          mache         [in-pod UDS, plain capnp, NO auth]
```

## What about `mache serve --http :PORT` for local dev?

Stays. It's loopback / laptop usage with no production exposure. If anyone deploys it exposed to the internet, they put a reverse proxy with auth in front — same pattern as nginx + a backend service. That's a deployer concern, not a mache concern.

## Refs

- cloister/docs/adr/0005-internal-wire-leyline-net.md — see "Amendment 2026-04-30 — cloister↔companion is IPC, not network wire"
- mache PR #370 — bundle (apko + melange) shipping
- mache-172a50 (closed) — the image work that made the bundle real

Don't re-open. If a future deployment surfaces a real need for mache-side perimeter auth, file a fresh bead with the specific deployment context.

title: duplicate_definitions (+ dead_code) false-positive on Rust impl/trait methods — method-exclusion is Go-schema-specific (methods/)
description:
The duplicate_definitions rule deliberately excludes methods (node_id NOT LIKE '%/methods/%' / 'methods/%') — its own description explains this is to stop 'every interface method implemented by N types colliding as a duplicate on the bare token.' That exclusion assumes the Go schema, which registers methods under methods/. The leyline RUST parser does NOT categorize impl-block methods or trait methods under methods/ (they land under functions/ or an impl path), so the exclusion misses them and Rust impl/trait methods get flagged — the exact false-positive the rule was written to prevent, now for Rust.

REPRO (rosary src/context/, a fresh module, clean under rustc + clippy -D warnings): 'mache build . db && mache find-smells --db db --rule duplicate_definitions' flags:
- policy.rs: hot_count x3 (PruningPolicy trait signature + TiersPolicy impl + RecencyPolicy impl) — a normal Rust trait+impl family, not duplication;
- ref_store.rs / envelope.rs: conventional new / render impl methods, sharing tokens with the ~dozens of other ::new/::render across the codebase.
Net: 11 spurious duplicate_definitions the compiler disagrees with; forced a baseline bump in rosary (docs/smell-baseline.json).

Same root likely affects dead_code and untested_function (they share the methods/ skip assumption, per the rule comments referencing PRs #234/#239).

FIX OPTIONS:
(a) leyline (ley-line-open) Rust parser: categorize impl-block + trait methods under methods/ like Go — one fix corrects every method-aware rule at once (preferred, seam-correct);
(b) mache rule-side: extend the exclusion to also match the Rust impl-method node_id shape (functions/ under an impl/ ancestor, or a trait-method signature node).

IMPACT: every Rust consumer with traits/impls (rosary, ley-line-open itself) accrues false duplicate_definitions/dead_code baseline entries, eroding the ratchet's signal. Filed from the rosary warm-resume work (rosary-dd5828).

comments.text:
FIX in PR #505 (branch fix/mache-22fecf-rust-method-falsepos, commit 78dc300).

ROOT CAUSE (ground truth from `leyline parse` of a 2-struct/1-trait Rust file): leyline's Rust node_defs render method tokens BARE (`new`, `compute`, `run` — no receiver) and file them under `impl_item_N/declaration_list/function_item_M` (and trait sigs under `trait_item/.../function_signature_item`) — NO `methods/` segment. So same-named methods across N impls collide by token, and the rule's `node_id NOT LIKE '%/methods/%'` exclusion never matches → 7 false positives reproduced empirically.

DEAD_CODE FINDING (differs from the bead's premise): I could NOT reproduce a dead_code false-positive on leyline-Rust. dead_code is INERT there — leyline leaves `source_file` empty on Rust nodes, so the `source_file != ''` filter drops every row (duplicate_definitions escapes this because enrichLocations backfills the file from _ast after the WHERE). So dead_code on leyline-Rust is a COVERAGE GAP (misses real dead code like an uncalled `never_called`), not a false-positive. Distinct issue — worth its own bead if we want dead_code to work on leyline projections (needs source_file resolution from _ast, or leyline to populate nodes.source_file). Latent secondary risk: if source_file WERE populated, the `types/`/`constants/` exclusions also wouldn't match Rust `struct_item`/`const_item` → struct false-positives. Both fold into the per-language-kind-mapping thesis (mache-463612).

This PR scopes to the reproduced duplicate_definitions bug per systematic-debugging discipline (fix what's reproduced + tested).

title: Incremental / content-addressed rule evaluation: node_hash memoization + sheaf-region recompute (the merkle+sheaf cash-out)
description:
The optimization that content-addressing + sheaves were built to enable, and mache isn't yet cashing in: rules currently do a FULL SCAN every run (bench: cyclomatic_complexity 181ms @10k defs, dead_code 92ms @10k — the steep ones). Exploit the two substrates shipped 2026-07-08 to make rule eval incremental + memoized.

## This is not a new problem — prior art to lean on
- Salsa (rust-analyzer's demand-driven, input-memoized recompute engine) — the canonical shape for code-intel over a content-addressed graph.
- Differential dataflow / Datalog incremental view maintenance — and mache's rules ARE SQL SELECTs, the friendliest IVM case.
- Bazel/Buck action caching (content-hash = cache key).

## The two ingredients (already in the tree)
1. node_hash = a memoization key. Rules that are a PURE FUNCTION OF A SUBTREE memoize by node_hash: identical subtrees compute ONCE; an edit only recomputes subtrees whose hash CHANGED. Poster child = cyclomatic_complexity (the steepest bench) — cyclomatic complexity is a pure function of a function's AST subtree. Also long_function, god_file, per-construct dead_code.
2. Sheaf current_root + generation (in the daemon.sheaf.invalidate payload, mache-e4c4ea) = per-region cache keys. Recompute only regions whose current_root moved; keep cached results for the rest. A "sub-DAG" = a region's induced subgraph; scope rule eval to it.

## Honest caveat — locality is a PER-RULE property
Aggregate/cross-cutting rules (fan_out_skew, duplicate_definitions, cross-file dead_code) need graph-global reasoning and don't memoize cleanly. So classify each rule: pure-subtree / region-local / global. THE HOOK: the SmellRule contract (mache-e0748c) is where a rule DECLARES its locality, and the engine picks the memoization strategy from that field.

## Phased path (cheapest-first)
1. node_hash result memoization for `locality: pure-subtree` rules — NO sheaf dependency; cache keyed by (rule_id, node_hash) in an LRU or the .db; kills recompute on unchanged/duplicated subtrees; directly targets the cyclomatic/long_function/god_file benches.
2. Region-scoped incremental via sheaf current_root/generation (rides mache-e4c4ea) — recompute only changed local sections.
3. Rule-locality field in the SmellRule contract (mache-e0748c) drives which rule gets which treatment.

Links: merkle node_hash work (v0.15.0/v0.16.0), mache-e4c4ea (sheaf region invalidation), mache-e0748c (rule contract / locality field), mache-b0b979 (rules-as-data). Evidence: the Go bench suite (cyclomatic 181ms@10k, dead_code 92ms@10k).

A DIFFERENTIAL ORACLE test asserting `incremental(edits) == full_scan` — BYTE-IDENTICAL findings — for every memoized rule, across:
  (a) random edit sequences applied to a fixture db;
  (b) dbs with DUPLICATED subtrees (one node_hash appearing N× — proves cache-hit correctness + dedup);
  (c) region-level invalidation driven by synthetic daemon.sheaf.invalidate events (proves the sheaf invalidation set is consumed correctly).
ANY divergence = an invalidation/locality bug → test FAILS.

Why this is sufficient (answers "cache invalidation is hard"): the node_hash / region current_root key is SOUND BY CONSTRUCTION — a BLAKE3 content address IS the complete dependency set for a pure-subtree/region-local rule (same hash ⟹ same content ⟹ same result). So there's no hand-rolled dependency graph to get wrong. The ONLY residual risk is a rule MIS-CLASSIFIED as local (depends on something outside the addressed content), and the oracle catches exactly that. The sheaf is consumed as the AUTHORITATIVE invalidation set, not derived — removing the classic missed-dependency failure mode. Same falsifiable-differential discipline as the smell-rule externalization (byte-identical vs baseline) + the determinism test (40× identical).

Test lives in cmd/smell_findings_incremental_test.go (added to test_files). Phase-1 (node_hash memo on cyclomatic_complexity, no sheaf dep) must pass the oracle + show sub-linear re-run on an unchanged/duplicated tree vs full-scan.

comments.text:
PHASE-1 STARTED (2026-07-09) — branch `feat/mache-238673-incremental-cyclomatic` off main (v0.16.2+2).

Scope: node_hash memoization on `cyclomatic_complexity` only. NO sheaf dep.

Design (confirmed against code):
- `cyclomatic_complexity` metric = COUNT of control-flow descendant `_ast` nodes under each function (`branch.node_id LIKE fn.node_id||'/%'`, kinds if/for/case/select-case). This is a PURE-SUBTREE rule: the metric is fully determined by the function subtree content = its merkle `node_hash` (written onto `_ast` by the LLO producer per mache-ff9a9d). Same node_hash ⟹ byte-identical subtree ⟹ identical metric. Sound by construction — no hand-rolled dep graph.
- Memo = in-process `map[nodeHashHex]int64`. Compute metric once per DISTINCT node_hash, fan out to every occurrence (per-occurrence start_byte/row/col preserved — only `metric` is memoized). Caller holds the memo across runs → unchanged/duplicated subtrees are cache hits (sub-linear re-run).
- Output must be BYTE-IDENTICAL to the current full-scan `runSmellRule`, including the `ORDER BY metric DESC, source_id, start_byte`.

TDD: differential oracle test FIRST in cmd/smell_findings_incremental_test.go —
  (a) random edit sequences: memoized(db) == full_scan(db) byte-identical;
  (b) duplicated subtrees (one node_hash at N occurrences): cache-hit correctness + dedup, all N occurrences surface.
  (c) sheaf region-invalidation is DEFERRED (needs sheaf dep; phase-2).
Plus a bench (cmd/find_smells_bench_test.go) showing sub-linear re-run on an unchanged/duplicated tree vs full-scan.

comments.text:
CDC IS THE MISSING THIRD PIECE, AND IT JUST SHIPPED — but not in the artifact mache reads. Measured 2026-07-29 against LLO v0.13.0.

## LLO names mache as the intended consumer

v0.13.0's changelog for `ley-line-open-f8ebe7` (incremental re-chunk: "a small edit no longer re-hashes the entire file") states verbatim: "load-bearing for sub-file consumers (LL wire CDC, **mache dataflow**)." So the upstream intent that mache consumes chunk-granular content is explicit, not inferred.

## But CDC is not in mache's .db, and it is not a flag away

- CDC content storage lives in `leyline-fs` (`rs/ll-open/fs/src/chunked.rs`), behind a **non-default** cargo feature: `default = ["validate", "fuse", "nfs"]` — `cdc` is opt-in ("Opt-in so the lean mount build is unchanged").
- It creates `content_chunks`, `content_manifest`, `content_manifest_meta`, `content_generation`.
- **Verified by direct query against a v0.13.0 `leyline parse` output: none of those tables exist.** mache's .db has nodes/_source/_ast/node_refs/node_defs/_imports/node_content/node_child/capnp_blobs/_ast_pointer/source_blobs/query_blobs/_queries/_file_index/_meta — no chunk manifest.
- `leyline-fs` is also the crate mache removed its FFI binding to (ADR-0012 status note), since mache uses its own NFS backend.

So enabling CDC for mache is not a feature flag: it requires either `leyline parse` emitting chunk manifests into the .db, or mache consuming the arena/graph path. That is a cross-repo design question, not a mache-side toggle.

## Read-paging is NOT the payoff — measured

CDC params (`rs/ll-open/cdc/src/lib.rs`): MIN_CHUNK 8 KiB, MAX 128 KiB, expected ~72 KiB.

From mache's own token-bench baseline (regenerated this session, v0.13.0 producer, docs/benchmarks/token-efficiency-baseline.json): arm_a_avg (whole file, cat -n charged) 9,221 B ≈ 7.8 KB raw; arm_b_avg (construct-granular) 731 B; median_file_lines 160.

- The average mache source file is at or BELOW one minimum chunk → chunk-paging is a no-op for whole-file reads on this corpus.
- A construct read (731 B) is ~100x smaller than one expected chunk (72 KiB) → paging by chunk would be strictly WORSE than the current PK-lookup-per-record content resolution.

CAVEAT, flagged deliberately because this exact error recurred several times this session: the above is mache's OWN repo. Corpora with large generated/vendored files (or non-source projections) could invert this. Any decision here must re-measure on the target corpus, and must state WHICH projection it measured (schema projection vs leyline-native) — that distinction produced four wrong conclusions this session.

## What this means for THIS bead

The payoff is incremental invalidation, not read bandwidth — which is exactly this bead's thesis. CDC's contribution is that content-defined boundaries are *stable under edits elsewhere in the stream* (a boundary is a pure function of the bytes from that chunk's own start), so sub-file identity survives an unrelated edit. That is what makes "recompute only the changed region" exact rather than approximate — the same property this bead already relies on node_hash for at construct granularity, extended BELOW the construct.

Concretely for the Phase-1 acceptance criteria here: node_hash memoization already gives recompute-avoidance for unchanged/duplicated subtrees. CDC would extend that to files whose constructs shift byte offsets without changing content (the case where every node_hash is stable but naive offset-keyed caching invalidates everything). Worth confirming whether that case is actually material before building for it — mache's ShiftOrigins path may already handle it.

Related: mache-463612 (analysis-as-substrate-query, the coverage+lint half of the same thesis).
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: A design note/ADR that: (1) defines the rule-locality taxonomy (pure-subtree / region-local / global) and how it maps to memoization strategy; (2) specifies the node_hash result cache (key, storage, invalidation) and the sheaf-region incremental path (current_root/generation); (3) ships a PHASE-1 prototype — node_hash memoization for one pure-subtree rule (cyclomatic_complexity), with a benchmark showing recompute-avoidance on unchanged/duplicated subtrees vs the current full-scan (target: sub-linear on re-run of an unchanged tree). Behavior identical to the non-memoized path (same findings).

title: perf: find_definition allocates O(N) per call due to DefsMap snapshot copy
description:
Surfaced by find_definition benchmarks landed in PR #220. AnchoredExact at defs=10K shows 405µs / 950 KB / 10K allocs per call — the underlying map lookup is O(1) but the handler obtains the defs map via dp.DefsMap() which returns a fresh copy of the entire token → []dirID map every call. Same shape on NotFound (snapshot cost dominates the cold path).

Not a regression — pre-existing behavior of MemoryStore.DefsMap(). Worth fixing if find_definition becomes hot in real usage. Three implementation options:

1. Stable read-only view: return a Read-only DefsMap interface that exposes Lookup(token) []string and ForEach(callback). No snapshot, no copy.
2. Snapshot-on-write with versioned reader: track a generation counter; readers cache against the current generation.
3. Direct Lookup method on Graph: dp.LookupDef(token) []string. Skips the map-copy entirely for the common case where a handler only needs one token.

Option 3 is the smallest change and fits the access pattern (handlers always look up a specific token, never iterate the full map). The fuzzy + case-insensitive paths still need iteration, so they'd keep DefsMap() for compat — only the anchored case-sensitive path benefits.

Not blocking; file as P3 perf backlog.

title: Untangle write-time validation: separate formatting from diagnostics
description: mache's write_file has write-time validation for some languages, but formatting is bundled with diagnostics. Formatting should be the LLM's responsibility (or pre-commit's), not mache's. Separate so mache write-time validation is purely structural/type diagnostics, and formatting lives in the pre-commit layer or is expected from the LLM. This makes the validation layers clean: mache = type errors + diagnostics (ms), pre-commit = formatting + linting (seconds), CI = full suite (minutes).

title: Define + implement mache↔llo IPC wire (client-side)
description:
Filed 2026-05-10. Surfaced during deployment-readiness audit (mache-172a50 work). User clarified: **mache communicates via IPC to LLO** — this is the real cluster-critical wire on mache's side, separate from the cloister↔mache serve surface.

## What needs to happen

mache should consume llo's IPC socket as a client to get memory-arena / userspace-projection access. Today's `cmd/serve.go` has `--http` and `--stdio` only (per audit of `mache-172a50`); there's no llo-client-socket flag, no capnp IPC client code, and no documented contract for what mache asks llo for over that wire.

## Open questions to resolve first

1. **What does mache need from llo?** Memory arena allocation? File-system projection reads? Both? Something else?
2. **Wire format**: capnp ToolCall (matching ADR-0005's cluster-internal wire convention)? Or a tighter custom message set just for mache↔llo?
3. **Socket path convention**: `/run/cloister-uds/llo.sock` (so llo's bundle in cluster.capnp publishes there)? Or a mache-private socket?
4. **Failure mode**: if llo is unreachable, does mache degrade gracefully (in-process fallback) or hard-fail?

## Scope

1. Decide the contract (probably an ADR in cloister/docs/adr/ or mache/docs/adr/ — whichever owns the cross-repo wire).
2. Add `--llo-socket <path>` flag to `mache serve` (or whatever the consensus flag name is).
3. Implement a capnp IPC client in mache's serve path.
4. Add an integration test that mocks an llo server and verifies mache's behavior.
5. Wire it into apko.yaml so the cluster.capnp launch args set the right socket path.

## Cross-repo context

- llo's MCP server today is HTTP-only on `:8384` (per ley-line-open-17739e audit). For mache↔llo IPC, llo will need its own UDS server-side counterpart — file a sibling bead in llo for that.
- cloister ADR-0005 specifies capnp ToolCall over UDS as the cluster-internal wire convention.
- `mache-172a50` (this bead's parent) shipped image scaffolding; this is the wire substance.

## Dependencies

- Probably depends on the cloister ADR amendment that names this contract.
- llo-side serve work is a sibling bead (TBD).

comments.text:
Closed 2026-05-10. This design bead is fully obsoleted — the schema it asked about already existed.

`daemon.capnp` (file ID `@0xa1b2c3d4e5f60001`) was authored long before this bead was filed and lives authoritatively at `~/remotes/art/ley-line-open/rs/ll-core/public-schema/capnp/daemon.capnp`. It defines every op the bead's "open questions" enumerated: ListChildren, ReadContent, FindCallers, FindDefs, GetNode, Query, Subscribe, Load, plus arena info via Status.

The remaining work (consumption pattern + Go bindings) was scoped through:
- `ley-line-open-41867b` — publish clients/go/leyline-schema as v0.2.1 (LANDED)
- `mache-3bf414` — replace mache's forked .capnp with import-from-LLO (LANDED)
- `mache-98aa97` — UDS query proxy (the actual implementation; still open, but the design questions this bead asked are answered)

No new ADR was needed; cloister ADR-0005 + LLO ADR-0014 + mache ADR-0014 already framed the constellation.

title: cache:sync / cache:restore / serve:remote Taskfile targets — mache↔cloister cache loop (blocked on cloister-f193d3)
description:
Salvage the one useful commit off the stale local branch feat/cache-sync-targets (commit 29c7369): Taskfile targets wiring the local-first mache↔cloister OCI build-cache loop.

- `cache:sync`: build a mache db from source and cache-push it to $REGISTRY under <REPO>/<COMMIT>.
- `cache:restore`: pull a repo's db from $REGISTRY into ./.mache/restored.db (no local build).
- `serve:remote`: cache:restore then `mache serve` on the restored db (thin consumer wrapper).

Verified end-to-end against a local cloister registry (docker cloister:0.1.0, localhost:8787) when authored.

## Why it's parked
The commit uses `--max-blob-bytes 2000000` on the push — that's the client-side skip we're REMOVING (proven broken; superseded by cloister's storage-layer BlobStore splitting, cloister-f193d3). So this target is BLOCKED on cloister-f193d3: once cloister splits oversized blobs across DO-SQLite rows, drop the `--max-blob-bytes` flag from cache:sync and land the targets clean off current main.

## To land
1. Wait for cloister-f193d3 (BlobStore blob splitting).
2. Cherry-pick 29c7369's Taskfile targets onto fresh main, DROP the `--max-blob-bytes` flag (cloister handles it).
3. Drop the stale branch feat/cache-sync-targets (its other 2 commits — 735658b broken skip, 277d508 old OCI spec — are already superseded/merged).
4. Add a smoke test or doc for the loop.

The full authored target text is in commit 29c7369 on the local branch feat/cache-sync-targets (not pushed) for reference.

title: mache serve: add --ipc-socket + capnp ToolCall framing per ADR-0005
description:
Filed 2026-05-10. Surfaced during mache-172a50 audit.

## What needs to happen

cloister's `cluster.capnp` declares mache's bundle launch as `args = ["serve", "--ipc-socket", "/run/cloister-uds/mache.sock"]`. Today's `mache serve` exposes only `--http <addr>` and `--stdio` — there is no `--ipc-socket` flag and no capnp ToolCall framing on the wire. cluster.capnp will fail to start the mache bundle as written.

## Scope

1. Add `--ipc-socket <path>` flag to `cmd/serve.go`.
2. Implement a UDS listener at that path.
3. Frame the wire as capnp `ToolCall` / `ToolResult` messages per `/Users/jamesgardner/remotes/art/cloister/docs/adr/0005-internal-wire-leyline-net.md`.
4. The capnp schema for ToolCall lives in `/Users/jamesgardner/remotes/art/cloister/wire/cloister.capnp` — generate Go bindings and use them.
5. Map mache's existing MCP tool set (the 11 tools the stdio mode advertises) onto the capnp ToolCall surface.
6. Integration test: spawn the binary with `--ipc-socket /tmp/test.sock`, send a capnp ToolCall via a small test harness, verify the response.

## Acceptance

- `mache serve --ipc-socket /tmp/X.sock` binds to that path.
- A capnp ToolCall request reaches the same tool dispatch path that stdio MCP uses.
- cloister-router can talk to a containerized mache via cluster.capnp launch args.
- Existing `--http` and `--stdio` modes still work (non-regression).

## Out of scope

- The mache↔llo wire (separate bead).
- Changing mache's tool surface itself.

Same pattern as the LLO 0.2.1 dance we just completed (mache-3bf414 ↔ ley-line-open-41867b).

**Order:**
1. cloister tags `clients/go/cloister-schema/v0.1.0` (or whatever version policy fits).
2. mache adds `require github.com/agentic-research/cloister/clients/go/cloister-schema vX.Y.Z` to `go.mod`.

Do not start this bead before step 1 lands; otherwise we'd re-introduce exactly the fork pattern `mache-3bf414` just removed.

title: Adopt entire-graph's fixed-answer accuracy benchmark (283 tasks / 21 repos) for mache
description:
Source: https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph (MIT, Go). Its README publishes a benchmark mache should adopt rather than invent.

METHODOLOGY (verbatim): 'Fixed-answer semantic tasks (definition lookup, call graph, imports, change-impact) on real checkouts, scored as correctness counts.'
Reported: entire-graph 265/283 (94%) on 21 repos multi-language; codebase-memory-mcp 191/283 (68%) on the same corpus.

WHY THIS BEATS THE ARENA (mache-b7ec42):
- Fixed answers scored as counts => objective and reproducible. The Arena is a 6-level agent benchmark whose scoring depends on an LLM's behavior, and its harness is currently rotted (assumes a flat mount layout that no longer matches).
- The four task types map 1:1 onto shipped MCP tools: find_definition, find_callers/find_callees, the imports projection, get_impact.
- It is a THIRD-PARTY task set. Publishing a self-designed benchmark invites the obvious objection; scoring on someone else's removes it.

WHAT MACHE ALREADY HAS: testdata/snapshots/manifest.toml plus tools/fixtures-snapshot already curate external repos into the tree with recorded upstream SHAs. That is the fixture half of this harness.

OPEN QUESTIONS:
- The 283 tasks do not appear to be published in the repo (only the score). Either derive an equivalent task set and say so plainly, or ask upstream. Do NOT report a number against a corpus we reconstructed and imply parity with theirs - that is exactly the false-precision trap.
- Scoring must distinguish wrong from unsupported. entire-graph's stated limitation is that CALLS is heuristic; mache's fidelity ordering (mention subset-of binding subset-of reachability, ADR-0013) means mache can report WHICH guarantee a hit carries. A benchmark that scores only correct/incorrect discards that, and it is mache's main differentiator.

comments.text:
RECON: the 283-task accuracy corpus is NOT in the repo. The caveat in this bead's description stands, and hardens.

Cloned entire-graph and searched: bench/ contains only the THROUGHPUT harness (repos.json / repos.fast.json / repos.lock.json / README). There are no eval, task, or accuracy fixtures anywhere in the tree. The 265/283 (94%) and codebase-memory-mcp 191/283 (68%) figures are published as results with no published task set.

CONSEQUENCE: mache cannot score on their corpus. Any number we produce comes from a task set we author, which means:
- Do NOT present a mache score alongside their 94% as if comparable. Different corpora, and ours would be self-authored — the exact bias their number also carries, which is worth stating plainly rather than exploiting.
- The honest framing is 'mache scores X on a task set we designed and published' with the tasks committed so a reader can check them. Publishing the corpus is the part that makes the number mean anything, and is the thing they did not do.

Their methodology line is still worth adopting verbatim as a design constraint: 'Fixed-answer semantic tasks (definition lookup, call graph, imports, change-impact) on real checkouts, scored as correctness counts.' Fixed answers + counts is the discipline; the specific tasks are ours to build.

Related: mache-543943 CAN reuse their corpus, since the throughput bench pins are published (repos.lock.json). Accuracy cannot. Worth splitting expectations accordingly.
comments.author: rsry-cli

comments.text: Codex recon 2026-07-23: public clone confirms the README claim only as prose: 265/283 (94%) vs 191/283 (68%) appears in README, but a search of the scratchpad clone found no published fixed-answer task board, answer file, scoring harness, or 21-repo task corpus. The published harness is performance/quality telemetry, not the 283-task accuracy board. Treat any mache number here as self-authored unless upstream publishes tasks or we clearly label a reconstructed corpus.
comments.author: rsry-cli

comments.text: Upstream clarification from current entire-graph main (2026-07-24): the public repo still publishes only the aggregate 265/283 fixed-answer accuracy claim. Its AGENTS.md explicitly points methodology/prompts/caveats to the private graphmark repo. Therefore exact adoption of “their 283 tasks” is currently impossible from public artifacts; this bead must remain a clean-room equivalent or wait for upstream disclosure, and results must not be labeled GraphMark-parity. Also distinct: GraphMark reportedly contains an agent-level SWE-bench Multilingual token-efficiency experiment; that is now tracked separately as mache-ee4216 rather than mixing agent outcomes into this fixed-answer correctness bead.
