title: R2 StorageBackend implementation
description: Implement GraphStore interface for Cloudflare R2. Key format: graphs/{repo-hash}/graph.db (zstd-compressed). Uses S3-compatible API via aws-sdk-go-v2. Debounced writes (caller responsibility — ADR-0010 specifies 30s quiet period + 5min max delay). Needed for Phase 1 of hosted mache (persistent cached graphs).

comments.text:
**Absorbed mache-d45da8 and mache-ae2432** (both closed as duplicates). They were chained `ae2432 → d45da8 → 2f0075`, but reading all three in full, the upper two restate one another rather than adding layers — `d45da8` itself notes "Relates to: mache-ae2432 (persistent mode)", and both independently specify BYO-R2 buckets and incremental-via-tropo delta. This bead is the only one with an implementable spec, so it survives. Recording everything from the other two that isn't already here:

## Economics (from d45da8)
- **Read path:** download SQLite from R2 → query locally → cache. Egress is free on R2 — that's the whole reason R2 beats S3/GCS here.
- **Write path:** project graph → upload. ~$4.50/M writes, and writes are infrequent (only on repo change).
- This pricing asymmetry is the argument for the download-and-query-locally design over querying remotely.

## Incremental projection (both)
Only re-project changed files; tropo provides the delta. Upload the diff, not the whole file. Both beads called this out independently, so treat it as a requirement rather than a nice-to-have.

## BYO-R2 productization (from ae2432)
- User supplies bucket URL + credentials; **credentials live in rig KV**.
- Benefits over ephemeral mode: no re-clone per session (seconds vs minutes on large repos), incremental projection, cross-session context (an agent can reference prior graph state), and ley-line's arena can share the same bucket.

## ⚠️ Key-format disagreement — needs a decision
The two beads specify **different** layouts:

| Source | Key |
|---|---|
| this bead | `graphs/{repo-hash}/graph.db` (zstd-compressed) |
| mache-ae2432 | `r2://{bucket}/mache/{repo}/graph.db` |

Repo-hash vs repo-name is a real fork: hashing avoids name collisions and leaking repo names into keys, naming is greppable and human-debuggable. Nobody reconciled these. Resolve before implementing.

## External dependencies inherited
- `ley-line-598681` — BYO-R2 arena (ae2432 notes the arena can share the bucket)
- tropo — incremental delta pull
- ephemeral mode as the baseline

Related but deliberately NOT merged: mache-d44509 (D1 backend) and mache-d47057 (GCS backend) are distinct targets with different pricing and access models.

title: ci: SIGSEGV in CGO tree-sitter during internal/ingest tests on ubuntu-latest
description:
Hit this on PR #210 (a docs-only refactor). The internal/ingest test package crashed with 'SIGSEGV: segmentation violation, signal arrived during cgo execution' on the GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest runner. Re-run passed. Same flavor as the macOS FSEvents flake fixed in mache-1jin (PR #193) — different test, different cause, same merge-train-erosion problem.

Likely culprits:
- tree-sitter grammar memory unsafety under concurrent parser use (Engine has a worker pool)
- Race between parser destruction and walker callback under high concurrency
- A specific test that exercises a corner-case input

Need to:
1. Capture which test was running when SIGSEGV hit (full log: gh run view --log 25143860360 -j 73699390112)

title: coverage-gate: handle dissimilarity index N% as in-place rewrite, not new file
description:
When a file is rewritten in-place beyond the git similarity threshold, `git diff` emits `dissimilarity index N%` in the diff header but no `rename from/to` metadata. The coverage-gate diff parser (tools/coverage-gate) has no handling for this case — it treats the rewritten file as a brand-new file, flagging all its uncovered lines as new coverage debt.

Discovered during /evolve --simplify evaluation of sqlite_graph.go decomposition (branch evolve/simplify-sqlite-graph). The gate flagged 110 lines as uncovered in the rewritten sqlite_graph.go, but spot-checks of 3 line ranges confirmed they were uncovered on the base branch too — pre-existing error paths that simply moved.

This is the sibling issue to mache-e256f5 (which added rename detection via similarity threshold). The fix should:
1. Detect `dissimilarity index N%` in the diff parser (same place that detects `similarity index N%` for moves)
2. When dissimilarity is present, mark the file as an in-place rewrite of itself
3. Apply the same base-coverage fallback used for renamed files: don't report uncovered lines as new debt if they were also uncovered on the base

Files: tools/coverage-gate/main.go (diff parser + gate logic)

comments.text:
DUPLICATE of mache-e256f5 — same defect, same parser, same fix. Closing into it; the full in-place-rewrite case, its reproducer branch (`evolve/simplify-sqlite-graph`, 110 false positives), and the three-step fix shape are all recorded verbatim on mache-e256f5 so nothing is lost.

This bead already identified the relationship itself: "This is the sibling issue to mache-e256f5 (which added rename detection via similarity threshold)", and step 1 points at "the same place that detects `similarity index N%` for moves". Two git diff-header forms — `dissimilarity index N%` with no rename metadata vs `similarity index N%` with it — but one parser and one shared base-coverage fallback.

Corroboration worth noting: rosary's SharedScope auto-clusterer had independently grouped these two into `backlog/mache-e256f5-mache-301daf` on file-scope overlap alone. Two unrelated signals — shared file scope and a read of the descriptions — converged on the same pairing.

title: LSP enrichment broken: mache sends HTTP /mcp tools/call shape (op:tool/name:lsp) over UDS — daemon UDS speaks named position ops (lsp_hover/lsp_defs/lsp_refs)
description:
## CORRECTED root cause (my earlier "daemon lacks LSP" was WRONG)

The leyline release daemon DOES ship LSP (it's `--features lsp`, on by default; "headless/mount features not compiled" in the log refers to FUSE/NFS mount, NOT LSP). Verified directly against the running daemon's UDS dispatch:

```
{"op":"lsp_hover","file":...,"line":..,"col":..}  -> runs (errors only "no such table _lsp_hover" pre-enrichment)
{"op":"lsp_defs","file":...}                       -> "missing field `line`"  (op EXISTS, needs position)
{"op":"lsp_refs","symbol":"run"}                   -> "missing field `file`"   (op EXISTS)
{"op":"tool","name":"lsp","args":{...}}            -> "unknown op: tool"        ← what mache sends today
```

Authoritative contract (ley-line-open `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/mcp.rs:192-217`): the UDS dispatch exposes NAMED ops directly:
- `lsp_hover` / `lsp_defs` / `lsp_refs` — **position_schema: {file, line, col}** (auto-enrich lazily on first call)
- `lsp_symbols` / `lsp_diagnostics` — **file_schema: {file}**

The `{op:"tool", name, args}` MCP tools/call wrapping lives ONLY on the HTTP `/mcp` endpoint (`--mcp-port`, default 127.0.0.1:8384; `mcp.rs:769`), NOT on UDS.

## Two mache-side bugs

1. **Wrong wire shape over UDS.** `cmd/serve_lsp.go:149,286` → `client.Tool("lsp", {file})` builds `{op:"tool",name:"lsp",args}` (`internal/leyline/socket.go:508`). UDS doesn't have a `tool` dispatch — it wants the named op directly.
2. **Symbol vs position mismatch.** mache's tools are symbol-based (`get_type_info(symbol, file)`), but the LSP ops are POSITION-based (file, line, col). mache must resolve symbol → (file, line, col) from the parsed `_ast` node positions (start_row/start_col) before calling `lsp_hover`/`lsp_defs`/`lsp_refs` — OR use the file-based `lsp_symbols`/`lsp_diagnostics`. (Note this is in tension with mache-7d321e "never expose line/col to agents" — fine: mache resolves position INTERNALLY, never asks the agent for it.)

Also: there is NO `version` op in LLO — mache-8kif's version-assert-on-connect must use a different mechanism (or LLO adds one).

## Fix options
- **(A) UDS named ops** — keep the UDS client, change `Tool("lsp",…)` to `SendOp({op:"lsp_hover"|"lsp_defs"|"lsp_refs", file, line, col})` after resolving the symbol's position from `_ast`; use `{op:"lsp_diagnostics", file}` for get_diagnostics. Reuses existing transport.
- **(B) HTTP /mcp** — point LSP enrichment at the daemon's `--mcp-port` HTTP endpoint, where the tools/call shape mache already builds is valid. More transport plumbing.
Recommend (A): smaller, same socket, and position-resolution is needed either way for the symbol→hover mapping.

## Acceptance
get_type_info/get_diagnostics produce real LSP data against the running daemon on a Rust file (verified end-to-end on lectio); the `tool`/`name:lsp` shape is gone from the UDS path; mache fails loud+truthful when an op is genuinely unknown; mache-8kif reworked off the nonexistent `version` op. Unblocks the mache-9108a1 benchmark LSP tier.

comments.text:
## mache-side protocol fix COMPLETE + proven (PR #452)

Implemented the corrected vocabulary and verified end-to-end against the real leyline 0.5.1 daemon:
- `Client.Enrich(pass, files)` sends `{"op":"enrich","pass":"lsp","files":[...]}` (was the bogus `{"op":"tool",...}`).
- Daemon auto-spawned with `--source <root>` (SetDaemonSource ← served dir); op_enrich requires ctx.source_dir.
- File paths relativized to source.

**Proven:** serving lectio, `get_type_info(file=...)` spawns `leyline daemon ... --source /…/lectio`, the enrich op runs, and the LSP pass completes: `pass_name:lsp, files_processed:1, items_added:25`. No more "unknown op: tool".

## TWO REMAINING LLO-SIDE GAPS (for the LLO author) — block hover TEXT surfacing

Drilled past the protocol layer; `get_type_info` still returns "no hover info" because:

### 1. enrich LSP pass populates `_lsp` skeleton, not `_lsp_hover` / `detail`
After `{op:enrich,pass:lsp,files:[lib.rs]}` (items_added:25):
- `SELECT name FROM sqlite_master ... '_lsp%'` → `_lsp, _lsp_defs, _lsp_refs, _lsp_hover, _lsp_completions`.
- `SELECT * FROM _lsp LIMIT 2` → rows exist but are tree-sitter-derived skeleton: `{node_id: ".../line_comment_3/inner_doc_comment_marker", symbol_kind:"module", detail:"", diagnostics:"", start_line:""}`.
- `SELECT ... FROM _lsp WHERE detail != ''` → **0 rows**. `SELECT ... FROM _lsp_hover` → **0 rows**.
So the enrich pass does NOT populate hover text or `detail`. Hover appears to come only from the position-based `lsp_hover` op (live rust-analyzer request), not the `enrich pass=lsp`. Q for LLO: should `enrich pass=lsp` populate `_lsp_hover`/`_lsp.detail`, or is hover strictly the per-position `lsp_hover` op? If the latter, mache must resolve symbol→(file,line,col) and call `lsp_hover` per def.

### 2. `query` op serializes int64 columns as empty strings — blocks position reads
`SELECT a.source_id, a.start_row, a.start_col FROM _ast a JOIN node_defs d ... ` returns `start_row:"" start_col:""` (the int columns come back empty via the capnp-json codec — matches mache's own SendOp "silently zeros Int64" note). Consequently `{op:lsp_hover, file, line:"", col:""}` → `"invalid type: string \"\", expected u32"`. So even if mache wanted to drive the position-based `lsp_hover`, it cannot read positions from the daemon via the `query` op. Q for LLO: can the `query` op emit int64 as JSON numbers (or strings parseable as ints) so consumers can read positions? This blocks any position-based op driven off SQL results.

## Net
mache's wire protocol is fixed (PR #452). Full `get_type_info` hover output needs an LLO decision on (1) which table carries hover after enrich, and (2) the query-op int64 codec. mache-side follow-up (resolve symbol→position + call lsp_hover) is only viable once (2) is fixed.

comments.text:
## Re-test against the FULL fixed stack: leyline 0.5.3 (built from #119) + mache #453

```
enrich pass=lsp files=[crates/memory-core/src/lib.rs]
  passes: [..., {pass_name:lsp, items_added:25, duration_ms:639, skipped:[]}]
  _lsp_hover=0  _lsp_defs=0  _lsp_refs=0
  daemon log: "lsp: crates/memory-core/src/lib.rs — 25 symbols, 0 defs, 0 hovers, 0 refs"
```

### v0.5.3 outcome
- ✅ Skip-reason plumbing (EnrichmentStats.skipped through capnp + Go) WORKS — `skipped:[]` present in the response. Confirms rust-analyzer was NOT skipped.
- ❌ Hover/defs/refs still 0. Not a skip — rust-analyzer ran, returned 25 document symbols, and **0 hovers / 0 defs / 0 refs**.

### Sharpened root cause (rust-analyzer readiness race, LLO-side)
The lsp pass completes in **639ms**. rust-analyzer's `documentSymbol` is syntactic → instant (→ 25 symbols). But `hover`/`definition`/`references` require the **cargo project model** (`cargo metadata` + initial index), which takes seconds. So the pass requests hover/def/ref **before rust-analyzer finishes loading the workspace** → all empty. The 639ms duration is the tell: that's far too fast for a cold rust-analyzer workspace index.

Fix (LLO): the lsp pass must await rust-analyzer's project-model/index-ready signal (e.g. the `$/progress` "Indexing" end, `workspace/didChangeWatchedFiles` settle, or a `cargo check` completion) before issuing hover/def/ref. Symbols-only with 0 hover/def/ref is the canonical "asked too early" signature.

mache side is fully done and current (PR #452 protocol + #453 v0.5.3 bump & skip-reason surfacing). No further mache change needed — when the pass awaits readiness and emits hovers/defs/refs, mache's existing _lsp_hover/_lsp_defs/_lsp_refs query path lights up.

PR #500 subscribed to BOTH `sheaf.invalidate` (pre-v0.6 consumer-driven emit) AND `daemon.sheaf.invalidate` (v0.6+ watcher-driven emit) as a forward+backward compat shim.

title: Engine AST arm keys ASTRoot.SourceID by filepath.Base, but leyline keys source_id by relative path — activation blocker
description:
Surfaced while building the multi-file query-parity gate (mache-1166aa).

FINDING: the engine's ASTWalker arm sets `ASTRoot.SourceID = filepath.Base(result.job.path)` (internal/ingest/engine_treesitter.go, processTreeSitterResult + the single-file path). But `leyline parse <dir>` keys both `_source.id` and `_ast.source_id` (and the node_id roots) by the RELATIVE PATH from the parse root — confirmed on a real leyline db: source_id='api/schema.go', node_id='api/schema.go/package_clause/...'. So when the engine ingests a multi-dir project against a real leyline-produced _ast db, it queries `WHERE source_id = 'schema.go'` (base) while the rows are keyed 'api/schema.go' (relative) → the AST query returns NOTHING → empty/wrong projection. A second hazard: two files sharing a base name (api/schema.go vs internal/schema.go) collide under base-name keying even if reconciled.

WHY IT'S LATENT: SetASTWalker has no production caller yet (the source-ingest path still uses tree-sitter), so the AST arm has never run against a real leyline db in production. The single-file parity gate hides it because for a single file at the root, base == relative path. The new flat multi-file gate (TestASTQueryParity_MultiFile_Go) ALSO uses base-name source_ids (matching the engine), so it's engine↔synthetic-db consistent but NOT leyline-faithful — it deliberately sidesteps this to test cross-file refs in isolation.

FIX (activation prerequisite for mache-33de70): the engine must compute source_id as the path relative to the ingest root (matching leyline's scheme), not filepath.Base — everywhere it constructs ASTRoot.SourceID and wherever node_ids/source_ids are keyed in the AST path. Then a leyline-faithful (relative-path, subdir) multi-file parity fixture should be added to lock it (extend the gate or fold into the axis-2 producer-parity suite / S5 conformance mache-33f69d). Until reconciled, wiring SetASTWalker into cmd/mount.go would silently produce empty projections on any non-flat project.

comments.text:
FIXED in PR #447 (test/multifile-query-parity, commit 6f55b02). Added Engine.sourceIDFor(realPath): returns the path relative to RootPath, forward-slashed (matching leyline's source_id scheme), with base-name fallback for single-file ingest (RootPath==file → Rel==".") and out-of-root paths. The AST arm now uses it for ASTRoot.SourceID + ExtractContext/ExtractGoImports/ExtractFileLevelRefs. Also fixed ASTWalker.ExtractContext to take source_id directly (dropped its internal filepath.Base, which would have re-broken the key). No absolute paths anywhere — always root-relative.

Pinned by TestASTQueryParity_MultiFile_Subdir_Go: pkg/a.go keyed by relative path projects identically on the AST path. RED before (subdir file landed in _project_files because source_id="a.go" matched nothing in the db keyed "pkg/a.go"); GREEN after. Flat multi-file + single-file + context parity stay green; full ingest suite + -race green.

REMAINING for full leyline-faithfulness (follow-up, not blocking activation): node source_file on graph nodes is still filepath.Base (separate from the AST query key); and a leyline-faithful producer-parity fixture (real leyline parse of a subdir tree) belongs with S5 conformance (mache-33f69d). This fix unblocks wiring SetASTWalker into cmd/mount.go — the engine's AST query now aligns with a real `leyline parse <dir>` db.

From external review ("mache — remediation order", highest ROI). arena.go enforces `if h.Version != ArenaVersion { return "unsupported arena version" }` at three sites (read, flush, control.go:99), but NO test feeds a Version:1 header and asserts rejection — while the sibling *magic* guard does (TestArenaHeader_CalculateActiveOffset_RejectsInvalidMagic). This is the marquee v0.8.0 contract ("pre-v2 files rejected, not silently misinterpreted"): delete/invert the check in a future refactor and the whole suite stays green while the guarantee evaporates. The one place the green suite would survive removal of a safety guard.

Fix: one negative test mirroring the magic test — write a header with Version:1, assert ReadArenaHeader/from_arena returns the "unsupported arena version" error (ideally asserting the message names both found and expected version).

Close: `go test -run 'TestArena' ./internal/graph/` (new test present + green). Part of decade analysis-substrate / thread W0.

title: M2: tighten FD-leak regression test to assert watched-path count, not callback count
description:
From external review ("mache — remediation order"). TestWatcher_TargetIgnored asserts the onChange callback fires zero times for target/ files — one layer removed from the actual failure mode ("the directory isn't watched / no FD consumed"). The fix is correct (gates addDirsRecursive on shouldIgnoreDir, returns SkipDir), but the test can't distinguish "dir skipped, FD saved" from "dir watched, callback filtered, FD still leaked." A refactor preserving the callback filter but dropping the SkipDir skip would pass this test and quietly reintroduce the 129K-FD leak this release fixed.

Fix: assert on the number of watched paths (or open FDs) directly — inspect the watcher's tracked-dir set after addDirsRecursive over a tree containing target/, assert target/** is absent.

Close: `go test -run 'TestWatcher' ./internal/ingest/`. Part of decade analysis-substrate / thread W0.

title: bundle leyline binary in mache release + auto-detect tiers
description:
## Problem

mache and leyline-open (LLO) are tightly coupled — mache consumes the .db files that LLO's `leyline parse` produces. But they ship separately, requiring users to manually build and install both.

## Design: Three Tiers

mache auto-detects what's available and activates features accordingly:

| Tier | Installed | Capabilities |
|---|---|---|
| mache only | mache | CGO tree-sitter, live parse at mount time |
| mache + llo | mache + `leyline` (open) | Pre-baked .db, instant mount, no CGO, splice |
| mache + ll | mache + `leyline` (extended) | Above + daemon, embeddings, semantic search |

Detection: `which leyline` → `leyline --version` → "(open)" or "(extended)" → feature activation.

## Work Items

1. **Release bundling:** mache CI builds the LLO `leyline` Rust binary and includes it in the release tarball alongside the mache Go binary
2. **Auto-detect:** At startup, mache checks for `leyline` on PATH (or next to the mache binary). Parses `--version` to determine tier.
3. **Integration:** When leyline is available, `mache serve` calls `leyline parse <source> -o <db>` instead of using CGO tree-sitter. The .db activates the existing fast path (useNodesTable=true) + ASTWalker.
4. **Fallback:** If leyline is not found, fall back to existing CGO path (no behavior change).

## Why

- Users install one thing, get the full stack
- Gradual CGO elimination — leyline replaces tree-sitter parsing, mache stays pure Go
- Same mache binary works at all three tiers

## Depends on

- ley-line-open CLI is done and pushed (leyline binary with parse/splice/serve/load/inspect/lsp)
- mache ASTWalker parity beads (mache-37646f, mache-377c4a, mache-37926d) for full CGO elimination

title: S5: Axis-2 _ast DB-schema conformance suite — pin ley-line's table contract, run in default CI
description: The real trust boundary is the _ast/_source/nodes SQLite schema across the Rust(ley-line)->Go(mache) process line — NO Go interface can enforce it (math-friend review). Axis-1 (mache-emitted _ast, same parse tree) proves only query-engine equivalence. Axis-2 (ley-line Rust parse vs mache parse) is what ships, and it's behind //go:build leyline so default CI never runs it (ast_parity_test.go:1). Build a conformance suite of FROZEN golden _ast fixtures (produced once by leyline parse, checked in) that pins the column contract: node_kind vocabulary, namedness, byte ranges, leaf record semantics, source_id derivation. Run in default CI so contract drift fails the build without a live leyline binary. This is the DB-schema-as-contract the SourceBackend interface cannot provide.

comments.text:
mache-7555da built the MINIMAL derivation it needed and left the rest of this bead open. Recording what exists now so this doesn't get rebuilt.

**Shipped in PR #592, `internal/fixturedb/schema_leyline_conformance_test.go`:**

`TestLeylineSchema_MatchesPinnedBinary` runs the PINNED `leyline parse` on a two-file (Go + Python, one import, one qualified call, one bare call) corpus, dumps `sqlite_master`, and diffs it against the DDL snapshot in `schema_leyline.go`. Covers `nodes`, `node_defs`, `node_refs`, `_ast`, `_source`, `_imports`, `node_content` plus the ten indexes ley-line creates on them. Comparison is normalized (`--` comments stripped, whitespace collapsed) so it catches SHAPE — columns, NOT NULL, PK, WITHOUT ROWID — and not formatting. Mutation-proven: adding a PK to node_refs turns it red.

It also asserts `leylineSchemaVersion == leyline.PinnedBinaryVersion()`, so a pin bump FORCES a re-derivation rather than silently comparing v0.13.0's snapshot against v0.14's output.

**What this bead still owns, and this does NOT cover:**
- The golden-`_ast` ROW-CONTENT parity in the acceptance criteria (`internal/ingest/ast_parity_test.go`, `testdata/golden_ast`). #592 pins the TABLE CONTRACT only — column sets and constraints — not that a given source produces given rows.
- Running in DEFAULT CI. It is gated on a cached pinned binary and skips when absent, like every other pinned gate here.
- The tables #592 deliberately does not model: `capnp_blobs`, `query_blobs`, `source_blobs`, `_queries`, `_meta`, `_ast_pointer`, `_file_index`, `node_child`.

**Blocker removed along the way:** `internal/lltest`'s pinned-binary resolution was resolving the LEGACY unversioned `~/.mache/bin/leyline` directly. mache-0acdf6 made the cache version-namespaced and stopped WRITING that path, so every pinned gate in this repo was skipping unconditionally on any machine past that migration. Now exported as `leyline.CachedPinnedBinary()` / `lltest.PinnedBinaryOrSkip(t)` — use those here rather than re-deriving the path, or this suite will silently never run either.

**Ground truth captured, ley-line-open v0.13.0** (`sqlite_master`, verbatim):

    node_defs(token NOT NULL, node_id NOT NULL, source_id NOT NULL,
              container_node_id, canonical_kind, node_hash BLOB REF node_content)
    node_refs(token NOT NULL, node_id NOT NULL, source_id NOT NULL,
              container_node_id, qualifier, node_hash BLOB REF node_content)
    -- neither has a PRIMARY KEY; neither is WITHOUT ROWID

Semantics worth pinning here too, since they are what a row-level suite would assert: `node_refs.node_id` is the call-SITE leaf and the enclosing def is `container_node_id`; a bare call stores `qualifier` NULL (not `''`); ley-line DUAL-EMITS `fmt.Println`/qualifier-NULL and `Println`/qualifier-`fmt` at the same node_id — which is precisely why the missing primary key is load-bearing; `_source.content` is NULL (bytes live in `source_blobs`, only `path` is set); `node_defs.container_node_id` is NULL for top-level items.

title: Pre-injection pipeline + daemon-warm-cache: the missing layer between mache's structural data and agent productivity
description:
## Strategic context

Mache produces objectively richer structural data than peer tools (GrapeRoot's dual-graph, codebase-memory-mcp's Cypher graph, agent-lsp's LSP wrapper) — schema-driven projection, cross-language ref/def index, community detection, LSP enrichment via ley-line, find_smells over the AST, mermaid diagram generation. The MCP tool surface (find_callers, find_definition, get_architecture, etc.) is the only delivery channel.

The cost-quality bench in `benchmarks/cost-quality/` (PR `feat/cost-quality-bench`) tried to measure this and produced inconclusive numbers (mache mode cost-neutral, slightly worse on turns and quality). The post-mortem at `benchmarks/cost-quality/RESULTS.md` traces the problem: **we measured mache in the wrong configuration, missing the layer that turns structural data into agent productivity.**

GrapeRoot's published comparison frames the gap precisely:
- vanilla Claude:                 $0.25/prompt
- CodeGraphContext (MCP-on-demand): $0.27/prompt  ← MORE expensive
- GrapeRoot (pre-injection):       $0.17/prompt

The MCP-on-demand mode is net-NEGATIVE because the agent burns turns deciding which tools to call and waiting on responses. Pre-injection wins because it pays the structural-work cost ONCE per session, then every prompt is fast. Mache currently has no pre-injection — it's MCP-on-demand only.

## The work, in three parts

### 1. Pre-injection pipeline (the highest-leverage missing piece)

A new command — `mache context-pack <repo>` or `mache serve --inject-bundle` — that produces a context bundle suitable for injection into an agent prompt. Composition:

- Top-level structure overview (existing `get_overview` output)
- Key abstractions (existing `get_architecture` top-N entry points + key types)
- Community summary (existing `get_communities --summary=true` top-N clusters)
- Optional: query-specific narrowing (which files / constructs are relevant to a given query)

We have all the inputs — we just don't have the packer. GrapeRoot's `context_packer.pack_for_query()` in `Codex-CLI-Compact/bin/context_packer.py` is a useful reference (MIT-licensed).

Integration shape: agents can either consume this via a top-level slash command (`/mache-context-pack`) that produces text to paste, or via an MCP `tools/call` of a new tool `pack_context(repo, query?)` that the agent invokes ONCE at session start before its real prompt.

Estimate: ~1-2 days of work.

### 2. Daemon-backed warm cache, end-to-end

`leyline daemon --source <path>` already watches source and warms an arena. Mache can connect via `mache serve --control <ctrl-path>`. What's missing:

**a) Readiness signal**. A daemon op `status` that returns `{phase: "warming" | "ready" | "reingesting", staleness_ms, last_change_at}`. Mache propagates this through `get_overview` so the agent knows whether to wait or proceed.

**b) Verified incremental re-parse granularity**. The daemon claims to re-parse on file change but the granularity hasn't been audited. If a single file edit causes whole-arena rebuild, the "always-ready" pitch is broken on large repos. Needs an empirical test: edit one file in a 100K-LOC repo, time the re-parse, measure what got re-touched.

**c) Persistent LSP enrichment**. `ley-line enrich-lsp` is currently a one-shot. The daemon should re-enrich incrementally as files change so `find_definition` / `get_type_info` / `get_diagnostics` don't go stale. Otherwise the LSP backend silently rots between sessions.

Estimate: ~3-5 days of work, mostly LLO-side.

### 3. Re-run the cost-quality bench

Once 1 + 2 land, the bench gets three modes instead of two:

- `normal` — Plain claude (baseline)
- `mache-mcp` — claude + `mache serve --control` (daemon-backed MCP tools)
- `mache-preinject` — claude + mache context bundle pre-injected via `--append-system-prompt`

If `mache-preinject` substantially beats `mache-mcp`, we have the win story. If they're equivalent, we know the pre-injection layer isn't worth the bytes. If `mache-mcp` is suddenly competitive (no more cold-start penalty), the warm cache was doing more work than we thought.

Estimate: ~half day to re-run + analyze + commit.

## Why this is a single bead, not three

The three parts are sequenced and gated:

- (2) without (1) gets us a warm cache but no measurement showing it matters
- (1) without (2) gets us a pre-injection bundle but a cold-start arena every session (slow)
- (3) without (1) and (2) is what we just did, and the result was "inconclusive"

All three are necessary for the bench to produce a result worth quoting. Splitting into three beads risks shipping one without the others and re-creating the current measurement-confounded state.

## What this DOESN'T cover (filed for follow-up if those land)

- **Tool-description audit** — if mache-mcp mode underperforms even with the warm cache, that's the next thing. Separate work.
- **FS-overlay measurement** — `/mnt/mache/...` via Read/Grep is a separate UX axis. Separate harness.
- **Public-corpus comparison** — running this against Kubernetes / Consul-scale corpora for direct agent-lsp parity. Separate research bead.
- **Sourcegraph head-to-head** — apples-to-oranges in some ways; requires a separate methodology decision.

## Acceptance

This bead closes when:

1. `mache context-pack` (or equivalent) produces a bundle that, when injected, lets the agent answer at least one bug_fix prompt from `benchmarks/cost-quality/prompts.json` without invoking any other tools.
2. `leyline daemon` + `mache serve --control` survives a 10-minute idle session with file watching active, and a single-file edit results in <500ms re-parse (audited).
3. Re-run of `bench.py` against all three modes produces a JSONL where the three modes are cleanly differentiated and the result is interpretable as a real product evaluation.

**Demoted / upstream gap identified (2026-05-13)**: the `mache pack` prototype on `feat/cost-quality-bench` produced output dominated by `_file_level:` sentinels and Go/testify primitives. The pre-injection layer this bead proposes is well-motivated, but **building it on top of uncurated refs would just pre-inject noise**.

The actual upstream work is consumer-side curation — using the structure mache already has (`node_defs` set, `_file_level:` sentinel prefix, construct-kind segments in node_ids) to filter user-facing aggregations. Filed as thread `0013-refs-defs-canonical-schema/consumer-curation` with 5 beads:

1. `mache-8f6abf` (P1) — strip `_file_level:` sentinels from consumer aggregations
2. `mache-8fab5d` (P1) — distinguish user-defined symbols from external tokens (intersect with node_defs)
3. `mache-8fe65f` (P2) — surface construct-kind (functions/methods/types) from node_id paths
4. `mache-90341d` (P2) — re-evaluate `mache pack` output once 1+2+3 land
5. `mache-9077ae` (P2) — cost-quality bench re-run "Claude with mache vs without," on curated data

This bead now depends on `mache-9077ae`. The "warm-cache" half of the original epic (LLO daemon readiness signals, incremental re-parse) is still real and unblocked — but its measurement story is also blocked behind curation, so practically it's downstream too.

**Strategic reframe**: the user observation that anchored this was "mache has 2 features and the middle is confusing — graph engine vs code intelligence." The confusion is precisely the curation gap. The graph engine projects everything tree-sitter found (raw L0). The code-intelligence consumers want clean structural facts. Today they're the same data with no filter between them. The thread above closes that gap by adding the filter at the consumer aggregation boundary — not a new schema, just respecting the structure that already exists.

The structural argument (user's words, paraphrased): "the way code is surfaced is mathematically structured isn't it?" — yes, the math is `token ∈ node_defs → internal`, `node_id matches _file_level:* → sentinel`, `node_id matches */kind/* → kind`. Three filter rules, derivable from the data we already store. Not a redesign.

title: [0013-refs-defs-canonical-schema] Mache's structural query layer reads from two physically ...
description:
Mache's structural query layer reads from two physically separate tables that
encode the same logical concept (a "reference" edge) at different fidelities:

- **Tree-sitter producer** (in-process, or via ley-line-open's `leyline-ts`):
  syntactic, polyglot, fast, **shallow**. Writes:
  - `node_defs(token TEXT, node_id TEXT, PRIMARY KEY(token, node_id))` — "the
    symbol named `token` is defined at `node_id`."
  - `node_refs(token TEXT, node_id TEXT, PRIMARY KEY(token, node_id))` — "the
    node at `node_id` references **something** named `token`." Dispatch is
    unresolved; `obj.Read()` and a free function `Read()` produce the same row.

- **LSP producer** (ley-line-open's `leyline-lsp`, spawning per-language
  servers — `gopls`, `rust-analyzer`, `pyright`, `clangd`, `jdtls`, `zls`,
  etc., 28 languages): semantic, type-resolved, slower. Writes:
  - `_lsp_defs(node_id, def_uri, def_start_line, ..., def_end_col)` — definition
    location for a node.
  - `_lsp_refs(node_id, ref_uri, ref_start_line, ..., ref_end_col)` — reference
    location for a node, with **dispatch already resolved** (LSP knows which
    `Read` is meant when the source says `r.Read()` and `r` is `io.Reader`).

These are not isomorphic. Two independent mismatches:

1. **Direction is flipped.** `node_refs.node_id` is the *referrer*; `_lsp_refs.node_id`
   is the *referenced definition*. Reversible — costs an index, not information.
2. **The non-keyed endpoint lives in different ontologies.** Tree-sitter's
   "other end" is a *string* (`token`); LSP's "other end" is a *byte range*
   (`ref_uri + line:col`). Tree-sitter doesn't know which definition a token
   resolves to. LSP doesn't store the textual lemma it resolved through.

The ontology mismatch is asymmetric: **LSP knows tree-sitter's view, tree-sitter
does not know LSP's view.** Given a `_lsp_refs` row you can recover the textual
token by reading `ref_uri[ref_start..ref_end]`. Given a `node_refs` row you
cannot in general recover which definition was meant — that's exactly the
`dead_code` skip-list bug.

title: [0013-refs-defs-canonical-schema] The right abstraction is **not a refinement lattice** (wh...
description:
The right abstraction is **not a refinement lattice** (which would imply meets
and joins both directions). The projection between fidelities is one-way.
Use a **poset of fidelity levels with a forgetful functor**:

```
  L₀ = mention      (a node uses a name)              ← tree-sitter
  L₁ = binding      (a node uses *this* definition)   ← LSP
  L₂ = reachability (this binding is executed)         ← future SSA
```

For `j ≥ i`, the projection `π_{j → i}: L_j → L_i` strips fidelity. Concretely
`π_{1 → 0}(lsp_ref) = (referrer_node, token_at_ref_uri)` — keep the textual
mention, drop the binding. Higher producers project *down* into lower views;
lower producers don't project up.

**The canonical view at level L_i is `⋃_j π_{j → i}(R_j)`** where `R_j` is the
rows produced at level `j`. Higher fidelity dominates without a merge step;
the dominance is the projection doing its job, not a CASE in a view definition.

### Concrete schema

Producer tables stay physically separate (no collapse into one wide table —
that's "schema-as-disjunction = consumer-side branching by another name").
Consumers query **canonical views** that union them:

```sql
CREATE VIEW v_defs AS
  SELECT token, node_id, 'mention' AS fidelity FROM node_defs
  UNION ALL
  SELECT def_token, node_id, 'binding' FROM _lsp_defs;

CREATE VIEW v_refs AS
  SELECT node_id AS referrer_node_id, token,
         NULL AS target_node_id, NULL AS ref_uri, NULL AS ref_line,
         'mention' AS fidelity
  FROM node_refs
  UNION ALL
  SELECT referrer_node_id, ref_token, node_id AS target_node_id,
         ref_uri, ref_start_line AS ref_line, 'binding'
  FROM _lsp_refs;
```

For this to be a trivial UNION ALL with no helper functions, **the LSP producer
must extract `ref_token` and `referrer_node_id` at write time** (it has source
bytes loaded — one `tree.root_node().descendant_for_byte_range(...).utf8_text(...)`
call per row). This is the migration's biggest single win: token extraction
happens once, in the producer that has the bytes already open.

### Rule rewrites

`dead_code` (and siblings) become correct by construction:

```sql
WITH alive AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT d.node_id
  FROM v_defs d
  LEFT JOIN v_refs r
    ON r.target_node_id = d.node_id           -- L₁: exact binding
    OR (r.target_node_id IS NULL              -- L₀: token fallback
        AND r.token = d.token)
  WHERE r.referrer_node_id IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT d.node_id FROM v_defs d
WHERE d.node_id NOT IN (SELECT node_id FROM alive);
```

The interface-method skip-list **disappears from rule SQL**. Where LSP coverage
exists, binding rows mark `Read`, `ServeHTTP`, etc. as referenced — LSP
already resolved the dispatch. Where LSP coverage is absent (build-tagged
files, generated code, reflection), the OR-fallback to token match runs and
the rule degrades to today's behavior. Same SQL, no consumer branching.

The skip-list survives only as **external per-rule config** for the lattice
ceiling — edges no static producer can see (reflection, runtime code-gen
dispatch, JSON Marshal/Unmarshal). The `MACHE_SMELL_RULES_DIR` mechanism
already supports this; the rule body becomes shorter and the skip set becomes
a config artifact tagged with "edges below the lattice ceiling."

comments.text:
PR #351 (feat/skip-list-precise-retreat) — consumes A's empirical result.

Falsifiability A passing (0 newly-flagged-dead defs when dropping the skip-list, on a real `leyline parse + leyline lsp` build of mache) was empirical evidence that LSP binding rows replace the skip-list compensation for cases LSP indexed.

Wholesale dropping the skip-list would regress on tree-sitter-only `.db`s (no LSP enrichment) — there the skip-list IS load-bearing for interface methods. Tree-sitter's call extractor can't see runtime interface dispatch.

Right move: precise retreat. Single CTE, two categories:
- **Category 1** (runtime / test-harness): main, init, Test*, Benchmark*, Example*, Fuzz*. Always skipped — neither tree-sitter nor LSP synthesizes refs for the Go runtime loader.
- **Category 2** (interface methods): String, Error, Read, Write, Close, ServeHTTP, ... Skipped only when `NOT EXISTS (binding-fidelity v_defs row for this node_id)`. LSP coverage of the def → don't skip → alive-check decides.

Three states:
- (a) No binding v_defs row → LSP didn't see this def → SKIP (tree-sitter compensation still load-bearing)
- (b) Binding v_defs row, no binding v_refs targets it → LSP confirmed dead → don't skip → alive-check flags it
- (c) Binding v_defs row + binding v_refs → alive-check matches via binding arm

The new state (b) is the finding the retreat unlocks: methods whose name happens to match the interface skip-list but are genuinely dead.

title: [ADR-0013] Falsifiability B: fidelity-projection π_{1→0} round-trip
description:
First-class deliverable per ADR-0013 (mache-346cd0). For every _lsp_refs row, compute (referrer_node_id, token) via the projection π_{1→0} (i.e. extract the token from the referrer's source byte range) and check the resulting pair appears in node_refs.

Pass criteria: every projected row has a matching textual mention in node_refs, with documented exceptions:
- Function values (closures, method values stored in slices/maps) — tree-sitter's call extractor doesn't match these as call sites
- Type-only references (e.g. type aliases, struct embedding) — call extractor only catches call expressions
- Macro-expanded code that LSP saw post-expansion but tree-sitter saw pre-expansion (Rust)

Fail criteria: an LSP-level edge has no matching textual mention AND is NOT in the exception list. Means either tree-sitter's call extraction is missing patterns (fixable in leyline-ts), or the projection is wrong (extracted the wrong byte range — fixable in the view definition).

Depends on: mache-346cef (Step 1 — LLO writes the columns). Does NOT depend on the rule rewrites; can run as soon as Step 1 ships.

Implementation: standalone Go test or CLI that opens a fresh-built .db with both producers run, iterates _lsp_refs, runs the projection, and joins against node_refs. Outputs a discrepancy list. Acceptable when discrepancies match the exception taxonomy.

comments.text:
PR #352 (feat/falsifiability-test-fixes) — noise-removal refinement on the B harness.

Pre-refinement, B compared `(_lsp_refs.referrer_node_id, ref_token)` directly against `(node_refs.node_id, token)`. On a real LLO-built `.db` this produced ~100% noise:

- LLO writes `referrer_node_id` pointing at the **leaf identifier** (`field_identifier` / `identifier` / `type_identifier` — wherever the symbol token textually appears).
- mache writes `node_refs.node_id` pointing at the enclosing **call_expression**.

The two paths share a common prefix but never match exactly. Every projection comparison reported a discrepancy — couldn't distinguish a real bug from the shape mismatch.

Fix: `astCallSiteWalker` finds the deepest `call_expression` ancestor of the leaf via `_ast`:

```sql
SELECT node_id FROM _ast
 WHERE node_kind = 'call_expression' AND ? LIKE node_id || '/%'
 ORDER BY length(node_id) DESC LIMIT 1
```

Rows whose leaf isn't inside any call_expression are documented ADR exceptions (type_identifier, function value, embedded type) — classified separately, excluded from denominator.

Plus two-step CLI: `leyline parse --lsp` is gone; tests now use `leyline parse` + `leyline lsp --merge-db`.

Results on mache self-build with single-file enrichment:
- **0.0% (0/12)** of call-site `_lsp_refs` rows lack node_refs match
- 8 non-call refs correctly classified as exceptions

Threshold tightens 50% → 25%. Bead closing once #352 lands.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

title: epic: eliminate CGO tree-sitter — ASTWalker feature parity
description:
## Problem

Mache has two Walker implementations: SitterWalker (CGO, parses at mount time) and ASTWalker (pure Go, queries pre-parsed _ast table from ley-line). The switching logic exists (SelectWalker in ast_walker.go:185, engine.go:755) but ASTWalker is missing features that force fallback to SitterWalker.

## Goal

Make ASTWalker feature-complete so SitterWalker + CGO tree-sitter can be removed entirely. Mache becomes a pure Go binary that consumes .db files produced by ll-open (Rust).

## Missing in ASTWalker

1. **#match? predicates** — ASTWalker only supports #eq?. Errors with "requires SitterWalker (CGO)" for #match?. Need regex matching against _source byte ranges.
2. **ExtractCalls / ExtractQualifiedCalls** — populates node_refs for callers/callees graph. SitterWalker-only today. Need SQL equivalent querying _ast for call_expression nodes.
3. **ExtractContext** — body text extraction for schema context fields. Need to query _source byte ranges for matched nodes.
4. **ExtractGoImports** — package alias resolution for qualified call resolution. Need to query _ast for import_spec nodes and extract alias/path pairs.

## Also CGO-dependent (outside ingest/)

5. **internal/writeback/validate.go** — syntax-checks edits via CGO tree-sitter before commit. Could be replaced by calling ll-open's validate (already exists in ll-open/fs/src/validate.rs) or by a pure-Go validation path.
6. **internal/lattice/project_ast.go** — lattice AST projection, uses CGO sitter.
7. **internal/ingest/sitter_flatten.go** — flatten AST for ingestion, CGO.

## Approach

- ASTWalker parity (items 1-4) can be done incrementally — each is independently testable
- Table-presence detection pattern: mache already does this for nodes table, extend to all optional tables
- CGO removal is the final step after all paths have pure-Go alternatives
- Mache should never care whether .db came from ll-open (base) or ley-line (enriched) — same tables, same queries

title: workerd + D1 isolation: SQLite as capability-scoped staging area for agent edits
description:
## Insight

SQLite (.db) becomes the staging area for agent edits, not the filesystem. workerd mediates all access through D1 bindings — capability-scoped, no fd escape, no path traversal.

## Current path (escapable)
```
agent → MCP write_file → mache WritableGraph → splice → real filesystem
```
NFS mount gives the agent a file descriptor into the real filesystem. Isolation is by convention (schema projection), not enforced structurally.

## Proposed path (isolated)
```
agent → MCP write_file → workerd D1 binding → SQLite rows → leyline splice (on commit)
```
- D1 binding = capability-scoped SQL. Agent can only touch rows the binding permits.
- No path traversal, no symlink escape, no `../../../etc/passwd`.
- Atomic multi-file edits (one SQLite transaction).
- Rollback = don't commit. Diff preview = `SELECT * FROM nodes WHERE modified > ?`.
- Filesystem is a materialization target, not the working copy.
- notme certs scope which agent can write which paths — audit trail built in.

## Architecture
```
workerd (config.capnp)
├── D1 binding → .db file (leyline-parsed, mache-projected)
├── Worker JS → thin MCP router (hot path: search, list_dir, read_file = SELECT)
├── external service → mache Go binary (cold path: graph analysis, communities)
└── notme auth → agent identity + scoped write permissions
```

## Why workerd
- Same deployment pattern as notme (local workerd, container, CF Workers)
- D1 is literally SQLite — same file format leyline produces
- Overhead is ~zero for local dev (V8 isolate + fd mediation)
- Capability system is structural, not convention-based
- Already proven in the notme stack

## Depends on
- WritableGraph (exists)
- leyline splice (exists)
- capnp schema for daemon ops (just landed)
- notme bridge certs for agent identity scoping

title: Preset schemas terraform/groovy/cue don't project cleanly under leyline _ast (selectors calibrated to old in-process tree-sitter)
description:
Surfaced during PR-B (mache-37ae8b, CGO removal) when TestPresetSchemas_AgainstFixtures ran against leyline instead of the removed in-process tree-sitter. Three presets project differently (or not at all) under leyline's _ast — this is preset-schema-vs-leyline-grammar compat, ORTHOGONAL to CGO removal (the node structure differs by producer, not by how leyline is invoked). Skipped in the preset test with this bead reference; the other ~12 presets (go/rust/bash/csharp/css/dockerfile/html/...) project correctly and stay asserted.

## The three
1. **terraform**: leyline projects HCL resources by TYPE label — `resources/"aws_s3_bucket"` — where the preset selector + test expect the NAME label `resources/"artifacts"`. Likely a one-line fix in cmd/schemas/terraform.json (capture block-label index [1] not [0], IF leyline's HCL _ast exposes both), or leyline's HCL block-label extraction needs both labels. Verify against leyline v0.8.0's HCL _ast node shape.
2. **groovy**: leyline parses (1 file) but the preset selector renders `functions/<no value>` — the name-template field the selector references isn't present on leyline's groovy _ast nodes. Only 6 skeleton nodes. cmd/schemas/groovy.json selector needs recalibration to leyline's groovy node kinds/fields.
3. **cue**: leyline has NO cue grammar (0 parsed — no tree-sitter-0.26 cue grammar exists anywhere). This one can't be fixed mache-side; it's the documented coverage gap (the schema coverage guard already errors on cue). Either drop the cue preset+fixture or keep it skipped until a cue grammar exists upstream. Related: ley-line-open-e5addb / ley-line-open-4aeb4f.

## Fix approach
Per-language: dump leyline's _ast node kinds for a terraform/groovy fixture, diff against what cmd/schemas/{terraform,groovy}.json selectors expect, update the selectors. Add the preset back to the test's asserted set (remove the skip) once it projects. cue stays skipped pending an upstream grammar.

title: Align server.json packages[].oci with ADR-0041 canonical form (identifier no-tag + version=git-tag + digest), not tag-in-identifier
description:
mache 0.16.1 fixed a v-prefix drift (image tagged `:v0.16.0` but packages[].oci.version was bare `0.16.0` → derived `:0.16.0` 404'd) — but fixed it by baking the tag INTO identifier: `{ identifier: "ghcr.io/agentic-research/mache:v0.16.1", version: null }`. That's the "tag-in-identifier" shape ADR-0041 (cloister) explicitly REJECTED as one of the 3-way designation drifts (llo baked tag into identifier; rosary split identifier+version; mache-local empty). ADR-0041's canonical form is `identifier` (no tag) + `version` (= git tag) + resolved `digest`; cloister pulls by digest. It's also non-standard for the MCP registry packages[] convention (identifier = name, version = tag).

Fix: emit `{ identifier: "ghcr.io/agentic-research/mache", version: "v0.16.x" }` (tagless identifier, version = the git tag). Single-source from buildinfo.Version + the tag as today, just place them per the contract. This lets cloister's resolver-digest work (cloister-091106) resolve tag→digest and pin `identifier@digest` cleanly, and keeps rosary/llo from copying the divergent shape. Coordinate with cloister ADR-0041 (cloister-bd73a7): if the producers prefer tag-in-identifier, revise the ADR instead — but producer + contract must agree. Filed 2026-07-08 from a cloister-side review of mache 0.16.1.
acceptance_criteria: server.json's packages[] oci entry follows ADR-0041's canonical form: identifier = the image name WITHOUT a tag (`ghcr.io/agentic-research/mache`), version = the git tag (`v0.16.x`), and (once cloister resolves it) a digest. NOT the current 0.16.1 shape (identifier baked with `:v0.16.1`, version null). Verified by the mache gen:server-json:check gate passing + a released tag (v0.16.2+) whose server.json shows `identifier` tagless + `version` = the tag. Runnable: `task gen:server-json:check` (or the mache test suite).

title: Flaky: TestProvenance_RecordAndReport times out under full -race suite (2s version-probe exec timeout)
description:
`internal/leyline/provenance_test.go::TestProvenance_RecordAndReport` fails intermittently ONLY under the full `task ci` / `go test -tags boltdb -race ./...` run; passes 100% in isolation (`-run … -count=3`) and package-alone (`./internal/leyline/ -count=1`, 4/4).

ROOT CAUSE: `internal/leyline/provenance.go:85` — the version probe does
```
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
out, err := exec.CommandContext(ctx, bin, "--version").Output()
```
Under `-race ./...`, many package test binaries run concurrently and starve subprocess spawning. The fake `sh` script (writeFakeLeyline) exceeds the 2s deadline → `Output()` errors → parsed version is empty → the `VersionMatches` assertion (provenance_test.go:40-42) fails. Observed test wall time 5.61s under contention vs ~0.4s isolated — confirms subprocess starvation, not a logic bug.

NOT a B4/B6 regression — B4/B6 (mache-ff9a9d/mache-ffabd1) only touched cmd/ + internal/graph/; this package was untouched. Pre-existing on main; can intermittently red CI (`go test -race ./...`).

FIX OPTIONS:
(a) [recommended] extract the 2s literal to an overridable package var `probeTimeout = 2*time.Second`; the test sets it generous (e.g. 30s). Preserves prod behavior AND keeps the test exercising the real exec+parse path (full fidelity, just not deadline-fragile under load).
(b) bump the prod timeout (changes prod semantics for a test-env artifact — weaker).
(c) inject a fake version-returner so the test spawns no subprocess (loses real-exec fidelity).
acceptance_criteria: TestProvenance_RecordAndReport no longer flakes under `go test -tags boltdb -race ./...`; the version-probe timeout is overridable so the test uses a generous deadline while prod keeps 2s. Verify: `cd /path/to/mache && go test -tags boltdb -race -count=5 ./internal/leyline/` green, and full `task ci` green across repeated runs.

title: mache build should accept --schema and --format flags
description:
`mache build [source] [output.db]` currently only works for code ingestion (tree-sitter). It needs `--schema` and `--format` flags to support data projection without mounting.

The root command's `--out` flag does index+materialize but hangs because it still tries to set up the NFS/FUSE mount before materializing. `mache build` should be the non-mounting path:

```bash
mache build data.db projected.db --schema trivy-v2-schema.json --format boltdb
```

This is blocking venturi's trivy-db projection test (venturi-a25eee) which needs to run mache in a test environment without NFS/FUSE.

## Proposed
Add `--schema` and `--format` flags to the `build` subcommand. Reuse the existing `materialize.ForFormat()` infrastructure from PR #133.

title: Replace daemon.capnp fork with import-from-LLO + Go-annotations wrapper
description:
Filed 2026-05-10. Architectural decision: mache must NOT carry a forked copy of `daemon.capnp`. LLO is the authoritative publisher (`rs/ll-core/public-schema/capnp/daemon.capnp` — the path name already commits to "public-schema"); mache is a consumer. Today mache has a byte-identical fork at `internal/leyline/schema/daemon.capnp` differing only in three lines of Go codegen annotations. That's the drift surface LLO ADR-0014 §F8.6.6 warns about.

## What needs to happen

1. **Delete** `internal/leyline/schema/daemon.capnp` (the forked copy).

2. **Add** a thin wrapper `internal/leyline/schema/daemon-go.capnp` (or whatever name fits the codegen pattern) that contains ONLY the Go-specific annotations:
   ```capnp
   using Go = import "/go.capnp";
   $Go.package("schema");
   $Go.import("github.com/agentic-research/mache/internal/leyline/schema");
   # then: import "daemon.capnp" (resolved via -I path)
   ```
   The annotations apply to imported types per capnpc semantics.

3. **Wire the consumption mechanism.** Two clean options — pick one:
   - **Submodule:** `git submodule add` the LLO schema dir into `internal/leyline/vendor/leyline-schema/` (or similar). Pinned commit per LLO ADR-0014's exact-pin discipline.
   - **Build-time fetch:** `task gen-schemas` copies/syncs `daemon.capnp` from a configurable LLO source path (e.g. `LLO_SCHEMA_ROOT=../ley-line-open/rs/ll-core/public-schema/capnp`). Committed alongside generated Go code for offline builds.

   Submodule is more rigid; build-time-fetch is more flexible. Whichever picks, document the contract in mache's README and a brief comment at the top of the wrapper file.

4. **Add a CI gate** that asserts the consumed `daemon.capnp` byte-equals LLO's authoritative copy (modulo the Go annotations which live separately). Drift = build failure, not a runtime mystery. Pattern from LLO ADR-0014 F8.6.3.

5. **Regenerate Go bindings** via the existing capnpc-go path. The generated `daemon.capnp.go` (or wherever bindings land) should be byte-identical before and after this change since the schema content is unchanged — that's the smoke test.

## Acceptance

- `internal/leyline/schema/daemon.capnp` no longer exists as a stand-alone fork — it's either a symlink, a submodule pointer, or fetched-at-build.
- Generated Go bindings unchanged byte-for-byte (other than path comments / source attribution).
- CI fails if mache's consumed schema diverges from LLO's authoritative copy.
- README documents the consumption mechanism so a contributor knows how to update on schema bumps.

## Cross-repo context

- LLO authoritative source: `~/remotes/art/ley-line-open/rs/ll-core/public-schema/capnp/daemon.capnp`
- LLO ADR-0014: capnp as protocol, append-only-additive, toolchain-pin discipline
- mache ADR-0014: mache as consumer/projector in the constellation
- mache-98aa97: the open implementation bead that USES this schema (UDS query proxy). This bead is its prerequisite — `mache-98aa97` should be re-checked once schema sharing is sound, since its description mentions "JSON result" in places that may be outdated relative to capnp ToolResult-style.
- mache-2aab1e: the design bead that asked "what wire format / what schema?" — now obsoleted by the existence of `daemon.capnp`. Close it once this bead is in flight.

## Out of scope

- Implementing the UDS client itself (`mache-98aa97`'s scope).
- Changing the schema content (LLO ADR-0014's append-only rule applies; any schema bump is upstream first, then mache regen).
- Publishing LLO's schema as a separate Go module (option B in the design discussion — rejected in favor of A; if appetite changes later, file a new bead).

title: design: extract find_smells to ext/machelint when product split is right
description:
find_smells lives in mache today and that's fine — substrate-tight access to _ast/node_defs/node_refs. But it's the only MCP tool with real opinionated logic (rule choices, thresholds, skip lists, scoring) — different shape than the thin graph-wrapper tools alongside it. Tipping points that should trigger a split:

1. User-extensible rules (declarative JSON / per-repo overrides) — already gestured at in mache-6z2e
2. Rules with non-SQL logic — dep_cycles (mache-unm5) needs Tarjan SCC in Go; breaks the 'just SQL' contract and forces a registry refactor
3. External consumers — separate linters, CI actions wanting machelint without all of mache
4. Rules that need their own data model — LSP / CVE DBs / type checkers

The clean way to split when ready: ext/machelint/ as a separate Go module (mirrors ext/boltdb/), imports mache's graph package for SQL handle, mache's MCP server gains a plugin/registration hook so machelint registers find_smells from outside. Default mache binary imports it; other consumers don't have to.

Don't act on this bead until at least one tipping point fires — premature split = double maintenance for no gain.

title: TestWatcher_NewSubdirectory — macOS FSEvents timing flake
description:
TestWatcher_NewSubdirectory in internal/ingest/watcher_test.go relies on FSEvents firing within a 2s 'eventually' window after a 250ms warmup sleep + file write. Observed flaky on macos-latest CI (PR #325 first run) — assertion 'should detect file in new subdirectory' never satisfied. Rerun went green.

The test already accounts for FSEvents latency:
- 250ms sleep after MkdirAll for sub-watcher install
- 2s require.Eventually poll for the callback

But macOS CI runners under load can still exceed those bounds. Same shape as the TestArenaFlusher_Coalesce flake (mache-02a9ab) — wall-clock timing assumptions break under noisy CI.

Fix options:
1. Bump the warmup sleep to 500ms and the eventually window to 5s — quick, increases flake-tolerance but slows the happy path.
2. Replace the FSEvents-based check with a deterministic fsnotify event injection (test seam in NewWatcher).
3. Mark macos as a known-flaky platform via t.Retry-style helper or skip with t.Skip on CI when GITHUB_ACTIONS+macOS — captures reality but masks regressions.

Option 1 is the smallest. Option 2 is the most correct but invasive.

title: find_smells dead_code: make LSP-binding the authoritative reachability path; shrink allowlists to reachability-roots
description: dead_code (cmd/smell_rules.go) is a graceful-degradation HYBRID: deterministic when the .db has LSP binding refs (v_defs.fidelity='binding' + target_node_id from LLO BindingRecord/_lsp_refs — 'no binding ref => dead' is authoritative), but heuristic when tree-sitter-only — it falls back to node_refs (CALL-extraction only, misses non-call uses) plus a pile of allowlists to suppress the resulting false positives: the interface-method list (String/Error/Read/Write/Close/.../ServeHTTP), main/init, Test*/Benchmark*/Example*/Fuzz*, the NOT LIKE types/|constants/|variables/ category exclusions, and the *.capnp.go/*.pb.go/*_generated.go blanket. Those allowlists exist ONLY to compensate for the incomplete (call-only) ref index. FIX: make LSP binding the required/preferred reachability source (Requires _lsp_refs/binding). LSP find-references sees ALL reference kinds, so the interface-method allowlist + type/const/var category exclusions + generated blanket disappear. Keep ONLY the principled reachability ROOTS that are true regardless of refs: main/init (program entry), Test*/Benchmark*/Example*/Fuzz* (test-runtime entry), exported-at-module-boundary (unresolvable in-scope). title: find_smells: new duplicate_code rule — AST-subtree structural-hash clones (pure-Go baseline) + HDC tier
description: duplicate_definitions detects dup DEFS (same token, N sites) — NOT duplicate CODE. Add a deterministic clone detector (Deckard / Type-1&2 clones = structurally-identical AST subtrees). TWO tiers, mirroring the engine's baseline+enrichment pattern: (1) BASELINE — pure-Go over _ast on any .db: compute a leaf-erased structural hash per subtree (hash the node_kind sequence of each subtree, ignoring identifier/literal text), report subtrees with >=N nodes whose hash collides >=2x, with file:line of each clone. No allowlists, fully deterministic. Computed via SQL/precompute pass over _ast (every node has node_kind + byte/row ranges + parent_id path). (2) ENRICHED — consume LLO _hdc/_hdc_subtree_cache when present (LLO hdc-1 storage schema + hdc-3a 'Deckard-style leaf-erased Merkle on canonical alphabet' = exactly cross-language clone detection); query for high-similarity subtree clusters instead of recomputing. NO new LLO data needed for the baseline (_ast suffices); the HDC tier rides LLO's existing HDC roadmap (additive when it lands). This is the user's 'find duplicated code, deterministically' ask. Relates to mache-445887.

title: find_smells: qualifier-aware fan_out_skew metric (replace name-pattern exemption)
description:
Follow-up to the projection-function naming-convention fix shipped today. The current `fan_out_skew` rule counts `COUNT(DISTINCT token)` per referrer. That conflates two structurally different cases:

1. **Orchestration** — calls many DIFFERENT functions/methods across multiple packages. Real signal.
2. **Projection** — calls many METHODS ON ONE RECEIVER. Mechanical translation; no signal.

Today's fix exempts (2) via a naming convention (`*FromRecord`, `*FromMessage`, `Project*`, etc.). That works but relies on developers adopting the convention.

**The proper fix:** count distinct *qualifiers* (receiver types / package origins) instead of distinct tokens. Then a 50-call function projecting one receiver scores as 1; a 5-call function calling 5 different packages scores as 5. The 3× mean threshold then aligns with the rule's stated intent ("constructs that touch too many neighbors").

## Data layer change

The call extractor (`internal/ingest/sitter_walker.go::ExtractQualifiedCalls`) already produces `graph.QualifiedCall{Token, Qualifier}`. The qualifier is dropped at `MemoryStore.AddRef(token, nodeID)` — only the token lands in `node_refs`.

Storage extension: add `qualifier TEXT` column to `node_refs`. Backfill via re-ingest. Update:

- `internal/graph/graph.go::AddRef` — accept qualifier
- `internal/graph/graph.go::FlushRefs` — write qualifier column
- `internal/graph/sqlite_graph.go::QueryRefs` — surface qualifier
- `internal/ingest/engine.go` — pass qualifier through from QualifiedCall
- `internal/refsvtab/refs_module.go` — schema bump for the vtab

## Rule change

Replace `COUNT(DISTINCT token)` with `COUNT(DISTINCT qualifier)` (or `COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(NULLIF(qualifier, ''), token))` to handle bare-token Go calls). Drop the projection naming-convention skip-list once this is live.

## Acceptance

- `internal/graph/graph_test.go` — qualifier round-trips
- `cmd/serve_find_smells_test.go::TestFindSmells_FanOutSkew` — verify projection functions now score low without naming convention
- Falsifiability: dogfood on mache itself, expect `bindingFromRecord` and similar projection functions to score 1-2, not 18

## Out of scope

- LSP-resolved targets (when qualifier is unknowable from tree-sitter alone — e.g. qualifier is `pkg.Method` but `pkg` is an alias). Resolution via canonical views (PR #341/#346) handles that for LSP-enriched DBs already; tree-sitter-only DBs use the surface qualifier and accept some imprecision.
- Renaming the rule. `fan_out_skew` stays the same name; only the metric semantics change.

## Refs

- Today's pragmatic fix: PR `fix/fan-out-skew-projection-functions`
- Triggered by: mache-190508 step 2 (PR #354)

comments.text:
**Cross-repo option to consider before starting this work** (surfaced post-mache-190508 by an LLO-side agent on 2026-05-09):

LLO's call extractor (`rs/ll-open/ts/src/refs.rs`) emits `(token, node_id, source_id)` today. It already has access to qualifier info during extraction — it's just not propagated through the SQL/capnp surface. Two paths:

| Path | Mache work | LLO work |
|---|---|---|
| **Mache-only** (current bead scope) | Plumb qualifier through `engine.go` → `MemoryStore.AddRef` → `sqlite_writer.go` schema → `refs_module.go` vtab → `serve_find_smells.go` rule SQL | none |
| **Cross-runtime** (architectural fit per T8/Σ) | Read `qualifier @7 :Text` field from `BindingRecord` capnp; add UNION arm | Add `qualifier` field to `binding.capnp` (next ordinal, additive per ADR-0014); populate in `rs/ll-open/lsp/src/project.rs::project_references` |

Path 2 is the T8 thesis applied: "two AST walkers in two languages converging on the same structural fact" is exactly what schema-as-data-plane was meant to dissolve. Mache rewalking the AST to recover qualifier that LLO already has is the kind of duplication T8 promised to retire.

**Recommended sequencing:** before starting the mache-only work, ping LLO. If they're up for adding the schema field, we ship a one-PR consumer change here instead of a 5-file migration. If LLO declines or it's a multi-quarter wait, fall back to the mache-only path.

Either way, the rule-SQL change is the same: `COUNT(DISTINCT qualifier)` instead of `COUNT(DISTINCT token)`. The naming-convention exemption from #355 stays in place until the new metric ships.

For the future agent who picks this up: start by checking whether LLO has shipped a `BindingRecord.qualifier` field (`grep "qualifier @" ~/remotes/art/ley-line-open/rs/ll-core/schema-capnp/schemas/binding.capnp`). If yes, this becomes a small consumer-side PR.

comments.text:
**Closed structurally.** Superseded by mache-6c0d07 / PR #358.

The qualifier-aware `fan_out_skew` metric this bead asked for shipped via the cross-repo path: LLO T8.7 added `qualifier @7 :Text` to `BindingRecord` (additive, byte-stable per ADR-0014), mache consumed it via `task gen-bindings` + `_capnp_binding_refs.qualifier` plumbing, and the rule SQL flipped to `COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(NULLIF(qualifier,''), token))`.

The mache-only path this bead originally proposed (extend `node_refs` with a qualifier column, plumb through engine + writer + sqlite_graph + refs_module) is no longer the right move. LLO is the producer with the AST in hand; consumer-side rewalking would have been duplicate work + a maintenance liability.

T8 thesis paid off: instead of two AST walkers in two languages converging on the same fact, one producer emits the field and every consumer picks it up via codegen.

title: Bumping leyline to v0.11.0 crosses an IR lineage boundary — derived .db artifacts go stale silently
description:
URGENT AND NOT BLOCKED. This needs handling whether or not LLO ever publishes a lineage field.

mache pins leyline v0.10.4 (internal/leyline/binary_pin.go, and go.mod:9 for leyline-schema). LLO shipped v0.11.0 on 2026-07-28T04:36:03Z, and that release carries a change to how merkle-AST node addresses are DERIVED: ley-line-open PR #282 merged, bumping IR_SCHEMA_VERSION from "merkle-ast-v1" to "merkle-ast-v2" (rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/cmd_parse.rs:50).

WHY THIS IS NOT AN ORDINARY MINOR BUMP. From PR #282's own description: `25811f` gave `function_signature_item` the kappa `function` it lacked, "rewriting every Rust trait signature's node_hash — the preimage hashes canonical_kind(raw).unwrap_or(raw). Sources are byte-identical, so the mtime+size skip cannot see it. A pre-change arena would serve stale addresses forever, and mache is about to pin node_hash."

BYTE-IDENTICAL SOURCES is the load-bearing part. Every staleness mechanism mache has is content- or time-based: cache lockfiles hash raw source bytes (cmd/cache.go:284, 546-547), the parse skip is mtime+size, and _mache_meta records backend/mache_version/mache_commit/built_at (cmd/build_meta.go:44-49) with no leyline version and no lineage tag. NONE of them can observe this change. Two .db files built from identical sources under different leyline lineages are indistinguishable to mache.

THE EXPOSED PATH is `mache build -o x.db` followed by `mache serve x.db` across the upgrade. Most mache paths write a fresh temp .db per parse (cmd/serve.go:797-812, cmd/build.go:96-110), and smellMemo is in-process only (cmd/smell_incremental.go:50-58) — so the exposure is narrow BY ACCIDENT rather than by design. A persisted .db built before the bump and served after it carries merkle-ast-v1 addresses while the binary computes v2.

WHAT TO DO WHEN BUMPING:
1. Treat the 0.10.4 -> 0.11.0 bump as invalidating: any persisted .db built by the previous leyline must be rebuilt, not reused.
2. Say so wherever the bump is recorded, so it is not rediscovered.
3. Consider whether _mache_meta should carry the leyline binary version at minimum — that is ~9 lines at cmd/build_meta.go:44 and would make "which leyline built this .db" answerable even before LLO publishes the lineage tag itself.

Item 3 is a genuine partial fix available TODAY with no dependency on LLO: mache already knows which leyline binary it invoked, because it pins and digest-verifies it (binary_pin.go). Recording that in the .db is entirely within mache's control.

THE DURABLE FIX IS SEPARATE and blocked on the producer: LLO must publish ir_schema_version before mache can compare lineages directly. Filed as ley-line-open-348de6 (P1), and mache's consumption side is tracked separately.

Detected by vigil's release-check evaluator against the live v0.11.0 release about an hour after publication: 11 clauses, 10 satisfied, 1 violated — the missing lineage field, naming mache as the consumer harmed. Spec: vigil docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-release-contract-design.md §5.1.</description>
<parameter name="acceptance_criteria">A decision is recorded about whether persisted .db artifacts must be rebuilt when the leyline pin crosses a lineage boundary, and if _mache_meta gains the leyline binary version, `mache build -o x.db` writes it and it is readable afterwards. Verified by building a .db, bumping the pin, and confirming the mismatch is detectable rather than silent.

comments.text:
DONE — merged to main as a5e5770 (PR #572).

`_mache_meta` now carries three leyline keys, verified end-to-end on a real build:

    leyline_pin      v0.10.4                    the compile-time pin, ALWAYS written
    leyline_version  leyline 0.10.4 (open)      what actually ran
    leyline_source   resolved                   resolution tier

A divergence between pin and version is the diagnostic — it means MACHE_LEYLINE_BINARY
was in play and the .db may not match what CI produces. An unresolved build writes
"unresolved" rather than omitting the key, so "built without leyline" stays
distinguishable from "built by an older mache that did not stamp this"; same for a binary
whose --version will not read, since an empty string in an artifact is worse than an
explicit marker.

ALSO FIXED, found while implementing: Provenance() was populated only by DiscoverOrStart,
the daemon route. `mache build` resolved a binary via autoInvokeLeylineParse, ran it, and
left Provenance() reporting "mache hasn't resolved one this process" — a lie by omission
in exactly the case the record exists for. Now records what it resolved, which is also
what makes the metadata available.

TWO PROCESS NOTES worth keeping.

The smell gate caught an untested RecordResolved after I had already run `task smells` and
seen it pass — because that run predated the commit, and the gate indexes `git archive
HEAD`. Running it before committing measures the old tree. That is the second time this
session; it is not a subtle trap, just an easy one.

The RecordResolved tests are declared in provenance_test.go after TestProvenance
deliberately: that test asserts the PRE-resolution state (ok=false), so it must run before
anything records. A separate provenance_record_test.go would sort ahead of it
alphabetically and break it. leylineMetaRows was also split into a pure
leylineMetaRowsFrom(prov, ok, pin) so every branch is covered without depending on an
installed leyline and without mutating a package-level singleton that has no reset.

SCOPE HONESTY: this is a proxy, not a lineage tag. A version string cannot express
lineage — two releases can share an IR schema and one release can change it. The durable
fix is mache-43d63d (consume LLO's ir_schema_version), still blocked on
ley-line-open-348de6. This was worth landing anyway because it is the half mache controls,
and because the v0.11.1 pin bump is itself lineage-crossing: persisted .dbs built by the
previous leyline must be rebuilt, not reused, and this makes which-leyline-built-this
answerable from the artifact.

Pin deliberately unchanged at v0.10.4 — the bump waits for v0.11.1.

title: Consume LLO's ir_schema_version once published — compare as an opaque token, not a semver
description:
BLOCKED on ley-line-open-348de6 — there is nothing to consume until LLO publishes the field. This is the durable half of the fix; mache-438104 is the unblocked operational half.

Once LLO publishes ir_schema_version (in compatibility.json via compat-gen, and as field @6 on LeylineVersionResponse), mache should read and act on it. Locations, already identified:

1. HANDSHAKE — internal/leyline/version_check.go:56. Compare as an opaque-token INEQUALITY, not with compareSemver. "merkle-ast-v2" is a lineage tag, not a version: there is no ordering between lineages, only same-or-different. Using a semver comparator here would be a category error that happens to compile.

2. THE ONE THAT MATTERS — cmd/build_meta.go:44. Read _meta.ir_schema_version off the parsed .db and stamp it into _mache_meta alongside backend/mache_version/mache_commit/built_at. Today two .db files built under different lineages are indistinguishable; this is the ~9 lines that fixes that. Note mache-438104 proposes recording the leyline BINARY VERSION here as an interim measure available now — if that lands first, this becomes an addition beside it rather than a new mechanism.

3. Consider surfacing it in Provenance() (internal/leyline/provenance.go:52-66), which is already the display surface for "what produced this".

WHILE HERE, two adjacent defects found in the same survey — both small, neither blocking:

- WRONG OPERAND in the existing handshake. version_check.go:35 passes leylineBinaryVersion where daemon.capnp:204-207 specifies "their schema-client version" — i.e. the go.mod schema pin. Invisible today because both are v0.10.4, but internal/leyline/version_parity_test.go:23-28 documents binary/schema divergence as NORMAL (its example is binary 0.8.0 with schema 0.7.1). The moment they diverge, the compat-floor check passes an under-floor client.

- TRIPLICATED FACTS. version_check.go:14, socket.go:832 and socket.go:842 restate LLO's numbers as mache-local constants, while LLO publishes compatibility.json precisely so consumers need not — and mache never reads it (zero hits repo-wide). Reading the published document instead of hand-copying it is the same declare-vs-generate rule this whole thread is about.

Context: LLO v0.11.0 (2026-07-28) is the first release to cross a lineage boundary, merkle-ast-v1 -> merkle-ast-v2, and it publishes nothing about it. Spec: vigil docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-release-contract-design.md §5.1.</description>
<parameter name="acceptance_criteria">With LLO publishing ir_schema_version, mache reads it at the handshake and compares it as an opaque token; a .db carries the lineage it was derived under in _mache_meta; and building a .db under one lineage then serving it under another is detected rather than silent. Verified with two .db files across a lineage-crossing pin bump.

comments.text:
Linked from 0day-d04426 ("Consume LLO release surfaces as map datasources: release-matrix.json + server.json + compatibility.json"), which now declares depends_on this bead.

Same work from the other end. 0day derives the ecosystem dependency map from what repositories already declare, and LLO has asked it to consume compatibility.json. You consume ir_schema_version to decide whether a .db rebuild is required; 0day would consume it to publish that relationship as derived data instead of it living in a comment.

WHAT THE DEPENDENCY ACTUALLY IS, so the link is not read as broader than it is:

An edge needs two sides. compatibility.json lets LLO declare what it PROVIDES; nothing yet lets a consumer declare what it REQUIRES. Until this bead lands — mache declaring its requirement rather than reading the field ad hoc — 0day can only publish an entity property, not a schema/lineage edge. Your durable half is what unlocks the edge half; the property half is unblocked and can proceed regardless.

The constraint recorded on this bead has been carried across verbatim, because it is the part most likely to be lost in translation: ir_schema_version is an opaque lineage tag with no ordering, while compat_min_schema_version in the same file IS an ordered semver range. Two fields, one file, two comparators — and using semver on the first is, as this bead puts it, a category error that happens to compile. Any edge 0day derives will compare lineage for equality only.

Context worth having: 0day RESERVES `schema` and `lineage` as edge kinds and states in its published contract that they "become derivable when a producer declares them; until then their absence is honest". LLO has now declared. This bead is the consumer side of the same promise — which is why it is the blocker rather than a nice-to-have.
