title: Capnp-default consumption + retire SQL _lsp_refs fallback (T8.8 mirror)
description:
Cross-repo paired bead for **ley-line-open T8.8** (mache-internal scope; no LLO blocker).

## Why

PR #356 shipped capnp readthrough as **opt-in** via `dbPathProvider`. Today canonical-view consumers default to the SQL JOIN path (`_lsp_refs` × `_ast`). That means be6136-class bugs (column-name-as-protocol disagreements between LLO writer and mache reader) are *prevention via flag*, not *structurally precluded*. A new contributor writing a `find_smells` rule against `_lsp_refs` columns tomorrow silently reintroduces the failure surface.

## Concrete deliverables

1. **Flip default**: `dbPathProvider` opt-in → capnp consumption is the default. Either remove the toggle entirely or invert it (default-on, opt-OUT for tests that need to verify SQL fallback explicitly).

2. **Migrate canonical-view consumers**: every consumer of `_lsp_refs` SQL columns (`v_refs` view + any direct queries) switches to reading from `_capnp_binding_refs` TEMP table. Audit:
   - `internal/ingest/sqlite_writer.go` `v_refs` view definition
   - `cmd/serve_find_smells.go` rules that JOIN `_lsp_refs`
   - `internal/refsvtab/refs_module.go` (the refs vtab implementation)
   - Any other consumer found by `grep -rn "_lsp_refs"`

3. **Remove SQL fallback path** once (2) is complete. Delete the dual-read code in `binding_log.go` / canonical view glue. The `_capnp_binding_refs` becomes the only source of truth for canonical-view queries.

4. **Mark `_lsp_refs` columns as legacy/deprecated** in any code-comment that referenced them as the contract. Update `ADR-0013` references in mache to point at LLO's ADR-0014 + the `BindingRecord` schema instead.

## Acceptance

- `dbPathProvider` no longer needs to be opt-in (default-on or removed)
- `grep -rn "_lsp_refs"` in mache returns 0 production consumers (test fixtures may keep it for legacy-LLO compatibility tests)
- Falsifiability A + B both pass against capnp-only path

- **The actual structural preclusion of be6136-class bugs.** Today they're flag-preventable; after T8.8+T8.9 they're impossible (no SQL surface to disagree on).

title: nodes.record holds two storage classes — ingest writes BLOB, write-back writes TEXT
description:
Distinct from mache-4b8a42 (declared affinity), though found while fixing it. That bead fixed the column's DECLARED type; this is about the VALUES the two writers put in it.

The same column receives two different SQLite storage classes depending on which writer touched the node last:

    internal/ingest/sqlite_writer.go:~460   record = n.Data              ([]byte -> BLOB)
    internal/graph/writable_graph.go:99     string(content)              (string -> TEXT)

So a freshly built .db has BLOB records everywhere; edit one file through the NFS mount and that single node silently becomes TEXT while its siblings stay BLOB.

WHY IT MATTERS: SQLite never considers a BLOB equal to a TEXT value.

    -- same 25-byte content, stored both ways
    SELECT id, typeof(record), record = 'func f() int { return 7 }' FROM nodes;
      ingested    | blob | 0     <-- does not match
      writtenback | text | 1     <-- matches

    SELECT id, record LIKE '%return 7%' FROM nodes;
      ingested    | 1          <-- LIKE coerces, fine
      writtenback | 1

    length(record) is 25 for both.

So `LIKE` and `length()` are safe, and `=` is not. Any query doing exact content equality matches ONLY nodes that have been written back, and silently misses every ingested node — which is essentially all of them.

NOT CURRENTLY EXPLOITED — verified, which is why this is P2 and does not block the mache-4b8a42 merge. Every production read of `record` either selects it by id/kind (internal/graph/nodes_table_reader.go:250, internal/materialize/{materialize,json}.go, sqlite_writer.go:617) or uses LIKE/length. No production SQL and no shipped smell rule compares `record` with `=`. Go-side reads scan into sql.NullString / []byte, and the driver converts both classes transparently.

It is a trap, not an outage: the first rule or query that reaches for `WHERE record = ?` gets a silent, partial, and confusingly INVERTED result — it works on exactly the nodes a developer is most likely to have hand-edited while testing, and fails on everything else.

FIX — pick one deliberately, since they are not equivalent:
  A. Make write-back bind []byte too (one-line: drop the string() conversion). Both
     writers then produce BLOB. Consistent, minimal, no artifact change. But `=`
     stays broken for everyone, so the trap remains, just uniformly.
  B. Make ingest bind string(n.Data). Both writers produce TEXT. Now that the column
     is TEXT-affinity (mache-4b8a42), this is the natural storage class for what is
     genuinely text content, and both `=` and LIKE work. Costs a []byte->string
     conversion per node at ingest (negligible) and CHANGES THE STORAGE CLASS OF EVERY
     EXISTING ARTIFACT — content bytes are identical, but typeof() flips blob->text,
     so anything asserting typeof or comparing dbs byte-wise will notice.

B is the better end state; A is the safer patch. Recommend B, done deliberately as its
own change with a note in the release notes, NOT folded into the affinity fix — that
one is provably projection-neutral (verified byte-identical rebuild) and should stay
that way.

Either way, add an assertion that both writers agree, so the two paths cannot drift
apart again.

comments.text:
FIXED — merged to main as 09a2fbe (PR #569), second commit.

Chose option B from the description: SQLiteWriter now binds a *string rather than n.Data ([]byte), so both writers produce TEXT. Now that the column has TEXT affinity (mache-4b8a42, same PR), TEXT is the natural storage class for what is genuinely text content, and `=` works alongside LIKE.

Option A (make write-back bind []byte instead) was rejected: it would have been consistent but left `=` broken uniformly — a consistent trap rather than an inconsistent one.

ARTIFACT CHANGE, as flagged: content bytes are unchanged (rebuilt fixture is 7 nodes / 254 bytes before and after) but typeof(record) flips blob -> text for every ingested node. Anything asserting typeof, or diffing two .db files bytewise across this commit, will see it. Reads are unaffected — Go scans into sql.NullString / []byte and the driver converts both classes transparently. Worth a release note; called out in the commit message.

Test: internal/graph/writable_graph_storage_class_test.go — writes identical content through both paths and requires the storage class AND the exact-equality result to be indistinguishable, plus asserts LIKE still matches both (guarding against a fix that trades one broken operator for another). Verified to fail on all three assertions with the old []byte bind.

Kept as a separate commit from the affinity fix deliberately: that one is provably projection-neutral and this one is not, and a reviewer should be able to see which is which.

Plus `go test ./internal/graph/ ./internal/ingest/` green.

title: Use BindingRecord.qualifier in fan_out_skew (replaces mache-42118e AST rewalk; T8.7 mirror)
description:
Cross-repo paired bead for **ley-line-open T8.7** (gated on T8.7 landing + mache vendoring updated schemas).

## Why

mache-42118e was filed as an internal AST rewalk to recover qualifier (the LHS of `selector_expression`) for the structural `fan_out_skew` metric. T8.7 changes the proposition: **LLO emits qualifier directly in BindingRecord**, eliminating the need for mache's `internal/ingest/ast_walker.go::ExtractQualifiedCalls` to recover that fact.

This is the T8 thesis applied: producer emits the structural fact, consumer projects. Without this, T8 leaks — every new "structural fact mache wants" becomes a parallel AST walker.

## Sequence

1. Wait for ley-line-open T8.7 to land — `BindingRecord.qualifier @7 :Text` shipped on main
2. Re-vendor schemas: `task gen-bindings` (existing target from PR #353 fixup) — pulls updated `binding.capnp` and regenerates `internal/lsp/bindings/binding.capnp.go`
3. Update `_capnp_binding_refs` TEMP table to expose qualifier as a column
4. Rewrite `fan_out_skew` SQL in `cmd/serve_find_smells.go` to use `qualifier` directly:
   - Today: `COUNT(DISTINCT token) per referrer` + naming-pattern exemptions for projection functions (PR #355 drive-by)
   - Tomorrow: `COUNT(DISTINCT (qualifier, token)) per referrer` — structural; no naming exemptions needed
5. Close mache-42118e — fully resolved by upstream schema change rather than internal rewalker

- `internal/lsp/bindings/binding.capnp.go` (regenerated)
- `internal/lsp/binding_log.go` (expose qualifier on Reader)
- `internal/ingest/sqlite_writer.go` (qualifier column on `_capnp_binding_refs`)
- `cmd/serve_find_smells.go` (rewrite `fan_out_skew` query)

## Acceptance

- `fan_out_skew` rule no longer relies on naming-pattern exemptions
- mache-42118e closes (resolved structurally)
- mache's `internal/ingest/ast_walker.go::ExtractQualifiedCalls` is now duplicate-of-LLO; document and queue for retirement (or repurpose for legacy `.db` consumption where capnp isn't present)

title: Auto-leyline serve path bypasses sheaf cascade (frozen .db has no watcher)
description:
## Surfaced by

PR #383 Copilot review comment #4 (https://github.com/agentic-research/mache/pull/383). Documented inline in `cmd/serve.go::buildServeGraph` at the auto-leyline branch.

## The gap

`buildServeGraph` has two ingest paths for directory sources:

1. **Default (auto-leyline)**: runs `leyline parse <dir> -o <tmp.db>`, opens the .db via `openDBGraph`. Fast cold-start (no CGO tree-sitter). **Returns nil `*SheafInvalidator`** because the .db is frozen at parse time — no watcher constructed.
2. **MACHE_NO_LEYLINE=1 (in-process)**: runs the in-process Engine + SitterWalker, constructs a watcher, returns a non-nil `*SheafInvalidator`. The full PR #383 cascade wiring engages here.

So in the default leyline-installed setup, agents get fast cold-start but **stale results after edits** — the watcher → sheaf cascade is structurally disabled. Only the MACHE_NO_LEYLINE fallback exercises the moat.

## Two paths to close it

**A. Flip auto-leyline from one-shot to managed daemon.** Replace `leyline parse` with a `leyline daemon --source <dir>` subprocess that watches the source dir, reparses on change, and emits `sheaf.invalidate` events. Mache subscribes to those events and flushes the SQLiteGraph caches accordingly. Requires:
  - [[mache-c14c43]] (subscribe to sheaf.invalidate events)
  - A new auto-leyline mode that picks daemon vs. one-shot based on whether mache is in serve mode (long-lived) vs. CLI mode (one-shot tools like `mache pack`)
  - Cache-flush primitive on SQLiteGraph that's reachable from the subscriber goroutine

**B. Always use in-process ingest for serve mode.** Forgo the auto-leyline speedup for the long-lived `mache serve` command and use MemoryStore + watcher unconditionally. Auto-leyline still applies to one-shot CLI tools that don't need live invalidation.

Option A is correct architecturally — the daemon owns parsing, mache owns presentation; the event bus is the seam. Option B is a smaller refactor but trades parse speed for moat correctness in the dominant agent-workflow case.

## Acceptance

- `TestBuildServeGraph_ReturnsInvalidatorForDir` runs under the default (leyline-available) setup and asserts non-nil invalidator.
- Edit a file, watcher fires, daemon's sheaf cascade reaches mache via the event bus, MCP-tool results reflect the edit within budget (mache-49bf9a's `<500ms` target).

## Dependencies

- Blocks: live cascade in default deployment
- Depends on: [[mache-c14c43]] (event subscribe) if going with Option A
- Related to: [[mache-49bf9a]] (the moat audit that surfaces the original wiring requirement)

title: serve.go auto-leyline comment + log message carry three stale post-v0.18.0 claims
description:
Found by the user reviewing cmd/serve.go:439-462. Three claims, one accurate, two not:

1. WRONG - serve.go:439 says the fallback is 'the in-process Engine + SitterWalker path'. SitterWalker was deleted in v0.18.0 (ADR-0012 step 4, mache-37ae8b). The fallback is Engine + ASTWalker.

2. ACCURATE - the log's 'frozen .db - sheaf cascade NOT engaged for live edits' is the real, still-open gap tracked as mache-6c9e1d. mache-018eee (closed) fixed only cache invalidation (ReIngestFile dropping stale ASTWalker caches), and its commit body said so explicitly: live reparse of a leyline-backed serve was left as remaining work.

3. MISLEADING - the log tells users to 'set MACHE_NO_LEYLINE=1 for the in-process watcher path'. The flag does have that routing effect (serve.go:458 gates the auto-.db path, and the in-process MemoryStore path does construct a watcher - the comment at serve.go:446 says so). But since v0.18.0 that path's sole walker is ASTWalker, which needs leyline to pre-parse _ast, and the SAME flag makes internal/leyline/socket.go:899 refuse to download leyline. So the escape hatch routes you to a path that still requires the binary the flag forbids fetching. It works only when a leyline matching the exact pin is already on PATH - which the message does not say.

Note the user's initial framing was that MACHE_NO_LEYLINE means only 'do not auto-download'; it actually has both effects. The defect is the unstated precondition, not the routing.

title: MCP startup and errors should report the resolved mache binary path and version
description:
Rescoped 2026-07-27. This bead previously bundled three claims ("Diagnose Codex mache PATH skew, exit SIGTRAP, and missing MCP root"); see the triage comment for the full diagnosis. Summary of what changed:

  - PATH skew: root-caused, NOT a mache defect. A stale homebrew install
    (/opt/homebrew/bin/mache -> Cellar/mache/0.1.31, binary reports v0.6.6
    commit dc0dc08) shadows ~/.local/bin/mache (v0.19.0-10-g1c3d812) whenever
    PATH is ordered homebrew-first, which Codex exec does and the interactive
    shell does not. Fixed by `brew uninstall mache` or PATH ordering.
  - SIGTRAP on exit 2: not reproducible. Both the stale v0.6.6 and current
    builds exit 0 for --version and --help. Environment-specific to the Codex
    sandbox under LLO; needs a fresh reproduction in that environment.
  - MCP "workspace root unavailable": duplicate of mache-76c919, which has the
    same error text from the same context and far more accumulated context.

WHAT REMAINS — the one piece that is real mache work.

The whole episode cost an afternoon because there was no way to answer "which mache is this, and where does it think it is?" from the tool's own output. The MCP server should say so itself.

On startup, and in the text of errors that depend on it, report:
  - the resolved executable path (os.Executable(), symlinks resolved) and its version
  - the workspace root it resolved, or why it could not resolve one

Today a root failure surfaces as "workspace root unavailable (context deadline exceeded)" with no indication of which binary produced it, so a version skew and a genuine root-resolution bug are indistinguishable from the message alone. Those are different problems with different fixes, and the error should separate them.

Keep it cheap: this is a log line at startup and a few extra fields in one error path, not a diagnostics subsystem. The value is that the next occurrence of this class self-identifies instead of requiring someone to audit PATH by hand.

comments.text: Reproduced in Codex non-interactive exec from /private/tmp/mache-llo-v0104: command -v mache=/opt/homebrew/bin/mache (ahead of /Users/jamesgardner/.local/bin/mache); it reports v0.6.6 dc0dc08 then SIGTRAPs in runtime.exit with exit=2. This is a real PATH precedence + stale binary fault, independent of the current branch-built bin/mache.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
TRIAGED — this bead conflates three claims. Two are resolved, one is a duplicate, and only a fraction is actual mache work. Diagnosed 2026-07-27 without needing the Codex environment.

CLAIM 1 — "mache --version resolves stale v0.6.6 (dc0dc08)". REAL, ROOT-CAUSED, and not a mache defect.

There are two mache binaries on PATH:

    /Users/jamesgardner/.local/bin/mache   v0.19.0-10-g1c3d812  (commit 1c3d812)
    /opt/homebrew/bin/mache                v0.6.6               (commit dc0dc08)  <-- the bead's binary

The homebrew one is a symlink into Cellar/mache/0.1.31 (note: formula version 0.1.31, binary reports v0.6.6 — the formula's own versioning is inconsistent, worth a separate look if we still publish it). Codex exec resolves homebrew-first; the interactive shell resolves ~/.local/bin first. Same PATH mechanism, different ordering, different binary. Nothing in mache chooses this.

Fix is environmental: `brew uninstall mache`, or reorder PATH. No code change resolves it.

CLAIM 2 — "prints normally, then SIGTRAPs in runtime.exit and exits 2". NOT REPRODUCIBLE from the binary.

    /opt/homebrew/bin/mache --version  -> exit 0
    /opt/homebrew/bin/mache --help     -> exit 0
    ./mache (v0.19.0) --version/--help -> exit 0

Both the stale v0.6.6 and current builds exit cleanly. The SIGTRAP is therefore specific to the Codex exec sandbox under LLO, not to any mache build — on macOS an exit-time SIGTRAP usually points at hardened-runtime / library-validation under a sandbox, which would implicate the codesigning step (`task build` does `codesign -s - --force --deep --entitlements entitlements.plist`) interacting with the sandbox, not mache's Go code. Reproducing requires that environment; it cannot be chased from here.

The AC line "supported mache version/help exits 0" is ALREADY SATISFIED on every binary available locally. Do not spend time on it without a fresh reproduction.

CLAIM 3 — "Connected Mache MCP get_overview reports workspace root unavailable". DUPLICATE of mache-76c919, which is titled exactly "MCP get_overview should resolve the active repo or accept an explicit path" and quotes the same error ("workspace root unavailable (context deadline exceeded)") from the same Codex-under-ley-line-open context. That bead has 9 comments of context; this one has 1. Track it there.

WHAT ACTUAL MACHE WORK REMAINS

One thing, and it is the genuinely useful part of the original AC: mache should make this class self-diagnosing. When the MCP server starts, and when it errors, it should report the resolved executable path and version alongside the workspace root. Had it done so, "which mache am I even talking to" would have been answerable from the error text instead of requiring a PATH audit.

That is small, testable, and independent of both the environment issue and the duplicate. Recommend rescoping this bead to exactly that and dropping the diagnosis framing from the title.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
PATH SKEW RESOLVED LOCALLY 2026-07-28, and the root cause was not what this bead (or my earlier triage) said.

    before:  /Users/jamesgardner/.local/bin/mache   0.19.0-10-g1c3d812
             /opt/homebrew/bin/mache                v0.6.6  (commit dc0dc08)
    after:   /Users/jamesgardner/.local/bin/mache   0.19.0-10-g1c3d812   (only)

`brew uninstall mache` removed it. Codex resolved homebrew-first, the interactive shell resolved ~/.local/bin first — same PATH mechanism, different ordering, different binary.

IT WAS NEVER A STALE MACHE INSTALL. The Cellar formula is kiln's:

    class Mache < Formula
      desc "Structural code projection as MCP — mache + ley-line in one binary"
      homepage "https://github.com/agentic-research/kiln"
      version "0.1.31"
      url ".../kiln/releases/download/v#{version}/mache-darwin-arm64"

agentic-research/homebrew-tap carries Formula/mache.rb that installs KILN's bundled
binary under the name `mache`. Its last three commits are "kiln v0.1.31", "v0.1.30",
"v0.1.29" — it tracked kiln releases, never mache's. The formula version (0.1.31) and the
binary's self-reported version (v0.6.6) disagree because they are versioning different
things.

WHY THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE UNINSTALL: this explains recurrence. The user reports having
uninstalled it before, and that is consistent — `brew install mache`, or any upgrade/
reinstall touching that tap, re-establishes the shadow. The Cellar entry was the symptom;
the formula is the mechanism.

Kiln is archived (confirmed by the user). The durable fix is deleting or repointing
Formula/mache.rb in the tap. The user is aware and has deferred it deliberately as part of
release work, so it is NOT tracked here and should not be re-raised as a defect — noted
only so the recurrence path is written down rather than rediscovered by whoever sees a
v0.6.6 mache next.

Worth stating the preference on record since it bears on agent-visible skew: repointing
mache.rb at mache's real releases would be better than deleting it, because mache does
publish binaries and `brew install mache` being CORRECT beats it being absent. Either
resolves the shadow.

THIS BEAD'S REMAINING SCOPE IS UNCHANGED and is the only actionable mache work here: MCP
startup and errors should report the resolved executable path and version alongside the
workspace root. Had they done so, "which mache am I talking to" would have been answerable
from the error text instead of requiring a PATH audit — which is exactly what this
investigation ended up being.

title: find_smells: lang-aware version-pin drift rule (trace canonical version per repo:lang, flag stale doc/code pins)
description:
User (2026-06-24): version-tracing "belongs in repo / should follow the lang paradigm" — a smell rule that traces "the version of code in <repo:lang>" and flags pins that disagree. LLO built a stopgap (Taskfile readme:version-check: reads rs/ll-open/cli/Cargo.toml, fails CI if README pins drift) and explicitly noted the upstream solution is mache's drift_doc_outdated_count (mache-e1b6c8).

SHAPE: a find_smells rule (sibling of / extension to drift_doc_outdated_count) that:
1. Resolves the CANONICAL version for the repo's language paradigm:
   - Go: internal/buildinfo/version.txt (mache's clean base) or go.mod module version
   - Rust: Cargo.toml [package] version (or workspace.package.version)
   - JS/TS: package.json version
2. Extracts version pins from docs/README/code (e.g. `<tool>:X.Y.Z`, `version X.Y.Z`, backtick-fenced semvers).
3. Flags any pin that != the canonical version (drift = doc/code stale vs source of truth).

This is the per-lang generalization of drift_doc_outdated_count's numeric-claim check, specialized to versions. The canonical-source-per-lang map mirrors lang.Registry's paradigm-awareness. Lands ADR-0018's doc-drift-as-executable-specs vision for versions specifically.

Relates: mache-e1b6c8 (ADR-0018 doc-drift rollout — the home), mache-048fb6 (cross-lang rule generalization), the LLO readme:version-check stopgap (ley-line-open Taskfile). Pairs with the now-merged-pending git-derive version work (PR #437): version.txt is mache's canonical Go version source.

title: BLOCKER: find_callees only restored on mount/in-process, NOT default `mache serve` .db paths (regression vs main)
description:
CONFIRMED empirically (adversarial review of PR #533, verified by owner). The scoped-_ast find_callees fix (mache-fd9982) needs BOTH persisted Properties (ast_source_id/ast_scope_id) AND a live _ast table — but they never coexist on a served .db: a --schema build has Properties + NO _ast (runBuildViaLeylineSchema discards _ast, cmd/build.go); auto-leyline `serve <dir>` has _ast + AST-shaped nodes with NO Properties. So GetCallees returns [] on both. Only mache mount + the MACHE_NO_LEYLINE MemoryStore path (in-process projection + live _ast handle) work. serve find_callees worked on main via tree-sitter → this is a REGRESSION. Retaining _ast is prohibitive (_ast table = 228MB + 162MB index for the whole repo).

FIX (hybrid, no bloat): the schema db ALREADY carries node_refs (per-construct call tokens: node_refs(token, node_id=construct/source)) + node_defs. For backends WITHOUT _ast (served built .db), resolve find_callees from node_refs (the construct's calls) → node_defs (their definitions) — no _ast needed, data already projected. Keep the scoped-_ast qualified path for backends WITH _ast (mount). Tradeoff: node_refs stores bare tokens (qualifier precision loss = cross-package same-name over-match) — acceptable, or store qualified tokens at projection. Also F3 (engine_walk.go:425-433 persists ast_scope_id for EVERY ASTScope match incl "$" grouping + package matches → whole-file scope = last-file-wins for functions//package root): only persist for real leaf constructs, or skip grouping/package nodes. F4 (sqlite_graph_callees.go:46 ignores record-read error → silent []): surface it. F2: the current tests hand-set Properties + _ast so they pass even with this gap — add a real projection→serve→GetCallees test.
acceptance_criteria: find_callees returns correct callees on BOTH default serve paths, proven by a REAL end-to-end test (projection → serve-shaped .db → GetCallees, NOT hand-set fixtures): (1) `mache serve <schema-built.db>` — the primary MCP build-then-serve workflow; (2) confirm mount still works. A test that builds a --schema .db, opens it as a SQLiteGraph (no _ast), and asserts find_callees resolves. F3: grouping/package dirs (functions/, package root) must NOT return a whole-file call union — either no callees or correctly scoped. `go test ./internal/graph/ ./cmd/` green.

title: Scoping hardening: queryCallPattern LIKE treats _ as wildcard; dedupAddrTokens exact-scope carve-out untested
description: Adversarial review of PR #533 (verified, no wrong answer TODAY — both are latent). (1) queryCallPattern (ast_walker_calls.go:364) scopes with `n_leaf.id LIKE scopePrefix||'/%'`; ley-line node ids contain literal `_` (function_declaration_1) which SQL LIKE treats as any-char wildcards — looser than a literal prefix, and inconsistent with the HasPrefix scheme ExtractCallsScoped now uses (line 97). No colliding real id exists (fixed kind vocab) but it's fragile + a filename containing `%` could over-scope. (2) dedupAddrTokens (ast_walker_extract.go:48) added `r.nodeID != scopeID` to let an exact self-match through, diverging from the old SQL `LIKE scopeID||'/%'` (never self-matches) — the comment claims byte-parity but it's a real behavior addition (git show 144a6ed), untested (no test references ExtractAddressRefsScoped/dedupAddrTokens), asymmetric with ExtractCallsScoped. Harden both.
acceptance_criteria: queryCallPattern's scope filter no longer relies on SQL LIKE wildcard semantics for the id prefix (escape _ and %, or filter by HasPrefix in Go to match the ExtractCallsScoped sibling at ast_walker_calls.go:97). dedupAddrTokens' exact-scope-match branch (ast_walker_extract.go:48, r.nodeID==scopeID) is either removed for consistency with ExtractCallsScoped or covered by a test asserting the intended semantics. title: Pre-existing data race: e.childSeen map mutated without lock; concurrent ReIngestFile (watcher) can crash
description: Adversarial review of PR #533 (verified pre-existing, NOT introduced by this diff, but downstream of ReIngestFile which the PR touches). e.childSeen is mutated with ZERO locking at engine_ingest.go:117-124 and engine_walk.go:330-337, while the sibling e.routedFiles IS e.mu-guarded (engine_treesitter.go:316-318). The live-edit file watcher (internal/ingest/watcher.go debouncedOnChange) runs one debounce timer per changed path; two different files changing in the same debounce window (mass gofmt -w ., branch switch) fire on separate goroutines and both call engine.ReIngestFile concurrently on the same shared Engine. Two files sharing a parent dir (common) → concurrent unsynchronized map write on childSeen[parentID] → go test -race failure / production crash. The PR's InvalidateSource wiring makes concurrent ReIngestFile more relevant. Guard childSeen with e.mu.
acceptance_criteria: e.childSeen (map[string]map[string]bool) is guarded by e.mu on all read/write paths (engine_ingest.go:117-124, engine_walk.go:330-337), matching how e.routedFiles is already guarded. title: Expose ingest engine + materializers as public pkg/ API
description:
Move the ingest engine and materializer interfaces from internal/ to pkg/ so downstream consumers (venturi, smelt) can import mache as a Go library instead of shelling out.

## What to expose
- `pkg/ingest.Engine` — schema loading, record processing, tree building
- `pkg/ingest.Walker`, `pkg/ingest.Match` — interfaces
- `pkg/ingest.LoadSchema()` or `pkg/schema.Load()` — parse schema JSON
- `pkg/materialize.Materializer` interface + `ForFormat()`
- `pkg/materialize.SQLiteMaterializer`, `ZIPMaterializer`
- `pkg/materialize.BoltDBMaterializer` (behind build tag)
- `pkg/graph.MemoryStore` or equivalent in-process store

## Consumer usage (venturi)
```go
schema, _ := mache.LoadSchema("schemas/trivy-os-schema.json")
store := graph.NewMemoryStore()
engine := ingest.NewEngine(schema, store)
engine.Ingest("data/amazon/results/results.db")
mat, _ := materialize.ForFormat("boltdb")
mat.Materialize(store.Path(), "trivy.db")
```

## Why
- No shelling out to mache binary
- No mount point / NFS / FUSE needed for projection
- Tests run as pure Go (no exec.Command, no timeouts, no hang risk)
- Schema can be embedded in consumer binary via embed
- Materializer choice is a Go function call, not a CLI flag

## Design notes
- Keep internal/ as implementation detail, pkg/ as stable API
- CLI (cmd/mount.go, cmd/build.go) becomes a thin wrapper over pkg/
- Template FuncMap should be exported so consumers can add custom functions

title: PR-A: migrate parse-side consumers off in-process tree-sitter (schema-on-leyline, FCA inference, linter→_ast, writeback→LLO validate op)
description:
First of the 2-PR CGO-removal shape (user decision 2026-07-14; PR-B = mache-37ae8b deletion). Migrates the 4 remaining parse-side consumers so PR-B is a pure deletion. Verify: task check.

## Scope
1. **Schema-on-leyline path** (user decision: teach leyline path schemas, unblocks the composite action's schema input): `mache build --schema X` on the leyline path = `leyline parse` → run the existing pure-Go Engine+ASTWalker with the schema over the _ast db → schema-shaped nodes table. Removes the warn-and-ignore in runBuildViaLeyline (cmd/build.go:239-250) and lets the action drop its `--backend tree-sitter` forcing (version-gated, same reconvergence pattern as --tags=gate in cmd/find_smells_action_test.go).

title: 24 test files hand-build LLO-shaped tables, so fixtures drift from the producer silently
description:
Surfaced by the LLO boundary rule (internal/lint/llo_boundary_test.go, mache-e64f36). Scoped OUT of that rule deliberately — it is a real problem but a different one from a layering violation, and allowlisting 24 files there would bury the three production entries that actually describe the boundary.

24 test files CREATE and INSERT LLO-owned tables (_ast, _source, _lsp, _lsp_defs, _lsp_refs, ...) to build fixtures by hand, among them:

    cmd/build_leyline_coverage_test.go     cmd/cache_ast_test.go
    cmd/cache_test.go                      cmd/call_extractor_ast_test.go
    cmd/dead_code_skip_list_retreat_test.go  ... and 19 more

WHY IT MATTERS: a hand-built fixture asserts against mache's IDEA of LLO's schema, not LLO's actual schema. When LLO changes shape, the fixtures keep passing and the production consumer breaks — the tests actively mask the regression they exist to catch. This is not theoretical for this producer: LLO ships _ast schema changes in PATCH releases (0.7.4 added container_node_id, 0.7.5 added canonical_kind), and v0.11.0 changed how node_hash is DERIVED without changing any column at all.

Worse, the fixtures encode a SUBSET. A test creating `_ast (node_id, node_kind, start_row)` passes regardless of what else LLO emits, so a consumer that starts depending on a new column has no failing fixture to tell it the fixture is stale.

THE PATTERN ALREADY EXISTS IN-REPO: internal/ingest/leyline_ast_test_helper_test.go's attachLeylineAST runs the PINNED leyline binary to produce a real _ast db, and skips when it is unavailable. That is the shape — fixtures generated by the producer, not hand-modelled after it. tools/gen-lsp-fixture/main.go should move the same way (it is allowlisted in the boundary rule with that note).

SCOPE / SEQUENCING
Not all 24 need converting, and converting them naively would make the suite depend on a leyline binary being installed — attachLeylineAST skips rather than fails for exactly that reason, and a skipped test is its own hazard. Suggested order:
  1. Inventory which of the 24 assert on SCHEMA SHAPE vs merely need any table to exist.
     Only the first group is genuinely at risk; the second can keep a minimal local table.
  2. Convert the shape-dependent ones to the attachLeylineAST pattern.
  3. Replace tools/gen-lsp-fixture with a leyline invocation.
  4. Then widen internal/lint/llo_boundary_test.go to cover _test.go files — a one-line
     change (drop the HasSuffix "_test.go" skip) once the count is small enough that the
     allowlist stays readable.

Step 4 is the close condition: the rule covering tests is what stops this recurring.

NOTE the interaction with mache-e64f36: if delegation lands, several of these fixtures disappear along with the code they test rather than needing conversion. Worth doing the inventory (step 1) before investing in conversion, so effort is not spent on tests that are about to be deleted.

comments.text:
Type-driven-correctness audit (2026-07-30, tree 6a37bb9) re-measured this and found the mechanism is worse than "drift risk" — a fixture's `CREATE TABLE` literal is a **hidden test parameter that selects which SQL the rule under test executes**. Recording the measurement, the load-bearing mechanism, a proposed shape, and an explicit not-in-scope list.

## Re-measured: 34 files, not 24

`grep -l 'CREATE TABLE (node_refs|node_defs|_ast)' **/*_test.go` → **34 test files** (was 24 when this bead was filed). Normalizing each DDL to (column list, has-PK, WITHOUT-ROWID):

**node_refs — 10 distinct shapes across test files:**
| shape | files |
|---|---|
| (token, node_id) PK WITHOUT ROWID | 13 |
| (token, node_id) PK, rowid | 4 |
| (token, node_id) no PK | 3 |
| (token, node_id, source_id, node_hash) | 2 |
| (token, node_id, source_id, container_node_id, qualifier) | 2 |
| (token, node_id, container_node_id, qualifier) | 1 |
| (token, node_id, container_node_id) | 1 |
| (token, node_id, qualifier) | 1 |
| (token, node_id, source_id, node_hash, container_node_id) PK WITHOUT ROWID | 1 |
| (token, node_id, node_hash) | 1 |

**_ast — 4 distinct shapes across test files** (5/6/9/10 columns; the 9-col no-node_hash variant in 14 files, the 10-col node_hash variant in 3). The audit's "~nine _ast spellings" does not hold; four is the real number.

**Correcting one audit claim:** it asserted ZERO fixtures reproduce either production shape. Half-wrong. The mache standalone shape — `internal/ingest/sqlite_writer.go:86`, `node_refs(token, node_id, PRIMARY KEY(token,node_id)) WITHOUT ROWID` — IS reproduced exactly by 13 test files. What is true, and verified by running `leyline parse` (v0.13.0) and dumping sqlite_master, is that **zero fixtures reproduce leyline's shape**:

    CREATE TABLE node_refs (
        token TEXT NOT NULL, node_id TEXT NOT NULL, source_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        container_node_id TEXT, qualifier TEXT,
        node_hash BLOB REFERENCES node_content(node_hash))   -- no PK, not WITHOUT ROWID

The closest (2 files) omits node_hash; the one self-described "Leyline column shape" fixture omits `qualifier`, omits `container_node_id` on node_defs, and ADDS a PK+WITHOUT ROWID leyline does not have — filed separately as [[mache-e3f3bf]].

## THE LOAD-BEARING POINT: DDL is a hidden test parameter

`ensureCanonicalViews` (cmd/smell_refs_views.go, 381 lines) PROBES for columns and emits a **structurally different `v_refs`/`v_defs` body per combination**. Verified probe sites: `_lsp_defs.def_token` (:39), `node_defs.node_hash` (:67), `node_defs.canonical_kind` (:82), `node_refs.node_hash` (:86), `node_refs.container_node_id` (:104), `node_refs.qualifier` (:119), `_ast.node_id` (:235), `node_content.token` (:243), `node_refs.source_id` (:253).

The sharpest instance, :156-158:

    refsReferrerExpr := "node_id"
    if hasRefsContainer {
        refsReferrerExpr = "COALESCE(NULLIF(container_node_id, ''), node_id)"
    }

So a rule tested against a 2-column node_refs runs the **degraded arm**; production runs the **full arm**; and neither side notices, because the fixture never declares which producer it is modelling — it only implies one, in SQL, by omission.

Compounding it: `node_refs.node_id` has TWO INCOMPATIBLE MEANINGS, documented in that file at :91-103. The mache/tree-sitter projection puts the ENCLOSING CONSTRUCT in node_id. leyline puts the CALL-SITE LEAF there and the enclosing def in container_node_id. **A fixture picks a meaning implicitly, by what it INSERTs** — there is no place in the test where it says which.

## Same defect class as mache-e3d9bb

mache-e3d9bb was: Children had two accessors that silently disagreed; the fix was removing the second way to ask. This is that, one layer down — 34 independent ways to state a schema, silently disagreeing about which producer they model. Same fix shape: **remove a test's ability to state a schema at all.**

## Proposed: `internal/fixturedb`

- A closed `Producer` type — `Leyline | Standalone` — with an unexported field so zero-value and third-party construction are impossible. A fixture cannot exist without naming its producer.
- A `Builder` with **no method that accepts SQL, DDL, a column name, or a table name**. Removing the ability, not documenting the convention.
- Semantic row constructors that make the node_id ambiguity into distinct parameters, e.g. `Ref(token string, from ConstructID, at SiteID, qualifier string)` — `from` is the enclosing def, `at` is the call site. The Standalone producer collapses them; the Leyline producer keeps them apart. The test states meaning; the builder states shape.
- `Build()` returns a querier **already wired through `ensureCanonicalViews`**, so a test cannot forget it.
- **The Leyline DDL must be DERIVED**, by snapshotting `sqlite_master` from the pinned binary — not hand-written, or the abstraction reproduces the bug in one place instead of 34. That makes [[mache-33f69d]] (pin ley-line's table contract) the natural supplier; linking it as a dependency.

## Migration honesty

Nominal blast radius is large — **194 `sql.Open` sites across 86 files** repo-wide — but that is not the real number. Only **11 files reference `ensureCanonicalViews`** (7 of them tests), and **34 test files** hand-build one of the three tables. The rest use unrelated tables and must be left alone. Budget for the migration to SURFACE BUGS rather than just move code: each of the 34 sites has to DECIDE which producer it meant, and some of them have never been asked. Expect findings.

The exit ratchet is already written into this bead's acceptance criteria: `internal/lint/llo_boundary_test.go:146` is the `strings.HasSuffix(path, "_test.go")` skip; deleting that clause is the one-line widening. (Note: there is no comment AT line 146 saying so — the plan lives here, in this bead, not in the source. Worth adding a pointer comment there so a reader of the lint file finds this bead.)

## Explicitly NOT to be unified — do not over-reach

- **The four e2e harnesses.** They answer four different questions and already share `runToolMatrix`. Leave them.
- **The `internal/testfixtures` registry vs the small adversarial rule fixtures.** Opposite requirements: one wants realism, the other wants a minimal input that isolates one rule arm.
- **memory-vs-sqlite backend separation.** That separation is what CAUGHT mache-e3d9bb and mache-655e98. Collapsing it destroys the detector.
- **`internal/lltest`.**
- **The named Taskfile signal targets.**
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
PR #592 (branch `feat/fixturedb`) ships the builder + both derivations + the exit ratchet + the first migration batch. Auto-merge deliberately NOT armed — more migration commits are queued for this branch.

## What shipped

`internal/fixturedb`, with the three load-bearing properties intact:
1. No method accepts SQL, DDL, a column name or a table name. DDL is unexported, no escape hatch.
2. `Ref(token, from ConstructID, at SiteID, qualifier string, detail ...Detail)` — the two meanings of `node_refs.node_id` are now two typed parameters. Leyline writes `node_id=<at>, container_node_id=<from>`; Standalone writes `node_id=<from>` and structurally cannot express `<at>`.
3. `Build() (path, *FixtureDB)` installs the canonical views itself, via an installer `cmd` registers once in `init()`. It also pins `SetMaxOpenConns(1)` centrally — TEMP views are per-connection, and every fixture was deciding that for itself (most did not).

One design deviation from the sketch, flagged for review: optional args are DECLARATIVE STRUCTS (`Where`, `Detail`) rather than functional options. Functional options tripped the repo's own `duplicate_code` gate — nine structurally identical one-line closures — and the struct form reads better anyway ("state a fact", not "configure a builder").

## The derivation (mache-33f69d's job, done minimally here)

mache-33f69d is UNSTARTED, so I built only what this needed — and both halves are re-derived by tests, not snapshots-of-snapshots:

- **Leyline**: `leyline parse` on a two-file corpus with the PINNED binary, `SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master`, byte-copied into `schema_leyline.go`. `TestLeylineSchema_MatchesPinnedBinary` re-runs that derivation and diffs. Gated (skips without a cached pin), never downloads. Also asserts `leylineSchemaVersion == leyline.PinnedBinaryVersion()` so a pin bump forces a re-derive.
- **Standalone**: reads `internal/ingest/sqlite_writer.go`'s own `schema := ...` literal out of the **Go AST**, executes it, diffs `sqlite_master`. UNGATED — pure Go, no CGO (importing `internal/ingest` would drag tree-sitter into every fixture consumer), no regexp (the repo ratchets those).

Both mutation-proven: adding a PK to ley-line's `node_refs` → red; dropping `nodes.context` from the writer's literal → red.

Ground truth recorded, v0.13.0: `node_refs(token NOT NULL, node_id NOT NULL, source_id NOT NULL, container_node_id, qualifier, node_hash BLOB REFERENCES node_content)`, **no PK, not WITHOUT ROWID**. `node_defs` is the same shape with `canonical_kind` where `qualifier` sits — so it ALSO carries `container_node_id`, which mache-e3f3bf called out. Bare calls store `qualifier` NULL (not `''`), and ley-line dual-emits `fmt.Println`/qualifier-NULL alongside `Println`/qualifier-`fmt` at the SAME node_id — which is why the missing PK matters.

## Findings (3)

**1. `writesTable` in llo_boundary_test.go could never match a table starting with `N`.** It matched `lit.Value` — the raw SOURCE text — where a newline inside an interpreted string is the two characters `\` `n`. The whitespace cutset therefore carried a backslash and an `n`, and since the text is uppercased first, an `N`. `TrimLeft` then ate the leading `N` of `nodes`, `node_content`, `node_defs`, `node_refs`. **`node_content` is in `lloOwnedTables`: the rule has been unable to enforce it since it was written.** Fixed via `strconv.Unquote` so escapes are real characters. This is also why the widening initially found only 24 files instead of 32.

**2. `internal/lltest`'s pinned-binary gate was DEAD.** `pinnedBinaryOrSkip` resolved the LEGACY unversioned `~/.mache/bin/leyline` directly. mache-0acdf6 made the cache version-namespaced and explicitly stopped WRITING the legacy path — so on any machine past that migration, every `lltest.UsePinnedDaemon` / `StartPinnedDaemon` consumer skipped unconditionally. On this machine the legacy file reports 0.10.2 against a v0.13.0 pin. Fixed: added `leyline.CachedPinnedBinary()` (exported wrapper over `resolveCachedPinned`) and `lltest.PinnedBinaryOrSkip`. **Worth a separate look at what those gates have not been running.**

**3. `cmd/cache.go`'s `_ast` DDL has drifted from ley-line's** — no `node_hash` column, and `NOT NULL` missing on start_row/start_col/end_row/end_col. Not fixed here; it is the allowlisted mache-e64f36 violation, and this is direct evidence for why that delegation matters. Filing separately.

**4 (gate hygiene, not a code bug): `god_file`'s threshold is CORPUS-RELATIVE** — `pf.n > 3.0 * AVG(n)` over every file. Adding this package's seven small files lowered the mean enough to push `testdata/snapshots/medium-rust-rosary/src/dispatch/session.rs` over, then a later commit pushed it back under. So the smell ratchet has a false-positive mode where an unrelated PR must absorb a baseline delta it did not cause. Deterministic, reproducible, not daemon jitter (verified by diffing HEAD vs origin/main finding sets).

## Exit ratchet — done, and wider than planned

`internal/lint/llo_boundary_test.go` now walks `_test.go`:
- Separate `lloTestFixtureAllowlist` (a slice with one shared reason) so the three production entries stay readable, per the original comment's own concern.
- Test files are held to a WIDER table set: `lloOwnedTables` PLUS `node_defs`/`node_refs`. Those two are absent from the production list because mache legitimately writes them — but for a TEST the question is not "who owns the table", it is "did this fixture invent a shape". Without this the ratchet would have missed the ten node_refs spellings, i.e. the whole point.
- Two directions, both mutation-proven red: a 35th hand-built fixture fails `NoNewWritersOfLLOOwnedTables`; a stale entry left behind after a migration fails `TestFixtureAllowlistIsStillEarned`.
- `internal/fixturedb/{schema_leyline,build,emit}.go` are on the PRODUCTION allowlist as the ONE sanctioned writer, with the reason spelled out.

## Migrated (5 of 37); 32 remain on the ratchet list

`untested_function_leyline_test.go` (closes mache-e3f3bf), `serve_find_smells_nodehash_test.go`, `serve_find_smells_fanout_test.go`, `smell_doc_refs_test.go`, `smell_test_nodes_test.go`.

**No test changed its result when given the shape it claimed** — the rules were already correct on the real ley-line shape; what was wrong was that the tests were not proving it. Two coverage improvements fell out anyway:
- `smell_test_nodes_test.go` was calling `testNodesViewSQL(true)` / `(false)` DIRECTLY, bypassing the `hasAST && hasContent` probe in `ensureCanonicalViews` entirely. It now goes through the real installer, so the probe is covered rather than assumed.
- The nodehash/fanout fixtures asserted on `X'DEAD'`-style hash literals. They now assert on "these occurrences are the same subtree" and read the hash back — a test no longer states bytes it does not own.

## Deliberately NOT touched (per the audit's list, confirmed correct)

The four e2e harnesses; `internal/testfixtures` (realism) vs the small adversarial rule fixtures (isolation) — fixturedb serves only the second; memory-vs-sqlite backend separation; `internal/lltest` beyond the pin-resolution bug; the named Taskfile signal targets; the ~150 `sql.Open` sites on unrelated tables.

One judgement call worth review: `cmd/serve_find_smells_views_test.go` has arm-probe tests using shapes NO producer emits (`node_refs(token, node_id, container_node_id)` with no qualifier). Those test the probe MECHANISM, so they legitimately need unrepresentable shapes. They stay on the allowlist rather than being forced into a producer.

comments.text:
Migration progress update — PR #592 now at 7 files migrated, `lloTestFixtureAllowlist` 32 → 30.

Added since the last comment:
- **`cmd/leyline_crosslang_smells_test.go`** — its helper took a `ddl string`, i.e. a fixture helper PARAMETERIZED ON SQL, layered on a hardcoded two-column `node_defs`. Now `[]crossLangDef{token, construct, κ}` through `fixturedb.Leyline`. title: Switch udsGraph wire from JSON to capnp framing (consume LLO daemon capnp migration)
description:
Filed 2026-05-11. Mache-side counterpart to LLO's daemon UDS wire migration (LLO Bead A, filed in parallel — search ley-line-open beads for "daemon UDS wire" / "capnp framing").

Surfaced during `mache-98aa97` audit: the bead's 2026-05-10 reconciliation comment notes "the contract is now daemon.capnp, NOT JSON. The description's 'JSON result' language is outdated" — but the daemon side (`rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/socket.rs:36`: "Each connection reads line-delimited JSON, dispatches, writes response") still speaks line-JSON. Both sides need to migrate together. LLO is handling the daemon-side migration in a parallel bead.

## Why this is a separate bead from mache-98aa97

`mache-98aa97`'s primary scope (mache as UDS query client, daemon owns SQLite, no in-process SQL on `--control`, no 352MB `ExtractActiveDB` temp copy) is **already shipped**:

- `cmd/serve.go:589` — `buildControlGraph` calls `newUDSGraph(sockPath)`
- `cmd/uds_graph.go` — full `graph.Graph` impl over UDS via `internal/leyline.SocketClient.SendOp`
- `--control` path bypasses `ExtractActiveDB` (the 352MB copy only happens on mount paths now; see mache-98b9bf for that remnant)

What's missing is the **wire format upgrade** (JSON → capnp). That's an additional structural improvement, not the original "UDS query proxy" intent. Treating it as a sibling bead keeps the original's scope coherent and gives this work clear, narrow acceptance criteria.

## Depends on

LLO Bead A (daemon-side wire migration). Concrete handshake (mirrors LLO 0.2.1 ↔ mache-3bf414):

1. LLO daemon ships capnp wire with `LEYLINE_DAEMON_WIRE=json|capnp` flag fallback.
2. LLO tags new leyline release (e.g. v0.2.2) that includes the daemon binary + the schema package bump.
3. mache pins to that version via `go.mod` (`leyline-schema/v0.2.2` if the schema needed any new fields for Bead B/C ops; otherwise stays at v0.2.1).
4. THIS bead lands the mache client switch.
5. LLO removes JSON path one release later (separate cleanup bead, LLO side).

Do not start this bead before step 2 — the daemon must accept capnp first, or the integration tests can't run.

## Scope

1. **Replace `internal/leyline.SocketClient.SendOp` JSON encode/decode in `cmd/uds_graph.go`** with capnp framing using `github.com/agentic-research/ley-line-open/clients/go/leyline-schema/daemon` types. Public API surface (`GetNode`, `ListChildren`, `ListChildStats`, `ReadContent`, `GetCallers`, `GetCallees`, `Invalidate`, `Act`, `Close`) stays unchanged — only the encode/decode path swaps.

2. **Frame the wire** the same way the daemon does (capnp `serialize::try_read_message` / `write_message`, one request envelope per write, one response envelope per read). Pick the same tagged-union-vs-per-op-multiplex choice the daemon side made in LLO Bead A.

3. **Implement `GetCallees`** once LLO Bead B (`find_callees` daemon op) is available. Mirror existing `GetCallers` shape using the `daemon.Ref` struct.

4. **Switch `ListChildStats` from N+1 to single-shot** once LLO Bead C (`list_child_stats` op) is available. Today it calls `GetNode` per child after `ListChildren`; the new op returns `List(Node)` directly in one round-trip.

5. **Add `cmd/uds_graph_test.go`** — there are currently zero tests for this file. Stub-daemon harness that speaks capnp (byte-equivalent to LLO's test fixtures from Bead A — share fixtures via T8.10 cross-runtime pattern, `ley-line-open-6b7d43` precedent). Round-trip each `graph.Graph` method.

6. **Reconnection-on-EOF.** Today, `SocketClient` does not handle daemon restart; first read post-restart returns EOF and `udsGraph` is permanently broken. Add a reconnect path that re-dials on next op after a transport error.

7. **`Invalidate` behavior.** Currently a no-op. The daemon owns invalidation (its SQLite snapshot updates on `current_root` bumps), so this is likely correct, but verify: should `Invalidate` send a hint to the daemon (e.g. force snapshot reload)? Or is the existing `current_root`-based hot-swap polling sufficient? Decide and document.

8. **Retire `internal/leyline/socket.go::SendOp`** as the wire-level method once nothing imports it. (The connection management bits — `DialSocket`, `DiscoverSocket`, `DiscoverOrStart`, daemon spawn — can stay; only the JSON op encode/decode goes away.)

9. **Bump `go.mod` require** for `leyline-schema` if LLO Bead C needed a schema field add. If not, stays at v0.2.1.

## Acceptance

- `cmd/uds_graph.go` no longer references `SocketClient.SendOp` or `map[string]any` request/response shapes — all wire I/O goes through capnp message read/write against `leyline-schema/daemon` types.
- `task test` green with the existing `--control` integration paths.
- `cmd/uds_graph_test.go` round-trips every `graph.Graph` method against a stub daemon.
- `git grep 'leyline.SocketClient'` returns no `*.go` matches outside `internal/leyline/socket.go` itself (or its tests).
- A daemon restart mid-session does not permanently break the client (covered by a test).
- README or `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` updated to reflect the wire format.

## Out of scope

- The daemon-side migration (LLO Bead A).
- New daemon ops themselves (LLO Beads B and C).
- The legacy 352MB `ExtractActiveDB` temp copy on the **mount** path (`cmd/mount.go:552, 622`) — that's `mache-98b9bf`.
- Changing `graph.Graph` interface (any change should be a separate refactor bead).

## Coordination notes

- Same dance as `mache-3bf414` ↔ `ley-line-open-41867b`. Don't push mache PR until LLO release exists; LLO release exists only after their PR lands + tag.
- The `LEYLINE_DAEMON_WIRE` env var in LLO Bead A gives a transition window — once mache lands this bead, the env var can be retired on the LLO side (separate cleanup bead).

title: Comparative MCP benchmark suite (mache vs codebase-memory-mcp vs Serena)
description:
Replicate codebase-memory-mcp's 12-question × 64-repo benchmark methodology and run mache + Serena against the same battery. Surface a comparable PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL grid so the "mache vs the field" claim is grounded in numbers, not anecdote.

Reference: ~/.claude/projects/-Users-jamesgardner-remotes-art-mache/memory/reference_competitive_landscape.md
- codebase-memory-mcp uses 12 standardized questions × 64 repos, manual/AI-assisted grading
- Serena has no published benchmark — neutral comparator if we run them all the same way
- mache's claim is "structure IS the query" (declarative schemas + projected FS) vs codebase-memory-mcp's Cypher executor vs Serena's live LSP

Scope (probably 2-3 separate beads when broken down):
1. **Methodology lock-in**: define the 12 questions (start from codebase-memory-mcp's set, mache-ify where their framing assumes Cypher/property-graph), pick the 64-repo corpus (use theirs verbatim if reproducible)
2. **Runner harness**: a Go program that takes a repo + question + MCP server, dispatches the question via the server's stated entry tool, captures the response, optionally pipes to an LLM for PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL grading
3. **Compete-and-report**: run all three servers on the corpus, produce a results table + writeup

Output artifact: `benchmarks/comparative/` directory with the runner, fixtures, methodology doc, and a results report. Wire to CI later (initial run is manual; this is research, not regression-gating).

Follows wire-decode microbench at PR #373 — that PR seeds the `internal/leyline/socket_bench_test.go` foundation; this bead is the macro-level competitive bench. Different scope, different audience (engineering vs strategic).

Memory note: comp doc is 61 days old; verify mache's tool surface (find_definition, get_architecture, etc.) is current before locking the question list.

comments.text:
**Add agent-lsp (Blackwell Systems) as a third comparator** — surfaced 2026-05-12.

- MCP server wrapping 30 language servers; **the product positioning is the *skills layer*** (21 workflow-enforcing skills wrapping 50 LSP tools), not the tools themselves. Their thesis: agents misuse raw LSP, skills enforce the correct multi-step sequence.
- Published per-codebase benchmark numbers (vs grep/read agents): 5x–34x overall, 52x–1,441x on rename specifically, 92–99% grep FP rates. Speculative edit (in-memory simulate before commit) clocks 60x.
- Credibility signal: `/lsp-inspect` found 12 bugs in Anthropic's MCP Python SDK; 2 PRs merged in 24h. Also bugs found + merged in mcp-go and mcp-grafana.
- Repo: github.com/blackwell-systems/agent-lsp; blog: blog.blackwell-systems.com/posts/agent-lsp-token-savings/

Implication for this bead:
- agent-lsp's win surface is **edit/refactor workflows** (rename, safe-edit, speculative simulation) — distinct from codebase-memory-mcp's **structural-navigation** axis. mache should be measured on BOTH axes against the right comparator on each.
- Methodology should split: (a) navigation questions à la codebase-memory-mcp's 12-q grid; (b) edit-prep tasks à la agent-lsp's rename/refactor harness. Run the same repo corpus through all four servers (mache, codebase-memory-mcp, Serena, agent-lsp) and emit a 2-axis report.
- Interesting hypothesis to test: does mache's projected-FS view collapse the grep FP rate to begin with? If a user reads `/pkg/foo/Close/callers/` instead of grepping for "Close" across 319K LOC, the 99% FP rate that agent-lsp wins on becomes 0% structurally. Worth a controlled measurement.

title: Record prior-art dates in the competitive landscape — mache predates tools that now cite each other
description:
Two gaps in docs/reference/competitive-landscape.md, both surfaced reviewing https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph.

1) NO ENTIRE-GRAPH ENTRY. Line 328 covers a different YC-backed review tool. entire-graph is closer to mache than anything currently listed: Go, MIT, local-only, symbol graph with definition/caller/callee/impact queries.

2) NO DATES ANYWHERE. entire-graph benchmarks itself against codebase-memory-mcp, which by the maintainer's account postdates mache. Without first-release dates the doc cannot support a priority claim, and a reader arriving from entire-graph's README will reasonably infer mache is the newer entrant.

Dates must come from verifiable sources - git tag dates, GitHub release pages - not recollection. If a date cannot be sourced, omit it rather than estimate.

THE HONEST FRAMING, which is stronger than a priority claim anyway: entire-graph requires CGO ('Go toolchain with CGO enabled (tree-sitter uses native parser bindings)') via smacker/go-tree-sitter - the exact dependency mache deleted in v0.18.0 - and it states 'CALLS, HANDLES_ROUTE, and HANDLES_TOOL relations are heuristic' and 'Dependent counts are heuristic, not compiler / type-checker accurate'. mache went the other direction with ADR-0013's (mention subset-of binding subset-of reachability) fidelity ordering and LSP-backed defs/refs. So it is 36 heuristic-relation languages vs 28 with a typed fidelity guarantee, and pure-Go vs a C toolchain. That contrast is the entry worth writing; who shipped first is a footnote.

Also worth noting it exposes no MCP tools - it is an 'entire graph ...' CLI plugin - so it does not contend for the same slot in an agent toolchain as mache's 18 MCP tools.

title: [design] MCP tool surface audit — symbol-aware ✓, resource-URI externalization needed, kind discriminator + find_implementations gaps
description:
## Audit context

Triggered by the LLO-side reframe of "agent-first language facts" (ADR-0023 in ley-line-open, drafted 2026-06-24): mache is the MCP code-intel surface Claude Code consumes, since v2.0.74. The cclsp project's design lessons (now-discontinued community LSP-MCP wrapper) named two load-bearing constraints:

1. **Agents emit wrong line/col**. cclsp's whole architecture used symbol_name + symbol_kind, then internally called `textDocument/documentSymbol` to find positions. Every implementation that exposed line/col-typed params hit this failure mode.
2. **JSON-RPC is the wrong carrier for bulk graph data**. MCP `resources` (out-of-band URI references with separate fetch) are the spec's escape hatch.

Plus the broader LSP-coverage question: does mache cover what Claude Code's agents expect from LSP-shaped tools?

## Current state — 18 MCP tools registered in cmd/serve_handlers.go

| Tool | Input | Symbol-aware | Bulk return? | LSP method |
|---|---|:-:|:-:|---|
| `find_definition` | symbol, fuzzy | ✓ | inline | textDocument/definition |
| `find_callers` | token | ✓ | inline | textDocument/references |
| `find_callees` | path (construct) | path-based | inline | (no direct LSP) |
| `get_type_info` | symbol, file | ✓ | inline | textDocument/hover |
| `get_diagnostics` | symbol, file, limit | ✓ | inline (capped) | textDocument/publishDiagnostics |
| `search` | pattern, type, role | pattern | **bulk-candidate** | workspace/symbol |
| `semantic_search` | query, k | NL | inline (k-capped) | (none) |
| `get_overview` | — | n/a | **bulk** | (none — agent-native) |
| `get_architecture` | — | n/a | **bulk** | (none — agent-native) |
| `get_communities` | min_size, summary | n/a | **bulk** | (none — agent-native) |
| `get_impact` | symbol, depth, direction | ✓ | **bulk at depth≥3** | (none — agent-native) |
| `get_diagram` | name, layout, exclude_tests, compact | n/a | **bulk** (mermaid) | (none) |
| `find_smells` | rule, source_id, limit | n/a | **bulk** | (none) |
| `list_directory` | path, exclude_tests | path | depends | (rough workspace/symbol) |
| `read_file` | path or paths[] | path | depends | (file content) |
| `get_sheaf_status` | — | n/a | tiny | (none — substrate-state) |
| `resolve_ref` | token, base_path | ref-token | tiny | (none — cross-lang ref) |
| `write_file` | path, content, format | path | tiny (status) | (LSP doesn't write) |

## Audit verdicts

**Axis 1 — symbol vs line/col.** ✓ Already fully aligned with cclsp's pattern. Zero tools require line/col; every position-based tool uses symbol/token/path. Agent-emitted-line/col failure mode is already designed away.

**Axis 1 gap — no `kind` discriminator.** When `Foo` is both a struct and a function (Go) or both a trait and a struct (Rust), name-only lookup is ambiguous. Add optional `kind` param to 4-5 symbol-aware tools.

**Axis 2 — inline vs resource URI.** mcp-go v0.54.0 supports `mcp.NewEmbeddedResource(ResourceContents{URI, MIMEType, Blob/Text})` and `s.AddResource(template, handler)`. Currently ALL tools inline-emit. ~7 of 18 are bulk-candidates that should externalize.

**LSP-coverage.** Strong on definition/references/hover/diagnostics. Missing: `find_implementations` (trait implementors, interface satisfiers). `documentSymbol` approximated by `list_directory` + `search`. Write surface (`write_file`) deliberately doesn't mirror `rename`/`code action` — that's bigger.

## Backlog (4 items, ordered by ROI)

1. **`kind` discriminator on symbol-aware tools.** Optional param on `find_definition`, `get_type_info`, `get_impact`, `find_callers`. One-file change in cmd/serve_handlers.go + handler-side filtering. Small mechanical PR. **This bead's first PR.**
2. **`find_implementations` as a new tool.** Closes LSP-coverage gap. Per-language backend: trait-impl edges for Rust, interface-satisfaction edges for Go. Probably one PR per language; design discussion in this bead before implementation.
3. **Externalize bulk tools via resource URIs.** Start with `get_communities`, `get_architecture`, `get_diagram`. Tool returns `mcp.NewEmbeddedResource(...)` with URI pointing at a resource the client fetches out-of-band. Per-tool PR; low risk per change.
4. **Registry-introspection test.** Test that inspects mache's MCP tool registry at startup and fails if any tool grows a `line` or `column`-named param. Prevents regression on Axis 1.

## Related

- LLO ADR-0023 (agent-first language facts) — drafted 2026-06-24, frames analyzer-as-library ingestion
- LLO bead `ley-line-open-5e05e6` (cloister↔LLO boundary design)
- mache bead `mache-e1b6c8` (drift_doc_outdated_count placeholder smell rule)
- cclsp design (now discontinued): https://github.com/ktnyt/cclsp
- Claude Code v2.0.74 release adding native LSP/MCP code-intel slot

## Acceptance criteria (for this design bead)

- Items 1-4 either shipped or have follow-up beads filed with rationale.
- A short cmd/MCP_DESIGN.md (or section in README) names the symbol-aware + resource-URI constraints as ongoing invariants.
- Axis-1 regression test (item 4) lands as part of the closing PR.

title: Unify language/extension registry — eliminate parallel drift
description:
## Problem

Four parallel registries drift independently, causing bugs like the 129K FD leak (#129):

1. **`langForExt()`** (engine.go) — maps extensions to tree-sitter grammars
2. **`sourceExtensions`** (watcher.go) — which extensions trigger re-ingest
3. **`ShouldSkipDir()`** (engine.go) — dirs to skip during walks
4. **`presetSchemas`** (schemas.go) — embedded schema registry

When we added 18 grammars, `langForExt` grew but `sourceExtensions` didn't get `.java`, `.c`, `.cpp`, `.rb`, `.php`, `.kt`, `.swift`, `.scala`. Same class of bug as the skip list divergence.

## Proposed fix

Single `Language` registry that all four derive from. One place to add a language, everything else follows.

## Related coupling issues

- **`buildServeGraph`** — god function mixing store creation, ingestion, refs, watcher wiring
- **`ingestTreeSitterParallel` vs `ingestTreeSitter`** — duplicated logic for schema filtering, _project_files fallback, broken file handling
- **`serve_registry.go`** — session mgmt, graph caching, worktree lifecycle, repo cloning, schema resolution all in one struct

PROPOSED DESIGN: Unified Language registry in internal/lang/

TYPE DEFINITION (internal/lang/language.go):

type Language struct {
    Name          string                  // canonical: 'go', 'python', 'typescript'
    Extensions    []string                // ['.go'], ['.ts', '.tsx'], ['.cpp', '.cc', ...]
    Grammar       func() *sitter.Language // tree-sitter grammar factory
    PresetSchema  string                  // 'schemas/go.json' or empty
    WriteBack     bool                    // true if validate/format/splice tested
    DisplayName   string                  // 'Go', 'C++', 'HCL/Terraform'
    Profile       *LanguageProfile        // AST enrichment (only HCL today)
    SentinelFiles []string                // ['go.mod'] for project detection
}

REGISTRY (internal/lang/registry.go):
var Registry = []Language{ ... } // all 18 languages, one entry each

DERIVED LOOKUPS (internal/lang/lookup.go):
func ForExt(ext string) *Language   // replaces langForExt, DetectLanguageFromExt, LanguageForPath
func ForName(name string) *Language // replaces GetLanguage
func IsSourceExt(ext string) bool   // replaces sourceExtensions map + isSourceFile
func Names() []string               // replaces manual name collection

WHY internal/lang/ (not api/ or internal/ingest/):
- Grammar field has CGO dep (*sitter.Language) -- must not leak into api/
- Cannot be in internal/ingest/ -- writeback/validate.go needs it, but
  importing ingest from writeback creates circular dep (ingest imports writeback)
- Separate internal/lang/ breaks the cycle cleanly
