title: Docs hostile to new users: First-run MCP config omits daemon-lifecycle, directory-vs-.db tier choice, and --control/--scope clarity
description:
## Why

Real onboarding failure (2026-06-25): a user configuring mache's MCP on a second machine hit `localhost:7532/mcp` "connection refused", couldn't tell whether `mache serve --stdio /path/to/output.db` (a leyline-parsed db) was right or wrong, and asked whether `--control` is required. Every one of these is answered by the CLI but NOT made clear by the docs. The docs are technically correct but incomplete in exactly the ways that produce confusion.

## Gaps to close (GETTING-STARTED.md "First run", README quick start)

1. **`mache serve` is a long-running foreground daemon.** The quickstart shows `mache serve .` then `claude mcp add --transport http ...` as if sequential, but the first command blocks. HTTP registration is dead-on-arrival unless the daemon stays running. Must state: open a second terminal / background it / keep it alive — and cross-ref the launchd lifecycle work (mache-823d91). This is the literal cause of the "conn refused" report.

2. **Directory-vs-`.db` is the heuristic-vs-semantic tier choice — undocumented.** `mache serve <dir>` = live, but tree-sitter/SitterWalker heuristic tier (Go-tuned; weaker find_callers/type-info on Rust). `mache serve <leyline.db>` = `_ast`/`_lsp` semantic tier (accurate find_callers, get_type_info, get_diagnostics; uniform across languages) but a static snapshot (re-run `leyline parse`, or use the ley-line daemon + `--control` for live). This is the project's own "shines on Go / shines after ll-parse" story (see mache-9108a1) and it appears nowhere in onboarding. A new user can't tell that pointing at `output.db` is the BETTER tier for Rust.

3. **Two `claude mcp add` forms, clearly separated.**
   - HTTP: `claude mcp add --transport http mache http://localhost:7532/mcp` (URL; run `mache serve` separately as a daemon).
   - stdio: `claude mcp add mache -- mache serve --stdio <source>` (command; Claude spawns it).
   Note `--scope user|project|local` controls where the config lands.

4. **`--control` is optional.** One line: not needed for basic config; only for live ley-line hot-swap (reads from arena). Kills a recurring question.

## Acceptance

GETTING-STARTED.md "First run" rewritten so a new user can, in one read: (a) understand `mache serve` must keep running and how, (b) choose directory vs `.db` with the tier tradeoff explained, (c) pick the right `claude mcp add` form for their transport, (d) know `--control` is optional. README quick start gets a one-line "keep this running / see GETTING-STARTED for stdio + .db" nudge so the 30-second path doesn't mislead. Consider the readme-restructure discipline (value-prop + audience first). Separate PR from #448.

## Cross-refs
- mache-823d91 (daemon launchd lifecycle — the keep-it-running fix)
- mache-9108a1 (heuristic vs semantic tier — the substance behind the directory-vs-.db doc)

title: Adaptive pre-injection: tool-call log + semantic bundle reshaping (the repo learns to onboard its agents)
description:
## The idea

Today's pre-injection bundle (`mache pack`, prototype on bench branch) is a static projection of the corpus → markdown. Adaptive pre-injection observes the tool-call log from past agent sessions on this repo, learns which structural facts the agent kept needing vs ignored, and reshapes the next bundle accordingly. The bundle becomes a **learned working-memory cache**, not a fixed view.

Mache is uniquely positioned to ship this because we have all three primitives latent:
- **Projection substrate** (constructs as directories, refs as graph, communities)
- **Sheaf invalidation** (precise change propagation; the learned overlay can be region-scoped)
- **MCP server in the loop** (every tool call is observable)

No peer has all three. codebase-memory-mcp has the projection; agent-lsp has tool-call observability; GrapeRoot has static pre-injection. Mache is the substrate where all three compose.

## Mechanism (sketch, not commitment)

1. **Log tool calls** in `wrapHandler` (cmd/serve_registry.go:126) — emit `{session_id, tool, args, response_size, response_summary}` to a per-repo SQLite table.
2. **Usefulness signal**: was this call followed by another structural query on the same/related token (= productive) vs by exploration that mentions tokens not in the bundle (= bundle missed something)?
3. **Aggregate prior**: per (repo, token, tool) → usefulness score with decay.
4. **Bundle reshape at generation time**: boost high-prior tokens in "key abstractions" section, expand context around tokens that triggered exploration grep'ing.
5. **Sheaf-bounded refresh**: when source changes invalidate a region, the learned overlay for that region invalidates too (don't reshape based on stale priors).

## Bias-avoidance (REQUIRED, not optional)

1. **Structure as ground truth, learning as overlay only.** The learned layer re-ranks and re-budgets what to surface from corpus-derived facts. It never invents content the source doesn't have. The bundle is bounded to ground truth.
2. **Aggressive decay.** Old patterns fade unless reinforced (TF-IDF-style or exponential). Last week's auth-debug session must not dominate this week's perf work.
3. **Per-repo, not per-user, not cross-repo.** Learning stays local. Generalizing across projects bakes one team's blind spots into another's.
4. **Inspectable + revertible.** Every adaptive reshape is logged with rationale ("boosted `Topology` because 3 of last 5 sessions grep'd for it post-bundle"). Operator can audit, override, reset, or pin.
5. **Hold-out baseline.** Every N sessions, ship the unadapted bundle and measure delta. Avoid the always-train-no-eval trap that produces drift.

## Why this is downstream, not now

This bead depends on:
- **`mache-49bf9a`** (sheaf audit) — without confirmed live invalidation, the region-scoped refresh has no anchor
- **`0013-refs-defs-canonical-schema/consumer-curation` thread** (5 beads) — without curation, the "ground truth" the learning overlays on is L0 noise
- **`mache-33ffb0`** (pre-injection epic) — pack itself needs to exist as a persistent artifact before it can be adaptively shaped

Filing as a research bead under the same thread. NOT a P0/P1 — it's the frontier-after-the-foundation.

## Strategic frame

This is the move that turns mache from "static structural projection" → "the repo learns how to onboard its own agents." That's the actual product story — "your codebase has working memory that gets smarter the more your team uses it." Nobody else can ship this; we should be the ones who do.

## Reference

- Conversation context: session 2026-05-16 where the framing crystallized (pre-injection = externalized agent working memory; adaptive = the cache learns; sheaf = the invalidation primitive that makes adaptation safe)
- `cmd/serve_registry.go:126` — `wrapHandler`, the observability hook
- `internal/leyline/sheaf.go` — invalidation primitive

title: Codegen API + MCP surface from a single contract (eliminate hand-rolled tool dispatch)
description:
## Idea

Mache's MCP tool surface (cmd/serve_handlers.go ~1000 LOC) and the leyline UDS dispatch (internal/leyline/socket.go) are both hand-coded against the same conceptual contract: a set of named ops with typed request/response shapes. LLO already generates its wire layer from capnproto schemas (rs/ll-open/proto/daemon.capnp). Mache reverse-engineers them as Go structs in internal/leyline/wire.go.

What if a single contract source generated all three:

1. **MCP tool definitions** for mache (cmd/serve_handlers.go)
2. **UDS dispatch table** for the daemon (rs/ll-open/.../sheaf_ops.rs and friends)
3. **Typed Go client** for mache (internal/leyline/wire.go)
4. **Optional REST/gRPC surface** for non-MCP consumers (kiln gateway, web UIs)

## Why this might matter

- Today every new op requires hand-edits in 3+ places — typed bindings, MCP tool handler, daemon dispatch
- Drift between mache's typed structs and LLO's wire format is a documented hazard (the v0.3 → v0.4 capnp-json migration is a recent example, see internal/leyline/wire.go history)
- The "consumer-side wiring is sketch" verdict from mache-49bf9a partially reflects this drift cost — every new daemon op needs a paired mache adoption PR, with the wire-format guessing that tools/sheaf-probe was needed to verify

## Open design calls

1. Source of truth: capnproto, protobuf, smithy, or something mache-native?
2. MCP-first vs REST-first vs schema-first generation order?
3. Does this couple mache to LLO too tightly, or does it loosen it?
4. What's the bootstrapping cost vs current hand-roll cost?

## When to do this

Probably AFTER the sheaf-incremental chain ships (mache-c11848 / c14c43 / 8e59a5 / 8e7794). That work surfaces what the contract needs to express; doing the codegen first would be premature.

Owner: architect-agent for the ADR sketch; then dispatcher decides.

Surfaced 2026-05-17 by jamestexas during sheaf-incremental e2e validation discussion.

title: Fix N+1 in udsGraph.ListChildStats — consume list_children response directly
description:
Filed 2026-05-10. Independent of LLO work — no cross-repo gate.

## Context

`mache/cmd/uds_graph.go:93-125` calls `list_children` on LLO, ignores the `[]{id,name,kind,size}` already in the response, then issues `GetNode` per child to "get the stats." This is N+1: one round-trip plus one per child.

The LLO daemon's `ListChildrenResponse` (`daemon.capnp:115-122`) already returns `List(Node)` with all stats (id, parentId, name, kind, size, record). LLO's TODO comment near the N+1 site already acknowledges this:
> *"// list_children returns IDs. We need stats. Use get_node for each. // TODO: add a list_child_stats op to the daemon for efficiency."*

The comment is outdated — the data is already in the response. No daemon op needed.

This pattern was already migrated for most readdir paths per `serve_listdir_bench_test.go:46-97` (which documents the N+1 → bulk refactor). `cmd/uds_graph.go:93-125` is the residual unmigrated site.

## Work

1. Read `list_children` response into a typed shape (today: `map[string]any`; can be improved further by Bead M2's typed Go bindings adoption)
2. Map the response `children` array directly to `[]graph.NodeStat` — no further round-trips
3. Remove the per-child `GetNode` loop
4. Bench: existing `serve_listdir_bench_test.go` should show improvement (or at minimum not regress) on the affected code path

## Acceptance

- `udsGraph.ListChildStats` makes exactly ONE daemon round-trip per directory listing
- All existing tests pass
- Benchmark shows improvement on the readdir-heavy path

## Cross-repo gate: NONE

This is purely a mache-side fix. LLO already returns the data needed; mache just needs to consume it. Can land before or after LLO's Bead `a373ba` (typed JSON wire) — independent of that work.

Optionally tighter version (lands AFTER M2): once mache adopts typed Go bindings from `clients/go/leyline-schema`, this becomes a typed-struct field access rather than `map[string]any` traversal.

comments.text:
Closed by d4dadd9 on PR #371.

Diagnosis was deeper than "N+1": `c.(string)` was failing every assertion, so `ListChildren` returned an empty slice for non-empty dirs in addition to `ListChildStats` falling through to no stats. Fix introduces `listChildrenResponse` helper that both methods share, parsing the `[{id, name, kind, size}, ...]` payload the daemon already returns. ListChildStats is now single-shot — no GetNode fan-out — pinned by a test that asserts no `get_node` ops fire during a ListChildStats call.

title: Adopt typed Go bindings from clients/go/leyline-schema in udsGraph
description:
Filed 2026-05-10. **BLOCKED on `ley-line-open-a373ba` (LLO typed JSON wire lockdown) landing + LLO release tag pushed.** Do not start until upstream tag exists.

## Cross-repo gate

⚠️ **Blocked on upstream**:
- LLO bead `ley-line-open-a373ba` ("Generate LLO's daemon UDS JSON wire from daemon.capnp typed structs") must merge to LLO main
- LLO must tag a release (e.g. `v0.3.0` or similar) AND that release must include updated `clients/go/leyline-schema/` Go bindings with typed JSON tags
- Once tag is live, `go get github.com/agentic-research/ley-line-open/clients/go/leyline-schema@<tag>` resolves — at which point this bead can start

Without that upstream landing, this bead's PR will either fail to compile (typed structs don't exist) or build against a phantom version.

Same cross-repo coordination pattern as `ley-line-open-41867b ↔ mache-3bf414` (v0.2.1 dance).

## Context

mache's `cmd/uds_graph.go` decodes LLO daemon responses into `map[string]any` and traverses untyped. With LLO's typed JSON wire (Bead `a373ba`) landed, mache can decode into typed Go structs from `clients/go/leyline-schema/daemon` (and friends), eliminating runtime type-assertion errors and giving IDE-level field discovery.

## Work

1. Bump mache's `go.mod` `require github.com/agentic-research/ley-line-open/clients/go/leyline-schema` to the new LLO tag
2. Swap `cmd/uds_graph.go`'s `json.Unmarshal` into `map[string]any` for `json.Unmarshal` into typed structs from `daemon` subpackage (or `binding`, `common`, etc. depending on op)
3. Update call sites in mache that consume the responses — typed field access instead of `resp["foo"].(map[string]any)["bar"].(string)`
4. Coordinate with Bead `mache-a55625` (N+1 fix) — the typed structs make the N+1 fix even cleaner (typed Node slice access)

## Acceptance

- `cmd/uds_graph.go` no longer uses `map[string]any` for LLO daemon responses
- All op shapes consumed via the v0.2.x+ Go bindings
- `task lint && task test` green
- Updated `go.mod` references the new LLO tag

## Why this needs the gate

Going early would mean either (a) compile-failure (typed structs don't exist), (b) building against `clients/go/leyline-schema@v0.2.1` whose shape doesn't yet include the typed-JSON-tagged structs (Bead `a373ba` may extend the Go binding regen to add `json:"..."` tags or restructure the package). Either way, the work is upstream-shaped.

## Downstream coordination

After this bead's PR merges, post a comment on `mache-98aa97` noting the contract-vs-encoding distinction is now realized end-to-end (LLO typed JSON wire + mache typed consumption).

comments.text:
**Updated context (2026-05-12): the LLO wire shape changed between when this bead was filed and now.**

Original blocking bead `ley-line-open-a373ba` was split into 4 sub-beads (b5a77b / b631c8 / b69606 / b0ea2e). The first three landed earlier and produced the v0.2.3 Go bindings; **b0ea2e (in flight via PR #12 on agentic-research/ley-line-open) changes the wire shape** — adoption work now needs to account for this.

## Concrete wire deltas to handle

Under post-b0ea2e (capnp-json codec, C++ JsonCodec compatible):

- **Int64 / UInt64 fields emit as JSON strings.** `"67108864"` not `67108864`. Caused by JS Number precision avoidance in the C++ codec. Inbound (mache→LLO) still accepts both.
- **Defaulted Int fields always emit `"0"`.** `last_reparse_at_ms` appears as `"0"` pre-first-reparse (was previously omitted). `generation` reappears as `"0"` on every response (legacy ordinal kept per ADR-0014 §2; semantically dead — use `current_root` for identity).
- **`enrichment` is a JSON-encoded `Text` field.** Per-pass status map rides as a JSON string inside the envelope's Text slot. Consumers parse twice (envelope → enrichment string → inner JSON object).
- **`ErrorResponse` gained `ok @1 :Bool`** (additive). Wire shape `{"ok":false,"error":"..."}` preserved.

## Empirical evidence of mache's behavior under the new wire

Ran a Go probe mimicking mache's exact decoder pattern (`internal/leyline/sheaf.go:147`-style — `map[string]any` decode + `.(float64)` type assertion) against a PR #12 daemon:

```
raw response: {"ok":true,"generation":"0","arena_path":"...","arena_size":"68157440","phase":"ready","current_root":"...","enrichment":"{}","last_reparse_at_ms":"0"}

mache-style decoder probes:
  resp["generation"].(float64)        → ok=false, value=0 (raw type: string)
  resp["arena_size"].(float64)        → ok=false, value=0 (raw type: string)
  resp["last_reparse_at_ms"].(float64)→ ok=false, value=0 (raw type: string)
  resp["ok"]          = true   (bool)   ← unaffected
  resp["phase"]       = ready  (string) ← unaffected
  resp["current_root"]= 5d25...(string) ← unaffected
  resp["enrichment"]  = {}     (string) ← was object, now JSON-text
```

**mache doesn't crash.** It silently zeros every Int64 field instead. Other fields (Bool, Text, Text-encoded JSON) decode fine.

## Production-code float64 assertions in mache today

These all silently zero under post-b0ea2e:

| File:line | Field | Op |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/leyline/sheaf.go:128` | `defect` | sheaf-status (private LLO ext) |
| `internal/leyline/sheaf.go:147` | `generation` | sheaf-status |
| `internal/leyline/sheaf.go:150` | `valid` | sheaf-status |
| `internal/leyline/sheaf.go:153` | `total` | sheaf-status |
| `internal/leyline/sheaf.go:156` | `defect` | sheaf-status |
| `internal/leyline/semantic.go:77` | `distance` | vec-search (LLO `vec_search`) |
| `internal/leyline/semantic.go:100` | `count` | vec-search |
| `internal/leyline/semantic.go:103` | `dimensions` | vec-search |
| `internal/leyline/semantic.go:131` | `embedded` | semantic |
| `cmd/serve_find_smells.go:813` | (varies) | smells output |

**Note:** `sheaf` and `vec_search` are LLO extension ops (not base ops). PR #12's migration only touched the 17 base ops + `ErrorResponse`. Extension ops still emit JSON via the old hand-rolled `json!()` path, so their Int64 fields may or may not be affected — depends on whether the extension layer is also migrated. **Worth verifying** with a live `sheaf_status` and `vec_search` call against a post-b0ea2e daemon before assuming.

For **base op** Int64 fields (which definitely change shape under PR #12):
- `StatusResponse`: `generation`, `arena_size`, `last_reparse_at_ms`
- `ReparseResponse`: `generation`, `parsed`, `unchanged`, `deleted`, `errors`
- `SnapshotResponse` / `LoadResponse` / `EnrichResponse`: `generation`
- `Node` (in `list_children`/`get_node`): `size`

mache code today doesn't appear to float64-assert on these base-op Int64 fields, so the *immediate* user-visible impact is small. But the typed-bindings adoption (the original scope of this bead) needs `,string` json tags everywhere a `*int64` / `*uint64` is declared.

## Adoption work needed

1. **Bump `clients/go/leyline-schema` to v0.3.0** once LLO PR #12 merges. The dependency's wire shape changed; new tag signals breaking change for consumers.
2. **Define typed Go structs** for the response types `udsGraph` consumes (status, list_children, find_callers, find_callees, find_defs, get_refs_map, get_defs_map, get_db_path, get_schema, read_content, get_node). Mirror the shapes in `clients/go/leyline-schema/daemon/daemon_protocol_test.go` from LLO's repo (which were updated in PR #12 with `,string` tags).
3. **Refactor `SendOp` consumers** in `cmd/uds_graph.go` from `map[string]any` to typed structs. Adds compile-time safety.
4. **Audit `float64` type assertions** for the at-risk fields above. If they're against extension-op responses (sheaf/vec_search), verify those ops' wire shape with a live probe; otherwise just leave them (they may be unaffected). If they're against base-op responses, fix.
5. **End-to-end smoke test**: `mache serve` against a PR-#12 LLO daemon, exercise every supported `udsGraph` method, verify no silent zeros. The compose-recipe bead (`ley-line-open-69072b`) when it lands will make this a one-command test.

## Sequence

mache adoption is unblocked the moment LLO PR #12 merges + `clients/go/leyline-schema/v0.3.0` is tagged. No further blocking; this bead is ready to dispatch on mache side.

Cross-repo bookkeeping: comment on this bead with the mache PR # once you open it so we can close the loop.

2. Replace the `return nil, nil` stub in `udsGraph.GetCallees`:

3. Add a test exercising the path: parse fixture with known A→B→C call chain, assert `GetCallees(A)` returns B
4. If Bead `mache-a5ad09` (typed Go bindings adoption) has already landed: use the typed `FindCalleesResponse` directly. Otherwise: untyped decode is fine (M3 supersedes M2 on this code path eventually).

## Acceptance

- Test asserts forward-reference walking against a fixture
- `task lint && task test` green
- Impact analysis (`serve_impact.go`) can route cross-repo callees through this method

## Coordination with mache-a5ad09

These two beads share `cmd/uds_graph.go` so they'll serialize at dispatch time. Order doesn't matter — either lands first, the other adapts. Suggest doing M2 first if both are dispatched at the same time so M3 gets typed consumption "for free."

comments.text:
**UNBLOCKED: LLO `clients/go/leyline-schema/v0.2.2` is tagged.**

The LLO daemon now exposes `find_callees` (bead `ley-line-open-a47d7d`, landed as PR #7 merge commit `d5d4769`, tag `clients/go/leyline-schema/v0.2.2`). This bead's gate is satisfied — you can start.

## How to consume

```
go get github.com/agentic-research/ley-line-open/clients/go/leyline-schema@v0.2.2
# proxy.golang.org may lag a few min; use GOPROXY=direct if so
```

The new typed Go binding is `daemon.FindCalleesRequest` / `daemon.FindCalleesResponse` in `clients/go/leyline-schema/daemon`.

## Daemon op shape

- **Request**: `{"op": "find_callees", "id": "<node_id>"}` over UDS, or `tools/call name=find_callees args={id}` over MCP HTTP
- **Response**: `{"ok": true, "callees": [{"node_id": "...", "source_id": "..."}, ...]}` — same shape as find_callers, just keyed on node-id input instead of token

Implementation in LLO is a DISTINCT JOIN: `node_refs r JOIN node_defs d ON r.token = d.token WHERE r.node_id = ?` — "given this node, find the definitions of every token it references."

## udsGraph.GetCallees minimal impl

```go
func (g *udsGraph) GetCallees(id string) ([]*graph.Node, error) {
    resp, err := g.sock.SendOp(map[string]any{"op": "find_callees", "id": id})
    if err != nil { return nil, err }
    rawCallees, _ := resp["callees"].([]any)
    nodes := make([]*graph.Node, 0, len(rawCallees))
    for _, c := range rawCallees {
        row, ok := c.(map[string]any)
        if !ok { continue }
        nodeID, _ := row["node_id"].(string)
        if nodeID != "" {
            nodes = append(nodes, &graph.Node{ID: nodeID, Mode: 0o444})
        }
    }
    return nodes, nil
}
```

Mirror of the existing `GetCallers` parse. Once this lands you can also re-apply the read-only `--control` mount switch (mache-98b9bf) — the regression that forced the revert is now closed.

Coordinated with `mache-a5ad09` (typed-bindings adoption) — these two share `cmd/uds_graph.go` so they'll serialize at dispatch time; order doesn't matter.

title: EPIC: agent-native mount — no-sudo mounting + CAS-backed worktree-free agent workspaces
description: Brainstorming output (2026-07-22). Started as 'fix mache's sudo mount', became a strategic cross-repo epic: the CAS/jj arena as a worktree-free agent workspace substrate (rosary payoff — replace git worktrees, kill N-times disk cost). Center of gravity is LLO (leyline-vcs jj sidecar, already ~half-built: 'the agent never needs to know it exists'). Decisions of record: no CGO in mache (ADR-0006 hard invariant); no-sudo mount = delegate to leyline serve --backend fuse; writes = file changes admitted by leyline's existing watcher (not a splice API); format off the write path (WASM canonical formatters as separate bead, topiary rejected for byte-for-byte); mount is OPTIONAL. Gated on a Phase-0 probe that can reshape/kill the epic. See the spec for the 5 blind spots (esp. data-projections break the clean split; concurrent-isolated-branches is the load-bearing unknown).

comments.text:
PHASE-0 PROBE RESULTS (2026-07-22):

P0.1 no-sudo mount — ✅ WORKS.
- Mount-capable leyline builds via 'task build:mount' (needs the fuse-t pkg-config WRAPPER at rs/pkgconfig — stock fuser wants libfuse>=2.6.0 but fuse-t's fuse.pc reports 1.2.1, so a raw 'cargo build --features full' FAILS; the wrapper presents fuse-t as fuse>=2.6.0).
- Runtime: binary needs libfuse-t on the loader path — DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib (or an rpath fixup via 'task install:full+mount'). Without it: 'dyld: Library not loaded: @rpath/libfuse-t.dylib'.
- With those two: 'leyline serve --backend fuse --mount <dir>' mounts via fuse-t with ZERO sudo (confirmed twice: 'FUSE mounted at ...', 0 sudo invocations). leyline 0.10.0.

P0.2 Linux-CI mount — NOT RUN (needs a GitHub runner). Low risk: Linux fuse via fusermount is established no-sudo; LLO CI already installs libfuse-dev (but only BUILDS, doesn't mount). Remaining probe = add an actual 'serve --backend fuse' mount smoke-test on ubuntu-latest, SHA-pinned actions.

P0.4 concurrent isolated branches (north-star) — PARTIAL: reachable, not built.
- leyline-vcs public API today = LINEAR snapshot history only: init/open, commit_snapshot, revert_to_commit, log_json.
- BUT it's built on jj_lib::workspace::Workspace, and jj's 'workspaces' ARE the worktree-replacement primitive (multiple working copies over one repo, COW, dedup). description:

2. **`_lsp` already has a `symbol_kind` column** (serve_lsp.go:300). For the LSP path, filtering on `symbol_kind` directly may be cleaner and more correct than resolving kind from node_id at all. Evaluate `symbol_kind`-based filtering vs routing through `filterDirIDsByKindGraph`.

## Fix

title: CDC activation targets the wrong granularity for mache: `leyline cdc enable` chunks constructs (100% sub-floor, +21% db size), while source_blobs is the table that would actually chunk
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-29 against LLO v0.13.0 on mache's own leyline-native projection (2.1 GB .db, 777 files). Corrects two of my own wrong assumptions in the process.

## Correction 1: CDC IS enabled in the shipped binary, and IS explicitly activatable

I initially claimed CDC was a non-default feature. Wrong — that's true of `leyline-fs`'s own defaults, but `leyline-cli` (the binary mache invokes) has `default = ["lsp", "validate", "hdc", "cdc"]`. It ships compiled in.

Activation is explicit by design (`rs/ll-open/fs/src/activation.rs`: "Activation is explicit: opening a writable graph does not create or populate the derived CDC tables"), exposed as a real CLI surface: `leyline cdc enable --db <DB>` (plus `leyline cdc gc`). So enabling it IS a supported operation, not a code change.

## Correction 2: but enabling it on mache's .db today is a REGRESSION, not a win

Ran `leyline cdc enable --db <copy of mache's projection> --json`:

    eligible_nodes         395,173
    populated_nodes        395,173
    processed_source_bytes 3,860,666  (3.86 MB)
    manifest_rows          387,779
    unique_chunk_rows       40,633
    unique_chunk_bytes   1,964,314    (1.96 MB)

    db size  2,109,931,520 -> 2,549,612,544   (+440 MB, +21%)

Content dedup is real but trivial in context: 3.86 MB -> 1.96 MB unique (≈2x on content, 9.5x manifest-row reuse). It cost **440 MB of manifest/schema overhead to save ~1.9 MB of content.**

Reads stay correct (fan_out_skew 120 before and after), so this is purely a cost regression, not a correctness one.

## Root cause: granularity mismatch, not a missing flag

CDC's chunk params (`rs/ll-open/cdc/src/lib.rs`): MIN_CHUNK 8 KiB, MAX 128 KiB, expected ~72 KiB.

`cdc enable` activates over `nodes` — which in mache's projection are AST **constructs**, not files:

    content_chunks chunk_len  min 1 / avg 48 / max 5,633 bytes
    nodes below the 8 KiB MIN_CHUNK floor:  395,173 / 395,173  (100%)

Largest single node is 5,633 bytes; the sample includes `AGENTS.md/section/atx_heading/atx_h1_marker` at **1 byte**. So the GearHash boundary predicate never fires even once — nothing is actually being *chunked*. Every node becomes one sub-minimum blob plus manifest rows. CDC is doing content-addressed dedup of construct bodies, which is not what it's for and not worth 440 MB.

## The table that WOULD chunk: source_blobs

Same db, whole-file content:

    source_blobs                     762 rows,  7,593,491 bytes total
    of those >= 8 KiB MIN_CHUNK      289 rows,  5,901,079 bytes  (78% of all bytes)
    blob size  min 55 / avg 9,965 / max 169,891 bytes

289 blobs would genuinely chunk, the max (170 KB) splits into multiple chunks, and 78% of file bytes live in the chunkable set. That is where paging and dedup would actually pay.

## So the ask is upstream + design, not a mache toggle

1. UPSTREAM (LLO): can `cdc enable` target file-content (`source_blobs` / `_source`) rather than `nodes`? Activation currently walks "authoritative readable leaf" nodes. For a construct-granular projection that's the wrong set. Worth raising on the CDC bead thread with these numbers — LLO's v0.13.0 changelog names "mache dataflow" as an intended sub-file consumer, so the intent exists; the activation target doesn't match it yet.
2. MACHE: do NOT enable CDC on the current projection. Note also that mache's own read pattern (construct-granular, avg 731 B/read per docs/benchmarks/token-efficiency-baseline.json) is ~100x smaller than one expected chunk, so chunk-paging cannot improve mache's PRIMARY read path regardless — mache already resolves content on demand per record via PK lookup.
3. The real payoff remains incremental invalidation, not read bandwidth — tracked on mache-238673 (node_hash memoization / merkle+sheaf cash-out) and mache-463612.

METHOD NOTE for whoever picks this up: measure on the leyline-native projection (`--backend leyline`), not a schema projection. Conclusions about rule/threshold/storage behavior drawn from the schema projection were wrong four separate times in the session that produced this bead.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) LLO's cdc activation gains a file-content target and a re-measurement on mache's projection shows a net size/read win over the current PK-lookup path, or (b) this bead records the measured reason mache does not adopt CDC for content storage and points at mache-238673 as the actual incremental-analysis payoff. Any decision must cite numbers measured on a `--backend leyline` projection.

title: AddFileChildren mutates *Node under RLock on concurrent readers
description:
## Finding from PR #148 review

`AddFileChildren` in graph.go acquires the write lock, then appends to `parent.Children` via the passed-in `*Node` pointer. The problem: the CALLER (processNode in engine.go) also holds a reference to that same `*Node` (`node` variable at line ~1482). After `AddFileChildren` returns and releases the lock, any goroutine that obtained the parent node via `GetNode` (which only takes an RLock and returns the pointer directly — not a copy) can now race against future appends to Children from a different goroutine.

The race is: goroutine A calls `store.GetNode("pkg/auth")` under RLock → gets `*Node` pointer → lock released. Goroutine B (engine) calls `AddFileChildren` on the same node → appends to Children → releases WLock. Goroutine A now reads Children while goroutine B wrote to it outside the lock.

Root issue: `GetNode` returns a live pointer to the stored node, not a copy. `AddFileChildren` mutates the slice on that same pointer. There is no lock held by the caller during the Children read.

## Fix needed
Either `GetNode` returns a shallow copy with a copied Children slice, or `AddFileChildren` creates a new node with a new Children slice (copy-on-write) rather than appending in place. The existing `AddNode` path has the same structural issue but AddFileChildren makes it worse by explicitly designing around pointer aliasing.

## Files
- internal/graph/graph.go — AddFileChildren (line ~230)
- internal/graph/graph.go — GetNode (returns raw pointer)

comments.text: Fixed in PR #170 (commit ed96101): AddFileChildren now COW into the node map; falsifiable -race test added.

title: Atomicity test for AddFileChildren is not actually testing atomicity
description:
## Finding from PR #148 review

`TestMemoryStore_AddFileChildren_Atomicity` in batch_test.go is structured to detect partial writes, but it has a fundamental timing problem: there is nothing that forces the reader goroutine to execute concurrently with the write. The goroutine starts, then `store.AddFileChildren` is called — by the time the goroutine gets scheduled, the write may already be complete. The 1000-iteration tight loop with no yield point makes this more likely to be a false pass.

Additionally, the test only calls `ListChildren` (which takes its own RLock snapshot of the IDs slice), but does not test that individual `GetNode` calls on partially-added children are safe. It tests the Children slice atomicity but not the node-map insertion atomicity.

A genuine atomicity test would need to use `runtime.Gosched()`, a start barrier (e.g. `sync.WaitGroup`), or `testing/synctest` to guarantee interleaving. As written, this test will almost always pass even if the implementation is broken.

## Files
- internal/graph/batch_test.go — TestMemoryStore_AddFileChildren_Atomicity (line 80)

comments.text: Strengthened in PR #174: 200 cycles with per-cycle WaitGroup barrier + runtime.Gosched in reader. New NodeMapConsistency test covers the index-before-publish invariant.

title: compactSorted returns input slice directly for len==1 (aliasing)
description:
## Finding from PR #148 review

`compactSorted` in internal/graph/sliceutil.go has this early return:

```go
if len(s) <= 1 {
    return s
}
```

The function comment says "Returns a new slice — does not mutate the input." But for len==1, it returns the SAME slice. This breaks the no-alias contract: the caller (mergeSortedDedup) passes `a` or `b` directly to compactSorted when the other slice is empty, and gets back an alias of the input. If the caller later appends to `result`, the underlying array of the returned slice could be stomped if it shared capacity.

In practice, `mergeSortedDedup` only hits this path when one slice is empty (the early-return guards), and the returned slice is used as `result` without further append, so it doesn't blow up today. But the comment is a lie and the aliasing is a latent hazard if the function is reused.

Fix: `return append([]string(nil), s...)` or `return s[:len(s):len(s)]` (restrict capacity) for the len==1 case.

## Files
- internal/graph/sliceutil.go — compactSorted (line 40)

comments.text: Fixed in cleanup PR (incoming): compactSorted now allocates a fresh single-element slice when len==1; len==0 returns nil. Adds TestCompactSorted_NoAliasing as a falsifiable guard, plus TestCompactSorted_EmptyReturnsNil.

Raised during a canonical-hours build session: could mache's declarative topology-schema system (examples/*.json — nvd, go, python, mcp, terraform, etc.) support transpiling data BOTH directions — source format → mache's structural projection AND back out to a (possibly different) declared target format — rather than only the current one-way `mache mount`/`build`/`serve` (source → tree/DB, read-only projection)?

title: bufferingTarget.AddFileChildren calls AddNode(parent) which passes dir through to inner store
description:
## Finding from PR #148 review

`bufferingTarget.AddFileChildren` (engine.go ~line 702) does:

```go
func (b *bufferingTarget) AddFileChildren(parent *graph.Node, files []*graph.Node) {
    b.bufferedNodes = append(b.bufferedNodes, files...)
    for _, f := range files {
        parent.Children = append(parent.Children, f.ID)
    }
    b.IngestionTarget.AddNode(parent)
}
```

`bufferingTarget.AddNode` filters: dirs pass through to the inner store immediately, non-dirs go to the buffer. This call goes to `b.IngestionTarget.AddNode(parent)` — the INNER store directly — bypassing the filter. That's intentional for the parent (it's a dir). But there's an asymmetry: the old loop called `store.AddNode(node)` twice per file (once for the file, once for the parent re-add). The new path only calls `AddNode(parent)` once per processNode invocation (not per file). 

The bigger issue: it appends to `parent.Children` in a loop, then calls `b.IngestionTarget.AddNode(parent)` once. If `processNode` is called multiple times for the same parent (multiple matches from a walker), each call creates a fresh `node` struct. The first call correctly captures its Children. But subsequent calls re-fetch `currentChildren` at line ~1474 from the store (which now has the first call's Children), build a new node with those, then call AddFileChildren. This part is actually correct — but only because the re-fetch happens BEFORE the file loop. Confirm this is correct, but it's subtle enough to warrant a comment.

## Files
- internal/ingest/engine.go — bufferingTarget.AddFileChildren (line ~702)

comments.text: Documented in PR #174: comment on bufferingTarget.AddFileChildren now spells out the multi-call/re-fetch invariant so a future refactor reusing the parent pointer can't silently lose children.

title: ListChildNodes is scope creep in this PR and has no callers

`ListChildNodes` was added to `graph.go` (and to the interface in `IngestionTarget`? — no, it was NOT added to the interface). It is a method on `*MemoryStore` only, not declared on any interface. There are zero callers outside of the test file. It was not mentioned in the PR description.

title: Portable mache db: sheaf-topology lockfile + CAS-backed remote build cache (uv.lock shape, keyed on code)
description:
## Framing (user, 2026-05-21)

> "I'm thinking… maybe a repo-portable, pre-compiled mache db? Or a way to recompile from <state>? Like uv.lock but from the code? The sheaves relate. […] it feels like you could solve that direction."

Symmetric to the me-bundle (ley-line-open-dffb77): same substrate (LLO CAS + sheaf + cloister registry + S3-compat transport), keyed by **commit-SHA + parser version** instead of signet identity.

## What this enables

- `mache pull` after cloning a repo: instant code-intel db, **no parse wait**.
- CI never re-parses from scratch — pulls chunks from cache, verifies, computes only deltas.
- New developer onboarding goes from "wait for mache to index your monorepo" to "pull and start."
- The mache db becomes a deterministic, distributable build artifact.

## Substrate (all already exists; this bead is the consumer)

- `BlobStore` trait (ley-line-open-783d72, open) — the CAS surface
- `FsBlobStore` impl (ley-line-open-bb0316, open) — multi-blob layout for the cache contents
- `leyline-sheaf` (ley-line-open-ae7a35, closed) — dependency topology, already the source of `sheaf_invalidate` / `sheaf_status`
- cloister OCI registry (ADR-0009) — content-addressed object distribution
- cloister registry endpoint (ADR-0016) — named-manifest vending
- ADR-0027 matchmaker (cloister-cf7a3b, open) — wires `build-cache/v1` provider/consumer once it lands

## Lockfile shape (uv.lock analogue)

```toml
# mache.lock.toml — generated by `mache push`, committed alongside the repo
[meta]
mache_version    = "0.x.y"
parser_version   = "tree-sitter-go@0.21.0"   # one row per language
schema_version   = "<capnp pin per ADR-0014>"

[sources]
"src/auth.go"  = { hash = "blake3:abc…", chunk = "blake3:111…" }
"src/main.go"  = { hash = "blake3:def…", chunk = "blake3:222…" }
…

[sheaf.topology]
# Per-file deps in the sheaf — invalidates propagate per these edges
"src/auth.go"  = ["src/types.go"]
"src/main.go"  = ["src/auth.go", "src/server.go"]
…
```

Restore semantics:
1. Read `mache.lock.toml` from the repo's working tree
2. For each `[sources]` row: re-hash the local source → compare to lockfile hash
   - Match: chunk is valid; fetch from CAS if not local
   - Mismatch: file diverged; re-parse + emit fresh chunk + invalidate dependents per sheaf
3. Reassemble the db from chunks (whole-db materialization, OR lazy/on-demand)
4. Verify the final db hash matches the lockfile's declared db root

## Phased delivery

**Phase 1 — lockfile schema + emit**
- Define `mache.lock.toml` schema (capnp-backed for IDL discipline + ADR-0014 alignment).
- `mache push` emits the lockfile from a current db state.
- No transport yet; lockfile + chunks land in local CAS.

**Phase 2 — restore from local CAS**
- `mache pull --from-local <cas-path>` reconstructs the db from a lockfile + local chunks.
- Verifies hash chain end-to-end.
- This proves the substrate works without networking.

**Phase 3 — remote cache (capability declaration)**
- Declare `provides = ["build-cache/v1"]` on whatever ships the chunks (R2-backed cloister bucket; OCI artifact; etc.).
- `mache push --to <cache-url>` / `mache pull --from <cache-url>`.
- Capability is the same one me-bundle will use — same matchmaker wiring (ADR-0027 lands later; until then, hand-wired URL).

**Phase 4 — incremental + sheaf-driven**
- On `mache push`, compute the delta from the last lockfile in this repo's history; push only new/changed chunks.
- On `mache pull`, fetch only chunks whose source-hash differs from local OR whose dependents transitively need them per sheaf.
- This is where the sheaf substrate earns its keep.

**Phase 5 — CI/dev UX**
- `mache pull` automatic in `task setup` or equivalent.
- CI workflow `.github/workflows/mache-cache.yml` — pushes on main, pulls on PR.
- Document the cache namespace pattern (per-org or per-repo bucket).

## Out of scope

- The transport itself. Phase 3 just declares the capability shape; the actual `build-cache/v1` impl is its own bead. Likely the simplest first impl is "push to an OCI artifact in cloister's existing registry endpoint" — content-addressable, signed, already deployed.
- ADR-0027 matchmaker landing. This bead works without it (hand-wired); matchmaker makes it cleaner later.
- Cross-language sheaf composition. v1 ships one lockfile per language pair (Go uses tree-sitter-go; Rust uses tree-sitter-rust); merging into a unified cross-language sheaf is v2.

## Symmetry with me-bundle (cross-link)

| Concern | me-bundle (ley-line-open-dffb77) | this bead (mache portable db) |
|---|---|---|
| Index key | signet identity fingerprint | code commit SHA + parser/schema versions |
| Manifest signer | signet | build authority (cloister or signet, decided in Phase 3) |
| Chunks | LLO CAS | LLO CAS (same store) |
| Transport | R2 + cloister registry | OCI registry + cloister registry (same surfaces) |
| Capability requires | identity/v1, signer/v1, blob-store/v1, object-store/v1, named-manifest/v1, transcript-stream/v1 | blob-store/v1, sheaf/v1, build-cache/v1 |

Both are "content-addressed manifests over derived chunks, distributed via cloister surfaces." The substrate is shared; the consumer surfaces (`me`, `mache`) are different.

## Files

- `cmd/cache.go` (new) — `mache push` / `mache pull` subcommands
- `cmd/lockfile.go` (new) — `mache.lock.toml` read/write + verification
- `cmd/cache_test.go` (new)
- `docs/adr/` — ADR for the lockfile schema decision (capnp-backed vs plain TOML)
- `mache.lock.toml.example`
- `.github/workflows/mache-cache.yml` (Phase 5)

## Dependencies

- Depends on: ley-line-open-783d72 (BlobStore trait), ley-line-open-bb0316 (FsBlobStore impl)
- Related to: ley-line-open-dffb77 (me-bundle — shared substrate), cloister-baac45 (ring-io interface — orthogonal but the same matchmaker model), cloister-cf7a3b (ADR-0026 / ADR-0027 implementation arc)

## 2026-05-21 — Portable Units relates; ADR-0020 drafted on branch

User shared the Portable Units design draft this session (cloister-a99b45 / `cloister/docs/seams/portable-units.md`). It's the architectural frame this bead consumes:

- The cache transport (Phase 3) is OCI artifacts in cloister's existing OCI registry — same envelope Portable Units uses for the units themselves.
- A `mache` server running on a developer's laptop becomes a `native` Portable Unit; later, a `wasi:http/proxy` mache becomes a `wasm` Portable Unit. Same unit model both ways.

Decision: **capnp source-of-truth, TOML on-disk via bidi pipeline (cloister ADR-0025), OCI JSON on the wire.** Triplet pattern matches the existing IDL discipline (ADR-0014 / ADR-0013) and reuses cloister's bidi pipeline for ergonomics, while keeping wire interop with the OCI ecosystem.

Three alternatives rejected (pure JSON, pure TOML, pure capnp, Cargo.lock-shape) — see ADR for reasoning.

## 2026-05-22 — Phases 1+2+3+5 complete; Phase 4 design notes

Across 13 `/evolve` iterations, the mache portable-cache feature shipped end-to-end except Phase 4 (chunks-as-parse-outputs). Worked from a `git worktree` at `~/.rsry/worktrees/mache/portable-cache-aeb262/` to sidestep the parallel `infra/elixir-parser-out-of-lfs` checkout occupying the main mache directory.

### Branch `feat/portable-cache-aeb262` — 5 commits

| SHA | Phase | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `3733813` | design | ADR-0020 consumer-side adoption of LLO CacheLockfile schema |
| `c7d90b7` | 1+2 | `mache cache push/pull` cobra subcommands, 7 tests |
| `98fe421` | 3 | OCI build-cache/v1 transport (`--remote` flags), 15 new tests |
| `36dcdfc` | 5 | Taskfile entries + cache-roundtrip GHA workflow |
| `89be3a2` | docs | ADR-0020 path correction (schema-capnp/, not public-schema/) |

### Test totals on this branch

- 7 local push/pull tests (Phase 1+2)
- 12 OCI client tests (Phase 3, httptest-mocked)
- 3 end-to-end remote round-trip tests (Phase 3 integration)
- **22 cache-related tests pass**; `task cache:test` runs them all in <1s

### What works today

```bash
# Local-only round-trip
mache cache push --db ./mache.db ./cache-out
mache cache pull --out-db ./restored.db ./cache-out

# Remote OCI transport
mache cache push --db ./mache.db ./cache-out \
    --remote https://registry.example.com --scope myrepo/abc123
mache cache pull --out-db ./restored.db ./cache-in \
    --remote https://registry.example.com --scope myrepo/abc123 --ref latest
```

### Phase 4 design notes (chunks-as-parse-outputs, sheaf-driven incremental)

The v1 chunk = raw source bytes is correct but uninteresting — it just content-addresses files. Phase 4's payoff: chunks become **the derived `_ast` rows for that source** so a `mache pull` produces a fully-parsed db without re-running tree-sitter.

Implementation sketch:

1. **New chunk shape**: per-source capnp message containing the source's `_ast` rows + its `nodes` rows. LLO's `ast.capnp` defines the wire shape; mache encodes one `AstNode` list per source and writes that as the chunk body.
2. **input_hash stays = BLAKE3(raw source)** — the address of the *input*; doesn't change.
3. **chunk_hash = BLAKE3(canonical capnp bytes)** — diverges from input_hash because chunk is the derived form, not the raw bytes.
4. **Topology**: populate `lockfile.topology` from `leyline-sheaf` edges so consumers can do incremental restore (re-fetch only changed sources + their dependents).
5. **Phase 2 pull becomes more interesting**: instead of just inserting into `_source`, it reconstructs `_source` + `_ast` + `nodes` from the chunks. `_lsp_*` tables are still re-ingest (mache doesn't include those in chunks).

Phase 4 cost estimate: ~500 LoC + new tests + LLO's `ast.capnp` integration on the Go side. The sheaf-edge population is the load-bearing piece — needs `leyline-sheaf` Go bindings to read the topology.

### Status

Phases 1+2+3+5 done. Phase 4 ready to start when prioritized; substrate (LLO `ast.capnp` + sheaf) is in tree.

The `feat/portable-cache-aeb262` branch is local-only (not pushed). All 5 commits on the branch are clean; CI workflow + Taskfile tasks are wired. When ready to ship, the branch can be pushed + PR opened against mache main.

| **Total** | **25 cache-related tests pass** |

`task cache:test` runs all 25 in ~1s. `task cache:roundtrip` runs the end-to-end smoke. `golangci-lint` clean.

### What works end-to-end

```bash
# Local round-trip with AST data
mache cache push --db ./mache.db ./cache-out
mache cache pull --out-db ./restored.db ./cache-out
# → restored.db has _source + _ast byte-equal with input

# Remote OCI transport
mache cache push --db ./mache.db ./cache-out \
    --remote https://cache.example.com --scope myrepo/abc123
mache cache pull --out-db ./restored.db ./cache-in \
    --remote https://cache.example.com --scope myrepo/abc123 --ref latest
```

### Phase 4 design decision: JSON chunks (not capnp)

Per ADR-0021 §"Topology semantics per consumer," chunk body is producer-defined. Mache picks JSON for v1 because:
- Human-readable + diff-friendly
- `encoding/json` is std-lib; no new dep
- No schema bump in cache.capnp
- Auto-detect path is trivial (look for `{"source_id"`)

Future bead can migrate to capnp-encoded `ast.capnp` `List(AstNode)` if cross-runtime byte-equal becomes a requirement.

### Status

The bead can close once the branch lands on main. Recommended close criteria:
- PR opened from `feat/portable-cache-aeb262` against `main`
- CI green (cache-roundtrip workflow)
- Code review

The `feat/portable-cache-aeb262` branch is local-only (worktree at `~/.rsry/worktrees/mache/portable-cache-aeb262/`). Whoever pushes the branch first should also bump `leyline-schema` to a tagged version that ships `cache.capnp` so the `go.mod` `replace` directive can come out.

title: Write-back support for JSON data sources
description:
## Problem

Mache's write-back pipeline only works for tree-sitter sources (Go, TS, Python,
etc.) where edits splice back into source files via byte-range replacement. JSON
data sources are always read-only — edits to projected files can't propagate
back to the underlying .json file.

This limits mache's value for coordination use cases (e.g. the-firm's .audit/
files) where agents need to both read AND write structured data. Currently
agents must bypass mache and edit the source JSON/markdown directly.

## Why it matters

The audit-schema example projects .audit/.index.json as a structured VFS, but
it's read-only. An agent can `cat /findings/by-severity/critical/C1/status` but
can't `echo FIXED > /findings/by-severity/critical/C1/status` to update it.
This makes the VFS a read-only lens rather than a true coordination surface.

More broadly, any JSON-backed mache mount (NVD, KEV, config files, etc.) would
benefit from write-back — edit the projected file, have mache write the change
back into the source JSON via JSONPath.

## Approach (sketch)

- Track JSONPath origin per node during ingestion (analogous to SourceOrigin
  byte ranges for tree-sitter)
- On write: validate new value, resolve JSONPath back to source JSON location,
  update in-place using json.Marshal round-trip
- For indexed sources (indexer → .index.json → mache): write-back to .index.json,
  optionally re-trigger indexer to sync back to markdown source files

## Files
- internal/ingest/json_walker.go (needs to emit origin metadata)
- internal/ingest/engine.go (wire JSON write-back path)
- internal/writeback/ (new JSON splice logic)
- cmd/mount.go (enable --writable for JSON sources)

title: Design write-schema spec for JSON write-back
description:
## Problem

JSON write-back needs a way to map projected file edits back to JSONPath
locations in the source. The current schema only defines the read projection
(selector + content_template). We need a write-side counterpart.

## Approach

Add an optional `write_template` or `write_path` field to Leaf that specifies
how to reverse the projection:

```json
{
  "name": "status",
  "content_template": "{{.status}}",
  "write_path": "$.findings[?(@.id=='{{.id}}')].status"
}
```

Or a `write_schema` top-level section that maps file paths back to JSONPath
mutations. Design considerations:

- How to handle type coercion (string "2" → number 2 for scores)
- Whether write_path is per-leaf or per-node
- Validation rules (enum constraints, required fields)
- Whether to support creating new records (POST-like) or only updates (PUT-like)

## Deliverable

RFC/ADR with the write-schema spec, covering edge cases and interaction with
file_sets/include.

title: Track JSONPath origin metadata during JSON ingestion
description:
## Problem

Tree-sitter sources track SourceOrigin (file, start_byte, end_byte) per node,
enabling surgical write-back via byte-range splice. JSON ingestion doesn't
track any origin metadata — we don't know which JSONPath produced a given node.

## Fix

During JSON walker iteration, record the resolved JSONPath + field name per
emitted value. Store as a new JsonOrigin struct alongside (or extending)
SourceOrigin. This is the prerequisite for any JSON write-back.

## Files
- internal/ingest/json_walker.go (emit origin during Values())
- internal/graph/graph.go (JsonOrigin struct or extend SourceOrigin)
- internal/ingest/engine.go (propagate origin to stored nodes)

title: Implement JSON splice write-back
description:
## Problem

Once we have a write-schema spec (mache-b1w.1) and origin tracking
(mache-b1w.2), we need the actual write-back logic: take an edited
file's content, resolve the target JSONPath in the source file, and
update the value in-place.

## Approach

- Parse source JSON into ast/map
- Navigate to target via stored JSONPath origin
- Replace value, handling type coercion per write-schema rules
- Marshal back with stable formatting (preserve indentation)
- Atomic write (temp + rename) to source file

## Files
- internal/writeback/json_splice.go (new)
- cmd/mount.go (wire --writable for JSON sources, currently skipped)

title: Sheaf cache should serve mache's own community/projection lookups, not just push downstream
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-09 from mache-6b6da6 phase 3 flamegraph review.

## What we observed

E2E heap-delta flamegraphs (post-PR #361) show:

| Tool | Top heap allocator | Share |
|---|---|---|
| `get_architecture` | `internal/graph.buildProjection` + `DetectCommunities` | ~85% cum |
| `get_communities` | same | ~44% |
| `get_impact` | `MemoryStore.DefsMap` rebuild | 52% |
| `get_overview` | `MemoryStore.DefsMap` rebuild | 32% |

Each call recomputes the projection graph + Louvain communities + defs map from scratch. On a real workload (mache-on-mache, ~241 files), these aren't tiny: `buildProjection` walks every ref, `DetectCommunities` runs Louvain modularity iterations, `DefsMap` allocates per-construct.

## What's already there

`internal/leyline/sheaf.go` defines `SheafClient.PushTopology()` which converts community detection output into `sheaf_set_topology` ops sent to the ley-line daemon over UDS. `cmd/serve_handlers.go::makeGetCommunitiesHandler` calls `DetectCommunities`, then fires-and-forgets the result to the sheaf cache.

Architecture today:

```
mache MCP call → DetectCommunities → push to sheaf cache → return result
                       ↑                         ↓
                       └───── never reads ───────┘  (one-way)
                                                 ↓
                                          (for downstream
                                           ley-line consumers'
                                           invalidation queries)
```

The cache exists for ley-line-driven invalidation of OTHER consumers. Mache itself does not use it to skip its own recomputation.

## The fix

Make the sheaf cache a real cache for mache's own MCP tools. Architecture target:

```
mache MCP call → check sheaf cache (sock query) → hit?
                                                   ↓ yes → return cached result
                                                   ↓ no  → compute → push → return
```

Concrete deliverables:

1. **Read API on SheafClient**: add `LookupTopology()`/`LookupDefsMap()`/etc. that query the daemon for cached results keyed by source-tree hash.
2. **Daemon-side cache slots**: ley-line daemon needs to serve back what mache pushes. Today it accepts `sheaf_set_topology` but there's no `sheaf_get_topology` op (per the `unknown op` errors in test logs).
3. **Cache-keying**: hash the input set (refs map for projection, node defs for DefsMap). When the source tree hasn't changed since the last push, reuse.
4. **Invalidation**: already half-built — sheaf is topology-aware. Extend `sheaf_invalidate` to invalidate downstream caches (projection, DefsMap) when their input regions change.

## Why this matters now

Heap-delta findings from the e2e harness (PR #361) are dominated by these recomputations on a TOY 4-package fixture. Scale to mache-on-mache (or any real codebase), and `get_architecture`/`get_communities` do real work that's wasted on every call. Caching is the obvious lever.

Plus: the sheaf cache infrastructure already exists, was already designed for this, just isn't wired both ways.

## Cross-repo

This is mache-driven primarily, but ley-line-open needs a `sheaf_get_topology` op (counterpart to `sheaf_set_topology`). Cross-repo paired bead in LLO once this scope settles.

## Out of scope

- LRU eviction policy for the daemon's cache (a separate bead)
- Cache persistence across daemon restarts (a separate bead)
- Cross-mache-instance cache sharing (the daemon already enables this; just needs the read path)

## Refs

- Surfaced post-PR #361 (mache-6b6da6 phase 3 flamegraphs)
- Existing infra: `internal/leyline/sheaf.go`, `cmd/serve_handlers.go::makeGetCommunitiesHandler`
- Pairs with the eventual ly-line-open `sheaf_get_topology` daemon op

title: Re-run ARENA + quantitative bench for v0.18.0 (pure-Go) — capture the O(n)-projection speedup rigorously
description: Post-v0.18.0 (pure-Go, PR-B merged). docs/ARENA.md covers v0.17.0 (last-verified 2026-07-08) — stale after the O(nodes²)→O(nodes) projection fix (mache-4f3840) + CGO removal. Re-run scripts/arena.sh + benchmarks/quantitative on the released pure-Go binary to capture the speedup rigorously (session ad-hoc: cmd/ 4m22s→3.1s ~78x; whole repo >3min/20min-hang→~10s; find_callees restored on serve). comments.text:
Perf half MEASURED (2026-07-21); ARENA half still open.

Method: two binaries from the same lineage — 3e13737 (pure-Go, pre-index-fix) vs shipped v0.18.0 — so this isolates the ASTWalker projection change, NOT the CGO cutover. Same pinned leyline both sides.

RESULT on cmd/ with examples/go-schema.json:
  before = 284.45s | after = 5.69s | 50.0x
  nodes = 3646 on BOTH sides (byte-parity: pure speed win, no coverage regression)

METHODOLOGY TRAP — my first measurement said the fix did NOTHING:
  - default _ast projection on cmd/: 2.43s -> 2.21s (~1.1x, noise)
  - dirs <=198KB, warm: no measurable difference
The O(n^2) lived in ExtractCalls/fileAddrRefs, which only run under a schema carrying call/reference
templates (go-schema.json). Benchmark the DEFAULT projection and the fix looks like a no-op.
Also: cold-vs-warm dominates small runs (0.60s cold vs 0.06s warm on a 6KB dir) — warm both sides.

SCOPE OF CLAIM: speedup scales with per-FILE node count, not repo size. cmd/ blows up because it
holds a 169KB and a 110KB test file. Quote as 'up to 50x on call-extraction over large files',
never 'mache is 50x faster'.

Corroborates the ad-hoc session figure (4m22s -> 3.1s, ~78x): same order, mine more conservative.

REMAINING: ARENA 6-level re-run (agent-driven) + docs/reference/projection-performance.md.
docs/reference/arena.md still carries last-verified 2026-07-08 pointing here.
comments.author: rsry-cli

comments.text:
SUPERSEDES the '50x' framing in my prior comment — that was n=1 and misleading.

RIGOROUS SCALING SWEEP (2026-07-21): single Go file, N functions x4 call sites each, go-schema, 3 warm runs/point, before=3e13737 vs after=v0.18.0 (same pinned leyline; isolates the ASTWalker fix, not CGO).

  n=125  (259 nodes):  before 2.345s  after 0.115s  ratio  20x
  n=250  (509 nodes):  before 9.486s  after 0.187s  ratio  51x
  n=500 (1009 nodes):  before 42.88s  after 0.353s  ratio 121x
  n=1000(2009 nodes):  before 152.6s  after 0.774s  ratio 197x

Power-law fit (log-log LSQ, 4 points):
  before: k = 2.02  (O(n^2), 4.07x per input doubling) — textbook quadratic
  after : k = 0.92  (O(n^0.9), ~linear)
Nodes identical before==after at every size -> pure speed, zero coverage change.

KEY: the SPEEDUP RATIO = before/after = n^2/n = n, so it DOUBLES when file size doubles. There is no single 'Nx' number — quote as 'O(n^2)->O(n) in per-file node count; observed 20x-197x over 259-2009 nodes/file, growing linearly beyond.' The earlier ad-hoc 50x and the cmd/ 50x are just the ~n=250 point.

DRIVER is per-FILE node count, not repo size (the quadratic was per-file in ExtractCalls/fileAddrRefs). Repos of many small files see little benefit; a repo with one huge file sees a lot.

MEASUREMENT TRAPS worth keeping: (1) the default _ast projection does NOT exercise the quadratic — only schemas with call/ref templates do; benchmark the wrong schema and the fix looks like a no-op (my first result). (2) cold leyline-parse dominates small runs; warm both sides.

Raw data: scratchpad/bench/scaling-results.tsv + scaling_sweep.sh.
STILL OPEN: docs/reference/projection-performance.md not written; ARENA 6-level re-run not done.

title: leyline schema↔binary version-parity gate: assert go.mod leyline-schema major.minor == leylineBinaryVersion
description:
Two independent leyline versions coexist in mache and today disagree:
- `go.mod` → `leyline-schema` v0.5.6 (post-#460)

title: 'context' virtual file absent in agent mount (0/236) — blog-headline `cat context` not surfacing node.Context
description:
VERIFIED 2026-06-24 by mounting assay via `mache /tmp/m -d <repo> --infer` (go preset, the agent-facing schema): the projection has 236 `source` files but **0 `context` files**. A substantive Go function (cmd/functions/detectDocsDir, 236B source) has `callers` + `source` but no `context`. The blog's headline differentiator — `cat context` = "only the imports and types visible to this scope" (internal/vfs/context.go ContextHandler) — does not appear for any construct.

node.Context IS populated in code: engine_walk.go:394 `Context: fileContext`, and read by memstore_callees.go (parseGoImports) for callee resolution. So the field carries the file's imports internally, but the VFS ContextHandler (serves node.Context when len>0) yields nothing in the mount. Investigate the disconnect — candidates: (a) the mount's graph backend (SQLiteGraph/NFS path) doesn't carry the MemoryStore-populated Context field; (b) Context is set on file-level nodes, not the construct dirs the ContextHandler matches; (c) fileContext is empty under the inferred go preset.

IMPACT: (1) blocks the M2 measurement (context-token efficiency = tokens(source+context) vs full file — can't measure an absent file); (2) it's a claim-vs-reality gap on a headline feature, same class as the symbol_lookup_fp_rate.md finding that find_definition was broken on its projection. Surfaced by attempting to actually RUN the measurement rather than spec it abstractly.

Files: internal/vfs/context.go, internal/ingest/engine_walk.go, internal/graph (mount backend). Relates to the measurement-contracts design + the Feb blog's M2 claim.

comments.text:
Fixed — PR opened (session 2026-07-01). Root cause was candidate (a): node.Context is set at ingest (engine_walk.go) and survives in MemoryStore, but the SQLite path dropped it — nodes table had no context column, SQLiteWriter.AddNode didn't write it, and neither GetNode path (SQLiteWriter.GetNode, NodesTableReader.GetNode) selected it. So vfs.ContextHandler always saw empty Context.

Fix: added `context BLOB` column; AddNode persists n.Context; both GetNode paths read it; SQLiteWriter.GetNode round-trips it too (else the engine two-pass write nulls it via INSERT OR REPLACE — same class as Properties/mache-d28eb1); NodesTableReader selects it only when the column exists (new graph.ColumnExists) for backward-compat with old/leyline nodes tables; incremental builds ALTER it in. Both mount backends (SQLiteGraph .db path + WritableGraph) delegate GetNode to NodesTableReader, so both are covered.

Tests added: writer persistence + writer GetNode round-trip (ingest); mount-path NodesTableReader.GetNode carries Context + backward-compat missing-column (graph). vfs.ContextHandler already tested against node.Context. Verified: graph+ingest+vfs green, -race clean, vet+golangci-lint pass. Close on merge.

title: SendOpInto: surface daemon-version mismatch as a clear error
description:
Follow-up from Copilot review on PR #372 (typed daemon-response decode).

When mache talks to a pre-b0ea2e daemon (or any daemon that emits bare numeric JSON for Int64 fields), `SocketClient.SendOpInto` returns a low-level `*json.UnmarshalTypeError` like:

  unmarshal response: json: invalid use of ,string struct tag, trying to unmarshal unquoted value into *int64

This is loud (good — silent zeros are gone) but doesn't point a user at the actual cause: daemon version skew vs. mache's required wire (LLO ≥ v0.3.0).

Proposed work:
- In `internal/leyline/socket.go::SendOpInto`, wrap the `json.Unmarshal` error: when the underlying error is a `*json.UnmarshalTypeError` whose Struct + Field would have decoded successfully with a `,string` tag, wrap with a message like: "decode failed (likely daemon wire mismatch — mache requires LLO ≥ v0.3.0): <orig>".
- Add a unit test in `internal/leyline/socket_test.go` that round-trips a fixture with bare numeric int64 through `SendOpInto[GetNodeResponse]` and asserts the error string contains the version-mismatch hint.

Scope is small (<50 LOC + one test). Non-blocking for PR #372 — the inverse-guard test `TestGetNode_RejectsBareNumericSize` in cmd/uds_graph_test.go already pins that the failure is loud; this just makes the message actionable.

Reference: https://github.com/agentic-research/mache/pull/372#discussion_r3229265418

title: Agent mount requires interactive sudo — route through fuse-t/leyline-fuse for the no-sudo userspace mount the blog promises
description:
VERIFIED 2026-06-24: `mache --agent` / NFS mount shells out to `sudo mount -t nfs` (internal/nfsmount/server.go:82, "Requires sudo on macOS") — an interactive password/Touch-ID prompt on every mount. This contradicts the blog's "mache on your laptop, one command" UX and the v0.9.0 "no sudo" framing (which is true for BUILDING/RUNNING the binary, but NOT for the mount action).

Root cause: go-nfs is a userspace SERVER, but the macOS NFS CLIENT mount is kernel-gated behind root. Userspace server != no-sudo mount.

The no-sudo path already exists in the stack: fuse-t mounts a userspace volume WITHOUT per-mount root (one-time-installed privileged helper), and leyline ALREADY has a `fuse` backend (`leyline daemon --mount <X>` → backend "nfs"|"fuse"). mache even auto-starts the leyline daemon during agent mode. So mache could route its mount through leyline-fuse / fuse-t instead of raw `sudo mount`, eliminating the prompt.

IMPACT: (1) blocks frictionless `mache --agent` (the headline laptop UX); (2) makes any mount-based automation/measurement CI-hostile (no non-interactive mount). Note for the measurement work: batch measurement should read from the .db (mache build --out + direct node access), not the mount, regardless of this fix.

Files: internal/nfsmount/server.go, cmd/mount.go. Relates to ADR-0006 (FUSE removed v0.7.0, NFS-only), the fuse-t learnings, and the Feb blog's UX claim.

title: cross-lang refs: `internal/resolve/` package — Resolver interface + Registry
description:
## What

Create `internal/resolve/resolver.go` defining the `Resolver` interface, `Registry` struct (scheme → Resolver), and sentinel errors `ErrNotResolvable` / `ErrSchemeUnknown`. Add a table-driven unit test (`resolver_test.go`) that registers two fake resolvers and verifies routing + sentinel returns.

## Interface shape

```go
type Resolver interface {
    Resolve(ctx context.Context, locator string) (graph.Graph, error)
}

type Registry struct { /* sync.Map[scheme]Resolver */ }

func NewRegistry() *Registry
func (r *Registry) Register(scheme string, res Resolver)
func (r *Registry) Resolve(ctx context.Context, scheme, locator string) (graph.Graph, error)
```

## Constraints

- Pure Go. No CGO, no tree-sitter dependency at this layer.
- No cache in `Registry` itself — caching is the resolver's responsibility.
- No global / package-level `sync.Map` — `Registry` is an explicit object passed to handlers (testable, avoids init-order issues).
- Depend only on `internal/graph` (for `graph.Graph`). No dependency on `ingest`, `cmd`, or `nfsmount`.

## Why this is bead #1

Establishes the contract every subsequent bead in the cross-language refs sequence builds on. Zero risk, dispatchable alone. Derived from `mache-q43l` synthesis (architect's bead #1, math friend confirmed the type signature should reflect the Kleisli-arrow effects monad — `error` is the V1 simplification; richer error types come later).

## Files

`internal/resolve/resolver.go`, `internal/resolve/resolver_test.go` (both new).

title: cross-lang refs: `LocalPathResolver` — local-relative-path ingestion
description:
## What

Implement `LocalPathResolver` in `internal/resolve/localpath_resolver.go`. Resolves `./X` / `../X` locators against an anchor directory, calls `ingest.Engine` with auto-schema to ingest the resolved directory, caches the result, and returns the resulting `graph.Graph`.

## Shape

```go
type LocalPathResolver struct {
    anchor  string         // absolute dir the locator is relative to
    engine  *ingest.Engine // injected
    cache   sync.Map       // absPath → graph.Graph
    sf      singleflight.Group // coalesce concurrent resolutions
}

func NewLocalPathResolver(anchor string, engine *ingest.Engine) *LocalPathResolver
func (r *LocalPathResolver) Resolve(ctx context.Context, locator string) (graph.Graph, error)
```

## Behavior

- Locator that isn't `./...` or `../...` → return `ErrNotResolvable` (caller decides whether to emit `remote_hint`). Move `isLocalRelativeLocator` from `cmd/serve_resolve_ref.go:138` into this file.
- Resolved absolute path that escapes the anchor → reject (`ErrNotResolvable` or new `ErrEscapesAnchor`).
- Use `singleflight.Group` keyed by absolute path to coalesce concurrent resolution of the same locator (also prevents A→B→A recursion within a single resolution).
- V1 cache: in-memory `sync.Map`, no eviction. Resolved sub-graphs are immutable for the parent session's lifetime.
- V2 (separate bead, not this one): if the resolved directory already has a ley-line-open `.db` sidecar, skip `ingest.Engine` and open via `SQLiteGraph`. One-line check in `Resolve` before falling through to ingest.

## Schema

Use `ingest.AutoSchema` (language detection + default source preset) — same path `cmd/mount.go` uses when no `--schema` flag is given. This is the resolver's one concrete dependency on the ingest package.

## Tests

Integration test (`localpath_resolver_test.go`): create a tempdir with two `.tf` files, instantiate `LocalPathResolver` anchored there, call `Resolve(ctx, "./")`, assert `ListChildren("")` is non-empty. Gate as needed for CGO (terraform tree-sitter grammar).

## Depends on

`mache-bd97d9` (the `Resolver` interface).

## Files

`internal/resolve/localpath_resolver.go` (new), `internal/resolve/localpath_resolver_test.go` (new).

title: cross-lang refs: wire `resolve_ref` to mount sub-graph in `CompositeGraph`
description:
## What

Modify `cmd/serve_resolve_ref.go` so that successful local-path resolutions actually **mount the resolved sub-graph** under `CompositeGraph` and add a `graph_path` field to the response. Today the handler ignores its `graph.Graph` parameter (line 47) and returns flat filesystem metadata — after this bead it returns a graph-mounted prefix that other MCP tools (`list_directory`, `find_callers`, `find_definition`) can immediately query.

## End-state behavior

```
MCP: resolve_ref(token="mod:./modules/vpc", base_path="/project/main.tf")
  → resolve.Registry.Resolve(ctx, "mod", "./modules/vpc")
  → LocalPathResolver.Resolve → subGraph
  → composite.Mount("resolve/<sha256-prefix>", subGraph)
  → response: {
        resolved: "/project/modules/vpc",
        graph_path: "resolve/<prefix>",   // NEW
        files: [...]                        // keep for orientation
    }

MCP: list_directory(path="resolve/<prefix>")
  → routes to subGraph.ListChildren("") → [functions/, variables/, ...]
```

## Implementation

- Change `makeResolveRefHandler(_ graph.Graph)` to `makeResolveRefHandler(g graph.Graph, reg *resolve.Registry, composite *graph.CompositeGraph)`.
- Add `wrapCompositeHandler(func(graph.Graph, *graph.CompositeGraph) ToolHandlerFunc)` variant to `cmd/serve_registry.go` alongside the existing `wrapHandler` — only `resolve_ref` uses it in V1.
- In `cmd/serve.go`: instantiate `resolve.Registry`, register `LocalPathResolver` for the `"mod"` scheme anchored to the session's data root, pass to `registerMCPTools`.
- Mount prefix: `resolve/<sha256prefix-of-absPath>`. Use a short stable hash so listings show `resolve/abc12345` and the prefix is collision-resistant. Include session ID if `cmd/serve_registry.go` shows session isolation is needed for multi-repo daemon mode.
- Mount idempotency: `CompositeGraph.Mount` errors on duplicate prefix. Check the cache (or use `composite.MountPrefixOf` if it exists) before mounting; on cached resolution, return the existing prefix.

## Why this is the Terraform → local-path E2E milestone

This is the first bead that makes cross-language refs *useful*: once a Terraform `mod:` ref is resolved, the agent can `find_callers` / `find_definition` / `list_directory` on the resolved module without further plumbing changes (federation via `CompositeGraph.DefsMap` is automatic). This proves the model end-to-end before generalizing to more schemes.

## Tests

Extend `cmd/serve_resolve_ref_test.go`: instantiate a session with a Terraform fixture, call `resolve_ref(mod:./submodule)`, assert `graph_path` is non-empty, then call `list_directory(graph_path)` and assert the response includes expected entries from the submodule.

## Depends on

`mache-bdcd2b` (the `LocalPathResolver`).

## Files

Modify: `cmd/serve_resolve_ref.go`, `cmd/serve_registry.go`, `cmd/serve.go`, `cmd/serve_resolve_ref_test.go`.

title: cross-lang refs: `callers/` virtual entries for scheme-typed ref tokens
description:
## What

Today `GetCallers("mod:./modules/vpc")` returns construct-dir nodes (the Terraform blocks that declare that module source). That's correct. But the `callers/` virtual directory under those construct dirs doesn't link to the **resolved sub-graph** when one is mounted. This bead closes that loop.

After this bead, a `callers/<construct>/` virtual dir on a scheme-typed-ref-bearing construct also exposes a symlink (NFS) or `graphFile` entry (MCP) pointing into the resolved sub-graph's mount prefix when a mount exists.

## Implementation

- Touch `internal/nfsmount/graphfs.go` `Lookup` / `Readdir` for `callers/` entries: when a `callers/` entry's parent path corresponds to a scheme-typed token (heuristic: contains `:`) and the `CompositeGraph` has a mount for that token's resolved target, emit an additional virtual entry pointing to the mount prefix.
- Parallels the existing `callees/` symlink pattern (`callersSymlinkTarget()` in `internal/fs/root.go`); use the same relative-path approach.
- Self-gating: only appears when the mount exists. Same predicate as the existing `callers/` and `callees/` self-gating.

## Why this is its own bead

Touches NFS virtual dir plumbing — higher blast radius than the pure-Go MCP handler changes in mache-be0b9f. Keeping it separate lets mache-be0b9f land and prove the model with MCP-only tooling first.

## Tests

`internal/nfsmount/graphfs_test.go` or a new test: ingest a Terraform fixture with a `mod:./submodule` ref, call `resolve_ref` to mount, then `Readdir` on `<construct>/callers/` and assert the resolved-sub-graph symlink is present.

## Depends on

`mache-be0b9f` (the mount must happen before this can hook into it).

## Files

Modify: `internal/nfsmount/graphfs.go`. Possibly `internal/fs/root.go` if the symlink-target helper needs a sibling for scheme-typed targets.

title: Drop SocketClient.Subscribe (dead method, 0 callers)
description:

If mache was LLO's only consumer of `subscribe`, LLO may also have dead machinery; that's tracked as a separate LLO-side audit (option b from the LL discussion).
