comments.text:
FIRST MEASUREMENT (2026-07-22) — hypothesis confirmed, plus a design correction.

HEADLINE: two modules for one line.
  golang.org/x/text/cases    -> 1 symbol, 1 file
  golang.org/x/text/language -> 1 symbol, 1 file
  Sole use: internal/template/render.go:80
      "title": cases.Title(language.Und).String,
  That is the whole surface. NOTE the tradeoff before "fixing" it: this is the
  Unicode-correct title-caser (the strings.Title replacement). Hand-rolling it would be
  heuristic character matching — precisely the smell this repo rejects (see
  feedback_regex_is_a_smell). So "thin" does NOT imply "removable"; the report must
  carry justification, not auto-fail.

OTHER THIN SURFACES (symbols/files): ojg/jp 1/1, go-billy/helper/chroot 1/1,
go-nfs 1/1, hclsyntax 1/1, hclwrite 1/1, go-nfs/helpers 2/1, mcptest 2/1, blake3 2/5,
go-task/taskfile/ast 2/1, leyline-schema/cache 2/2, gofumpt/format 2/1, toml 3/5,
bbolt 3/1. Deep/healthy for contrast: testify/assert 41/156, mcp-go/mcp 17/21.

DESIGN CORRECTION — do NOT guess package names from import paths. My first cut derived
the local alias from the path's last segment, which is wrong for versioned modules:
  github.com/hashicorp/hcl/v2 -> package is "hcl", NOT "v2"
  go.yaml.in/yaml/v3          -> package is "yaml", NOT "v3"
Both reported a FALSE 0 symbols despite real use (hcl.InitialPos, hcl.DiagError,
yaml.Unmarshal). The accurate source is the toolchain:
  go list -json <path>  ->  {"ImportPath": "...", "Name": "hcl"}
Use go list for names + imports, then go/ast for symbol counting. No new dependency
(go list is the toolchain), and no path heuristics.

ALSO: blank imports must be classified separately, not flagged as thin. modernc.org/sqlite
shows 0 symbols across 76 files because it is `_ "modernc.org/sqlite"` — the SQL driver,
legitimately symbol-less.

title: ADR-0034 sub-bead: per-tenant mache + per-tenant LLO composition
description:
Per cloister ADR-0034 §Sequencing (deferred-but-tracked).

## Context

cloister's multi-tenant direction (ADR-0030 + ADR-0034) requires per-tenant mache instances. mache's FUSE projection + tree-sitter index + LLO backend all currently assume single-tenant scope.

## Scope

1. **Per-tenant mache instance**: each tenant's cloister-router gets its own mache sidecar with its own mounted code scope.
2. **Per-tenant LLO backend**: mache internally consumes ley-line-open's LSP. Per-tenant mache → per-tenant LLO. **Blocks on**: LLO repo's multi-tenant work.
3. **Identity-aware queries (optional)**: mache could grow a tenant-scoped query layer that scopes `find_callers` / `search` / etc. by tenant identity, instead of relying on per-instance isolation alone.

## Two migration shapes

**Option A (preferred, simpler)**: per-tenant mache binary, each indexing its own per-tenant code mount. Cluster.toml `[bundles."mache-tenant-<id>"]` per tenant.

**Option B (more complex)**: shared mache binary with a tenant-aware query layer. Adds tenant-scope check to every MCP method.

Recommend Option A — matches the per-tenant workerd shape from ADR-0030.

## Blocks on

- cloister `[[tenants]]` schema bead (cloister-ce936e) — defines the operator-facing shape
- LLO multi-tenant work (ley-line-open repo bead — file there)

## Parent

- cloister ADR-0034 (filed in cloister tracker as `cloister-cbfd7f`)

## Estimated effort

2-4 weeks per ADR-0034. Substantial because LLO is in the dependency chain.

title: Smell rules as a capnp-schema-defined format (IDL + generated validators)
description: mache's smell rules are hand-authored JSON today (could be YAML). Define the smell-rule shape as a **capnp schema** so the format is IDL-defined once and consistent across every consumer, then generate validators/types from it. Authoring can stay JSON/YAML (human-friendly) while validation runs against the generated schema — capnp is the contract, JSON/YAML the ergonomics. Generation could reuse cloister's schema-bridge (ADR-0036: capnp → zod TS + Go multi-output) as a third input alongside cluster.capnp + identity.capnp, or mache can own its own emit. This belongs in mache (it owns the smell surface / find_smells), NOT cloister — moved out of cloister-ffab6a which only retains the (now-shipped) cluster.toml boilerplate cleanup. Consider: does mache want the capnp schema vendored locally or to depend on schema-bridge as a build tool?

comments.text: Clarification from the user: **schema-bridge stays in cloister** (`tools/schema-bridge/`, ADR-0036) — it may move out eventually, but today mache *leverages* it, doesn't own its own emitter. So the shape is: mache defines its smell-rule shape as a **capnp schema** (mache's domain), and runs cloister's schema-bridge over it to generate the validator/types (Go for mache, zod TS if useful). The value is "representation consistency across things + more linting power" — one IDL, generated validators, JSON/YAML authoring validated against the generated schema. Not "mache owns a parallel emitter." Cross-repo dependency: mache build-depends on (or vendors output from) cloister's schema-bridge, same as cluster.capnp + identity.capnp are its inputs today.

title: semgrep2mache: transpile semgrep-rules DSL → SmellRule SQL over the _ast substrate (falsifiable corpus experiment)
description:
User ask 2026-07-14: "given mache's examples folder, can we expose the DSL of semgrep into SQL?" Answer: a transpiler, not an engine — semgrep is a fused special case of the substrate's three-tier stack with a YAML front-end.

## Construct → substrate mapping (analyzed 2026-07-14)
| semgrep | substrate | fidelity |
|---|---|---|
| pattern (kind + field shape) | _ast.node_kind + node_child.field + node_content.raw_kind joins (= today's smell rules) | clean |
| pattern-inside (ancestor) | node_id materialized path: LIKE ancestor.node_id || '/%' | clean |
| $X == $X (metavariable unification) | node_hash equality — structural subtree identity is an INDEX JOIN via the merkle CAS. Better than semgrep's per-candidate structural compare | better-than-original |
| metavariable-regex | _source byte ranges + the #match? machinery ast_walker_selector.go already SQL-compiles | exists |
| pattern-either / pattern-not | UNION / NOT EXISTS | trivial |
| ... (ellipsis) | node_child ordinal-gap predicates | clunky but expressible |
| typed metavariables | binding tier (_lsp_hover) | partial |
| import aliasing (np.array ≡ numpy.array) | name-resolution tier: _lsp_refs qualifier + ExtractGoImports (Go alias→path already exists) | partial |
| f(x) ≡ f( x ) formatting | FREE — _ast never sees whitespace | free |
| constant/symbolic propagation | dataflow: must-reach fixpoint over _cfg with constants lattice — same machinery as taint (ADR-0024 arm-C), gated on LLO populating _cfg | planned |
| taint mode (sources/sinks) | ADR-0024 arm-C literally | planned |

NO structural gap: every construct lands on a named tier — syntactic (_ast+CAS, shipped), binding (_lsp/qualifier, partial), dataflow (_cfg fixpoints, ADR-0024).

## Deliverable shape
`semgrep2mache <rule.yaml>` → SmellRule JSON consumable by the existing rules-as-data pipeline (MACHE_SMELL_RULES_DIR overlay, find-smells CLI, composite action). Transpiler, not engine — zero new runtime machinery in mache for the syntactic tier.

## The falsifiable corpus experiment (the point)
The semgrep-rules OSS repo (~2,000 rules, user has it locally as a repo) is a ground-truth corpus:
1. Transpile ALL rules; report N% compiles cleanly + a construct histogram of failures.
2. Every failure buckets as: transpiler gap / LLO substrate gap (the container_node_id pattern — missing columns are fixable upstream) / genuine expressiveness boundary.
3. Differential oracle: run transpiled rules + real semgrep on the same fixture corpus, diff findings (claim↔ground-truth-diff, match-truth-not-model per project_smell_enforcement).

## Spike scope (weekend-sized, do first)
Transpile the ~10 most-used Go rules from the corpus by hand-or-tool, run on mache itself, diff against semgrep output. Kills or confirms the thesis before any real transpiler investment.

## Relations
- ADR-0024 / mache-463612 (dataflow arms are the planned tiers this consumes)
- mache-472f60 (normalized cross-language code-fact layer — same "plain SQL, no bespoke DSL" thesis; semgrep-YAML becomes a FRONT-END to it, not a competitor)
- mache-cff68e / mache-e0748c (SmellRule as validated contract — transpiler output should validate against it)
- examples/smell-rules starter kit (mache-fe3a4a) — transpiled rules are overlay rules; corpus results feed the starter examples
- Competitive positioning: reference_competitive_landscape — "runs your existing semgrep rules on the substrate" is an adoption wedge

comments.text: TWO REFINEMENTS (2026-07-15): (1) LICENSING — the upstream semgrep-rules repo was RELICENSED (~Dec 2024) from LGPL to the Semgrep Rules License, which restricts use with competing engines; transpiling it into mache SQL is arguably the exact restricted use (this is what triggered the Opengrep fork). Corpus target must be **opengrep-rules** (the LGPL-era fork) — verify license text before shipping any transpiled output. checkov (Apache-2.0) is unencumbered for the infra-side comparison (boundary-refs B1). (2) FIDELITY-RUNG HISTOGRAM — the fatal_call ladder work (see the fatal-call fidelity bead) maps semgrep tiers onto the poset: syntactic patterns=mention/rung1, typed metavariables=binding/rung2, taint=reachability/rung3. The corpus experiment's construct histogram should therefore bucket rules BY REQUIRED RUNG, which directly yields "expressible today vs gated on _lsp coverage vs gated on _cfg" — a sharper deliverable than a flat can/can't-compile split.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

title: find_callees MCP tool returns [] — construct nodes missing `lang` Properties on mache build
description:
Surfaced empirically by the PR #373 post-fix bench audit (see `benchmarks/serena/results/mache_cc_fresh_eval_macherepo_postfix.md` Issue A).

`find_callees` MCP tool returns `{"callees":[],"hint":"no resolved callees"}` for every construct path on a .db built via `mache build --backend tree-sitter`, even though the materialized `<construct>/callees/<name>` virtual directory IS populated for the same construct.

## Root cause

`SQLiteGraph.GetCallees` reads the construct node's `record` JSON to extract `langName`:

```go
// internal/graph/sqlite_graph.go:780-790
_ = g.db.QueryRow("SELECT record FROM nodes WHERE id = ? AND kind = 1", id).Scan(&recordJSON)
if json.Unmarshal([]byte(recordJSON.String), &props) == nil {
    if lang, ok := props["lang"]; ok {
        langName = string(lang)
    }
}
```

Empirical SQL query on a fresh `mache build`:

    sqlite3 /tmp/mache_fixed.db "SELECT json_extract(record, '$.lang') AS l, count(*) FROM nodes WHERE kind=1 GROUP BY l;"
    -- | 3654

ZERO of 3,654 construct nodes have `lang` set. Every record column contains only `location`. So `langName=""` for every call, the extractor's `lang.ForName("")` returns nil grammar, and `find_callees` always returns empty.

## Where `lang` SHOULD be set

`internal/ingest/engine.go:1421-1438`:

    if _, ok := walker.(*SitterWalker); ok {
        if ctxAny := match.Context(); ctxAny != nil {
            if root, ok := ctxAny.(SitterRoot); ok && root.LangName != "" {
                node.Properties["lang"] = []byte(root.LangName)
                ...
            }
        }
    }

The same code block sets `location` on the next branch (line 1582). `location` is consistently set on every construct node; `lang` is not. Either the type assertion fails (walker isn't *SitterWalker in the affected path) or root.LangName is "" somehow. Needs investigation.

## Why this isn't bug 3 (mache-9ca6af, the suffix-match fix)

That bead was about resolver-side disambiguation for receiver-method calls. This bead is ingestion-side: the live `GetCallees` path can't even reach the extractor because langName is empty. Different layer, different fix.

## Why the virtual dir works despite this

Virtual `callees/` directories are populated by `materializeVirtuals` (run during mache serve startup) which uses a SEPARATE SQL-based extraction path. That path doesn't depend on the construct's `lang` property — it joins node_refs against node_defs directly. So agents using `list_directory <construct>/callees` get correct results; agents using the `find_callees` MCP tool get [].

## Verification path

1. Add a regression test that ingests a small Go file via `mache build --backend tree-sitter` and asserts every construct node has a `lang` property set
2. Find where SitterWalker path drops the lang property
3. Fix; verify against the same .db that the MCP find_callees now returns the same callees the virtual dir does

## Scope

Pre-existing bug, NOT introduced by PR #373. Affects every `mache build --backend tree-sitter` output. The PR #373 post-fix audit caught it because it was the first measurement with real MCP-tool exercise on a freshly built .db. Should land as its own PR after PR #373 merges.

title: Heterogeneous-code test harness for find_smells qualifier-aware metrics
description:
Cross-language acceptance harness for the structural metrics that consume LLO `BindingRecord.qualifier` (T8.7). Surfaced post-mache-6c0d07 (PR #358).

## Why

Existing test coverage is layered as:

| Layer | Coverage | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| L1: synthetic SQL fixtures | Plumbing works | Doesn't prove metric matches real code shapes |
| L2: real-LLO integration on mache itself | Single-language (Go) end-to-end | Can't catch cross-language qualifier-extraction shape mismatches |

When LLO T8.9 lands and people start running mache on heterogeneous codebases (Go + Rust + Python + TypeScript), qualifier-extraction subtleties surface as user pain rather than caught regressions. Examples we'd hit blind:

- Rust `&self.method()` vs `obj.method()` — does qualifier resolve to `self` or the type name?
- TypeScript `this.foo()` — is qualifier `this`, or empty (since `this` is implicit), or the class name?
- Python `cls.method()` vs `self.method()` — same question
- Chained selectors `a.b.c.d()` — qualifier is `c` (immediate predecessor) per current LLO logic; needs cross-language confirmation
- Macro-expanded code (Rust `info!()`, C/C++ preprocessor) — qualifier extraction sees the post-expansion form; consumer behavior?

Without an L2-style hetero harness, the qualifier metric is structurally-correct-by-design but empirically untested across the language matrix LLO actually produces.

## Concrete deliverable (L2 scope)

`testdata/hetero/` corpus with paired files per language:

```
testdata/hetero/
  go/
    projection.go         # ≥10 method calls on a single receiver `rec`
    orchestrator.go       # ≥10 calls across ≥10 distinct packages
  rust/
    projection.rs         # method-chain on &self
    orchestrator.rs       # crate-spanning calls
  python/
    projection.py         # self.* method calls in a class
    orchestrator.py       # cross-module imports
  typescript/
    projection.ts         # this.* method calls in a class
    orchestrator.ts       # cross-package imports
```

Each language ships TWO functions (or methods) at minimum:
1. **Projection** — N method calls, all sharing one qualifier. Should NOT be flagged by `fan_out_skew`.
2. **Orchestrator** — N calls across N distinct qualifiers. Should be flagged.

## Test

`cmd/find_smells_hetero_test.go` (gated behind `MACHE_HETERO_INTEGRATION=1` + presence of language servers):

```go
func TestFanOutSkew_HeteroFixtures(t *testing.T) {
    if os.Getenv("MACHE_HETERO_INTEGRATION") != "1" { t.Skip(...) }
    
    // Run leyline parse + leyline lsp over testdata/hetero/
    // for each language whose LSP is on PATH.
    // Then run fan_out_skew via mache binary.
    
    findings := runFanOutSkew(t, enrichedDB)
    
    // Acceptance:
    for _, f := range findings {
        require.NotContains(t, f.NodeID, "/projection.",
            "projection function flagged — qualifier metric broken for %s", f.Language)
    }
    expectedOrchestrators := []string{
        "go/orchestrator.go::Orchestrator",
        "rust/orchestrator.rs::orchestrator",
        ...
    }
    for _, o := range expectedOrchestrators {
        require.Contains(t, findingIDs(findings), o,
            "orchestrator NOT flagged — qualifier metric not reaching threshold for %s", o)
    }
}
```

Pass criterion:
1. Every projection function unflagged across all languages
2. Every orchestrator function flagged across all languages
3. Document any wedge cases per language (e.g. "Rust macro-expanded calls fall into qualifier=''; expected slack")

## Acceptance

- L2 harness in `testdata/hetero/` covers Go, Rust, Python, TypeScript at minimum
- Test gated on `MACHE_HETERO_INTEGRATION=1`; skips cleanly when LSPs unavailable
- README in `testdata/hetero/` documents the corpus convention so adding a 5th language is a one-directory add
- Acceptance test passes locally with all 4 LSPs installed (`gopls`, `rust-analyzer`, `pyright-langserver`, `tsserver`)
- CI workflow optional (depends on language-server setup cost vs. value)

## Out of scope (file follow-ups if needed)

- **L3 vendored open-source corpus** (k8s, tokio, pandas pinned at commits). Bigger investment; better caught by user-reported issues.

comments.text:
ADR written: docs/adr/0010-hosted-mache-architecture.md

Covers all five design questions from the brief:
1. Pluggable storage backend (StorageBackend interface, SQLiteWriter as wire format)
2. Debounced persistence with quiet-period + max-delay model, snapshot isolation for concurrent persist+swap
3. Cache invalidation: webhooks primary, TTL polling fallback, engine_version field for schema migration
4. Concurrent sessions share a single GenerationalGraph (epoch-based ref counting, replaces simple HotSwapGraph)
5. Graph state (nodes/refs/defs/file_index in .db) persisted; source data (git clone) ephemeral; embeddings separate

Key architectural decisions:
- SQLite as wire format (not protobuf) because SQLiteGraph reads it natively -- zero deserialization overhead
- GenerationalGraph extends HotSwapGraph with reference counting so retired generations drain safely
- Workspace is the unit of isolation (one per repo+branch), sessions route to workspaces
- 4-phase rollout: ephemeral-only -> R2 persistence -> webhooks -> multi-worker+auth

Also relates to bead mache-ae1149 (ephemeral mode) which maps to Phase 0 of the ADR.

title: Data-source topology schemas cannot be driven by either documented command — build wants a directory, mount rejects the documented arity
description:
Found 2026-07-29 while writing a topology schema for 0day's published artifact. Reproduced against mache's OWN shipped examples, so this is not about my file.

## Neither documented way to drive a data-source schema works

`examples/README.md` says topology schemas "drive `mache mount` / `mache build` / `mache serve`", and gives this worked example:

```
python examples/audit-indexer.py examples/test-audit/
mache mount examples/test-audit/.index.json --schema examples/audit-schema.json /tmp/audit
```

Both verbs refuse it. mache 0.19.0-10-g1c3d812 (commit 1c3d812, built 2026-07-24):

```
$ mache build --schema examples/audit-schema.json examples/test-audit/.index.json /tmp/a.db
auto-leyline: parsing examples/test-audit/.index.json -> /tmp/mache-leyline-*.db
Error: examples/test-audit/.index.json is not a directory
Error: leyline backend: leyline parse: exit status 1

$ mache mount examples/test-audit/.index.json --schema examples/audit-schema.json /tmp/mnt
Error: accepts at most 1 arg(s), received 3
Usage:
  mache [mountpoint] [flags]
```

Two distinct failures:

- **`build`** routes every source through ley-line, which wants a DIRECTORY of source files. A single JSON document cannot go through it at all — the error is a filesystem-type check, not a parse failure.
- **`mount`** does not accept the documented argument shape. Its usage line is `mache [mountpoint] [flags]`; the README's three-argument invocation has no matching signature.

## Scope: 11 of the 18 shipped example schemas

Classified by selector style — a schema whose selectors are JSONPath only is a data-source schema; tree-sitter s-expression selectors mean it projects code and goes through ley-line legitimately.

```
audit  bdr  bdr-hierarchy  kev  llm-conversations
mcp  mcp-registry  notion  notion-repos  nvd  trivy-ghsa
```

Each of those is documented in `examples/README.md` with a described directory layout, and none can currently be driven by the commands that README gives. The tree-sitter seven (go, python, rust, sql, terraform, markdown, cli) are unaffected — they project source directories, which is what ley-line wants.

## Probable cause, stated as a lead rather than a finding

`mache build --backend` is described as a *"Deprecated no-op: ley-line is the sole parser since ADR-0012 step 4."* If consolidating on ley-line removed the JSON/SQLite ingest path, the data-source half of the schema system lost its driver and the examples, the README and the schemas themselves were left in place describing it. That would make this a capability regression rather than a CLI bug, and it would explain both failures at once.

Not verified — I have not read the ingest code. Worth checking before designing a fix, because "restore the JSON path" and "update the docs to match reality" are very different pieces of work and the choice belongs to whoever knows why ADR-0012 went that way.

## Why it is worth a bead rather than a doc tweak

`internal/ingest/` tests reference JSON/SQLite ingestion, and the README frames data sources as a first-class half of the system — the NVD, KEV, Notion, MCP-registry and beads projections are the examples a newcomer is pointed at first ("read a small schema (`kev-schema.json` for JSON data)"). Whatever the resolution, right now the documented on-ramp does not run.

## Related

0day now publishes a generated mache topology schema for its own artifact at `https://xn--w6j.day/schema/v1/mache-topology.json` (JSONPath over `site-map.json`). Its structure is tested against the contract it derives from, but it has never been mounted, for exactly this reason. It is a ready-made external test case once the path works.

comments.text:
INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED 2026-07-29 on main at feecc97 (post-#581, leyline pin v0.13.0), fresh `task build`. Both halves confirmed, plus one detail that makes the mount half worse than "rejects the documented arity".

## Half 1: build — confirmed, fails clean

    $ ./bin/mache build --schema examples/audit-schema.json examples/test-audit/.index.json /tmp/audit-out.db
    auto-leyline: parsing examples/test-audit/.index.json -> /var/.../mache-leyline-181680335.db
    Error: examples/test-audit/.index.json is not a directory
    Error: leyline backend: leyline parse: exit status 1
    REAL_EXIT=1

No partial .db is left behind (verified: output path does not exist afterward), so it fails clean rather than producing a corrupt artifact — worth noting as the one thing that is right here.

Root cause visible in the log: `build` routes through `auto-leyline: parsing <source>` **unconditionally**, before/regardless of `--schema`. `leyline parse` requires a directory. But a JSONPath data-source schema needs no leyline at all — that path is the JSON walker into MemoryStore. So a `--schema` pointing at a single JSON file is unreachable through `build` by construction, not by a validation quirk.

Note the `--backend` flag is now a documented no-op ("Deprecated no-op: ley-line is the sole parser since ADR-0012 step 4... Accepted for backward compatibility and ignored"), so there is no flag left to opt out of the leyline route either.

## Half 2: mount — worse than an arity mismatch. The subcommand does not exist.

The README (examples/README.md:193) documents:

    mache mount examples/test-audit/.index.json --schema examples/audit-schema.json /tmp/audit

Actual:

    Error: accepts at most 1 arg(s), received 3
    Usage:
      mache [mountpoint] [flags]

The 3 args are `mount`, `examples/test-audit/.index.json`, `/tmp/audit` — i.e. `mount` is being parsed as a positional arg to the ROOT command, not as a subcommand. Confirmed against the full command list: build, cache, clean, completion, find-smells, help, init, list, pack, serve, unmount, version. **There is no `mount` subcommand.** (`unmount` exists; `mount` does not — asymmetric, which is probably how the README drifted.)

Mounting is the root command, `mache [mountpoint]`, which takes exactly one positional (the mountpoint) and no positional source slot. So it is not that the documented arity is rejected — there is no arity of `mache mount` that could work, and the root form has nowhere to put the data source positionally.

## Bearing on scope

This is the data-source (JSONPath → MemoryStore) path specifically. The source-code path is fine — it is exercised by `task check`, the smell gate, and the token bench on every run. The data-source path has no equivalent gate, which is why an ADR-0012-era change to how `build` resolves sources could break all 11 JSONPath examples without any test noticing.

Suggest the acceptance criteria's "verified by running one JSONPath-only example ... and reading a projected file out of the result" become a Taskfile target wired into `task check`, not a one-time manual verification — otherwise the next unification pass through `build` reintroduces this. Related: the two-backend asymmetry discussed on mache-abf404 / mache-238673 — MemoryStore's data-source path is the under-gated half of the same split that produced mache-e3d9bb's Children divergence.

comments.text:
Doc half fixed + gated in PR #585 (bead mache-e7c825).

`examples/README.md`'s `mache mount <src> --schema <s> <mnt>` is replaced with the two invocations that actually work — `mache serve --schema examples/audit-schema.json examples/test-audit/.index.json` (verified by running it: MCP initialize returns a live server) and the root mount form `mache --schema … --data examples/test-audit/.index.json /tmp/audit`. New gate `cmd/docs_cli_surface_test.go` resolves every documented `mache …` invocation against the live cobra tree, so this class cannot regress.

**Explicitly NOT closed by that gate: the `build` routing bug (half two of this bead).** `mache build --schema … x.json out.db` is a *well-formed* invocation — `build` declares `ExactArgs(2)` and every flag exists — that then fails at runtime inside `leyline parse` with "is not a directory". The gate proves a documented command PARSES, not that it SUCCEEDS, so it passes this line and will keep passing it. Catching it needs execution, which is out of scope (documented commands variously need a network, an NFS mount, a daemon, or a real source tree). The 11 JSONPath-only schemas and the "restore the JSON path vs update the docs" decision are untouched and still belong to this bead.

Data point for that decision: the JSON data path is NOT gone — `mache serve --schema <s> <file.json>` projects `examples/test-audit/.index.json` correctly today. Only `build` is unconditionally routed through leyline.

title: Smell ratchet launders debt under refactor — baseline keyed on file path, not node content hash
description:
The smell baseline is keyed `(rule_id, source_id)` — rule per file, count only. That predicate is machine-decidable but NOT refactor-invariant, and refactoring is exactly when debt moves.

## Verified in code (2026-07-27)

`cmd/smell_ratchet.go`:
- `computeBaseline` → `counts[[2]string{f.RuleID, f.SourceID}]++` — keyed on rule + file path
- `lookup` → "returns the grandfathered count for (rule, file), **or 0 if absent**"
- `docs/smell-baseline.json` entries are `{rule_id, source_id, count}`

## Two failure directions, both live

**1. False positives block legitimate refactors.** Move a 400-line offender out of `a.go` into `b.go`/`c.go`/`d.go`. The new files have no baseline entry, so `lookup` returns 0, so every relocated finding is NEW debt and the gate fails. The debt didn't grow — it moved. Renames are the same.

**2. Stale budget launders debt.** The vacated `a.go` entry persists at count N forever; nothing reclaims it. You can now add N fresh findings back into `a.go` and the ratchet passes. This is the laundering — debt is not detected as new because a file is still spending an allowance it no longer needs.

The existing doc comment shows how close this already is: "Count-based rather than line-based so it's stable across incidental line shifts (adding a line above a finding must not 'move' it into new-debt)." Line-shift invariance was solved deliberately. File-move invariance stops one level short.

## The substrate for the fix already exists

`cmd/smell_incremental.go` (mache-238673 phase-1) already memoizes rule metrics keyed by **merkle node_hash**: "Each distinct function subtree's metric ONCE, keyed by its merkle node_hash" — and each finding already carries `hashHex`. Keying the baseline on the node's content hash instead of its path makes it survive moves and renames by construction: same node, same hash, same grandfathered entry, wherever the file lives.

⚠️ Constraint to design around: `smell_incremental.go:69` — `hashHex string // "" when the producer wrote no node_hash (standalone db)`. Hash-keyed baselines only work on an LLO-backed `.db`. Standalone backends need a documented fallback (probably path-keyed, explicitly degraded) — which interacts directly with the sibling bead on silent rule-skipping: on a weak backend you would get no hash AND invisible skips at once.

## Same defect class as mache-e256f5

mache-e256f5 is the coverage-gate scoring pure moves as 100% new code. Identical blind spot in a second, independently-written gate: neither reads structure, both key on path. Worth fixing as one idea applied twice rather than two coincidences — whatever move-detection story lands here should inform that one.

Verification: `task check` green, and a fixture that relocates a known offender between files produces ZERO new debt while genuinely-new findings in the same commit still fail.
acceptance_criteria: A test moves a file containing N known findings to a new path with content unchanged and asserts `newDebt` returns empty; a second test adds a genuinely new finding in the same moved file and asserts it IS reported; a third asserts a vacated baseline entry cannot grandfather fresh findings re-added to the old path. Baseline schema version bumped with a documented migration from v1 path-keyed entries, and the standalone-backend (empty node_hash) fallback path is explicitly tested and documented. `task check` green.

title: Silent rule-skipping is a coverage lie — skipped-rule count must reach the ratchet and SARIF
description:
"A rule that needs tables your backend doesn't have skips itself instead of lying" is the right instinct, but a rule that no-ops and reports nothing is **indistinguishable from a rule that ran clean**. That is the same failure mode as a disabled linter, arrived at politely.

## Verified in code (2026-07-27)

- `cmd/find_smells_cli.go:227` warns to stderr: `find-smells: skipping rule %q — requires absent tables [%s]` — transient, not a structured signal.
- `cmd/smell_digest.go:38` DOES carry it: `Skipped []string \`json:"rules_skipped,omitempty"\`` — but that's the digest format only.
- `cmd/smell_ratchet.go` has **no notion of skipped rules**. `newDebt` diffs findings against baseline counts; a skipped rule contributes zero findings, which is byte-identical to a rule that ran and found nothing.
- `cmd/smell_sarif.go` — grep for `skipped` / `invocation` / `toolExecutionNotification` returns **nothing**. SARIF carries no skip signal at all.

Net effect: on a backend missing `_ast`, the `_ast`-dependent rules vanish and the gate reports green. The ratchet quietly ratchets nothing.

## Why this is live, not theoretical

`.github/workflows/find-smells.yml:10-11` states the design outright: "The `_ast`-dependent rules skip automatically on the standalone (no-LLO) .db via `--rule '*'`; the cross-ref rules enforce." So there is a documented, intended configuration in which a subset of rules silently produce no output — and nothing downstream records that it happened.

Concretely: `duplicate_code` and `long_function` are both `_ast`-dependent. Both fired on PR #567 and blocked a merge until real defects were fixed. On a standalone `.db` the same commit would have passed clean with no indication those two rules never ran.

## Fix shape

1. Thread `rules_skipped` from the digest through `smell_ratchet.go` so the gate knows its own coverage.
2. Print skipped-rule count in the gate's stdout summary alongside the new-finding count — `smell ratchet: 0 NEW finding(s) above baseline (3 rules SKIPPED: …)` reads very differently from `0 NEW`.
3. Emit skips in SARIF. SARIF 2.1.0 has the slot: `runs[].invocations[].toolExecutionNotifications` (or per-rule via `runs[].tool.driver.rules` + a notification descriptor), so this is expressible without leaving the spec.
4. Decide policy: should a skipped *gate*-tagged rule be a hard failure in CI where the backend is supposed to be LLO-backed? A skip there means the gate is misconfigured, not that the code is clean.

## Interaction with mache-dd45a3

The sibling ratchet bead needs `node_hash` for a refactor-invariant baseline, and `node_hash` is empty on standalone backends. So a weak backend loses hash-keyed baselines AND silently drops rules simultaneously — the two degradations compound and neither is currently visible. Whatever surfaces skipped rules should surface degraded-baseline mode on the same line.
acceptance_criteria: `find-smells` gate output reports the skipped-rule count and IDs alongside the new-finding count; a test runs the gate against a standalone (no-`_ast`) fixture db and asserts the output names every skipped rule rather than reporting a bare clean result; SARIF output carries skips via `invocations[].toolExecutionNotifications` and a test validates the emitted SARIF against the 2.1.0 schema; a documented policy decides whether a skipped `gate`-tagged rule fails CI. `task check` green.

title: [composite.go] ListChildren at root returns non-deterministic mount order
description: Line 110-114: ListChildren("") iterates `c.mounts` (a map) and appends prefix names. title: SmellRule as a validated contract: capnp shape (schema-bridge) + SQL-safety via SQLite's own authorizer/read-only (no new deps, no ORM)
description:
Formalize the SmellRule contract now that rules are data (mache-b0b979). TWO validation layers, deliberately kept dep-light:

## Shape — capnp IDL via cloister schema-bridge
Author `SmellRule.capnp`; run cloister's `tools/schema-bridge` (capnp → IR → Go + zod + JSON Schema; see cloister-7536e7 epic + A-E, and the design bead cloister-ffab6a "capnp-schema-driven config/smell-rules"). Outputs: mache's hand-written `SmellRule` struct becomes GENERATED (reduces code), `cmd/rules/*.json` validate against the generated JSON Schema, TS/cloister consumers get zod. Consume schema-bridge via the SAME pattern mache already uses for leyline (published binary + regen-verify gate) OR vendor the generated output — monorepo-vs-publish is undecided (operator's call); it changes only the fetch URI, not the design (monorepo/polyrepo isomorphism). NET DEP IMPACT: neutral-to-reducing — capnp is already in mache (leyline-schema); schema-bridge is a TOOL, not a go.mod dep; generated code replaces hand-written.

## Safety — SQL is executed, so validate it IS a solved problem, using SQLite's OWN machinery (ZERO new deps, NO ORM, NO external SQL parser)
A `SmellRule.Query` is arbitrary SQL mache runs against the .db. Today `validateSmellRule` only checks non-empty + one `%s`. For shared/external/agent-authored rules that's insufficient (a Query could ATTACH/DROP/stack statements/read outside Requires). DO NOT add a SQL-parser dependency and DO NOT introduce an ORM. Use SQLite itself (already present via modernc.org/sqlite):
- RUNTIME: execute rules on a connection opened read-only (`?mode=ro`) and/or `PRAGMA query_only=ON` — SQLite refuses writes/DDL. Gold standard: a SQLite AUTHORIZER callback (sqlite3_set_authorizer) that denies everything but SQLITE_READ/SQLITE_SELECT on the Requires-declared tables (verify modernc.org/sqlite exposes the authorizer; if not, read-only mode + query_only covers the write/DDL class).
- LOAD-TIME: `PREPARE` the Query (SQLite's own parser) to catch syntax + unknown-table errors before dispatch; with the authorizer active, prepare fails on disallowed ops.
This turns "ensure safe SQL" into "let the database enforce it" — solved-problem, dep-free, anti-ORM.

Links: cloister-ffab6a (design), cloister-7536e7 (schema-bridge), mache-b0b979 (externalization), mache-a533a9 (single-contract codegen). A security-lens (authorizer coverage, table-scoping) review is warranted.
acceptance_criteria: SmellRule.capnp exists + schema-bridge generates the Go struct + JSON Schema (regen-verify gate green); cmd/rules/*.json validate against the JSON Schema; rule Queries execute on a read-only/query_only connection (writes/DDL/ATTACH denied — proven by a test that a malicious Query fails safely) with an authorizer scoping to Requires tables where modernc exposes it; NO new SQL-parser dep and NO ORM added to go.mod; existing find-smells behavior unchanged (task smells baseline byte-identical).

title: Comments as a reconstructable occurrence overlay (producer emits comment occurrences; render re-interleaves)
description:
Today comments are second-class: only the contiguous doc-comment block preceding a matched construct is captured (extractDocComments, sitter_walker.go:275) as a construct attribute; free-floating/inline/trailing comments are dropped; and the merkle `node_hash` deliberately EXCLUDES comments from the content fold.

Design insight (from a 2026-07-08 conversation): because code content is already comment-free and content-addressed, comments should live as an OCCURRENCE-LAYER OVERLAY (byte-range + text + attached-construct link), NOT interleaved into the content-addressed node_content. This is the SAME content/occurrence split the merkle work shipped:
- code = content (deduped, comment-free node_content) ; comments = occurrence overlay (position-bound, like _ast/node_defs).
- Reconstruction = re-interleave comments by position → the exact commented source rebuilds, so you get dedup + separability WITHOUT losing the original.
- Interleaving comments into content would be WORSE: a comment edit changes node_hash, dedup misses, intent welds to structure.

Payoff: comments become queryable → directly powers the `drift_doc_*` smell rules (now JSON, mache-b0b979) and the assay doc-coverage direction. Producer-side (leyline walker) emits comment occurrences as first-class _ast/occurrence rows; mache reads them additively (same additive pattern as the node_hash column — B4/B6). Cross-repo: needs a leyline producer change; mache side is a reader + a comments lens (virtual dir, like context/callers).
acceptance_criteria: A design note (or ADR) that decides comments-as-overlay vs interleaved, specifies the leyline producer emission (comment occurrence rows: byte-range, text, attached-construct link) and the mache reader + reconstruction (re-interleave by position round-trips the original source), and connects it to drift_doc_* rules + assay. Prototype: a mache read path that surfaces comment occurrences for a file and reconstructs the commented source byte-identically.

title: Guarantee internally-connected communities: connected-components post-split + O(E) modularity
description:
DetectCommunities (internal/graph/community.go) is Phase-1-only local-moving Louvain and can, in principle, emit internally-disconnected communities (Traag et al. 2019 "From Louvain to Leiden"). The community is the sheaf cache-invalidation region (sheaf_invalidate.go, internal/leyline/sheaf.go), where a disconnected region causes over-invalidation and, via a misfiled bridge node, delta-0-prunable UNDER-invalidation (stale cache reads) — the only correctness-breaking vector.

EMPIRICAL STATUS (verified): an env-gated experiment on mache's self-graph found 0/2064 disconnected communities at every density regime (oracle validated against a planted split). The shared-token projection is a clique-union (no articulation points) with NO Phase-2 aggregation to freeze splits, so the pathology structurally cannot fire TODAY. This is therefore a DEFENSIVE fix + regression gate, NOT a live bug.

WHY IT WILL MATTER: the flaw goes live when community detection runs over ADR-0023's typed fact_edges IR (calls/contains/references), which HAS real bridge edges + articulation points. The dense token projection is masking the pathology; sparsifying the input flips it latent->live.

FIX (do NOT adopt full Louvain Phase-2 or Leiden — both coarsen; Leiden's randomization thrashes the deterministic sheaf cache key):
1. Member-gated connected-components BFS post-split: relabel any internally-disconnected community into its connected pieces before result collection (reuse ConnectedComponents, restricted to one community's member set; ~40 LOC). RECOMPUTE modularity AFTER the split (current community.go:147 value describes the pre-split partition).
2. Replace O(N^2) computeModularity double loop with O(E) internal-weight sweep: Sum_c[inW_c/m2 - (commDegree_c/m2)^2] (commDegree already maintained incrementally); parity test vs old impl on small graphs; then drop the 5000-ref guardrail in cmd/pack.go.
3. Land the existing experiment (preserved: scratchpad/community-experiment/community_disconnected_experiment_test.go) as a skipped-by-default test, then flip it to a CI gate.

Split-only stays monotonically finer (safe for pack granularity) and deterministic (safe for the sheaf cache key). Residual "badly-connected single-bridge" communities are NOT fixed by split-only — low severity now; a CPM/RB gamma resolution knob (~20 LOC, deterministic) is the future dial, not Leiden. Orthogonal to the IR producer/reader PRs; does not block them.

Effort ~1 day.
acceptance_criteria: go test ./internal/graph/ -run 'TestCommunit|TestDisconnected|TestModularity' passes, INCLUDING: (a) a CI-gated invariant asserting 0 returned communities span >1 connected component on mache's self-graph; (b) a parity test asserting the O(E) modularity equals the old O(N^2) impl on small graphs. cmd/pack.go 5000-ref guardrail removed.

title: coverage-gate: add rename/similarity detection (treats pure-move refactors as 100% new code)
description:
## Surfaced by

The `feat/evolve-coverage-trunk` campaign's wave-6b god-file split attempt (2026-05-18). Mechanical decomposition of `cmd/serve_handlers.go` (1374 → 182 LOC, 10 new per-tool files) — build/vet/lint/test all green, no behavior change. **Coverage-gate flagged 185 prod lines as "new and uncovered."**

Verification: the same lines, in their original file location, were ALREADY uncovered on trunk pre-refactor (same `go test -coverprofile` output with the WIP stashed = identical zero-hit ranges). The gate didn't detect that the lines moved; it treated every new file's contents as net-new code.

The WIP lives on `evolve/godfile-serve-handlers` as the canonical reproducer.

## What the gate is missing

Git's diff format supports rename detection (`git diff -B<n>% -M<n>% -C<n>%`) — these flags use similarity heuristics to recognize that a file's contents moved between locations. When applied, the 185-line false-positive set drops to 64 (still nonzero, because some lines were lightly edited during the move — imports trimmed, comments adjusted — but a tractable number).

The gate currently parses a plain unified diff and treats every `+` line as new. It has no awareness of:

1. **Rename hunks** — `git diff` emits `--- a/oldpath\n+++ b/newpath` with `similarity index 95%` for renames. The gate skips this metadata.
2. **Copy hunks** — same shape, `similarity index 60%` for copies.
3. **Move-aware diffs** — `git diff -B5% -M5% -C5%` collapses pure moves into rename hunks instead of delete+add pairs.

## Fix shape

Option A — **diff-format flag**:
- Add a flag `-rename-aware` or auto-detect that the input diff includes `similarity index` metadata.
- When a hunk is a rename with similarity ≥ threshold (say 50%), exclude its lines from the uncovered set ENTIRELY — they're moves, not new code.
- Lines that ARE genuinely new in a rename hunk (the post-similarity delta) still count.

Option B — **two-input mode**:
- Accept both old-coverage + new-coverage profiles, plus the diff. If a "new" line was covered at the same content in the old profile (via fuzzy match against old-file path), treat as still covered.

Option A is simpler — defers detection to git, the gate just respects the metadata.

## Implementation sketch (Option A)

In `tools/coverage-gate/main.go::parseDiff`:

1. When parsing a `diff --git` block, look for `similarity index <N>%` line BEFORE the `---`/`+++` lines.
2. If `N >= renameThreshold` (default 50%):
   - Record the rename as `(oldPath, newPath, N)`.
   - Skip the hunk's `+` lines from the new-lines set.
3. Otherwise treat normally.

CLI flag: `-rename-threshold N` (default 50, 0 disables, 100 requires exact-match).

## Test plan

Add to `tools/coverage-gate/main_test.go`:

1. `TestParseDiff_RenameHunkExcludesAllLines` — feed a diff with `similarity index 100%` and an uncovered profile range covering the renamed file; assert no flagged lines.
2. `TestParseDiff_RenameHunkBelowThresholdCountsAsNew` — `similarity index 30%` with default threshold 50%; assert lines counted as new.
3. `TestParseDiff_RenameHunkWithEditsCountsEdits` — `similarity index 80%` where 1 line was edited; assert ONLY the edited line is flagged if uncovered.
4. Integration: take the WIP godfile-serve-handlers diff, run the gate with `-rename-threshold 50`, assert exit 0 (185 false positives gone).

## Acceptance

- Gate exit 0 on `evolve/godfile-serve-handlers` (the WIP) with `-rename-aware`.
- Pure-move refactors no longer require coverage:ignore annotations.
- Lines that ARE genuinely new in a renamed file (e.g., an import added during the move) still get flagged.

## Why this matters now

The god-file decomposition campaign (`mache-godfile-decomposition`, sibling) blocks on this OR on policy:
- Without it: every god-file split needs to either annotate hundreds of lines or backfill hundreds of tests
- With it: clean mechanical refactors merge clean; only TRUE new code gates

## Files in scope

- `tools/coverage-gate/main.go` (parseDiff + intersect logic)
- `tools/coverage-gate/main_test.go` (4 new tests)

## Related

- The `mache-godfile-decomposition` campaign — this bead unblocks it
- `mache-66d8df` — original coverage-gate bead; this extends it
- Branch `evolve/godfile-serve-handlers` — preserved WIP as the canonical reproducer
- The wave-6b god-file agent's report (2026-05-18) — the trigger that surfaced the gap

comments.text:
Shipped in PR https://github.com/agentic-research/mache/pull/391 (base: feat/godfile-decomposition).

Implementation:
- Added `-rename-threshold N` (default 50, range 0..100) flag via stdlib `flag` package.
- Added `parseDiffWithRenames(r, threshold)`; kept `parseDiff(r)` as a thin wrapper at the default — zero changes to existing 34 tests.
- Per-block state machine: when a `diff --git` block carries `similarity index N%` AND N >= threshold, the block's `+` lines are excluded from the new-lines set entirely (still advances `newLine` so subsequent context counting is correct).
- Added `parseSimilarityPercent` helper.
- `dissimilarity index` header is recognized but does NOT trigger exclusion (conservative).

Demo against /private/tmp/mache-worktrees/godfile-serve-handlers `git diff -B5% -M5% -C5% origin/main..HEAD`:
- `-rename-threshold 50` → 76 lines uncovered
- `-rename-threshold 100` → 76 lines uncovered (same — the godfile diff's similarities are 5-16%, so threshold doesn't change which `+` lines are flagged; `git -C5%` already preprocessed the copy blocks to contain only `-` deletions, leaving the residual `+` lines from genuinely-new files [`find_callers`, `get_sheaf_status`, `semantic_search`] plus `serve_handlers.go` edits and the coverage-gate tool itself).

The original "185 → ~0" estimate in the bead was based on plain `git diff` baseline (216 lines, actually) — documented in `TestRenameDetection_GodfileServeHandlersWIP` for posterity. End-to-end firing is proven by synthesizing a 95% rename hunk and showing the threshold gates inclusion/exclusion correctly.

7 new tests added (4 from bead spec + 3 boundary cases). 0 modified. Total 34 → 41 tests, passes under `go test -race -count=10`, `task check` clean.

comments.text:
**Absorbed mache-301daf** (closed as duplicate) — the in-place-rewrite case of this same parser gap. Recording it here so the second case can't be lost when this is implemented, since the title only names the move case.

## The two diff-header forms tools/coverage-gate must handle

| Case | git emits | Current behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| File **moved** (this bead) | `similarity index N%` + `rename from/to` | every line in the new path scored as net-new |
| File **rewritten in place** (301daf) | `dissimilarity index N%`, **no** rename metadata | whole file scored as brand-new |

Same root cause — the parser reads a plain unified diff and treats every `+` as new, ignoring git's similarity metadata entirely. Both land in the same place: the diff parser in `tools/coverage-gate/main.go`.

## 301daf's reproducer (distinct from this bead's)

Branch `evolve/simplify-sqlite-graph`, `/evolve --simplify` on sqlite_graph.go decomposition. Gate flagged 110 uncovered lines; spot-checks of 3 line ranges confirmed all were uncovered on the base branch too — pre-existing error paths that only moved.

This bead's own reproducer stays `evolve/godfile-serve-handlers` (cmd/serve_handlers.go, 1374 → 182 LOC, 185 false positives, dropping to 64 under `-B5% -M5% -C5%`).

## 301daf's fix shape, folded in

3. When `dissimilarity index N%` is present, mark the file as an in-place rewrite of itself and apply the **same base-coverage fallback** used for renames — don't report a line as new debt if it was uncovered on the base too.

That fallback is shared with Option A here, which is why these are one fix and not two.

## Proposed acceptance criteria

title: server.json should declare mache's session requirement so consumers derive it
description:
mache's MCP HTTP transport is session-stateful — CLAUDE.md says so ("HTTP mode uses stateful sessions — each client gets its own session ID mapped to the projected graph") and the code backs it (cmd/serve_repo.go sanitizeSessionID maps a session ID to a per-session filesystem path). But server.json says nothing about it, so every consumer has to know independently and declare it by hand.

Cloister does exactly that, and got it wrong. Verified 2026-07-27 in ~/remotes/art/cloister:

    cluster.toml
      [inputs.rosary]  requiresSession = true
      [inputs.mache]   (absent -> defaults false)

    src/generated/cluster.ts  (the emitted artifact that actually runs)
      { "name": "mache",  ..., "requiresSession": false }   <-- wrong
      { "name": "rosary", ..., "requiresSession": true  }

So the cluster runs mache as sessionless while mache's own transport is
session-stateful. Nobody wrote a bug; the information simply is not published
where the consumer reads it, and the default is the wrong answer.

WHY FIXING IT IN CLOISTER ALONE IS INSUFFICIENT
Adding `requiresSession = true` to [inputs.mache] is correct but is a second,
hand-maintained copy of a fact mache owns. The next consumer repeats the guess,
and the failure mode is silent (a false default, not an error). It also does not
take effect on its own — the emitter reads the lockfile's generated_backends, not
[inputs.*], so the declaration is inert until cluster.lock.toml is regenerated
(diagnosed on cloister-af794d, where the change was correctly reverted rather
than shipped as a no-op).

PROPOSAL
Publish the session requirement in server.json, where consumers already look for
transport facts. There is no standard field for this in the 2025-12-11 server
schema, but mache already carries a vendor-namespaced block —
`_meta["io.github.agentic-research.mache/transports"]` — that describes stdio and
http transports. Session semantics belong next to the transport that has them.

Sketch (exact key shape to be agreed with cloister, since it is the consumer):

    "_meta": {
      "io.github.agentic-research.mache/transports": {
        "http": { ..., "requiresSession": true,
                  "note": "each client gets its own session ID mapped to the
                           projected graph; a sessionless client shares state" },
        "stdio": { ..., "requiresSession": false }
      }
    }

Note the answer differs BY TRANSPORT — stdio is a per-client subprocess and needs
no session, http does. A single repo-level boolean (which is what cloister models
today) cannot express that, so the schema question is worth settling before the
value is copied further.

ALSO FOUND, worth relaying to whoever owns the cluster config: cloister pins
mache at `server.json@a585418...` reporting version 0.17.0, while mache is on
0.19.0. Two minor versions stale. That is precisely the unrelated-pin churn a
lockfile regeneration would surface — an argument for doing the regen
deliberately and soon rather than continuing to avoid it.

Out of scope here: the cloister-side fix and the lockfile regen. This bead is
only mache publishing the fact.

comments.text:
SCOPE CHANGE — do not hand-edit server.json. LLO is adding schema generation for server.json, because cloister and notme both consume it (jamestexas, 2026-07-27).

This bead proposed mache publish its session requirement in server.json's vendor `_meta` block, with the key shape "agreed with cloister since they are the consumer". That reasoning was right about WHERE the fact belongs and wrong about HOW it gets there: with generation upstream, a hand-authored `_meta` key becomes a second, ungenerated statement of the same fact — the exact duplication this bead was filed to remove one instance of.

REVISED SHAPE
  1. The field belongs in LLO's server.json schema, not in mache's file. mache's job is
     to POPULATE the generated field, not invent a key.
  2. The per-transport requirement stands and is the substantive input mache owes the
     schema: the answer differs by transport. stdio is a per-client subprocess and needs
     no session; http is session-stateful (cmd/serve_repo.go sanitizeSessionID maps a
     session ID to a per-session graph path). A single repo-level boolean — which is what
     cloister's cluster.toml models today — cannot express that. If the generated schema
     lands as a repo-level boolean, the bug is re-encoded upstream where it is harder to
     fix.
  3. mache should also gain a check that the generated file matches what mache actually
     does, rather than trusting the declaration. `task server-json` / the
     server-json-drift gate already exists; the session field should be inside its
     coverage.

BLOCKED until the LLO schema-gen bead exists and states the field. Ask before it lands:
does the schema model session semantics per-transport or per-server? That is the one
decision mache has evidence for and should supply.

The underlying defect is unchanged and still real, verified 2026-07-27: cloister's
generated cluster.ts runs mache with `"requiresSession": false` while mache's http
transport is session-stateful; rosary declares true and mache declares nothing, so the
false default wins silently.

Also still worth relaying: cloister pins mache at server.json@a585418 reporting version
0.17.0, two minor versions behind 0.19.0. Whoever regenerates picks that up.

comments.text:
RESCOPE, not close: the original ask ("put session-ness in the shared descriptor") was the wrong shape and won't be built by LLO. Investigated via a background agent (2026-07-29) reading ley-line-open's actual source:

- `TransportMeta` in `leyline-mcp-descriptor` still only has `typ`/`url` — no session field, and per the resolving discussion on `ley-line-open-4ec276` (still open) it never will: "The registry schema has no session field because session semantics do not belong to the producer." Cloister's actual mechanism is operator-declared, consumer-side: `[inputs.mache] requiresSession = true` in cloister's own `cluster.toml` (`manifest/cluster.capnp:483`).
- Bigger wrinkle found independently while investigating: MCP protocol revision 2026-07-28 (SEP-2567/SEP-2575) removed protocol-level sessions (`Mcp-Session-Id`) from the spec entirely. So the field mache originally asked for models a deleted concept, not just a wrong-repo concept.

Separately verified this is NOT a live break: mache pins `github.com/mark3labs/mcp-go v0.57.0` (latest published), whose `LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION = "2025-11-25"` — it hasn't adopted 2026-07-28 yet, and its Streamable HTTP transport (`server/streamable_http.go`) still reads `Mcp-Session-Id` directly off the wire. mache's own dedup mechanism (`cmd/serve_registry.go`: `graphs sync.Map // rootPath -> *lazyGraph`, session ID used only to discover which root path a connection belongs to via ListRoots, so N sessions on one repo share one graph) currently depends on that header continuing to exist.

Action: close this as "resolved by relocation, not implementation" once cloister's requiresSession approach is confirmed sufficient on their side. Separately, before ever bumping mcp-go past whatever version adopts protocol 2026-07-28, mache needs a plan for how graphForSession's root-path correlation keeps working without Mcp-Session-Id — filed as a new bead for that specifically, since it's a distinct concern from this one.
