title: "every MCP tool" harness has never called get_sheaf_status — completeness is a comment, and it is already false
description:
TestE2E_AllMCPTools claims to prove every registered MCP tool can be invoked without a transport-level failure. It does not. One registered tool has never been called by it.

## Measurement (verified)

`internal/mcpregistry.ToolRegistry()` (registry.go:91-111) returns **18** tools:
list_directory, read_file, find_callers, find_callees, search, semantic_search, get_communities, find_definition, get_type_info, get_diagnostics, get_overview, **get_sheaf_status**, get_impact, get_architecture, get_diagram, write_file, resolve_ref, find_smells.

The `invocations` table in `runToolMatrix` (cmd/all_tools_e2e_test.go:264-289) has **16** entries. The delta:

- `write_file` — absent WITH a written reason (lines 285-288: happy path mutates the fixture and would invalidate downstream results in a single-pass harness; deferred to SB-16). This is a legitimate, reviewable skip.
- `get_sheaf_status` — absent with NO reason. It is registered at cmd/serve_handlers.go:173, deliberately outside the graph-registry wrapping (it talks to the ley-line daemon over UDS rather than depending on session state), and that difference is exactly why it is the tool most likely to fail in a way the harness was built to catch — yet the harness has never invoked it.

## Why it drifted

The completeness invariant is a COMMENT, not an assertion. cmd/all_tools_e2e_test.go:259-261:

    // Each entry: tool name, handler factory, args. Order matches
    // registerMCPTools (cmd/serve_handlers.go) so a missing tool
    // here is visually obvious.

"Visually obvious" is the whole enforcement mechanism, and it has already failed once. Note that get_sheaf_status sits in the middle of the registry order (position 12 of 18), so even the ordering convention the comment relies on did not make its absence obvious.

The blast radius is larger than one test: `runToolMatrix` was extracted (per its own doc comment) so SB-02 (WritableGraph, CompositeGraph) and SB-04/05/06 (alt fixtures) share the inventory. Every harness built on it inherits the same hole.

## The fix pattern already exists in this repo

cmd/readme_tool_matrix_test.go derives its ground truth from the live registry via `inspectRegisteredToolsForInvariants(t).Result.Tools` rather than a hand-maintained list, precisely because a hand-copied count had drifted before ("Eighteen MCP tools" in prose vs "17 tools" in the Status table). Same shape applies here: the harness should iterate the registry and look up a handler+args per tool, so an unregistered-in-the-table tool is a compile/runtime failure rather than an absence.

Deliberate skips (write_file) stay — but as an explicit, reasoned entry in a skip map, not as an absence.

Filed from a type-driven-correctness audit; all counts and line numbers re-verified against the working tree at 6a37bb9.
acceptance_criteria: `go test ./cmd/ -run TestE2E_AllMCPTools` passes with runToolMatrix deriving its tool inventory from mcpregistry.ToolRegistry() rather than a hand-written literal, such that (a) get_sheaf_status is actually invoked and profiled, and (b) adding a tool to ToolRegistry() without adding args/handler to the harness FAILS the test rather than silently reducing coverage. Deliberate skips (write_file) are expressed as an explicit skip map entry carrying its reason, and the test asserts skips ∪ invoked == registry. Verify the gate trips by temporarily adding a dummy tool to ToolRegistry().

title: IngestionTarget implementations disagree on Children — a latent trap, guarded not fixed
description:
There are three IngestionTarget implementations (engine.go:20) and two of them answer `GetNode().Children` differently. Engine logic that reads Children therefore behaves differently depending on which backend it is writing to, and the SAME source projects to DIFFERENT graphs.

    MemoryStore.GetNode      (internal/graph/memstore.go:187)  -> `return n, nil`
                             returns the LIVE node pointer, Children populated.

    SQLiteWriter.GetNode     (internal/ingest/sqlite_writer.go:582)
                             rebuilds from `SELECT kind, mtime, record, context, props`
                             and never assigns Children. Always nil.
                             Its ListChildren is `return nil, nil // Not used during ingest`.

    bufferingTarget          (internal/ingest/engine_refs.go:33) wraps either.

PROVEN, NOT INFERRED — internal/ingest/store_parity_collision_test.go (passing, added with this bead). Same fixture, same rust-schema.json, same leyline `_ast` db, same ASTWalker, same Engine. The ONLY difference is the IngestionTarget:

    MemoryStore ....... 2 nodes: [functions/new, functions/new.from_lib_rs]
    SQLiteWriter ...... 1 node:  [functions/new]

Input is three `impl {A,B,C} { pub fn new() }` in one file. The correct answer is 3. Memory gets 2, build gets 1, and neither is right.

WHY THIS IS THE ROOT BUG, not a detail of mache-c725e9
mache-c725e9 is the visible symptom (constructs silently lost). This is the mechanism class: the engine treats Children as readable state, one backend provides it and one does not, and nothing detects the disagreement. The dedup guard at engine_walk.go:222 is only the first casualty. The second is engine_walk.go:236-241, whose comment says "preserve existing children when merging multiple files into the same node (e.g. multiple .go files in one package)" — also inert on the SQLite path for the same reason. It survives in practice only because the parent-child wiring at engine_walk.go:326-338 maintains its own IN-MEMORY set (`e.childSeen`) instead of trusting the store.

That last point is the tell: the codebase already worked around this once, locally, without fixing the contract. Any future engine code that reads Children will hit it again.

ARCHITECTURAL STAKE
CLAUDE.md and internal/graph/graph.go present Graph as "backend-agnostic", and the three presentation paths are supposed to be interchangeable views of one projection. They are not: a graph served from a pre-built .db is not the graph served from memory for the same source. That undermines every cross-backend claim, including the parity assertions the test suite makes elsewhere (TestASTQueryParity asserts WALKER parity; nothing asserts TARGET parity).

FIX OPTIONS (decide deliberately — this is an interface-contract decision, not a patch)
  A. Make Children part of the IngestionTarget contract and have SQLiteWriter honour it. Costs a per-node query on the ingest hot path to answer something the engine already knows in memory. Probably wrong.
  B. Remove Children from the readable contract during ingest — make it write-only — and move every read to engine-side in-memory state, following the `e.childSeen` precedent. Then the guard cannot silently depend on backend behaviour.
  C. Split the interface: an ingest-time write target (no Children reads) vs a query-time Graph (Children readable). Makes the distinction unrepresentable rather than merely documented.

B or C. Whichever is chosen, add a shared conformance test run against EVERY IngestionTarget implementation so a future backend cannot quietly answer differently. That test is the durable fix; the collision repair is downstream of it.

RELATED
  mache-c725e9 — the silent construct loss this causes (P0)
  mache-c777ef — the bare-name identity that creates the collisions in the first place
  Note that fixing identity (c777ef) would make THIS bug invisible again without resolving it, since unique names never hit the guard. Fix the contract regardless.

comments.text:
FIX OPTIONS A/B/C ARE FRAMED TOO NARROWLY — see mache-e64f36.

All three options in the description (make SQLiteWriter honour Children / make Children write-only / split the interface) assume mache continues to maintain two hand-rolled IngestionTarget implementations and just needs to police the disagreement between them. That accepts the premise that produced the bug.

Option D, and the one to weigh first: LLO's arena already provides fs, sqlite, and wire presentations of one substrate, with CDC arriving. mache's MemoryStore / SQLiteWriter / SQLiteGraph / GraphFS are a parallel, weaker implementation of that same idea, and this bug lives in the seam between two of them. Delegating presentation to the arena removes the seam rather than adding a conformance test to guard it.

The conformance test in the acceptance criteria is still worth having — it is cheap, it pins the contract today, and it protects whatever transition happens. But it should not be mistaken for the fix.

Directional constraint for whoever picks this up: prefer a fix that moves construct identity toward (semantic path, node_hash) — both sourced from LLO — over one that entrenches mache's rendered-name identity. Measured basis on mache-e64f36: node_hash is durable across insertions that shift node_id, and rendered bare names are what lose 733 Rust constructs (16.9%) and 9 of mache's own cmd/ init() functions.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
AUDITED ACROSS ALL BACKENDS — the divergence is wider than the SQLiteWriter case this bead was filed on, and it splits cleanly along storage lines.

    backend                            GetNode().Children
    MemoryStore                        POPULATED   (returns the live node pointer)
    HotSwapGraph                       POPULATED   (wraps MemoryStore in the fixture)
    SQLiteGraph                        EMPTY       (rebuilds from one row)
    WritableGraph / NodesTableReader   EMPTY       (same)
    SQLiteWriter                       EMPTY       (same; not in the suite at all)

Concretely: ListChildren("pkg") returns 3 children while GetNode("pkg").Children returns 0 on both SQLite-backed readers. EVERY SQLite-backed implementation leaves it empty; only the in-memory one fills it. So the same data is reachable through two accessors that disagree, and which answer a caller gets depends on a backend it usually does not know it has.

The user's framing, which is the right one: the interface is uneven because it hands back a wide `Node` struct and says nothing about which fields are meaningful, so each implementation populates whatever its storage makes cheap. A struct with discretionary fields is not an interface.

WHY THE EXISTING CONFORMANCE SUITE MISSED IT
internal/graph/graph_suite_test.go already has the right machinery — RunGraphSuite, per-backend factories, SuiteOpts for pinning allowed variation. Two gaps:

  1. It never asserted Children. Zero occurrences of `.Children` in the suite before this work.
  2. SQLiteWriter is not in it AND STRUCTURALLY CANNOT BE. The suite lives in package
     internal/graph; SQLiteWriter lives in internal/ingest, which imports internal/graph.
     Import cycle. The backend the build path actually writes through was never
     conformance-testable. That layout guarantees a blind spot for any implementation
     outside package graph.

LANDED (on the mache-c725e9 branch / PR #570)
A GetNodePopulatesChildren flag on SuiteOpts, following the RootEmptyReturnsDir precedent, asserted in BOTH directions — a backend that starts populating fails as loudly as one that stops. Verified by flipping a flag and confirming the failure. This does not bless the divergence; it makes it explicit and drift-proof while the contract is decided. It is also the test that would have caught mache-c725e9.

Also converted the four near-identical suite entry points into a table, because adding the flag made two bodies structurally identical and tripped duplicate_code — the entries had been copy-per-backend all along. Adding a backend is now one row. Baseline untouched (the smell gate correctly caught that I had orphaned RunGraphSuite by converting its last two callers; deleted it rather than baselining it).

STILL OPEN — THE CONTRACT DECISION
  A. Populate Children in every backend. Uniform, but costs an extra child query per
     GetNode on the hottest read path in the system.
  B. Remove Children from the READ contract; ListChildren becomes the sole accessor.
     Cheaper and more honest, but an API change, and MemoryStore returns the live node
     so it cannot comply without a narrower read type — i.e. this collapses into option
     C from the description (split the interface).

B/C is more likely right, and it points where mache-e64f36 points: if the arena becomes the substrate, mache stops maintaining four readers that can disagree at all. Worth settling that before paying for either.

SEPARATE, DO REGARDLESS: extract the conformance suite into an importable package so SQLiteWriter and any future out-of-package backend can be held to it. The current layout makes the blind spot structural rather than accidental.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
Re: "e3d9bb may be moot if e64f36 lands and mache delegates presentation to the arena."

Agreed on the expensive half, not on the cheap half — and the premise needs a caveat from this side.

## Agreed: do not build the parity harness yet

Correct call. A cross-implementation contract harness is exactly the thing not to build for implementations you may delete. Hold it.

## Not moot: the dead guard is wrong under ANY architecture

SQLiteWriter.GetNode never populates Children, so `len(existing.Children) > 0` is STRUCTURALLY unreachable on the build path — it is not racy or order-dependent, the field is simply never filled. That is true whether storage stays in mache or moves to the arena. The fix is small: populate it, or delete the guard and the "preserve existing children when merging" logic at engine_walk.go:236 that depends on the same nil.

Leaving an unreachable guard in place while waiting on an architecture decision means shipping a projection that silently drops constructs in the meantime, and it costs almost nothing to close. I would split the bead: cheap fix now, harness deferred to e64f36.

## The caveat: from LLO's side, that delegation is NOT yet a plan

e64f36 is a proposal. Nothing on the LLO side has committed to being mache's storage and presentation layer, so "may be moot" is currently conditional on a decision NOBODY has made — including us. Concretely, these would all need to land before delegating presentation is safe:

- ley-line-open-4ec276 — schema-bridge is in-tree and wired into ZERO Taskfile targets and ZERO workflows. A generator nobody runs prevents no drift.
- ADR-0034 (construct identity) is Proposed, not Accepted. ADR-0027, which it builds on, is ALSO still Proposed.
- ley-line-open-470290 — merge_symbol's _ast JOIN has no source_id predicate, so in the daemon an LSP symbol can bind to a node in a different FILE. If you consume _lsp from a multi-file projection, those bindings are suspect today.

None of that says no. It says the dependency runs both directions, and a P0 deferred behind it is a longer bet than it looks.

## What DID land on our side today

- ley-line-open-23377a — the address half. node_defs now qualifies by the full enclosing named-scope path, in the language's own separator: alpha::beta::f, Outer1.Builder.build, geo::Shape::area, A.C.walk, deco1.wrapper. Bare aliases preserved throughout, so existing unqualified lookups are unaffected. Go emission byte-identical (it was the only clean language).
- ley-line-open-25811f — bodyless trait signatures now carry canonical_kind='function' instead of NULL. Rust was the outlier: C folds prototype+definition to function, Java's abstract methods to method, TS interface signatures to method.

  NOTE THE SEQUENCING, it matters to you: this REWRITES every trait-signature node_hash, because the preimage hashes canonical_kind(raw).unwrap_or(raw) and the kind moved from the raw "function_signature_item" to "function". This is the generation-lineage event I warned about. It has now LANDED, so the ordering constraint is satisfied — node_hash is safe to pin after this ships, not before.

- ADR-0034 records the whole contract, including that separating declarations from projectable constructs (your ask) is a distinct cross-language request needing a kappa vocabulary addition. Deliberately not folded into 25811f, which would have silently changed four languages' emission under a bug fix.

All on PR #281.
comments.author: rsry-cli

comments.text:
PRIORITY CORRECTION — nothing is broken today. This is a latent trap, not an active defect, and P0 misrepresents it.

I described this as "still P0" without checking whether any current code gets a wrong answer from it. It does not. Verified 2026-07-28 on main:

    gofix/functions   children=3    (all three init() from the mache-c725e9 fix)
    gofix             children=6
    orphaned nodes    0

WHY IT WORKS DESPITE THE DIVERGENCE — the two backends persist the parent/child
relationship differently, and each path uses the one it actually needs:

  SQLite path   children come from the parent_id COLUMN. NodesTableReader.ListChildren
                runs `SELECT id FROM nodes WHERE parent_id = ?`. The Children array is
                never the source of truth there, so GetNode leaving it nil costs nothing.
  MemoryStore   the Children array IS the mechanism.

So the projection is correct on both. The divergence is real and measured (see the
earlier audit comment: MemoryStore and HotSwapGraph populate Children; SQLiteGraph,
NodesTableReader/WritableGraph, and SQLiteWriter do not) but it only produces a wrong
answer for code that treats Children as a SIGNAL rather than as storage.

Exactly one thing did that: the dedup guard asking "does this node already have
children?" to detect a name collision. That got the backend-dependent answer, dropped
540 constructs, and is fixed (mache-c725e9, #570) by tracking claimed IDs in the engine
instead of reading them back from a store.

WHAT ACTUALLY REMAINS: the next person to write `if len(node.Children) > 0` gets a
backend-dependent answer with no warning. The GetNodePopulatesChildren pin (#575) makes
a backend CHANGING its behaviour fail loudly, but nothing stops new code from asking the
question in the first place.

Downgrading P0 -> P2. Under the arena-delegation decision (mache-e64f36) this dissolves
rather than gets fixed — delegation deletes the second store, so there is nothing left to
disagree. Until delegation ships, the honest status is "a trap with a guard rail", not
"a data-loss bug".

Method note, since this is the fifth time in this session I asserted something I had not
measured: "is anything broken" is a question with a cheap empirical answer (build a
projection, count children, check for orphans). Ask it before assigning severity.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
NORMALIZE THE OPERATION INSTEAD OF WAITING FOR DELEGATION (user, 2026-07-28: "shouldn't we normalize ops and use the right pattern here so we don't rewrite the world?"). That reframes this correctly and my previous two comments both got it wrong in the same direction — I treated the options as "police the divergence with a conformance harness" or "wait for the arena to delete one store". Both are large. There is a small one.

THE PATTERN: children have ONE accessor, ListChildren, correct on every backend. GetNode().Children is not read.

Today that does not work, because SQLiteWriter.ListChildren is:

    func (w *SQLiteWriter) ListChildren(id string) ([]string, error) {
        return nil, nil // Not used during ingest
    }

FEASIBILITY PROVEN, and it is the thing that made me think this was hard: that stub
looks like a constraint (you cannot read children mid-write) but it is not one. Rows
INSERTed in an open transaction are readable inside that same transaction — probed
directly with modernc.org/sqlite: 3 rows inserted, 2 children visible via
`SELECT id FROM nodes WHERE parent_id = ?` before commit. SQLiteWriter already holds
w.tx and already writes parent_id on every node. It can answer.

So the normalization is: implement SQLiteWriter.ListChildren as the same parent_id query
NodesTableReader already uses, then move the three ingest-time readers of
GetNode().Children onto it —

    engine_walk.go:317   existingChildren = existing.Children   (the "preserve children
                         when merging files into one node" logic, currently inert on the
                         write path)
    engine_walk.go:409   childSeen seeding
    engine_ingest.go:124 childSeen seeding

— after which no production code reads Children off a GetNode result and the trap has
nowhere to live. The struct field stays for MemoryStore's internal use; it stops being an
accessor.

WHAT MUST BE CHECKED BEFORE DOING IT, because I have been wrong repeatedly this session
by assuming:

  1. bufferingTarget defers FILE nodes to a later ReplaceFileNodes swap, so file children
     may not be in the table at read time while directory children are. The three call
     sites care about different things; confirm which need file children and whether the
     deferral breaks them. This is the real risk, not the transaction visibility.
  2. Deleting the seeding outright is NOT equivalent. e.childSeen is reset per Ingest, and
     on MemoryStore the store read carries children across Ingest calls. Removing it
     changes MemoryStore behaviour on a second Ingest. Normalizing onto ListChildren
     preserves that; deleting does not.
  3. A per-node query on the ingest hot path has a cost. Measure it — the projection is
     250k+ nodes on a mid-size corpus.

WHY THIS IS WORTH DOING AHEAD OF DELEGATION: it is small, it is independent of the arena
decision, and it removes the class rather than guarding it. The GetNodePopulatesChildren
pin (#575) makes a backend CHANGING its answer fail loudly but does nothing about new
code asking the question. This does.

Keeping P2. Not urgent — nothing is broken today (see previous comment: projections are
correct, children come from parent_id on the SQLite path) — but now it is a bounded task
with a known shape rather than "blocked on an architectural decision".
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: A conformance test parameterised over every IngestionTarget implementation (MemoryStore, SQLiteWriter, bufferingTarget wrapping each) asserts identical observable behaviour for the Children contract — whether that is "populated" or "not readable during ingest", one answer for all. Plus internal/ingest/store_parity_collision_test.go's TestStoreParity_AllConstructsRetained is unskipped and passes on BOTH backends with all 3 constructs retained.

title: Fixture documents itself as "Leyline column shape" but diverges from leyline on both node_refs and node_defs
description:
`buildLeylineGoProjectionFixture` (cmd/untested_function_leyline_test.go:32-109) carries a comment at lines 40-42 asserting what it is:

    // Leyline column shape: node_defs carries canonical_kind, node_refs
    // carries container_node_id — the probes in ensureCanonicalViews
    // activate the leyline arms only when these columns exist.

I verified the real shape by running the pinned producer (`leyline 0.13.0 (open)`) over a two-function Go fixture and dumping sqlite_master:

    -- leyline v0.13.0, ACTUAL
    CREATE TABLE node_refs (
        token TEXT NOT NULL, node_id TEXT NOT NULL, source_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        container_node_id TEXT, qualifier TEXT,
        node_hash BLOB REFERENCES node_content(node_hash))
    CREATE TABLE node_defs (
        token TEXT NOT NULL, node_id TEXT NOT NULL, source_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        container_node_id TEXT, canonical_kind TEXT,
        node_hash BLOB REFERENCES node_content(node_hash))

    -- the fixture, lines 50-59
    CREATE TABLE node_defs (token, node_id, source_id, node_hash, canonical_kind,
        PRIMARY KEY (token, node_id)) WITHOUT ROWID;
    CREATE TABLE node_refs (token, node_id, source_id, node_hash, container_node_id,
        PRIMARY KEY (token, node_id)) WITHOUT ROWID;

Three divergences, on BOTH tables (the audit that surfaced this only caught node_refs):

1. **Missing `qualifier` on node_refs.** ensureCanonicalViews probes for it (cmd/smell_refs_views.go:119) and emits a different v_refs body depending on the answer. This fixture therefore exercises the degraded `'' AS qualifier` arm while every real leyline .db exercises the real one. A rule that ever reads qualifier is being tested against a projection production never produces.

2. **Missing `container_node_id` on node_defs.** leyline emits it on defs too; the fixture omits it entirely.

3. **Adds `PRIMARY KEY (token, node_id) WITHOUT ROWID` to both.** leyline has NO primary key and is not WITHOUT ROWID. The PK imposes a dedup production does not perform, and the NOT NULLs leyline does impose are absent.

## Honest scoping of the consequence

The audit claimed "any count/aggregate-over-refs assertion in that file measures a quantity production does not produce." That overstates it for the file as it stands TODAY. The single test in the file (TestFindSmells_UntestedFunctionLeylineProjection, line 118) asserts `resp.Total == 1` over a fixture with exactly two ref rows whose (token, node_id) pairs are already distinct — so the PK currently dedupes nothing and the assertion happens to be correct.

The defect is that nothing holds it correct. The fixture is a self-described model of leyline that is not one, and any future row added to it (a token called twice from the same container, a dual-emit qualifier pair — precisely the shape ley-line-open-4dde42 introduced) would be silently collapsed by a constraint the producer does not have, while the test's comment continues to assert leyline fidelity. Plus the missing `qualifier` column is an ACTIVE divergence today: the SQL under test is structurally different from the SQL production runs.

This is a specific instance of the general problem in [[mache-7555da]]; it is filed separately because it is a concrete, self-contained fix that does not have to wait for the fixture-builder abstraction.

Verified 2026-07-30 against working tree 6a37bb9 with leyline 0.13.0 on PATH.

comments.text:
Fixed in PR #592 (mache-7555da). `buildLeylineGoProjectionFixture` no longer states a schema at all — it is `newSmellFixture(t, fixturedb.Leyline, ...)`, and the DDL comes from `internal/fixturedb/schema_leyline.go`, which is a byte-copy of the PINNED binary's own `sqlite_master` output with a conformance test (`TestLeylineSchema_MatchesPinnedBinary`) that re-derives it and fails on drift.

Every divergence this bead named is gone by construction, and each one was real. Ground truth from `leyline parse` v0.13.0:

| the fixture said | ley-line actually has |
|---|---|
| `node_refs(token, node_id, source_id, node_hash, container_node_id)` — no `qualifier` | `qualifier TEXT` present |
| `node_defs(token, node_id, source_id, node_hash, canonical_kind)` — no `container_node_id` | `container_node_id TEXT` present |
| `PRIMARY KEY (token, node_id) WITHOUT ROWID` on both | **no primary key, not WITHOUT ROWID** |
| nullable columns | `token`/`node_id`/`source_id` are `NOT NULL` |

The missing PK was the sharpest of these and this bead did not name it: ley-line DUAL-EMITS a qualified and a bare row for the same call site (`fmt.Println` with qualifier NULL, and `Println` with qualifier `fmt`, both at the same node_id). A fixture with `PRIMARY KEY (token, node_id)` dedupes rows production keeps, so any COUNT/AVG-over-v_refs rule measures a different quantity in test than in prod — the fan_out_skew class (mache-50e939).

**The acceptance criterion about the qualifier arm is met, but not where this bead expected it.** Rather than a `cmd`-side assertion that the emitted `v_refs` is the full-arm body, the property is pinned at the source: `internal/fixturedb`'s `TestRef_NodeIDMeansDifferentThingsPerProducer` and `TestRef_EmptyQualifierIsNULL` assert that a Leyline fixture carries `qualifier` (NULL for bare calls, which is what ley-line writes and what `COALESCE(qualifier,'')` exists to handle) and `container_node_id`, and `TestLeylineSchema_MatchesPinnedBinary` asserts those columns are what the producer really emits. Given those, `ensureCanonicalViews`'s probes cannot select the degraded arm — and the assertion holds for every fixture, not just this one.

`TestFindSmells_UntestedFunctionLeylineProjection` passes unchanged. **The rule was already correct on the real shape; what was wrong is that the test was not proving it.** No behaviour change, which is itself the finding: the fixture had been claiming coverage of an arm it was not running.

Suggest closing once #592 merges.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: `go test ./cmd/ -run TestFindSmells_UntestedFunctionLeylineProjection` passes against a fixture whose node_refs and node_defs DDL matches `leyline parse` output for the pinned version — qualifier and container_node_id present on the tables leyline puts them on, no PRIMARY KEY, no WITHOUT ROWID, NOT NULL where leyline has it. Preferably the DDL is obtained from the pinned producer (snapshot or attachLeylineAST-style) rather than re-typed; if hand-written, a comment names the leyline version it was snapshotted from. A test asserts ensureCanonicalViews activates the qualifier arm on this fixture (i.e. the emitted v_refs is the full-arm body, not the degraded one).

title: Installing a new mache binary left the supervised daemon serving the old process — every MCP session got pre-release code silently
description:
Found 2026-07-30 immediately after the v0.20.0 release, by checking what an MCP client actually connects to rather than assuming the install took.

## Measured

    installed  ~/.local/bin/mache        0.20.0-5-g9c0e374
    daemon on  localhost:7532           0.19.0-10-g1c3d812   <- 10 commits behind, PRE-v0.20.0

The launchd plist (`com.agentic-research.mache`) already pointed at the correct path — `~/.local/bin/mache`. `task install` had replaced that file. But a running supervisor keeps serving the inode it exec'd; replacing the file on disk does not re-exec it. So the daemon kept serving a build from before v0.20.0, including the P0 construct-loss bug (mache-c725e9) that release exists to fix, and nothing anywhere reported the mismatch.

This is the same shape as mache-0acdf6 (stale leyline shadowing the pin on PATH): the install SUCCEEDS, and the thing actually serving you is older. Both are invisible because the failure is a silent version skew between "what I installed" and "what is running", with no assertion joining the two.

Aggravating factor observed at the same time: 76 `mache serve` processes were alive on the machine — the daemon-pollution pattern previously seen with stale leyline daemons, now on mache itself. Worth a separate look; not fixed here.

## Fixed

`mache daemon restart`, invoked from both install paths — `mache install` (only when the binary actually changed; sameFile and --dry-run must not disturb a running daemon) and the Taskfile `install` target, which copies the binary directly and never routes through the subcommand. Verified end to end: `task install` now prints the restart and daemon/binary report identical versions where they had diverged.

RESTART ONLY, NEVER START — the load-bearing design constraint. `launchctl kickstart -k` and `systemctl --user try-restart` are restart-if-running; `bootstrap` / `enable --now` would conjure a background daemon on a machine whose owner never ran `mache init --global`. Deciding to run a daemon belongs to that command. A not-loaded supervisor stays SILENT rather than erroring or — worse — claiming a restart that did not happen, which would imply the daemon is current when it is not.

Supervisor invocation sits behind a `runSupervisorCmd` seam so tests assert the ARGV shape. That is the only way the guarantee is checkable: restart-form-vs-start-form is not observable from a return code. The first draft of the tests executed the real command and restarted the developer's own daemon as a side effect — recorded because it is an easy mistake to repeat. Falsified by mutating `kickstart -k` to `bootstrap`, which fails the three assertions separating the two.

## Residue worth follow-up (NOT fixed here)

1. **Nothing asserts daemon-version == installed-version.** The fix prevents the skew at install time, but a daemon started by other means, or a binary replaced by something other than these two paths (a `go build -o`, a Homebrew upgrade, a manual cp), reintroduces it undetected. `task install:verify` (mache-19326d) now verifies an INSTALLED binary; the analogous check for the RUNNING daemon does not exist. That would have caught this in CI rather than by hand.
2. **76 stale `mache serve` processes.** Unexplained; may be orphaned per-session servers rather than the supervised one. mache has `mache clean` for mounts and `mache list` for instances — neither was reaping these.
3. `mache init --global` writes the plist AND bootstraps, so a first-time install is fine. The gap was only on RE-install, which is the common case for anyone tracking releases.</description>
acceptance_criteria: After replacing the mache binary via `task install` or `mache install`, a supervised daemon that was already running serves the NEW version — verified by comparing `mache version` against the `serverInfo.version` returned by an MCP `initialize` against localhost:7532, which must be identical. On a machine with no supervised daemon loaded, both install paths succeed silently and start nothing. A test asserts the supervisor argv is a restart-if-running form (kickstart -k / try-restart) and never a start form (bootstrap / enable --now), and fails when mutated to the start form.

title: nono profile translation schema: project nono JSON profiles into AppArmor/K8s/OCI
description:
## Problem

Agent sandboxing needs to work across local (Landlock/Seatbelt), container (K8s securityContext), and MAC (AppArmor/SELinux) enforcement targets. Each has its own config format. No canonical capability format exists that translates between them.

## Insight

nono profiles are structured JSON with a formal JSON Schema (draft 2020-12). mache is a schema-driven projection engine that transforms structured data into different filesystem layouts. nono profiles → mache ingest → translation schema → target enforcement format.

## Design

Create a mache schema that ingests nono profile JSON and projects into:

1. **AppArmor profiles** (~90% fidelity — both path-based, both use composable rule sets)
   - `filesystem.read[*]` → `r` permission rules
   - `filesystem.write[*]` → `w` permission rules  
   - `security.groups[*]` → `#include <abstractions/{group}>`
   - `extends` → child profile inheritance
   - `network.block` → `deny network`

2. **K8s securityContext + seccomp** (~50% fidelity — volume vs path granularity)
   - `filesystem.read[*]` → `volumeMounts.readOnly: true`
   - `capability_elevation: false` → `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`
   - `network.block` → NetworkPolicy deny-all egress
   - `network.allow_domain[*]` → egress rules (lossy: L7→L3/L4)

3. **OCI runtime spec** (~40% fidelity — structural mismatch but partial)
   - `filesystem.*` → `mounts[]` with `ro`/`rw` options
   - `env_credentials` → `process.env`
   - `network.*` → partial namespace config

4. **Reference Landlock** (what nono already does — used for validation)

## Integration with ART stack

- **mache (Go)**: Hosts the translation schema. Uses nono-go SDK to read/validate profiles. Produces projected enforcement configs.
- **ley-line (Rust)**: Embeds nono crate for local kernel enforcement. Exposes arena + NFS with capabilities as signed Cap'n Proto manifests.
- **rosary (Rust)**: Builds nono CapabilitySet from bead file scopes at dispatch time. For local: passes to ley-line/nono. For containers: queries mache for K8s securityContext projection.

## nono profile structure (for reference)

```json
{
  "extends": "default",
  "filesystem": { "allow": [], "read": [], "write": [] },
  "network": { "block": bool, "allow_domain": [], "credentials": [] },
  "security": { "groups": [], "signal_mode": "isolated", "capability_elevation": false },
  "workdir": { "access": "readwrite" },
  "env_credentials": { "KEYSTORE_ACCOUNT": "ENV_VAR" },
  "rollback": { "exclude_patterns": [] }
}
```

Supports `extends` inheritance (max depth 10), variable expansion ($WORKDIR, $HOME), 32 built-in policy groups.

## Mapping quality matrix

| Target | Filesystem | Network | Composition | Overall |
|--------|-----------|---------|-------------|---------|
| AppArmor | ~90% | ~50% | ~80% | Strongest |
| SELinux | ~40% | ~50% | ~60% | Lossy |
| K8s | ~30% | ~60% | N/A | Partial |
| OCI | ~40% | ~30% | N/A | Structural mismatch |

## Depends on

- rosary-394890 (nono sandbox integration in rosary dispatch — Stage 1 validates nono works at all)

description:
Mache can detect .from_store_dolt_rs variants via search, but there's no dedicated tool for "find functions with the same name defined in multiple modules." This is a common code smell query that should be a first-class mache capability.

Would complement get_communities (structural clustering) with a specific dedup-oriented query.

title: Add parent context (_parent key) to child selector matches
description:
When a schema node uses a child selector like `$.item.Vulnerability.FixedIn[*]`, the match context becomes the FixedIn entry and the parent record's fields are inaccessible. Projection schemas (like trivy-db) need both parent and child fields to construct output nodes.

## Problem
```json
{
  "name": "{{.Name}}",
  "selector": "$.item.Vulnerability.FixedIn[*]",
  "children": [{
    "name": "{{.item.Vulnerability.Name}}",  // ERROR: .item not in scope
    "selector": "$"
  }]
}
```

## Proposed fix
In `collectNodes()` (internal/ingest/engine.go ~line 1107), when recursing into children, merge the parent match values into the child match values under a `_parent` key:

```go
// Before passing to child, enrich match values with parent context
childValues := match.Values()
childValues["_parent"] = parentMatch.Values()
```

Then templates can reference: `{{._parent.item.Vulnerability.Name}}`

## Impact
- Enables the trivy-db projection schema (venturi-a25eee) to reference both NamespaceName (parent) and FixedIn fields (child) in the same tree
- Generally useful for any schema that needs to fan out nested arrays while keeping parent context

comments.text: Starting TDD. Plan: inject _parent key into child match values in both collectNodes() and processNode(). Test via JSON ingestion with nested array selectors.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

title: SheafSubscriber: consume watcher-driven daemon.sheaf.invalidate event (LLO v0.6+ payload contract)
description:
LLO v0.6.0 (merged 2026-07-08 via PRs #138/#139/#140) closes the sheaf-invalidation loop end-to-end inside LLO but ships the wire contract with **no mache-side subscription update**. Mache's existing `SheafSubscriber` was written for the pre-loop world where consumer-invoked `op_sheaf_invalidate` was the only source; now the daemon emits watcher-driven `daemon.sheaf.invalidate` too, and the payload contract is different.

## The wire contract shipped in LLO v0.6

Watcher-driven `daemon.sheaf.invalidate` payload (coarse-v1 per LLO bead `e40566`):

```json
{
  "region_ids": ["<id>", "..."],   // ALL currently-known regions (coarse-v1)
  "count": <n>,
  "scope": "all-known",             // sentinel: distinguishes coarse-v1 from future fine-grained
  "changed_files": ["path/a", "path/b"],
  "current_root": "<64-char BLAKE3 hex>",
  "generation": <u64>,
  "prior_generation": <u64>,
  "timestamp_ms": <i64>
}
```

Event topic: `daemon.sheaf.invalidate` (unchanged — same topic as consumer-driven emits).

## What mache needs to do

1. **`internal/leyline/sheaf.go` (`SheafSubscriber`)**: update payload parsing to handle the new fields (`scope`, `changed_files`, `generation`, `prior_generation`, `timestamp_ms`). Existing `region_ids` + `current_root` fields unchanged; just extend the struct.
2. **Eviction policy**: on `scope: "all-known"` (coarse-v1), invalidate ALL sheaf-scoped cache entries. On future `scope: "changed-only"` (LLO bead `e40566`), invalidate only the region_ids in the payload. Design the switch as a `switch` on `scope` so both forms work.
3. **Integration test** that verifies the receive path against a v0.6+ daemon.

## Why this matters

Without this update, mache continues to work (LLO's event fires but mache ignores the new fields), but the moat claim is only half-closed — mache doesn't learn from watcher-driven invalidation, still relies on consumer-invoked polling. The whole point of the LLO gap 1/2/3 work is that mache DOESN'T have to poll anymore.

## Depends on

- LLO v0.6.0 shipped (already done — 2026-07-08)
- LLO integration test bead `ley-line-open-e46151` (end-to-end test) — mache-side implementation can start immediately; the E2E test proves it works

## Coordination hooks

- LLO bead `ley-line-open-a3f764` — the sheaf audit that identified the gaps
- LLO bead `ley-line-open-e40566` — fine-grained diff follow-up (upgrade coarse-v1)
- Related to but not merged with `mache-ffe168` — that bead is about the pointer-store cutover; this one is about the invalidation loop wire contract

comments.text:
Reconciliation (2026-07-08): MUCH OF THIS IS ALREADY IMPLEMENTED. cmd/sheaf_subscribe.go's routeSheafEvent already switches on scope (changed-only → per-region eviction via community IDs; all-known/empty → InvalidateAllScoped), and both topics decode to SheafInvalidateEvent. Predecessor mache-c14c43 (the subscribe+flush mechanism) is now CLOSED as implemented.

REMAINING DELTA for this bead (smaller than the original description implied):
1. Confirm the full v0.6 payload fields (changed_files, generation, prior_generation, timestamp_ms) are parsed + surfaced (e.g. generation → get_sheaf_status), not just region_ids/current_root.
2. DAEMON.-UNIFICATION SIMPLIFICATION (operator 2026-07-08: LLO is unifying on the `daemon.` namespace): drop the legacy pre-v0.6 `sheaf.invalidate` dual-handling and standardize on `daemon.sheaf.invalidate` ONLY — remove the dual-topic branch once LLO stops emitting the old topic.
3. Integration test against a real v0.6+ daemon (the receive path end-to-end).
This is now the one actionable freshness thread; the mechanism underneath it is built.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
Reconciled against #500 (merged as commit 5676684). DELIVERED: the v0.6 watcher-driven payload consumption + scope handling (internal/graph/sheaf_invalidate.go + the scope enum on sheaf_subscriber.go) + tests (cmd/sheaf_subscribe_test.go, internal/graph/sheaf_invalidate_test.go, internal/leyline/sheaf_subscriber_test.go). This is the freshness win — mache now learns from watcher-driven daemon.sheaf.invalidate. Closing as delivered.

Dropping it is GATED on LLO fully retiring the consumer-driven `sheaf.invalidate` topic; while LLO still emits both, mache must keep both. Revisit as a trivial cleanup once LLO confirms the old topic is gone. Noted in RESUME.md.

title: Ship a reusable/includable Taskfile module so consumers (cloister) can run mache's smell gate on their own source
description:
Blocker for using mache's smell gate in ../cloister. Today the `smells` Taskfile target hardcodes `.` (mache's own repo: `mache build . "$DB"` then find-smells), so it can't run against another repo. But the enablers now exist: rules are EMBEDDED in the binary (mache-b0b979/#497) and mache ships an OCI image (v0.15.0) + released binaries — so a consumer already HAS the tool + rules; only a reusable invocation is missing.

Ship a parameterized, INCLUDABLE Taskfile module (e.g. `taskfiles/smells.yml`) that:
- takes SOURCE (dir to scan), optional BASELINE + RULES-override + DB path;
- builds a .db from SOURCE via the mache binary OR `docker run ghcr.io/agentic-research/mache find-smells` (image path needs no local Go toolchain — best for cloister/TS repos);
- runs find-smells --rule '*' against the baseline, failing on NEW findings.
Consumers pull it via Taskfile `includes:` (local path or remote git/http — see taskfile.dev/docs/reference/includes and the package ref the operator flagged) and run `task mache:smells SOURCE=.`. Provide docs + a cloister example.

Relates to taskfile-ci-parity, the OCI distribution work (v0.14.0/v0.15.0 image), and mache-b0b979 (embedded rules). This is what makes the smell gate a cross-repo product, not a mache-internal gate.

comments.text:
Taskfile-docs research (2026-07-08): the distribution unit should be the OCI IMAGE, not a shared Taskfile. Rationale from taskfile.dev docs:
- Taskfile `includes:` supports parameterized vars but requires a LOCAL file (vendor/sync).
- Remote git/http includes DO exist (`includes: mache: https://github.com/agentic-research/mache.git//taskfiles/smells.yml?ref=v0.16.0`, checksum-verified, `?ref=` pinned) BUT are EXPERIMENTAL (`TASK_X_REMOTE_TASKFILES=1`; docs say "production use isn't advised").
Since #497 embeds the rules in the binary and mache ships an OCI image, the robust/portable unit is the IMAGE. Build order:
1. PRIMARY: document + provide a thin consumer task that runs `docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/src" ghcr.io/agentic-research/mache:<tag> find-smells /src ...` (no Go toolchain, no vendoring, pinned by image tag — ideal for cloister/TS repos).
2. CONVENIENCE: ship `taskfiles/smells.yml` (parameterized SOURCE) for repos wanting a local `includes:`.
3. FUTURE: adopt the remote git-include once Task de-experimentalizes it.
Deliver a cloister example using the image path.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: A reusable Taskfile module (includable via Taskfile includes:) runs mache's embedded smell rules against an arbitrary SOURCE dir (via binary or OCI image), failing on new findings vs a baseline; cloister can `includes:` it and run `task mache:smells SOURCE=.` green against its own source; docs + a cloister example included.

title: CLI and MCP are two surfaces with one shared execution core and no parity gate — decide whether one declarative registry is the right target for mache
description:
Owner's framing, verbatim: *"since mache runs as a daemon an 'api' that is both the CLI and MCP is correct (we do this don't we?) and i have this problem in every fucking repo which is why we wanna use the server.json gen."*

I investigated rather than assumed. **Answer to "we do this don't we?": no — not in the sense the framing implies.** But the shape of the gap in mache is materially different from the sibling repos, and the difference should drive the design.

## What I verified (tree 6a37bb9)

**MCP side is already the STRONG half — declaration-driven, with a closed ratchet loop:**
- `internal/mcpregistry.ToolRegistry()` (registry.go:91-111) is the single declarative list — 18 tools with tier annotations.
- `cmd/serve_handlers_test.go:26` (`TestRegisterMCPToolsMatchesMcpRegistry`) asserts symmetric difference between the registry and what `registerMCPTools` actually registers on a live server. Registry ↔ handlers cannot drift.
- `tools/server-json-gen/main.go:253` GENERATES server.json from `ToolRegistry()`, and `validateCoverage` (:371) fails when a registry tool is claimed by no cloister group or a group claims a non-registry tool.
- `cmd/readme_tool_matrix_test.go` pins README's matrix and headline count to the live registry (`tools/list` on a real server, not a grep).

So the owner's instinct is right and already realized on this surface: **server.json generation is the forcing function that made the MCP registry authoritative.** Same conclusion ley-line-open-4ec276's thread reached (its comment #404 argues LLO has the strong half — generate from the in-code registry so drift is unrepresentable — while rosary has the weak half, hand-maintained + assert).

**CLI side is a separate hand-built cobra tree** (`cmd/`), rooted at `rootCmd` ("mache [mountpoint]"), with subcommands wired by scattered `AddCommand` calls in 8 files: build, serve, init, pack, version, list, unmount, clean, find-smells, cache (→ push/pull/verify/inspect), leyline (→ path/exec). No registry, no generated manifest.

**The overlap is ONE capability, not a broad shared surface.** `find_smells`:
- CLI: `cmd/find_smells_cli.go` — cobra command, ~10 package-level flag vars, its own `dbQuerier`, four output formats (json/md/ci/sarif), baseline/ratchet flags.
- MCP: `cmd/serve_find_smells.go` — `makeFindSmellsHandler`, mcp inputSchema.
- They **DO share the execution core**: both call `runSmellRule(qg, rule, sourceID, limit)` — find_smells_cli.go:244 and serve_find_smells.go:121. This is the same pattern rosary reached with `src/bead_ops.rs`.
- They **DO NOT share the surface definition**: flags vs inputSchema, arg parsing, defaults, and output shaping are parallel implementations. The CLI's own Long help even says "Runs the same rule registry that powers the find_smells MCP tool" — a prose claim nothing enforces.

Everything else is disjoint by design: navigation/query tools (list_directory, read_file, find_callers, get_overview…) have no CLI equivalent; operational commands (build, mount, pack, cache, leyline proxy) have no MCP equivalent.

**Nothing gates CLI↔MCP.** Verified: no test reads both `rootCmd` and `mcpregistry.ToolRegistry()`. The repo has parity ratchets for every ADJACENT pair and none for this one:
- docs ↔ CLI: `cmd/docs_cli_surface_test.go` — every documented `mache …` invocation must resolve in the live cobra tree, with valid flags (pflag lookup) and a satisfied `cobra.Args`, recovered via a real POSIX-shell parse. Strong gate.
- Taskfile ↔ GitHub action: `cmd/find_smells_action_test.go:74` (`TestFindSmellsAction_TaskfileParity`), pinning the shared `--rule '*' --tags=gate --limit 100000` invocation shape.
- README ↔ registry, registry ↔ handlers, registry ↔ server.json: above.

## The honest design question

For rosary the framing lands cleanly — `rosary-1a4c0b` measures **10 shared / 31 MCP-only / 38 CLI-only**, i.e. genuine broad overlap where two surfaces really are two spellings of one API. **mache's split is 1 shared.** So "one declarative registry driving CLI *and* MCP" may be answering a question mache does not have; the surfaces are largely orthogonal (operational vs query) rather than redundant.

Two candidate targets, and this bead should pick one:

1. **Narrow (cheap, defensible now):** extend the existing ratchet family with a find_smells CLI↔MCP contract test — same rule selection semantics, same finding shape, same defaults — so the CLI's prose claim ("same rule registry that powers the find_smells MCP tool") becomes enforced. One gate, matching gates that already exist.
2. **Broad (the owner's framing):** a declarative command registry that both the cobra tree and the MCP registry derive from, so a capability is declared once and projected to both. Justified only if the intent is that more capabilities become dual-surface. That is a real question — a daemon-shaped mache arguably SHOULD expose build/pack/cache over MCP, and the read tools over CLI — but it is a product decision, not a refactor, and should be stated before it is built.

## Cross-repo context (record for findability)

- `rosary-1a4c0b` — same bead, other repo: "Conformance/no-drift harness: exercise every tool path + assert CLI↔MCP parity from one declarative registry" (10 shared / 31 MCP-only / 38 CLI-only). Related: `rosary-08a278` (capnp tool registry → generates MCP inputSchemas + clap CLI; DONE), `rosary-8a7305` (generate server.json from the registry), `rosary-c1f669` (EPIC: one declaration per set, every projection derives) — the epic mache's version belongs under conceptually.
- `ley-line-open-4ec276` — generalize notme's schema-bridge into a public substrate crate (one generator/evaluator core, Rust/Go/TS bindings), scoped for exactly this reason; its comment #404 is the strong-half/weak-half argument.
- Related here: [[mache-e390e4]] — the "exercise every tool path" half of rosary-1a4c0b, which mache also fails today (its every-MCP-tool harness has never called get_sheaf_status).
acceptance_criteria: An approved design decision recorded on this bead (or as an ADR in docs/adr/) that: (a) states which of the two targets mache is taking — narrow find_smells CLI↔MCP contract gate, or a shared declarative command registry projecting to both cobra and mcpregistry — with the reason, given the measured 1-shared-capability overlap; (b) if narrow, ships a test in cmd/ that fails when the CLI and MCP find_smells paths disagree on rule selection, finding shape, or defaults, verified by deliberately diverging one and seeing it trip; (c) if broad, names which capabilities become dual-surface and what generates what, following the mcpregistry→server.json precedent. Either way the decision is linked from rosary-1a4c0b and ley-line-open-4ec276 so the three are findable from each other.

title: Consume LLO's arena as the substrate instead of maintaining a parallel one
description:
STRATEGIC FRAMING (from the user, 2026-07-27): "we need to build toward the future LLO is creating, not the weird thing here. LLO offers an fs, sqlite, and wire thing via arena, and is adding CDC etc. i am not saying anything is wrong just that we have improvements to offer."

THE OBSERVATION
LLO's arena already IS a multi-presentation substrate: filesystem (leyline serve, NFS/FUSE), SQLite (_ast/_source/node_defs/node_content), and a wire presentation, with content-defined chunking being added (`leyline cdc`). mache independently maintains a weaker subset of the same idea — MemoryStore, SQLiteWriter, SQLiteGraph, GraphFS/NFS — and the seams between those reimplementations are where the current bug cluster lives:

  mache-e3d9bb  two IngestionTargets disagree on the Children contract, so the same
                source projects to different graphs depending on backend (PROVEN)
  mache-c725e9  constructs silently lost to name collision (P0)
  mache-c777ef  bare, unqualified construct names; 46KB impl blobs
  mache-c7d56d  test vs production constructs indistinguishable

None of these are exotic. They are all consequences of mache re-deriving, in its own store layer, information LLO already computed — and doing it with a weaker identity model.

MEASURED: THE IDENTITY MODEL IS THE CRUX
Identity needs two halves. LLO ships one of them today, and mache uses NEITHER.

  CONTENT half — `_ast.node_hash` (BLOB REFERENCES node_content(node_hash)). Already
  shipping. Verified DURABLE: inserting a function at the top of a file shifts every
  subsequent node_id (function_item_0 -> _1) while every node_hash stays identical.
  This is the right key for dedup, CDC, and incremental memoisation.

  ADDRESS half — MISSING. `node_id` is positional (proven above, so unusable as durable
  address) and `node_defs.token` is not module-qualified, so there is no stable semantic
  path. Verified: two `helper` fns with identical bodies in `mod alpha` and `mod beta`
  share one node_hash (3B23BAE7C8F79967) — correct as content, but it means node_hash
  ALONE cannot address them. They need distinct semantic paths and do not have them.

  mache today uses a THIRD thing: a rendered bare name from a per-language schema
  template. That is why 733 Rust constructs (16.9%) are unaddressable and why 9 of
  mache's own cmd/ init() bodies are absent from its own graph.

WHAT MACHE SHOULD BUILD TOWARD
  1. Key construct identity on (semantic path, node_hash) sourced FROM LLO, rather than
     re-deriving names via tree-sitter selectors per language schema. This kills the
     per-language variant of the naming bug and gives durable identity for free.
  2. Stop maintaining parallel store implementations where the arena already provides
     the presentation. This DELETES the mache-e3d9bb bug class instead of adding a
     conformance test to police it — the fix options currently listed on that bead
     (A/B/C) all assume mache keeps hand-rolling two stores, which is the wrong frame.
  3. Use node_hash + CDC as the incremental-memo substrate, which is what
     project_analysis_as_substrate_query / mache-463612 wants for coverage+lint and what
     warm-resume (rosary-e7a267) wants for cross-session re-reads. One substrate, three
     consumers, rather than a bespoke cache per consumer.

WHAT WE OWE LLO (the improvement to offer — see comments for the exact ask)
Module-qualified definition tokens. `node_defs` qualifies associated functions by impl
type (`FsBlobStore::open`) but not by enclosing module: seven distinct functions across
seven `mod` blocks in ll-open/ts/src/refs.rs all carry the bare token `walk_and_insert`,
with seven distinct node_ids and one identical token (same for all_defs/all_refs/
all_imports). This is the missing ADDRESS half. It also affects LLO's own
find_definition, independent of mache.

SCOPE / NON-GOALS
This bead is the design decision, not the migration. It should produce an ADR: what
mache keeps (schema projection, smell rules, MCP surface — the actual IP) versus what it
delegates to the arena (storage, presentation, identity, chunking). Explicitly NOT a
rewrite; the schema engine is the thing worth keeping and is unaffected.

Do not close the four bugs above by waiting for this. They are real now and need fixing
now. This determines the DIRECTION of those fixes — specifically, prefer fixes that move
identity toward (semantic path, node_hash) over fixes that entrench rendered names.

comments.text:
LLO answer to the three questions (2026-07-27, from the ley-line-open side). Your Q2/Q3 dissolved correctly on your side; Q1 was real. Full detail in ley-line-open-2037b4 / 23377a / 25811f.

## Q1 — deliberate scope, and now the wrong scope

rust_impl_receiver (rs/ll-open/ts/src/refs.rs:531) walks exactly
  function_item -> declaration_list -> impl_item|trait_item
mod_item ALSO has a declaration_list, so it REACHES the match and hits `_ => return None` at :541. Bead caf423 scoped it to receiver qualification. Modules were out of scope then; they should not be now.

Do NOT apply the one-line fix. `"mod_item" => "name"` is wrong: modules NEST (mod a { mod b { fn f } } needs a::b::f) and rust_impl_receiver returns ONE level — correct for impls, which do not nest. It needs an ancestor walk. Also not Rust-only: TS `namespace` has the identical defect (measured). Go/Java/C need NOTHING — your 0 collisions for Go (token, source_id) is real: Go's bare `init` rows are package-level free functions that source_id genuinely addresses, and Go methods already qualify as A.init/B.init.

## The bigger finding — the address half ALREADY EXISTS in LLO

rs/ll-open/lsp/src/project.rs:1028 (walk_symbol), and :925 (flatten_symbols):

    let id = format!("{parent_id}/{}", sym.name);

NAME-keyed, recursive, over the hierarchical DocumentSymbol tree (client.rs:171 requests hierarchicalDocumentSymbolSupport). LLO has been building file/Container/name on the LSP side the whole time. The tree-sitter projection walks the same tree and keys each step by ORDINAL instead.

Same walk, two keying choices, one already correct. So the ask shrinks: not "design qualification for LLO" but "make the tree-sitter walk name-keyed like the sibling projection already is." In-tree prior art.

## What this means for mache

1. ADOPT node_hash NOW — do not wait on the ADR. Verified durable under insertion (inserting a mod above others leaves the hash unchanged). Right key for dedup / CDC / incremental memo. But NEVER use it to ADDRESS: two identical-bodied fns in mod alpha / mod beta share one hash BY DESIGN (node_content is keyed node_hash PRIMARY KEY for intrinsic dedup).

2. Do not build a third identity, and do not entrench rendered names. Your e3d9bb correction was right.

3. Do not block the four bugs on the ADR. They are real now and the direction is settled enough: move toward (address, node_hash).

## What the ADR actually has to do

Namespace reconciliation, not inventing identity. Two id namespaces exist today:
    tree-sitter:  x.rs/mod_item_0/declaration_list/function_item
    lsp:          x.rs/alpha/walk
They are reconciled POSITIONALLY — enrich_symbols resolves referrer_node_id via an _ast JOIN on line/char (ADR-0013 Step 1). That JOIN is exactly where be6136 happened.

Also worth knowing: "path never enters the address" is scoped to node_hash ONLY. _source.id IS the relative path (measured: id = "x.rs"), so the occurrence key (token, node_id, source_id) is path-bearing. ADR-0027 handled that by making be6136's class LOUD (fail-loud FK integrity, unbound_facts) rather than eliminating it.

## Caveats — not verified, do not rely on yet

- walk_symbol does INSERT OR REPLACE INTO _lsp (node_id, ...). If two symbols in one file ever produce the same parent_id/name, the second SILENTLY REPLACES the first. Rust likely cannot hit it; C++ overloads and multiple trait impls might. Needs a fixture; I have not run one.
- LSP is an enrichment pass needing a live language server, so it is not reproducible from source alone the way tree-sitter is. It can be the authority the tree-sitter walk is VALIDATED against, not the substrate identity itself.

## Two more things

- container_node_id is NULL on every def row measured (Rust and Go), despite carrying the partial index idx_defs_container. That fallback does not exist either.
- mache pins leyline-schema v0.10.3. nodes.record's declared type just changed JSON -> TEXT in ley-line-open-f7966d (JSON gave it NUMERIC affinity, so '007' was stored as 7). That pin now matters.

## Release / blocking

LLO is due for a release and is being trued up now. Blocking the mache PR on this is a VALID call — the primitives to do it right exist (node_hash ships and is durable; the name-keyed walk exists in the LSP path), so mache does not need to ship a weaker identity and migrate off it later. Coordinate the schema pin bump with that release rather than landing on v0.10.3.

comments.text:
CORRECTION to "adopt node_hash now" — it carries a condition I did not state, and the ordering matters.

(Reposted: the first version of this comment lost four quoted identifiers to a shell-quoting error on my side, including both ids in correction 1 below — which were the whole point of it.)

## The landmine

node_hash's preimage hashes canonical_kind(raw).unwrap_or(raw)
(rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/cmd_parse.rs:2978 and :3213). So changing a kind's kappa mapping REWRITES every node_hash of that kind.

Concretely: fixing ley-line-open-25811f — giving function_signature_item a non-NULL kappa — rewrites every trait-signature node_hash. I told you to adopt node_hash now in the SAME message that filed that fix. If you had acted on both, the hashes would have moved under you.

Sequence: 25811f lands BEFORE you pin to hashes.

## Two more durability conditions, same root cause

- Most raw kinds are UNMAPPED and fall through to the raw tree-sitter kind, so a grammar bump that renames productions silently rewrites hashes. node_hash durability is conditional on kappa-map AND grammar version. I stated neither.
- Rust attributes are SIBLINGS of the item, not children. #[inline] / #[cfg(...)] change the parent declaration_list's hash but NOT the function's own. Function-granularity memoization keyed on node_hash misses attribute-only changes, which are semantically meaningful.

The advice still stands — node_hash is the right content key, durable under insertion and reflow (both re-verified) — but "durable" is conditional, and the 25811f ordering is a real hazard I created.

## Two further corrections, both mine

1. I said the LSP walk produces ids of the form

       x.rs/alpha/walk

   It does not. The walk is rooted at the literal string "symbols" (lsp/src/project.rs:217, :957), so ids are

       symbols/alpha/walk

   with NO file segment at all. Consequences: they collide ACROSS files, and project_hover is INSERT OR REPLACE on that id (lsp/src/project.rs:783-786), so the last file processed wins. Also walk_symbol runs ONLY in the standalone single-file path (project_lsp_into, :198); the merged/daemon path (merge_lsp_into_ast, :288) keys _lsp POSITIONALLY instead.

   So "the address half already exists in LLO" was too strong. What exists is a name-keyed walk MECHANISM, not a usable address. The DocumentSymbol tree is also not the AST — AST scope nodes are frequently NAMELESS (impl_item has no name field; rust-analyzer synthesizes "impl Handler" server-side), so name synthesis is part of the work, not free.

2. I said "Rust likely cannot hit" the _lsp INSERT OR REPLACE collision. WITHDRAWN. Two cfg-paired impl blocks on the same type in one file render as two same-named DocumentSymbols. Needs a live-server fixture; do not presume Rust-safe.

## Your container_node_id correction went further than you framed it

You showed it is populated for function-local items. Its actual semantics are "nearest enclosing kappa container", so NULL at top level is BY DESIGN and a partial index is the correct shape for a sparse column. It is not a defect at all. My "kill it or fill it" open question started from a false premise and has been removed.

## Also worth knowing

New bug filed on our side from the same review: ley-line-open-470290 — merge_symbol's _ast JOIN has no source_id predicate, so in the daemon an LSP symbol can bind to a node in a DIFFERENT file at the same coordinates. It is the be6136 class, but no counter catches it: a wrong-file match RESOLVES successfully, so it is not an unbound fact and fail-loud FK integrity does not fire. If you consume _lsp from a multi-file projection, treat those bindings as suspect until 470290 lands.

Full evidence — 38 claims with method, verdict, and refs pinned to SHA abd5b86 — is in docs/problems/symbol-identity.md, shipped in PR #281.

comments.text:
DECISION, 2026-07-27 — this supersedes my previous comment on e3d9bb.

I told you "from LLO's side, that delegation is NOT yet a plan" and that e64f36 was
conditional on a decision nobody had made. That decision has now been made:

    LLO COMMITS to being mache's storage / presentation substrate.

So the premise of your "e3d9bb may be moot" note is now sound, and my caveat is
withdrawn.

## What LLO takes on by committing

This is not a free yes. It carries obligations, and I would rather name them than let
you plan against an unqualified promise:

1. ADR-0027 (unified code-fact IR) and ADR-0034 (construct identity) move from Proposed
   to ACCEPTED. You are pinning against them, so they cannot stay drafts.
2. ley-line-open-470290 gets fixed — merge_symbol's _ast JOIN has no source_id
   predicate, so in the daemon an LSP symbol can bind to a node in a DIFFERENT file.
   If you consume _lsp from a multi-file projection, that is load-bearing for you.
3. ley-line-open-4ec276 ships a generated consumer surface with a drift gate. Without
   it, "adopt LLO's schema surface" has nothing to adopt, and you would hand-mirror
   again — which is the class this whole thread exists to close.

## What does NOT change

My recommendation to split e3d9bb still stands, for a different reason now. Even under
delegation, SQLiteWriter.GetNode never populating Children is a bug in code that runs
today, and the guard is structurally unreachable regardless of who owns storage later.
Fix the dead guard now; defer the cross-implementation parity harness to the delegation
work. The harness is the expensive part and the part delegation makes moot — the guard
is neither.

## Sequencing against the release

v0.11.0 is being cut now and carries what you have been waiting on:
  - the address half (23377a) — node_defs qualified by full enclosing scope path
  - the kappa fix (25811f) — trait signatures carry canonical_kind='function', and the
    node_hash rewrite this caused HAS NOW LANDED rather than being pending
  - record JSON -> TEXT (f7966d) — the schema pin you are holding PR #568 for
  - ir_schema_version merkle-ast-v1 -> merkle-ast-v2, and it is now LOAD-BEARING: it
    joins the incremental-reuse guard, so a lineage mismatch forces full re-derivation.
    Previously it was write-only — nothing read it. You now have a programmatic way to
    ask whether cached node_hash values are comparable, which you did not have when I
    first told you to adopt node_hash.

Pin against v0.11.0, not against main.
comments.author: rsry-cli

comments.text:
RATIONALE for the commitment (jamestexas, 2026-07-27) — the "why", which the decision
comment above does not capture.

Delegating to LLO's arena REMOVES A HOP. FS mediation through Rust is cheaper than
mache's current shape, where a Go store layer sits between mache and the data:

  today       mache -> Go store layer (SQLiteWriter/ListChildren) -> SQLite
  delegated   mache -> LLO arena (mmap'd, zero-copy sqlite3_deserialize)

LLO already ships the pieces that make this the cheaper path: SqliteGraph over
sqlite3_deserialize (zero-copy), the mmap'd Controller block carrying current_root, the
reader pool, and the mount projection — which moved to LLO from mache some months ago,
so the precedent for this direction already exists in-tree.

## Why this also dissolves a bug class rather than just being faster

mache-e3d9bb exists because mache maintains TWO IngestionTarget implementations that
disagree. Delegation deletes both, so there is nothing left to hold to a contract. That
is what mache meant by "fewer implementations to hold to a contract at all", and it is
why the expensive parity HARNESS is genuinely moot under this decision.

The cheap half is not moot and should still land: SQLiteWriter.GetNode never populates
Children, so `len(existing.Children) > 0` is structurally unreachable in code running
today. Delegation is not shipped yet; the wrong answers are.

## What must be measured, not assumed

"Cheaper" is the premise of this decision and it is currently unmeasured on our side. It
should not stay that way — LLO already has the harness shape for it (task test:perf,
cold_parse_perf_regression, the p99 read-latency work in ley-line-open-98fb67). Before
declaring the delegation successful, measure the hop removal end to end rather than

Filing that expectation here so the claim is falsifiable later rather than folklore.

comments.text:
CORRECTION to my rationale comment above (jamestexas, 2026-07-27).

I recorded the delegation as a PERFORMANCE argument — "removes a hop, FS mediation via
Rust is cheaper" — and then flagged "cheaper" as an unmeasured premise that had to be
validated before declaring success.

That framing is wrong, and the caveat mostly falls away with it.

## It is a principle, not a performance claim

LLO IS THE DATA PLANE. That is a statement about architectural role, not about latency.

  data plane     moves and stores bytes: content addressing, the arena, CAS,
                 projections, mount, CDC                                -> LLO
  control plane  decides what to do with them: smell rules, queries,
                 code intelligence, the MCP surface                     -> mache

Under that split, mache maintaining its own store is a control-plane component doing
data-plane work. That is a layering violation whether or not it is slow. Delegation is
therefore CORRECT LAYERING, and the hop removal is a consequence of fixing the layering
rather than the reason to fix it.

## What this changes about mache-e3d9bb

Two IngestionTarget implementations that disagree are not an independent bug — they are
a SYMPTOM of the violation. That is why mache's instinct was right that the parity
harness is moot: you do not build a conformance harness across implementations that
should not both exist. The dead-guard fix still stands, because that code runs today.

## What is actually worth verifying

Not "is it faster". The falsifiable question is whether the BOUNDARY HOLDS: after
delegation, does any data-plane logic remain on the mache side? That is checkable by
inspection and by a rule, in a way a benchmark is not — and it is the same shape as
cloister-5e4402's rule for its own boundary ("anything in cloister named `leyline-*` is
a smell; primitives belong in LLO").

Performance should still be observed, but as evidence the layering is sound, not as its
justification. Withdrawing the "unmeasured premise" framing: a role assignment does not
need a benchmark to be correct.

## Ecosystem shape this implies

  LLO       substrate / data plane
  mache     code intelligence over that substrate
  cloister  agent execution + network topology
  rosary    orchestration
  signet    identity
  vigil     observation

cloister-5e4402 already states its half of this. Worth stating LLO's half explicitly
somewhere durable — probably ARCHITECTURE.md — so "is this ours?" has an answer that is
not per-case judgement.

comments.text:
Answering your session-semantics question on 4ec276 — and the answer is worse than
the option you were guarding against.

## Neither. It models NO sessions, and ONE transport.

leyline-mcp-descriptor's ServerMeta carries:

    pub transport_type: &'a str,
    pub transport_url:  &'a str,

Two scalars. There is no session field at all, and because the transport is
singular rather than a list, per-transport session semantics is not merely
unmodelled — it is UNREPRESENTABLE in the current shape.

So your input landed before adoption, which is what you asked for, and it is
correct.

## It is already wrong for LLO, not just for mache

v0.11.2 added `--mcp-uds` (ley-line-open-6569de) so the daemon can serve MCP over
a Unix socket for the cloister attested path. LLO therefore serves TWO transports
now — streamable-http over TCP, and UDS — and its own server.json can describe
only one. The producer broke the shape within hours of the shape being written.

That is independent confirmation of your point from the other direction: it is
not a mache quirk, it is the shape being wrong.

## What I have NOT done, deliberately

I have not guessed at a fix. Two things need deciding and one needs verifying,
and you hold context I do not:

1. WIRE SHAPE. Does the pinned MCP registry schema
   (static.modelcontextprotocol.io/schemas/2025-12-11/server.schema.json) permit
   more than one transport per package, or a session/stateful attribute on a
   transport? If it does not, the honest emission may be one package PER
   TRANSPORT rather than one package with a transport list — and that changes
   what `identifier` + `version` mean per entry. I have not verified this against
   the schema and will not assert it.

2. WHERE SESSION SEMANTICS BELONG. Your framing says per-transport (http
   stateful, stdio not). LLO's UDS carries the same streamable-http protocol over
   AF_UNIX rather than TCP, so for us the session semantics track the PROTOCOL,
   not the socket family. If that generalises, the attribute may belong on the
   protocol rather than on the transport entry — which would be a third answer,
   not either of the two on the table.

3. CLOISTER'S BOOLEAN. You said cloister models one boolean per input and
   currently runs mache sessionless. If the descriptor grows per-transport
   semantics, something has to consume them — otherwise we have moved an
   unrepresentable defect into a representable-but-ignored one, which is not
   obviously better.

## Timing

Cheap to change now: only LLO uses the emitter, the crate shipped in v0.11.2
today, and there is no adopter to migrate. It gets expensive the moment
rosary-1a4c0b or vigil-cd74de wires it in — which is exactly the window you were
trying to catch.

Tell me the shape you want and I will build it. If the answer needs the schema
checked first, say so and I will check it rather than assume.

title: sheaf e2e tests orphan a `mache serve` daemon per run — 84 accumulated, control dirs already deleted, and they share the default arena
description:
Measured and cleaned 2026-07-30. Reaped 84 orphans by hand; filing because hand-reaping does not stop recurrence and the count demonstrably grows during ordinary work.

## What was found

    total `mache serve` processes    87
    sheaf-e2e / sheaf-sub-e2e orphans 84   <- all PPID=1, reparented to init
    legitimate survivors               3   (see below)

Every orphan was of the form:

    mache serve --control /tmp/sheaf-e2e-<rand>/test.ctrl
    mache serve --control /tmp/sheaf-sub-e2e-<rand>/test.ctrl

Oldest had ~6h uptime, each ~10-15 MB RSS (≈1.1 GB resident in aggregate).

**Their control directories no longer exist**: `ls -d /tmp/sheaf-e2e-*` matched ZERO. So the test harness removes its temp dir (t.TempDir cleanup, or an explicit RemoveAll) but never stops the daemon it spawned. The daemon outlives the fixture that owned it and keeps running against a deleted path.

All 84 exited on plain SIGTERM — none needed SIGKILL. They were not wedged; nothing ever signalled them.

## It grows during normal work

Counted 76 earlier in the same session, 87 shortly after — the delta came from my own `task check` runs. Anyone running the suite repeatedly accumulates these silently.

## Why it matters beyond untidiness

These share `~/.mache/default.arena`. Stale daemons against a shared arena are the documented cause of smell-count jitter — the reason `mache build --backend leyline` is preferred as one-shot and isolated. So this is not merely resource waste: it is a source of nondeterministic gate results, and "pkill + move the arena to reset" has been the manual workaround.

Related in shape to mache-e418ce (a supervised daemon kept serving a stale binary): both are "a process outlived the thing that was supposed to own its lifetime, and nothing noticed."

## What must NOT be reaped (for whoever automates this)

Naive `pkill -f "mache serve"` is WRONG. Three legitimate processes matched that pattern today:

    18187  mache serve --http localhost:7532                    <- the SUPERVISED daemon (launchd)
    29352  mache serve --control ~/.mache/default.ctrl           <- the real default arena
    72928  mache serve --control /tmp/cloister-e2e/test.ctrl     <- ANOTHER REPO's e2e leftover

Any reaper must scope to this repo's own test-fixture prefixes and must exclude the supervised daemon explicitly.

## The actual fix

Test-side, not a cleanup script: whatever spawns these must stop them. A `t.Cleanup` that signals the child and waits for exit, so the daemon cannot outlive its fixture. A cleanup script treats the symptom and will drift out of sync with the prefixes it greps for. If a reaper IS wanted for pre-existing strays, it belongs behind `mache clean` (which today handles mounts only) with the exclusion rules above encoded rather than remembered.

Worth also asserting in the suite: after the e2e tests complete, zero `--control /tmp/sheaf-*` processes remain. That turns a silent leak into a failing test, which is the only form that stays fixed.</description>
acceptance_criteria: Running the sheaf e2e suite to completion leaves zero `mache serve --control /tmp/sheaf-*` processes, asserted by the suite itself so a regression fails a test rather than accumulating silently. Any reaper added to `mache clean` must not match the supervised daemon (`serve --http`), the default arena (`--control ~/.mache/default.ctrl`), or other repos' fixtures (e.g. /tmp/cloister-e2e) — proven by a test that plants look-alike processes or argv strings and asserts they are excluded.

title: bug: ListChildren returns internal slice alias — caller mutation corrupts state
description: MemoryStore.ListChildren (graph.go:854) returns `n.Children` — the live backing array. A caller doing `sort.Strings(children)` silently reorders the store's internal state. Fix: `copy(out, n.Children)` before return.

title: bug: ShiftOrigins uint32 underflow on negative delta
