title: Cross-language reference graph: typed locators that span languages
description:
## Problem

mache today treats each file as standalone source. A Terraform module declaring `source = "github.com/foo/bar"` produces a string literal — not a navigable link to the Go HTTP server that lives at that URL. Same gap across the board: Terraform module/provider sources → upstream Git repos; npm/yarn imports → @scoped packages; Go imports → github.com/... module roots; Python pip → PyPI; Docker FROM → upstream images; OpenAPI/proto refs → schema files in another repo.

We have the building block: RegisterAddressRefQuery in internal/ingest/sitter_walker.go (scheme:value, e.g. env:DATABASE_URL). Only used for in-source environment refs today.

## Design space

1. Scheme registry — formalize the currently-implicit list. Each scheme has a name, language origin(s), resolver.
2. Resolver interface — lazy, cacheable: Resolve(scheme, locator) -> (Graph subtree, error). terraform-module-resolver clones the repo and projects via go schema if Go files detected; npm-resolver fetches tarball metadata; etc.
3. Federated graph — cross-refs surface as virtual symlinks (/terraform_modules/foo/... mount points), or edges in find_callers/find_callees that span backend graphs.
4. MCP tool — follow_ref(scheme, locator) -> projected target, or find_callers extending across the boundary.
5. CompositeGraph — already exists (browser/iterm). Extends naturally.

## Open questions

- Eager vs lazy resolution: pulling every upstream dep eagerly would explode disk/time. Lazy means agents discover by walking, not enumeration.
- Caching: per-locator content hash, GC policy.
- Trust: arbitrary git URLs are dangerous. Allowlists or sandboxed projection.
- Cycles: A imports B imports A. CompositeGraph has callerDepth guard; extend cross-language.
- Polyglot targets: the schema for the target is selected by extension/sentinels.

## Existing infra to lean on

- RegisterAddressRefQuery (per-language, per-scheme query)
- CompositeGraph (mount sub-graphs under prefixes)
- callers/ virtual dir (already follows refs across files)
- mache serve <dir> auto-leyline (PR #170) — multi-language ingestion already wired

## First milestone candidate

Pick ONE pair end-to-end:
- Terraform 'source = "..."' (extract via address ref query) → if locator is a local path, project the target dir → expose as a virtual symlink in callers/.
Even just that ships the model and proves out the pieces. Schemes/resolvers grow from there.

comments.text: PR #177 ships the first milestone end-to-end: terraform mod: scheme address-ref query (lands tokens in node_refs/callers/) + resolve_ref MCP tool (local-relative paths only, returns dir listing with detected lang). Remote schemes (npm, go-mod, github) deliberately deferred — they need allowlist/sandbox/cache design first.
comments.author: jamestexas

comments.text:
## Subagent review synthesis (2026-05-10)

Three agents reviewed the cross-language refs proposal in parallel. Strong convergence on shape; explicit corrections to the pitch.

### Implementation reality check (skeptic, paradigm-assessor)

The current implementation is much thinner than this bead's prose implies. Found by reading code, not the bead:

- `internal/ingest/address_refs.go` — real `RegisterAddressRefQuery` extractor registry. Working.
- `internal/ingest/engine_languages.go:157–191` — **3 registered queries total**: `go→env:`, `terraform→env:`, `terraform→mod:`.
- `cmd/serve_resolve_ref.go:62-67` — `switch scheme` with **one arm** (`mod:`), and that arm only resolves `./` and `../` (`isLocalRelativeLocator`, line 138). Everything else returns "remote resolution not yet implemented."

The "no OSS tool occupies this cleanly" framing in the original bead and the just-merged competitive landscape doc is overstated. Stack-graphs (GitHub, tree-sitter-based, declarative scope rules, polyglot composition) occupies an adjacent slice cleanly. SCIP + Sourcegraph occupy the heavyweight slice. **The honest position is: a thin declarative address-level cross-system reference layer integrated with mache's existing projection graph. Polyglot at the *address* layer, not the *type* layer.** Drop "we project, we don't index" as a slogan — for any non-trivial case, the resolver fetches bytes, runs tree-sitter, builds defs/refs, caches, invalidates. Same cost model as Kythe extractors.

### Formal model corrections (theoretical-foundations-analyst)

The URI + resolver + fidelity-poset model is **sound as a structuring principle but conflates three independent axes** that the design will have to separate:

- **Naming**: `scheme:value` is a free monoid over a scheme alphabet, each scheme carrying a partial canonicalization. Already correct.
- **Resolution**: NOT a function — a Kleisli arrow in `(Graph, T)` where `T` is an effects monad capturing `Maybe Graph + Fetching + Forbidden + StaleAt(σ)`. Today's bead pretends resolvers are functions; that leaks partiality into every consumer (same anti-pattern ADR-0013 eliminated).
- **Fidelity**: cleanly separate from naming and resolution. Don't let "trust/freshness of a resolved subgraph" leak into the L₀⊑L₁⊑L₂ poset.

**Better formalism**: Grothendieck fibration `p: GraphMounts → Σ` over the scheme category. **Not a full sheaf** — sheaf gluing requires strict equality on overlaps; cross-language overlaps agree only after lazy fetch settles. Honest framing: "separated presheaf on a coverage, sheafified by arena-clock advance" (ADR-0014's sheaf-cache vocabulary is reaching for this).

**Fidelity cross-language**: chain L₀⊑L₁⊑L₂ does not survive crossing language boundaries. Correct generalization is a **product poset** `L_src × L_tgt`; refs typed `(source_lang, target_lang, fidelity_src, fidelity_tgt)`. L₂ (reachability) saturates at L₁ across language boundaries until a runtime trace exists. ADR-0013 generalizes mechanically.

**"We project, we don't index" is real** at the category-theory layer: indexers are *algebras* over the source functor (derived structure has canonical form, cache key is `Σ_root(index)`). Mache is *coalgebras* — source is canonical, projection is fungible, cache key is `Σ_root(source) × schema × parser_version`. Real distinction, but **the *cost* is identical** — the skeptic's point stands.

**Monorepo = polyrepo**: categorical at the **naming layer only**. Same morphism class. Different *functor properties* at synchrony (one state vs product of arena clocks), failure semantics (miss = bug vs miss = default), trust (capability labels via signet vault slices), refactor atomicity. Saved this caveat in memory.

### Concrete implementation plan (code-architect)

The architect proposed a 5-bead sequence starting from the existing stub:

1. **`internal/resolve/` package**: `Resolver` interface (`Resolve(ctx, locator) (Graph, error)`), `Registry` (scheme → resolver, no global; explicit object per session), sentinel errors `ErrNotResolvable` / `ErrSchemeUnknown`. Pure Go, zero CGO, zero risk. Establishes the contract.

2. **`LocalPathResolver`**: implements `Resolver` for the existing `mod:` local-relative case. Moves `isLocalRelativeLocator` out of `cmd/serve_resolve_ref.go` into the resolver package. Calls `ingest.Engine` with auto-schema for resolved directories. Uses `singleflight.Group` keyed by absolute path to coalesce concurrent resolution. In-memory cache for V1.

3. **Wire `resolve_ref` to mount the sub-graph in `CompositeGraph`**: today the handler ignores its `graph.Graph` parameter and returns flat filesystem metadata. After this bead, successful resolutions mount the resolved sub-graph under `resolve/<prefix>` and add `graph_path` to the response. `find_callers` / `find_callees` / `find_definition` / `list_directory` then work across the boundary **with no changes to those handlers** (federation via `CompositeGraph` is automatic). This is the Terraform → local-path end-to-end milestone for this bead.

4. **`callers/` virtual entries for scheme-typed ref tokens**: extend `GraphFS.Lookup` to emit virtual symlinks from `callers/` entries to mounted sub-graph prefixes when the parent token is a resolvable scheme. Parallels the existing `callees/` symlink pattern.

5. **Second scheme to prove generalization**: either `NPMResolver` (for `npm:` tokens from `package.json`) or `GitResolver` stub (returns `ErrNotResolvable` with a structured `RemoteHint`). Validates that adding a scheme requires one `RegisterAddressRefQuery` call and one `Registry.Register` call — zero changes to core graph or MCP plumbing.

Key architect insight: **don't unify `RegisterAddressRefQuery` with the resolver registry**. Extraction runs at ingest (build phase); resolution runs at query time (read phase). Keep them separate. The `resolve.Registry` is an explicit object passed to handlers, not a process-global sync.Map — testable, no init-order issues, session-isolatable.

### Convergent findings (all three agents agreed)

- **Stack-graphs is the unmentioned closest neighbor** — should appear in `competitive-landscape-2026.md` next refresh. Filed as a follow-up note.
- **Resolvers do real work** — fetch, cache, invalidate. Pretending otherwise (whether via "we project not index" or by typing them as pure functions) creates the same downstream consumer mess.
- **Honest scope is the address layer, not the type layer** — pyo3, cgo, WASM-binding refs need type-system bridging, not URI resolution.

### Recommendation

Ship the proposal with three explicit corrections:

1. Reformulate the model as **fibration over scheme category + product fidelity poset + Kleisli arrow for resolution** (math friend). Probably wants its own ADR — drafting one as 0016 next.
2. Replace the pitch with the skeptic's narrower one: "thin declarative address-level cross-system reference layer." Drop "we project, we don't index."
3. Follow the architect's 5-bead sequence; the first three are pure Go / low-risk / dispatchable in order; beads 4-5 add real cross-system coverage.

Sub-beads 1-5 from the architect's plan should probably be filed as separate beads with this bead becoming the epic. Will file on confirmation.

title: schema-driven read modes for read_file (signatures / map / diff)
description:
## Idea

Add a `mode` query arg to the `read_file` MCP tool so agents can request a compressed projection of a file/dir instead of full content. lean-ctx popularized this; mache has the substrate to do it strictly better.

## Why now

T2.4 (mache-1afff0, merged in PR #365) gives us the `current_root` snapshot identity primitive — that's what makes `mode=diff` expressible ("what changed between root A and root B").

## Modes

- **`mode=full`** (default): existing behavior, render full template content
- **`mode=signatures`**: walk children and concat each child's `signature` leaf instead of `source` — schemas already split a function into `source/`, `signature/`, `doc/` (see examples/go-schema.json). Pure presentation reshape, no new ingestion.
- **`mode=map`**: names only, recursive `list_directory`. Trivial wrapper over `ListChildren`.
- **`mode=diff`**: needs ETag-style content hashing on Node + a `since=<root-hex>` param. The arena's `current_root` is the snapshot identity; the diff is "nodes whose content hash changed between root A and root B."

## Strictly better than lean-ctx's design

lean-ctx bakes 4 fixed modes. Mache's modes can be **schema-driven** — `mode` maps to "which leaf do I render" — so a schema can ship its own modes (`mode=public-api`, `mode=protocol-only`, etc.) without code changes.

## Implementation sketch

- `cmd/serve_handlers.go::registerMCPTools` — accept `mode` param on `read_file`
- New helper that resolves `(node, mode) → content` by picking the leaf name to read
- For `signatures` / `map`: ~50 lines plus possible schema additions for languages that don't already split signature from body
- For `diff`: snapshot-aware, depends on stable per-node content hashes — separate slice of work

## Out of scope

- PR aggregation (lean-ctx `pack --pr`) — belongs in rosary, not mache
- Shell output compression — different layer entirely
- `.lctxpkg` bundles — not mache's product shape

## Refs

- lean-ctx: https://github.com/yvgude/lean-ctx
- Mache PR #365 (merged 2026-05-09): T2.4 `current_root` migration — provides the snapshot identity primitive
- examples/go-schema.json — already splits function nodes into signature/doc/source leaves

comments.text:
**P2 → P1. This is the mache-side lever on the single largest line in the token bill, and it was already scoped correctly.**

## The measurement (2026-07-27, 250-session transcript decomposition)

Carry-weighted cost = block size × number of subsequent requests that re-read it — what the cache-read bill actually tracks.

- `tool_result` = **82.2%** of carry-weighted token cost
- within it, **`Read` = 69.8%** (891 calls, avg **11,149 chars**) vs `Bash` 22.1% (2,424 calls, avg 1,299)
- → **`Read` alone is ~57% of the total bill**
- concentration: top 1% of tool results = 28.6% of bytes; top 5% = 54.1%

The largest single results are whole-file dumps where the question was almost certainly about one construct: 70k of `ll-open/ts/src/refs.rs`, 61k of `cmd_daemon.rs`, 60k of `ARCHITECTURE.md`, 59k of `smell-projector/src/main.rs`, 57k of `cmd/smell_rules.go`.

`mode=signatures` and `mode=map` are exactly the substitution that collapses those. This bead's own note — that the modes are *schema-driven* rather than lean-ctx's four fixed modes, because `mode` maps to "which leaf do I render" and Go schemas already split `source`/`signature`/`doc` — means the cheap half is a presentation reshape with no new ingestion.

## Ownership correction

An earlier framing of this measurement filed the fix against rosary's warm-resume context envelope. That was wrong: rosary's envelope bounds the **handoff chain between dispatch phases** (`src/context/envelope.rs` — "recent phases render hot; older ones demote to CAS refs"). rosary is not in the loop when an agent calls `Read` mid-session; its only tool-level lever is `--allowedTools` at spawn (`src/verify.rs:364`). rosary dispatches; **mache supplies the content**. The content-supply problem is this bead's.

## Sequencing note

A sibling finding — 44.1% of `Read` bytes are in files read more than once (`cmd_daemon.rs` 21×, `rosary/src/main.rs` 16×) — is a *deduplication* concern, not a projection one, and no component in the stack currently owns the built-in `Read` path to fix it. That makes this bead the load-bearing one: a `mode=signatures` response is small enough that re-reading it 21× costs a fraction of re-reading the file 21×. **Compression beats deduplication here because it's the lever we actually own.**

## Measure on Go first

The biggest oversized reads in the sample are `.rs` files in ley-line-open, and Rust def/ref extraction is the known LLO gap (mache-048fb6, mache-9108a1). Go schemas already split signature from body, so `mode=signatures` works there today. Prove it on Go; the Rust win follows the extraction fix, not this bead.

Related: mache-544659 measures the token-efficiency claim this bead is the mechanism for; mache-8fe65f (surface construct kind from node_id paths) is adjacent plumbing.

comments.text:
⚠️ **A load-bearing premise in this bead is factually wrong. Verified against the tree 2026-07-27.**

This bead states:

> "**`mode=signatures`**: walk children and concat each child's `signature` leaf instead of `source` — schemas already split a function into `source/`, `signature/`, `doc/` (see examples/go-schema.json). **Pure presentation reshape, no new ingestion.**"

`examples/go-schema.json` has **no `signature` leaf**. The string `signature` does not appear anywhere in the file. Functions and methods each declare exactly one file:

```json
{"name": "{{.name}}",
 "selector": "(function_declaration name: (identifier) @name) @scope",
 "files": [{"name": "source", "content_template": "{{.scope}}"}]}
```

`@scope` captures the entire declaration including the body. Confirmed in the built db: 5,312 nodes named `source`, zero named `signature`.

**Consequence:** `mode=signatures` is **not** a presentation reshape. It needs new tree-sitter capture groups to grab the declaration head without the body (`(function_declaration name: … parameters: … result: …)` minus `body:`), added to the Go schema and every other language schema that wants the mode. That is ingestion work. The "~50 lines plus possible schema additions" estimate is low; the schema additions *are* the work, and they're per-language.

`mode=map` is unaffected — it's a genuine `ListChildren` wrapper and remains cheap.

## What this does NOT change

The measured win is real and available **today**, without `mode=signatures`, because `find_definition` already returns the construct rather than the file. Baseline from `tools/token-bench` (commit 3a29ac6):

- arm A (whole-file `Read`) **8,455 bytes avg** vs arm B (construct-granular) **748 bytes avg** = **11.3×**
- breakeven **8.7 constructs/file** — beyond that, whole-file is cheaper

So the ordering shifts: **the cheap, already-built lever is getting agents to use construct-granular retrieval at all** (transcripts show 94.4% of `Read`s had no prior structural query on that file), not adding a signatures mode. `mode=signatures` would push arm B below 748 bytes, but it starts from an 11.3× win that already exists and costs per-language schema work to improve.

Recommend: keep P1, but re-scope the first slice to `mode=map` + adoption, and treat `mode=signatures` as a separate, per-language costed piece rather than the headline. Full falsification state (F1 5.6% but over a rarely-taken path, F2 unmeasured, F4 Go-only so far) is on mache-544659.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
**Reversing my own recommendation from earlier today. `mode=signatures` is the load-bearing slice, not `mode=map` + adoption.**

I previously wrote here: *"re-scope the first slice to `mode=map` + adoption, and treat `mode=signatures` as a separate, per-language costed piece rather than the headline."* That was wrong, and the per-answer accounting is what showed it.

## What changed: round trips entered the arithmetic

Measuring bytes-per-read made a line cap look competitive (2.01×, "half the ceiling"). Charging round trips inverts it — per **answer**, a cap's effective ratio is **0.98×**, below parity. It buys the byte saving by covering 49% of the median file and pays it straight back locating the construct.

The reason is an *information* requirement, not protocol overhead: `read_code(path, start, end)` cannot express "the function I care about," so the offsets must be computed first — and computing them **is** the search.

## Why signatures specifically

Signatures is the one mode that eliminates the round trip, because it does not need to know **which** construct — it returns all of them:

| | bytes | round trips | needs intent | % of ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| whole file | 9,363 | 1.0 | no | — |
| **all signatures** | **528** | **1.0** | **no** | **94.4%** |
| one construct | 748 | 1.05 | **yes — a symbol name** | 96.0% |

Same call, same single `path` argument the model already passes, **17.7× less payload, zero positioning.** It reaches 94.4% of ceiling against the construct arm's 96.0% with *one fewer information requirement* — so it works even when the model does not yet know what it is looking for, which is the orientation case that produces the largest reads in the transcripts (`ARCHITECTURE.md`, `Taskfile.yml`, `cmd_daemon.rs`).

`mode=map` is still cheap and still worth having, but it is names-only — it does not answer, it only locates, so it keeps the round trip.

## Caveats on the number

- The 528 B figure uses **first-line-of-construct** as a signature proxy. Sound for Go (one-line signatures); it would undercount multi-line parameter lists and overcount one-line functions where body == signature. Real numbers need the actual leaf.
- That leaf **still does not exist** — the falsification recorded above stands, and this is ingestion work (new tree-sitter captures per language), not a presentation reshape. What changed is that it is now clearly worth the cost, where before I judged it wasn't.

Bench artifact: `docs/benchmarks/token-efficiency-baseline.json` on `feat/mache-544659-token-bench` (pushed), which carries the per-arm and per-answer tables.

title: Terraform ACI: project infrastructure by service via dependency graph
description:
## Problem

Terraform codebases are navigated file-by-file. Agents answering "what does the
API service look like?" grep through dozens of .tf files and correlate with state.

## Proposal

Use mache as an ACI for Terraform:

1. **Parse HCL source** (already supported via tree-sitter)
2. **Parse terraform.tfstate** (JSON — resource attributes, dependencies, outputs)
3. **Cross-reference state ↔ HCL** — state resource → HCL definition
4. **Project by service** — cluster resources via module boundaries, tags, or
   Louvain community detection on the dependency graph
5. **Dependency graph as callers/callees** — depends_on → callees, dependents → callers

Projected view:
```
/services/
  api/
    aws_api_gateway_rest_api.main/
      source        # HCL definition
      state         # live attributes (ARN, endpoint URL)
      depends_on/   # → aws_lambda_function.handler
      dependents/   # → aws_route53_record.api
  database/
    aws_rds_instance.primary/
      source
      state
```

## Key Challenge

Terraform has no native "service" concept. Need module boundaries, tagging
conventions, or community detection to auto-cluster resources into services.

## Prerequisite

- Terraform provider schema (`terraform providers schema -json`) for type-aware
  projection — see sibling issue for schema-driven projection

FUSE was removed in v0.7.0 (ADR-0006-pure-go-mcp-first.md) — NFS via go-nfs/billy is the only mount backend. Scrub stale references; keep ADR-0001 link as historical context. Quick docs PR.

title: find_smells: dep_cycles via SCC over node_refs

Pure-SQL is awkward (recursive CTE termination); pure-Go is cleaner — read (caller_dir, callee_dir) tuples from node_refs, run Tarjan SCC in-process. Doesn't fit the 6-column SQL contract; this is the bead that motivates extending SmellRule beyond pure SQL (Go-callback rules).

title: find_smells: untested_function (static proxy for coverage)

False positives for table-driven tests and helpers — acceptable for a proxy.

title: Expose file-level imports as a virtual node for semantic editing
description: Agents editing functions or traits via AST nodes often need to add new dependencies to the file. Currently, there's no clean way to do this without falling back to raw file editing, which breaks the semantic UX. We should expose a virtual node like `mnt/<File>/imports/source` (or `rust/files/<filename>/imports`) that allows agents to surgically add or modify file-level imports (e.g., `use crate::session::AgentSession;`) safely via the Mache splice pipeline.

title: Support Transactional/Atomic multi-node writes for complex refactors
description: When an agent refactors a trait signature, it must simultaneously update all implementations. If Mache evaluates writes strictly and sequentially, intermediate states will fail tree-sitter validation. Mache needs an atomic batch-write API (or deferred validation until a `commit` signal) to allow interdependent cross-construct refactoring without the safety pipeline incorrectly rejecting the first edit.

title: Implement Sticky/Zombie node handles to preserve AST identity during renames
description: If an agent completely renames a function or alters its core signature, its identity and path in the AST virtual filesystem changes. This can cause the agent to suddenly lose its file handle or fail to read the `last-write-status` diagnostic node. Mache should implement "Sticky Nodes" that temporarily lock the node identity or provide a 301-style redirect to the new AST path during an active session, ensuring the agent's feedback loop isn't broken by its own successful edits.
